entries.title: Abellio, Raymond
entries.heading: Abellio, Raymond (ps. of Georges Soulès), * 11.11.1907 Toulouse, † 26.8.1986 Nice
entries.author: jérôme rousse-lacordaire

body.text: At the end of World War II and a development that had led him from the left wing of the Socialist Party, through Deloncle and Déat’s collaborationist parties, to the Resistance Movement, Georges Soulès, a trained engineer, left politics for esotericism. He did so under the influence of Pierre de Combas, a man well versed in esoteric traditions, whom he met in 1943. Considered one of the great French prose writers of his time, Soulès published his works from 1946 until his death under the pseudonym Raymond Abellio; they comprise a play, novels, autobiographical writings and theoretical essays. By means of these various genres he has developed an all-encompassing system for interpreting the world and history, sustained by elements from the various esoteric traditions to which Pierre de Combas had introduced him, and by the Husserlian phenomenology that he encountered in the 1950s.
body.zh: 第二次世界大战结束之际，乔治·苏莱斯（Georges Soulès）——一位受过训练的工程师——离开了政治，转向秘传主义；此前的一段发展历程曾把他从社会党左翼，经由德隆克尔（Deloncle）与德阿（Déat）的附敌政党，带到了抵抗运动。他之所以如此，是受了皮埃尔·德·孔巴（Pierre de Combas）的影响；此人精通秘传传统，苏莱斯于1943年与他相识。苏莱斯被视为他那个时代法国最伟大的散文作家之一，自1946年起直至去世，他一直以雷蒙·阿贝利奥（Raymond Abellio）为笔名发表作品；这些作品包括一部剧作、若干小说、自传性作品以及理论随笔。借助这些不同的体裁，他发展出一套包罗万象的、用以解释世界与历史的体系；这套体系既得自皮埃尔·德·孔巴向他介绍的种种秘传传统中的要素，也得自他在1950年代接触到的胡塞尔现象学。

body.text: In 1965 Abellio published his book La Structure absolue (The Absolute Structure) which may be considered the key to his philosophical system. The “structure” in question is partly inspired by arithmological traditions [→Number Symbolism] and “kabbalistic” gematria [→Jewish Influences V], along with other influences such as the I Ching, the →Tarot, and →astrology; and partly it is inspired by Edmund Husserl’s phenomenological philosophy. The structure is visually presented as a sphere, similar in some respects to the one presented by → René Guénon in his Le Symbolisme de la croix (1931), and which can be described as follows. First, a horizontal cross (four angles of 90 degrees). Second, a vertical line which runs across that cross, passing through its middle. Third, the cross and the line are enclosed within a sphere whose center is the point of intersection between the horizontal cross and the vertical line. By the same token, the sphere has six poles (the four extremities of the cross, and the two extremities of the vertical line); the point of intersection is not a pole proper, but is considered as important as the poles themselves. This three-dimensional figure is supposed to provide important insights into any domain (science, metaphysics, philosophy, psychology, history, etc), and into the relationships between them, provided that whenever one uses it, the poles have been properly “qualified” in accordance with the kind of enquiry one has chosen to carry out (i.e., the terms or notions one has decided to impart to each of the six poles, whenever one makes use of the sphere, must have been chosen in a pertinent way). Ontologically, as it were, the basic idea that underlies the figure may be summarized as follows. The two lines of the horizontal cross represent two dualities. The extremities of the one line stand respectively for our sense organ(s) and our body; the extremities of the cross’s other line stand respectively for the “object” and the global “world” (the object “detaching” itself, in husserlian terms, from the “world”). As a result we have two dualities, which are said to be “turning” or “moving” around; but not only horizontally, for they are also constantly either tending upward toward the upper part of the horizontal line (the “assumption” toward unity) or descending along its lower part (descent toward multiplicity). As for the center of the sphere, it stands for the “transcendental Self”.
body.zh: 1965年，阿贝利奥出版《绝对结构》（La Structure absolue）一书，此书或可视为其哲学体系的关键。这里所说的“结构”，一部分受数秘学传统［→数字象征］与“卡巴拉式”字母数值学（gematria）［→犹太影响 V］的启发，此外还有其他影响，如《易经》、→塔罗与→占星学；另一部分则受埃德蒙·胡塞尔（Edmund Husserl）现象学哲学的启发。该结构在视觉上呈现为一个球体，在某些方面类似于→勒内·盖农（René Guénon）在《十字架的象征》（Le Symbolisme de la croix，1931）中所展示的球体，可以这样描述：第一，一个水平的十字（四个90度角）。第二，一条垂直线穿过该十字，经过其中心。第三，十字与直线被包含在一个球体之内，球心即水平十字与垂直线的交点。同样地，球体有六个极点（十字的四个端点，以及垂直线的两个端点）；交点本身并不是一个极点，但被认为与诸极点同等重要。这一三维图形据说能为任何领域（科学、形而上学、哲学、心理学、历史等）以及各领域之间的关系提供重要的洞见，条件是：每次使用它时，诸极点都已按照所选择进行的探究类型而得到恰当的“限定”（也就是说，每当使用这个球体时，人们决定赋予六个极点各自的术语或概念，都必须以恰当的方式加以选择）。可以说，在本体论上，这一图形所依据的基本观念可概括如下。水平十字的两条线代表两组二元性。其中一条线的两端分别代表我们的感觉器官与我们的身体；十字另一条线的两端则分别代表“客体”与作为整体的“世界”（用胡塞尔的术语说，客体从“世界”中“脱离”出来）。于是我们便有了两组二元性，据说它们在“旋转”或“运动”；但不只是在水平方向上，因为它们还不断地或者向上趋向横线的上部（朝向统一的“升举”），或者沿着横线的下部下降（朝向多样性的下降）。至于球体的中心，则代表“先验自我”。

body.text: This structure Abellio claims to be “absolute” because he considers it to be applicable – in the context of a doctrine of “universal interdependence” or universal →correspondences – to all areas of reality, including even history. It is supposed to reveal the “invisible history”, or “metahistory”, of civilizations, interconnected with psychology, politics, physics, biology, etc., as well as of the transcendental Self of the human being. Two main elements are said to distinguish the Abellian absolute structure from the Husserlian scheme. First, the fact that he considers his notion of “interdependence” and “intersubjectivity” to be the starting point of the gnostic experience to be achieved, not as its end. Second, his notion of “intensifying dialectic”, by which he means the dynamic movement to be imparted to the sphere, it being understood that, as already noted, its poles have been properly “qualified”.
body.zh: 阿贝利奥宣称这一结构是“绝对的”，因为在他看来，在一种“普遍相互依存”或普遍→对应的学说脉络中，它适用于现实的一切领域，甚至包括历史。据说它能揭示各文明的“看不见的历史”或“元历史”，这些历史与心理学、政治、物理学、生物学等相互关联，同时也能揭示人的先验自我。据说有两个主要因素使阿贝利奥的绝对结构有别于胡塞尔的图式。第一，他认为自己的“相互依存”与“主体间性”概念是要达成的诺斯经验的起点，而非其终点。第二，他的“强化辩证法”（intensifying dialectic）概念，指的是应当赋予球体的动态运动；当然，如前所述，其诸极点须已得到恰当的“限定”。

body.text: Abellio’s essays, works of fiction and autobiographies all must be understood in the context of this dynamics. They are reflective of an ongoing process whose final term he calls the “assumption” (Abellio readily uses Christian terminology: baptism, communion, assumption, etc.) of the world’s multiplicity into the “inner Man”. Man is thus supposed to be able to achieve the complete unification of that multiplicity, a unification that will end up providing the subject with a “gnostic consciousness”, also called “second memory”, by the same token leading to the “transfiguration of the world”. History – the real one as well as Abellio’s historical fictions – then comes full circle, the past being connected to the future in a present beyond time.
body.zh: 阿贝利奥的随笔、虚构作品与自传，都必须在这样一种动态的脉络中加以理解。它们反映着一个持续进行的过程，这一过程的终点，他称之为世界之多样性向“内在之人”的“升举”（assumption；阿贝利奥乐于使用基督教术语：洗礼、圣餐、升举等等）。人因此被认为能够实现那种多样性的完全统一，而这种统一最终将赋予主体一种“诺斯意识”，又称“第二记忆”，并由此导向“世界的变形”。历史——无论是真实的历史还是阿贝利奥的历史虚构——于是完成了一个循环，过去在一种超越时间的当下中与未来相连。

body.text: The various literary genres that comprise Abellio’s work are closely interconnected. They all tend toward the same spiritual goal: the emergence of a transcendental Self. The essays proceed analytically and tend to use autobiographical material. The autobiographical work describes the genesis of the novels and of the essays, and integrates various theoretical elements. Abellio considers the novel to be the most complete form of writing, because it is the most synthetic one. It is not strictly analytical like the essay – it shows more than it demonstrates –, and it is not unfinished like the autobiography. This is why Abellio ascribes to his novels, which are meant to be ‘a call to the reader’s active awareness’(Visages immobiles, 11), a particularly potent initiatic value. Due to this primacy given to novelistic fiction and its supposed power of initiation, Abellio’s work occupies a place apart in 20th-century esotericism: it is certainly one of the rare cases where novelistic material is presented as the catalyst for a gnostic “transmutation of consciousness”. Indeed, although Abellio announced the “end of esotericism” through disoccultation (La fin de l’ésotérisme, 1973) and systematically distanced himself from the esoteric authorities of the past, his thought presents all the elements typical of Western esotericism: the notion of a transmutation of consciousness, the interdependence of various degrees of reality, a particular interest in natural phenomena, the creative →imagination, symbolic hermeneutics, and so forth. By virtue of this, he remains one of the more interesting figures in French esotericism in the 20th century. In addition to his fame as a writer, he is also noted as an epistemologist whose views continue to be instrumental in fostering interdisciplinary research and reflections.
body.zh: 构成阿贝利奥作品的各种文学体裁彼此紧密相连。它们都朝向同一个精神目标：先验自我的显现。随笔以分析的方式推进，并且倾向于使用自传材料。自传性作品描述小说与随笔的生成过程，并整合了各种理论要素。阿贝利奥认为小说是写作中最完整的形式，因为它最具综合性。它不像随笔那样严格地分析——它展示多于论证——，也不像自传那样未完成。正因如此，阿贝利奥赋予他的小说一种特别有力的入门（initiatic）价值，这些小说意在成为“对读者主动觉知的呼唤”（《静止的面容》，11）。由于这种对小说性虚构的优先地位及其所谓的入门力量，阿贝利奥的作品在20世纪秘传主义中占据着一个独特的位置：这无疑是罕见的情形之一，即小说材料被呈现为诺斯式“意识嬗变”的催化剂。的确，尽管阿贝利奥通过“去隐秘化”（disoccultation）宣告了“秘传主义的终结”（《秘传主义的终结》，1973），并系统地与过去的秘传权威保持距离，他的思想却呈现出西方秘传主义的一切典型要素：意识嬗变的观念、不同实在层次的相互依存、对自然现象的特殊兴趣、创造性的→想象、象征诠释学，等等。因此，他仍然是20世纪法国秘传主义中较有趣味的人物之一。除了作为作家的声名之外，他还以认识论者的身份著称，其观点持续在促进跨学科研究与思考方面发挥作用。

entries.title: AE
entries.heading: AE (ps. of George William Russell), * 10.4.1867 Lurgan, † 17.7.1935 Bournemouth
entries.author: henry summerfield

body.text: Theosophist, poet, prose author, artist, journal editor, officer of the Irish Agricultural Organisation Society, and member of the Irish Convention of 1917. George William Russell is best known by his pen-name AE, which he adopted after a compositor was unable to read more than the first two letters of Æon, the Gnostic word for a higher being with which he signed a letter to the editor of the Theosophical journal Lucifer in 1888. Russell was born into a Protestant family in the north of Ireland, and from adolescence onwards he experienced visions of superhuman beings and of scenes from the past and future, visions of which he sought explanations in exoteric and esoteric literature. Soon he came to believe that he possessed memories of previous lives. Around the age of twenty, he was drawn towards the teachings of Madame →Blavatsky, and he joined the Dublin Theosophical Lodge about 1890. Thereupon he embarked on seven years of intense study and systematic meditation. During this period, he made his living as a retail cashier and shared a house, at least intermittently, with other zealous Theosophists. Among these, from 1895, was Violet North, whom he married in 1898. On one wall of the house, he painted a still surviving mural of visionary figures, and in 1894 he published Homeward: Songs by the Way, the first of his many collections of poetry. By the following year, having decided that ancient Irish mythology embodied Theosophical doctrine, he was becoming an enthusiastic patriot. In 1896 he deduced from a vision that there was about to appear in Ireland an avatar who would recreate the nation after the imminent crumbling of the British Empire, and for the rest of his life he hoped to see in the flesh the face that had risen before his inner eye. From 1895 to 1896, he was the student of the visiting American Theosophist James Morgan Pryse (1859-1942), who knew Greek and expounded the esoteric meaning of the New Testament.
body.zh: 神智学者、诗人、散文作家、画家、期刊编辑、爱尔兰农业组织协会（Irish Agricultural Organisation Society）干事，以及1917年爱尔兰制宪会议（Irish Convention）的成员。乔治·威廉·拉塞尔（George William Russell）以其笔名 AE 最为人知。1888年，他致信神智学刊物《路西法》（Lucifer）的编辑，署名 Æon——诺斯替主义用以指称更高存在的“移涌”一词——排字工只辨认得出这个词的前两个字母，他遂采用了 AE 这一笔名。拉塞尔出生于爱尔兰北部的一个新教家庭；自少年时代起，他便经历到超人之存在者以及往昔与未来景象的异象，并试图在显传与秘传文献中为这些异象寻求解释。不久，他开始相信自己拥有前世的记忆。二十岁左右，他被布拉瓦茨基夫人（→Blavatsky）的学说所吸引，约于1890年加入都柏林神智学会分会。此后，他开始为期七年的密集研习与系统冥想。在此期间，他以零售业出纳员的身份谋生，并至少时断时续地与其他热忱的神智学者合住一所房屋。自1895年起，薇尔莉特·诺斯（Violet North）也在这些同住者之中，他于1898年与她结婚。他在房屋的一面墙上绘制了一幅异象人物的壁画，此画至今尚存；1894年，他出版了《归途：途中之歌》（Homeward: Songs by the Way），这是他众多诗集中的第一部。到次年，他已认定古代爱尔兰神话体现了神智学教义，并日渐成为一位热忱的爱国者。1896年，他从一次异象中推断，爱尔兰即将出现一位化身（avatar），此人将在英帝国即将崩解之后重建民族；此后终其余生，他一直希望亲眼见到那张曾在他内心视野中浮现的面孔。1895年至1896年间，他师从来访的美国神智学者詹姆斯·摩根·普赖斯（James Morgan Pryse，1859—1942），此人通晓希腊语，并阐释《新约》的秘传含义。

body.text: In 1897, Russell was persuaded by his intimate friend the poet →W.B. Yeats (1865-1939) to accept employment in the agricultural co-operative movement, which was designed to raise the Irish peasant farmers out of material and mental poverty. Russell believed that, like all human beings, they had fallen from a higher state into the cycle of →reincarnation, and he strove through this work to bring out the buried nobility within them. For more than seven years he persuaded poor men to help themselves by forming credit banks, planned schemes to ameliorate hardship, and shouldered administrative work. But his literary gift was not wasted, for in 1905 he was appointed editor of the Irish Homestead, the weekly journal that existed to support the agricultural co-operative movement, and he held the appointment till the paper ceased publication in 1923. Meanwhile, disillusioned with the Theosophical Society, he left it in 1898 to found his own Hermetic Society [→Hermeticism and Hermetic Societies], in which he taught his followers in Dublin at weekly meetings. He continued to publish poetry, assisted other poets, painted landscapes and visionary figures, and helped to found the Irish National Theatre. As a patriot who combined his nationalism with pacificism, he campaigned for complete self-government for a united Ireland within the British Empire. From 1923 to 1930, he edited the Irish Statesman, a weekly designed to foster the cultural and political life of the newly independent Irish Free State. In 1930, while lecturing in the U.S.A., he rejoiced in a brief reunion in Los Angeles with James Pryse. His wife died in February 1932, and eighteen months later, unhappy with the narrow-minded provincialism engulfing the Free State, Russell moved to London. He died in a nursing home in Bournemouth in 1935.
body.zh: 1897年，拉塞尔在其挚友、诗人叶芝（→W.B. Yeats，1865—1939）的劝说下，接受了农业合作社运动中的职位；该运动旨在使爱尔兰小农摆脱物质与精神上的贫困。拉塞尔相信，农民们如同全人类一样，已从一种更高的状态堕入→转世（reincarnation）的循环；他力图通过这项工作唤起他们内心里埋藏的高贵品质。七年多的时间里，他劝说穷人通过组建信贷银行来互助，筹划缓解困苦的方案，并承担行政事务。但他的文学天赋并未虚掷：1905年，他被任命为《爱尔兰家园》（Irish Homestead）的编辑，这份周刊以支持农业合作社运动为宗旨；他一直担任此职，直到该刊于1923年停刊。与此同时，他对神智学会感到幻灭，于1898年退出，另行创立了自己的赫尔墨斯学会（Hermetic Society）[→赫尔墨斯主义与赫尔墨斯学会]，每周在都柏林的集会上教导追随者。他继续发表诗作，提携其他诗人，绘制风景画与异象人物画，并协助创办爱尔兰国家剧院（Irish National Theatre）。作为一名将民族主义与和平主义结合于一体的爱国者，他为统一的爱尔兰在英帝国之内实现完全自治而奔走呼吁。1923年至1930年，他编辑《爱尔兰政治家》（Irish Statesman），这份周刊旨在促进新近独立的爱尔兰自由邦（Irish Free State）的文化与政治生活。1930年，他在美国讲学期间，于洛杉矶与詹姆斯·普赖斯短暂重聚，深感欣喜。他的妻子于1932年2月去世；十八个月后，由于对笼罩自由邦的狭隘地方主义深感不满，拉塞尔迁居伦敦。1935年，他在伯恩茅斯（Bournemouth）的一所疗养院去世。

body.text: Russell’s early esoteric writings were published in the Irish Theosophist from 1892 through 1897. His principal mystical book is The Candle of Vision (1918), which shows that his beliefs were as firmly rooted in his own visionary experiences as in the syncretism of Blavatsky’s The Secret Doctrine. Towards the end of his life, disappointed that he had never encountered the Incarnation of his vision of 1896, he described the imagined impact of such a being in his romance The Avatars (1933). Even in his editorial articles in the Irish Homestead, evidence of his Theosophical world view occasionally peeps out. Thus his reference to ‘the guardians of humanity’ who will not allow the human race to flee permanently from nature into city life (Notes of the Week, 5.3.1911) refers to the Masters, perfected individuals who have ascended to a higher plane to watch over human life on earth. Similarly ‘the secret Ruler of the World’, who seems to be guiding farmers all over the earth into the co-oper-ative movement, is the Planetary Spirit of Theosophy (Notes of the Week, 7.1.1911). Russell’s recommendation that systematic thought should entail approaching any matter from three viewpoints – its relation to consciousness or the human spirit, to forces or energies, and to material things – is based on the Theosophical trinity of primal emanations from the Deity: the Logos or Divine Mind, the Light of the Logos or the Divine Energy, and the Archaeus or that aspect of the Divine from which matter evolves. Russell’s poetry contains many comparable allusions couched under such seemingly vague phrases as “the Ancient One” (the Planetary Spirit) and “the Mighty Mother” (the Archaeus). In The Interpreters (1922), written during the Anglo-Irish War and the Irish Civil War, Russell traces socialism, nationalism and imperialism to their roots in the Logos, the Archaeus, and the Light of the Logos respectively.
body.zh: 拉塞尔早期的秘传主义著述于1892年至1897年间发表在《爱尔兰神智学者》（Irish Theosophist）上。他的主要神秘主义著作是《幻象之烛》（The Candle of Vision，1918），此书表明，他的信念既深植于他本人的异象经验，也同样深植于布拉瓦茨基《秘密教义》（The Secret Doctrine）的融合主义。晚年，他因始终未能遭遇1896年异象中那位降世化身而深感失望，遂在其传奇小说《诸化身》（The Avatars，1933）中描写了这样一位存在者可能带来的影响。即便在他为《爱尔兰家园》撰写的社论文章中，其神智学世界观的痕迹也偶尔显露。例如，他提到“人类的守护者”不会允许人类永久地逃离自然、遁入城市生活（Notes of the Week，5.3.1911），这指的是“大师”（Masters）——那些已升至更高层面、守望地上人类生活的臻于完善的个体。同样，那位似乎在引导全世界农民投入合作社运动的“世界的神秘统治者”，就是神智学所称的“行星之灵”（Planetary Spirit）（Notes of the Week，7.1.1911）。拉塞尔主张，系统性的思考应当从三个视角考察任何事物——它与意识或人类精神的关系、与力量或能量的关系，以及与物质事物的关系——这一主张依据的是神智学关于神性原初流溢的三位一体：逻各斯（Logos）或神圣心智、逻各斯之光或神圣能量，以及阿奇乌斯（Archaeus），即神性中使物质得以演化的那一面向。拉塞尔的诗作中包含许多类似的典故，它们借“古老者”（the Ancient One，即行星之灵）与“大母”（the Mighty Mother，即阿奇乌斯）这类看似含糊的短语表达出来。《阐释者》（The Interpreters，1922）写于英爱战争与爱尔兰内战期间；在该书中，拉塞尔将社会主义、民族主义与帝国主义分别追溯至其根源：逻各斯、阿奇乌斯与逻各斯之光。

body.text: Although Russell sought to spread the spiritual knowledge that he found in Theosophy and the science of penetrating to reality through inward meditation, he probably had more success in promoting the arts in Ireland, and he played a part in the widespread quest in the early 20th century for economic democracy as a means of stemming the rural exodus. Most of his poetry has faded, but his book The Candle of Vision continues to impress many readers.
body.zh: 尽管拉塞尔力图传播他在神智学中发现的精神知识，以及通过内在冥想洞彻实在的这门“科学”，但他在爱尔兰推动艺术方面或许更为成功；在20世纪初为遏制农村人口外流而普遍寻求经济民主的努力中，他也发挥了一份作用。他的大部分诗作已渐被淡忘，但《幻象之烛》一书至今仍打动着许多读者。

entries.title: Agrippa, Heinrich Cornelius
entries.heading: Agrippa, Heinrich Cornelius, * 1486 Nettesheim, † 1535 or 1536 Grenoble
entries.title_zh: 阿格里帕，海因里希·科尔内利乌斯
entries.author: michaela valente

body.text: German Humanist and theoretician of →magic. Agrippa’s family belonged to the middle nobility in Nettesheim, near Cologne. He studied in Cologne from 1499 to 1502, when he received the degree of magister artium, and later in Paris. During his studies in the latter city, Agrippa seems to have taken part in a secret circle or self-help society, the members of which were interested in studying res arcanae, and with whom he tried to remain in contact in later years. In 1508 he traveled to Spain, where he got involved in an adventurous military campaign to seize a fortified castle near Barcelona. From there he continued traveling, by way of Valencia, the Baleares, Sardinia, Naples, Avignon, and Lyon. Agrippa’s family was by tradition in the service of the Roman Emperors, and thus in his early years as well as later he served as a captain in the army of Maximilian I, Holy Roman Emperor, who awarded him the title of Ritter or knight. His irregular career as a university professor began at the university of Dôle (Burgundy) in 1509, where he was given the opportunity to lecture on → Johannes Reuchlin’s De verbo mirifico, and wrote his De nobilitate et praecellentia foeminae sexus (On the Nobility and Excellence of the Feminine Sex), partly no doubt in an attempt to win the favour of Margaret of Austria. Agrippa’s lectures attracted much interest and earned him a doctorate in theology, but he was forced to leave the city in 1510, after having been attacked by the Franciscan prior Jean Catilinet for judaizing heresy. His study of Reuchlin’s work first suggested to Agrippa the project of a radical restoration of magic. In the winter of 1509-1510 he discussed this with →Johannes Trithemius, to whom he dedicated the first draft of his De occulta philosophia (On the Occult Philosophy), which remained unpublished for the time being. Trithemius – whose own experiences had taught him caution – advised him to persevere with his studies but to ‘talk about arcane secrets only with proper friends’.
body.zh: 德意志人文主义者、→魔法理论家。阿格里帕的家族属于科隆附近内特斯海姆（Nettesheim）的中层贵族。他于1499年至1502年在科隆求学，并于1502年获文学硕士（magister artium）学位，其后又赴巴黎学习。在巴黎求学期间，阿格里帕似乎参加过一个秘密团体或互助会社，其成员热衷于研究 res arcanae（隐秘之事），此后数年间他一直设法与他们保持联系。1508年，他前往西班牙，卷入了一场冒险的军事行动，企图夺取巴塞罗那附近的一座设防城堡。此后他继续旅行，途经巴伦西亚、巴利阿里群岛、撒丁岛、那不勒斯、阿维尼翁与里昂。阿格里帕的家族历来效命于罗马皇帝，因此他早年以及后来都曾在神圣罗马帝国皇帝马克西米利安一世的军队中担任上尉，皇帝授予他 Ritter（骑士）称号。他作为大学教授的生涯并不循常规，始于1509年勃艮第的多勒（Dôle）大学；在那里他获准讲授→约翰内斯·罗伊希林（Johannes Reuchlin）的《论奇妙之言》（De verbo mirifico），并撰写了《论女性性别的尊贵与优越》（De nobilitate et praecellentia foeminae sexus），其中无疑部分是为了博取奥地利玛格丽特的恩宠。阿格里帕的讲座引起很大反响，并为他赢得神学博士学位，但1510年，在遭到方济各会会长让·卡蒂利内（Jean Catilinet）指斥其犯有犹太化异端之后，他被迫离开该城。正是对罗伊希林著作的研究，最初使阿格里帕萌生了彻底复兴魔法的构想。1509年至1510年冬，他与→约翰内斯·特里特米乌斯（Johannes Trithemius）讨论此事，并将《论秘传哲学》（De occulta philosophia）的初稿题献给他；该稿当时并未出版。特里特米乌斯——自身的经历使他学会了谨慎——劝他坚持研究，但“只应与适当的朋友谈论隐秘之事”。

body.text: Having left Dôle, Agrippa went to London, from where he wrote his Expostulatio super Expositione sua in librum De verbo mirifico (Opera II, 508-518) in an attempt to defend himself against Catilinet’s accusations. He repeated his ideas about Reuchlin’s De verbo mirifico, and affirmed that his Christian faith was in no way incompatible with his appreciation for Jewish thought and exegesis: ‘I am a Christian, but I do not dislike Jewish Rabbis’. While in England, he met the Humanist and Platonist John Colet, with whom he studied the Epistles of Paul; and we know that in the following years he was working on a commentary on the Epistle to the Romans. Having returned to his hometown Cologne, at the Faculty of Theology he gave some religious disputations – unfortunately lost – on religious practices in the contemporary church.
body.zh: 离开多勒后，阿格里帕前往伦敦，并在那里写下《就自己对〈论奇妙之言〉所作阐释的申辩》（Expostulatio super Expositione sua in librum De verbo mirifico，Opera II, 508-518），试图为自己辩护，以回应卡蒂利内的指控。他重申了自己关于罗伊希林《论奇妙之言》的观点，并申明自己的基督教信仰与他对犹太思想及解经学的推重绝不相悖：“我是基督徒，但并不厌弃犹太拉比。”在英格兰期间，他结识了人文主义者和柏拉图主义者约翰·科利特（John Colet），并与其一同研读保罗书信；我们可知，此后数年间他一直在撰写一部《罗马书》注释。回到家乡科隆后，他在神学院就当时教会的宗教实践举行过若干场神学辩论——可惜已经散佚。

body.text: From 1511 to 1518 Agrippa lived in northern Italy, and was involved in the conflict between the French and Imperial armies: first in the service of the Emperor Maximilian and later in the circles of William IX Paleologus. In these years he came into contact with Agostino Ricci and perhaps Paolo Ricci, and deepened his knowledge of the writings of →Marsilio Ficino, →Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, and the kabbalah [→Jewish Influences III]. He took part in the schismatic Council of Pisa (1512), but his loyalty to the Roman Church is attested by a letter (Agrippa, Opera II, 710) in which Pietro Bembo, the secretary of Pope Leo X, thanks him and acknowledges his orthodox position. Afterwards he lived for several years in Pavia, where he lectured at the University. His first course was probably devoted to Plato’s Symposium (1512), and in 1515 he lectured on Ficino’s Pimander. Around the same time he composed the Dialogus De homine, which remained unpublished during his lifetime and has survived only in a fragmentary state; based upon Pico della Mirandola’s Heptaplus, it is full of references to the →Hermetic literature. Agrippa married his first (Italian) wife in Pavia, and experienced here one of the happiest periods of his life.
body.zh: 1511年至1518年，阿格里帕居于意大利北部，卷入了法国军队与帝国军队之间的冲突：先是为皇帝马克西米利安效力，后来又进入威廉九世·帕莱奥洛古斯（William IX Paleologus）的圈子。这些年里，他与阿戈斯蒂诺·里奇（Agostino Ricci）有所往来，或许还有保罗·里奇（Paolo Ricci），并加深了对→马尔西利奥·费奇诺（Marsilio Ficino）、→乔瓦尼·皮科·德拉·米兰多拉（Giovanni Pico della Mirandola）的著作以及卡巴拉[→犹太影响 III]的了解。他参加了分裂性的比萨会议（1512），但他对罗马教会的忠诚有一封信为证（Agrippa, Opera II, 710）：教皇利奥十世的秘书彼得罗·本博（Pietro Bembo）在信中向他致谢，并认可其正统立场。此后他在帕维亚居住数年，在该大学授课。他的首门课程大概是讲授柏拉图的《会饮》（1512），1515年则讲授费奇诺的《皮曼德》（Pimander）。大约同时，他撰写了《论人对话》（Dialogus De homine），此书生前未刊，今仅存残篇；它以皮科·德拉·米兰多拉的《七重创世记》（Heptaplus）为基础，充满对→赫尔墨斯主义文献的征引。阿格里帕在帕维亚娶了他的第一位妻子（意大利人），并在此度过了一生中最幸福的时期之一。

body.text: As a consequence of the 1515 French victory at Marignano, where the duchy of Milan was reconquered and the imperial army defeated, Agrippa had to flee from Pavia. He had to leave behind many of his manuscripts, which were later recovered by one of his friends. He moved to Casale, where he wrote his Liber de triplici ratione cognoscendi Deum (Book on the triple way of knowing God) dedicated to his protector William Paleologus. As in earlier and later works, he refuted scholastic theology and emphasized faith rather than human reason as the exclusive way to approach God. His Dehortatio gentilis theologiae, probably written in this period, was based upon a convivial talk given by Agrippa to some friends a few years after his course on the Pimander. He significantly warned them, and all intellectuals, not to go too far in their admiration for the Hermetic writings and neglect the primacy of Christian revelation: ‘if, by taking away secretly, so to speak, the rich spoils from their illegal possessors, the Egyptians, and by elevating yourselves with their riches, you enrich the Church of God, then I no longer advise against pagan literature, but I recommend it to you’. In Turin, his last Italian stay, he lectured on the Epistles of Paul in 1516: it was to be his last appearance in a university context.
body.zh: 1515年法国在马里尼亚诺（Marignano）获胜，米兰公国被重新征服，帝国军队战败，阿格里帕因此不得不逃离帕维亚。他不得不留下许多手稿，这些手稿后来由他的一位友人找回。他迁往卡萨莱（Casale），在那里写成《论认识上帝的三重方式》（Liber de triplici ratione cognoscendi Deum），题献给其庇护人威廉·帕莱奥洛古斯。与此前及此后的著作一样，他驳斥经院神学，强调信仰而非人的理性才是接近上帝的唯一途径。大概写于这一时期的《对异教神学的劝阻》（Dehortatio gentilis theologiae），本于阿格里帕在讲授《皮曼德》数年之后与几位友人的一次宴谈。他意味深长地告诫他们以及所有知识分子，不要因推崇赫尔墨斯主义著作而走得太远，以致忽视基督教启示的首要地位：“如果你们可以说是在暗中从那些不正当的占有者即埃及人手中取走丰富的战利品，并以他们的财富提升自己，从而使上帝的教会富足，那么我便不再劝阻你们研读异教文献，反而向你们推荐它。”在意大利的最后一站都灵，他于1516年讲授保罗书信：这将是他最后一次在大学环境中露面。

body.text: After a short intermezzo at the court of Charles III, Duke of Savoy, Agrippa was employed in 1518 as public advocate and defense lawyer in the free imperial city of Metz. On the eve of the Reformation the religious and theological debate was explosive. Agrippa and his humanist friends followed the developments with great interest and often with sympathy for the Reformers, without going as far as supporting the schism. It is worth noting in this context how in De peccato originale (1518), as in some other writings, Agrippa addressed the problem of salvation: faith is central, while reason is accorded only a secondary role. Agrippa was quite original, furthermore, in suggesting that original sin had consisted in the act of sexual intercourse, and in holding Adam rather than Eve responsible for the Fall. In this same period he also got into a conflict with the Dominicans, Claude Salin in particular, over his support of →Lefèvre d’Etaples’s De una ex tribus Maria. Lefèvre had argued against the popular opinion that Saint Anne had been married three times and had given birth to three daughters: Mary the mother of Jesus, and two other Marys who were considered to be mothers of Apostles. The conflict turned very nasty, with professional teachers sermonizing against Agrippa from the pulpit.
body.zh: 在萨伏依公爵查理三世的宫廷短暂停留之后，阿格里帕于1518年受聘为自由帝国城市梅斯（Metz）的公共辩护人与辩护律师。在宗教改革前夕，宗教与神学论争一触即发。阿格里帕及其人文主义友人极为关注事态发展，且往往同情宗教改革者，但并未走到支持分裂的地步。在此背景下值得注意的是，阿格里帕在《论原罪》（De peccato originale，1518）以及另外一些著作中处理了得救问题：信仰居于中心，理性只被赋予次要地位。此外，阿格里帕颇具独创性地提出，原罪在于性交行为本身，并认为应为堕落负责的是亚当而非夏娃。同一时期，他还因支持→勒费弗尔·戴塔普勒（Lefèvre d’Etaples）的《论三位马利亚中的一位》（De una ex tribus Maria）而与多明我会士、尤其是克洛德·萨兰（Claude Salin）发生冲突。勒费弗尔反驳了当时流行的看法，即圣安妮曾三次结婚并生下三个女儿：耶稣的母亲马利亚，以及另外两位被视为使徒之母的马利亚。冲突变得十分难堪，身为职业教师的对手们在讲道坛上抨击阿格里帕。

body.text: In his capacity of legal advisor to the magistrate of Metz, Agrippa played a crucial role in a famous witch trial in 1519, where he defended a woman accused of witchcraft and, as a result, got into great trouble with the Inquisition. The woman was accused because her mother was considered a witch, and the pact with the devil was believed to be hereditary; but Agrippa argued that the sacrament of baptism was stronger than the pact with the devil. He implicitly accused the inquisitor not only of acting contrary to human decency, the law, and the spirit of Christianity, but also implied that his implicit denial of baptism as a sacrament was heretical. Although Agrippa succeeded in saving the accused’s life, his conflict with the Dominican authorities made his position in Metz untenable and forced him to leave.
body.zh: 作为梅斯市政官的法律顾问，阿格里帕在1519年一桩著名的巫术审判中发挥了关键作用：他为一名被控行巫术的妇女辩护，并因此与宗教裁判所发生严重纠纷。这名妇女之所以被指控，是因为其母亲被视为女巫，而与魔鬼的契约据信可以遗传；但阿格里帕主张，洗礼圣事比与魔鬼的契约更为有力。他隐含地指控宗教裁判官的行为违背人情、法律与基督教精神，并且暗示，此人实际上否认洗礼为圣事，已属异端。尽管阿格里帕成功保住了被告的性命，但他与多明我会当局的冲突使他在梅斯的地位难以维持，迫使他离去。

body.text: Agrippa moved with his wife and child back to Cologne, where he stayed for a year, apparently without regular employment. Here his wife fell ill, and she died soon after, probably during the travel with her husband to Geneva, where Agrippa became a citizen and worked as a physician. He remarried a few months later, with a woman from Geneva who would bear him six children. They traveled to Fribourg early in 1523, where Agrippa continued to work as a physician and gained increasing recognition as a progressive thinker.
body.zh: 阿格里帕携妻儿迁回科隆，在那里逗留了一年，似乎并无固定职务。在此地，他的妻子病倒了，不久便去世，大概是在随丈夫前往日内瓦的途中；阿格里帕在日内瓦取得市民权，并以行医为业。数月后他再婚，娶了一位日内瓦女子，她为他生了六个孩子。1523年初，他们前往弗里堡（Fribourg），阿格里帕继续行医，并作为一位进步思想家日益获得认可。

body.text: He made the mistake of leaving Fribourg in 1524 and accept a position in Lyon, as physician to Louise of Savoy, Queen Mother of France. Agrippa’s expectations were disappointed, for the Queen forced him to write astrological prognostications – a practice he despised – and suspected him of being a partisan of Charles of Bourbon, who was fighting against the King on the side of the Emperor. The Queen’s treasurers refused to pay him his salary, and the court ridiculed him behind his back; at the end of 1527 Agrippa finally left his employment, but his criticisms of the Queen later caused him to be imprisoned for a time. In spite of his troubles in Lyon, Agrippa managed to remain productive. He wrote a commentary to →Llull’s Ars Brevis and a declamation De sacramento matrimonii (On the sacrament of marriage); and in september 1526 he completed one of his most important works: the declamation De incertitudine et vanitate scientiarum et artium atque excellentia verbi Dei (On the uncertainty and vanity of sciences and arts, and on the excellence of the word of God). Apart from his financial troubles, his wife was ill as well, and De incertitudine certainly reflects his depressed mood at the time.
body.zh: 他犯了一个错误：1524年离开弗里堡，接受了里昂的职位，担任法国太后萨伏依的路易丝（Louise of Savoy）的医生。阿格里帕的期望落空了：太后强迫他撰写占星预言——这是他鄙夷的做法——并且怀疑他是波旁的查理（Charles of Bourbon）的党羽，后者正站在皇帝一边与国王作战。太后的司库拒付他的薪俸，宫廷中人也背后讥笑他；1527年底，阿格里帕终于辞去职务，但他对太后的批评后来使他一度入狱。尽管在里昂诸事不顺，阿格里帕仍保持着旺盛的著述。他写了→卢尔（Llull）《简略艺术》（Ars Brevis）的注释，以及一篇演说《论婚姻圣事》（De sacramento matrimonii）；1526年9月，他完成了一部最重要的著作：演说《论科学与技艺的不确定性与虚妄，兼论上帝之言的卓越》（De incertitudine et vanitate scientiarum et artium atque excellentia verbi Dei）。除了经济上的困扰，他的妻子也患病，而《论不确定性与虚妄》无疑反映了他当时消沉的心境。

body.text: In 1528 a new and more successful phase in Agrippa’s life began, with his appointment in Antwerp as advisor and historiographer to the governor of the low countries, Margaret of Austria. He wrote speeches, historiographical works and a document with instructions about an expedition to the Turks. Among the increasing number of students who sought him out was Johann Wier (1515- 1588), who would study with him for four years. At the Imperial Court Agrippa had an influential friend, Eustache Chapuys, an Erasmian humanist (later Charles V’s ambassador in England) to whom he later dedicated his Querela. The first years in Antwerpen seem to have been relatively peaceful and happy for Agrippa. He was able to devote himself to studies in the occult sciences, and in 1529 managed to publish a volume of collected writings; they contained largely theological writings, but also a text on the treatment of epidemic disease. A second edition published in 1532 also contained treatises on monastic life and on the relics of Saint Antony. In August 1529 Agrippa’s peace was interrupted when his wife died of the plague that was sweeping Antwerp. While most of the town physicians fled the city, Agrippa remained on his post, only to be accused by his colleagues later, for illegal practice.
body.zh: 1528年，阿格里帕的人生进入了一个更为顺遂的新阶段：他在安特卫普受聘为低地国家总督奥地利玛格丽特的顾问与史官。他撰写演说、史学著作，以及一份关于远征土耳其人的指示文书。前来求教的学生日渐增多，其中有约翰·维尔（Johann Wier，1515-1588），他随阿格里帕学习了四年。在帝国宫廷中，阿格里帕有一位颇有影响力的朋友欧斯塔什·沙皮伊（Eustache Chapuys），一位伊拉斯谟派人文主义者（后来出任查理五世驻英格兰大使），阿格里帕后来将自己的《怨诉》（Querela）题献给他。在安特卫普的最初几年，对阿格里帕而言似乎较为平静而幸福。他得以潜心研究秘传科学，并于1529年出版了一部文集；其中主要是神学著作，但也有一篇论流行病治疗的文字。1532年出版的第二版还收录了论修道生活与论圣安东尼遗物的论文。1529年8月，他的妻子死于席卷安特卫普的鼠疫，他的平静生活就此中断。当城中大多数医生逃离城市时，阿格里帕坚守岗位，结果后来却被同行指控非法行医。

body.text: Agrippa had obtained an Imperial Privilege to publish several of his works, including De incertitudine; but after it had been published, in 1530, Princess Margaret began to suspect him of heterodoxy and solicited the opinion of the Theology Faculty of Louvain. She died in December, before her suspicions could be confirmed by the theologians, but Agrippa’s troubles were not over: Charles V’s brother, Ferdinand, detested the contents of De incertitudine and wrote about it to the Emperor. The inquiry was continued, and the Louvain theologians judged parts of his work heretical. Agrippa wrote an Apologia in his defense, and a Querela against those who were attacking his good reputation with the Emperor; but meanwhile the Sorbonne theologians attacked and banned De Incertitudine as well, for favouring Lutheranism. As a result of this increasing hostility, including accusations of black magic, Agrippa’s position at the court became unstable and he no longer received payment. In August 1531 he was briefly imprisoned for debt in Brussels.
body.zh: 阿格里帕曾获得帝国特许状，可以出版自己的数部著作，其中包括《论不确定性与虚妄》；但此书于1530年出版后，玛格丽特公主开始怀疑他持异端邪说，并征询鲁汶（Louvain）神学院的意见。她于12月去世，未及由神学家证实其疑虑，但阿格里帕的麻烦并未结束：查理五世之弟斐迪南憎恶《论不确定性与虚妄》的内容，并就此致信皇帝。调查继续进行，鲁汶的神学家判定其著作的部分内容为异端。阿格里帕撰写了《辩护》（Apologia）为自己申辩，并作《怨诉》抨击那些在皇帝面前攻击他声誉的人；但与此同时，索邦的神学家也攻击并查禁《论不确定性与虚妄》，指其偏袒路德宗。由于敌意日增，其中还包括行黑魔法的指控，阿格里帕在宫廷中的地位变得不稳，他也再无薪俸。1531年8月，他因债务在布鲁塞尔短暂入狱。

body.text: In the same year appeared the first book of his De occulta philosophia, dedicated to the progressive Archbishop elector of Cologne, Hermann von Wied, who played an important role in supporting his work in spite of the opposition. However, the
body.zh: 同年，他的《论秘传哲学》第一册问世，题献给思想开明的科隆选帝侯大主教赫尔曼·冯·维德（Hermann von Wied），后者不顾反对，在支持他的工作方面发挥了重要作用。然而，

body.text: Inquisitor of Cologne, Konrad Köllin, denounced De occulta and its author as heretical before the City Council. In his response to the Council, Agrippa accused the theologians of hindering the reform of the Church with their battle against humanists such as Reuchlin and Erasmus (who in a letter to Agrippa praised De incertitudine, but did not want to get involved in the controversies). Against the witch-hunters, whom he claimed were more interested in their own profit than in matters of faith, he seems to have issued a pamphlet denouncing the dangerous misdeeds of the Dominicans; but we only know of this work thanks to a reference in Sisto da Siena’s Bibliotheca Santa. Finally, Agrippa wrote a preface to a work by a Cistercian monk, Godeschalcus Moncordius, in which he opposed the Cisterciansian methods against those of the Dominicans.
body.zh: 科隆的宗教裁判官康拉德·科林（Konrad Köllin）在市议会面前指控《论秘传哲学》及其作者为异端。在给市议会的答复中，阿格里帕指责神学家们对罗伊希林、伊拉斯谟等人文主义者的攻击妨碍了教会改革（伊拉斯谟曾在致阿格里帕的信中称赞《论不确定性与虚妄》，却不愿卷入论争）。针对猎巫者——他声称这些人关心自身利益甚于信仰之事——他似乎还印行过一本小册子，谴责多明我会士的危险劣行；但我们只是通过西斯托·达·锡耶纳（Sisto da Siena）《圣文库》（Bibliotheca Santa）中的一处提及才得知此书。最后，阿格里帕为熙笃会修士戈德沙尔库斯·蒙科迪乌斯（Godeschalcus Moncordius）的一部著作撰写了序言，其中以熙笃会的方法对抗多明我会的方法。

body.text: According to Johannes Wier, Agrippa married a third time, but his wife (a woman from Malines) betrayed him and he repudiated her in 1535. From 1532 on he seems to have resided mainly in Bonn. In 1533 appeared the final and complete version of De occulta philosphia, as well as his commentary on Llull’s Ars Brevis. Agrippa’s last surviving letter dates from the middle of 1533, and for the final years of his life we are dependent on Wier’s account. According to him, Agrippa went to Lyon, where he was briefly imprisoned by King Francis, but released thanks to the intercession of friends. He died in Grenoble in 1535 or 1536 and his body is – ironically – buried in a Dominican church.
body.zh: 据约翰内斯·维尔记载，阿格里帕第三次结婚，但他的妻子（一位梅赫伦女子）背叛了他，他于1535年休弃了她。自1532年起，他似乎主要居住于波恩。1533年，《论秘传哲学》最终完整版问世，同时出版的还有他对卢尔《简略艺术》的注释。阿格里帕现存最后一封信写于1533年年中，关于他生命的最后几年，我们只能依赖维尔的记述。据维尔说，阿格里帕前往里昂，在那里被国王弗朗索瓦短暂囚禁，后经友人斡旋获释。他于1535年或1536年在格勒诺布尔去世，其遗体——颇具讽刺意味地——葬于一座多明我会教堂。

body.text: In spite of his profound religiosity and his deep knowledge, Agrippa was always in danger of being considered a dangerous outsider by the representatives of mainstream Renaissance culture. He lived in an age marked by religious turbulence and never-ending wars. While he liked to adopt an attitude of being “above the parties”, Agrippa did not hesitate to criticize Catholics and Lutherans alike. Nominally a Catholic, he appreciated Luther, whose attack against the abuses of the church and initiatives for reformation he claims were never intended to destroy the idea of the Church itself. Agrippa’s epistolary reflects his ambiguity in this regard: in a letter to his friend Campeggi (Opera II, 1010- 1012), he expresses his hope that the Church will soon be reunified and ‘freed from the impiety of the heretics and the darkness of the Sophists’ (that is to say: the scholastic theologians). The successive letter, dated 17 September 1532, is addressed to Melanchton and is famous because of its reference to ‘that unconquered heretic Martin Luther’ (a formulation repeated in De incertitudine, but in a less favourable context). Discussing Agrippa’s relation to contemporary Reformation currents, Paola Zambelli (1967) has placed him in the context of the radical Reformation and the spiritualists, nicodemism in particular.
body.zh: 尽管阿格里帕宗教情感深沉、学识渊博，他却始终面临被文艺复兴主流文化的代表们视为危险局外人的处境。他生活的时代以宗教动荡与无休止的战争为标志。阿格里帕喜欢采取一种“超然于党派之上”的姿态，却又毫不犹豫地批评天主教徒与路德宗信徒。他名义上是天主教徒，却赏识路德；他声称，路德对教会弊端的抨击与改革举措，从来无意摧毁教会本身这一理念。阿格里帕的书信反映出他在这方面的含混态度：在致友人坎佩吉（Campeggi）的一封信中（Opera II, 1010-1012），他表示希望教会早日重新合一，并“摆脱异端的不敬与诡辩家的黑暗”（也就是说：经院神学家）。紧接着的一封信写于1532年9月17日，收信人是梅兰希顿（Melanchton），因其中提到“那位不可战胜的异端者马丁·路德”而闻名（这一说法在《论不确定性与虚妄》中重复出现，但语境较为不利）。在讨论阿格里帕与同时代宗教改革思潮的关系时，保拉·赞贝利（Paola Zambelli，1967）将他置于激进宗教改革与唯灵论者、尤其是尼哥底母主义（nicodemism）的语境之中。

body.text: In the De nobilitate et praecellentia foeminae sexus (published in 1529) Agrippa argued, against the traditional misogynic perspective, that women are superior to men, even though the representatives of the public sphere from which they had long been excluded did not accept this point of view. At the beginning of the 15th century a feminist trend had emerged in France, Italy and Spain, contradicting the traditional idea of female inferiority, and the responsibility of woman for original sin; inspired by the Roman de la Rose, it presented women as good, noble and pure. The originality of Agrippa’s treatise lies in his use of kabbalistic and neoplatonic sources [→Neoplatonism], according to which woman is an immediate manifestation of the divine, a principle of original life. For Agrippa all the virtues of Nature were evident in woman, considered superior by him because of her proximity to the divine. The treatise is important for having introduced into France the Platonic and Ficinian cult of beauty, according to which woman is the mediator between the human and the divine. As to the question of why women were excluded, he argued that this had to do with social conditions, education, and the prejudices of the age: obstacles that could be removed.
body.zh: 在《论女性性别的尊贵与优越》（1529年出版）中，阿格里帕反驳传统的厌女视角，主张女性优于男性，尽管长期将女性排斥在外的公共领域的代表们并不接受这一看法。15世纪初，法国、意大利与西班牙曾出现一股女权主义潮流，反驳女性低劣以及女性应对原罪负责的传统观念；它受《玫瑰传奇》（Roman de la Rose）启发，把女性描绘为善良、高贵而纯洁的。阿格里帕此论的独创性在于，他运用了卡巴拉与新柏拉图主义的资料[→新柏拉图主义]，据此，女性是神性的直接显现，是原初生命的原则。在阿格里帕看来，自然的一切德性都在女性身上彰明，而他认为女性因其接近神性而更为优越。这篇论著的重要性在于，它把柏拉图式与费奇诺式的美的崇拜引入法国；依此，女性是人与神之间的中介。至于女性为何遭到排斥，他主张这与社会环境、教育以及时代的偏见有关：这些都是可以清除的障碍。

body.text: Agrippa’s most notorious work, his masterpiece, and the one which gave rise to his undeserved reputation as a black magician, is his De occulta philosophia, whose final version in three books was published in 1533. It is a systematic synthesis of “occult philosophy” or “magic” (Agrippa originally wanted to call it De magia): the first book treats of the natural magic relevant to the sublunar or elementary world; the second book discusses → number symbolism, mathematics, →music and → astrology as relevant to the celestial world; and the third book is largely Christian-kabbalistic, focusing on angelology and prophecy as relevant to the highest or intellectual world. Magic emerges from Agrippa’s magnum opus as the most perfect science, by means of which one may come to know both nature and God. Prior to the final version of 1533, Agrippa’s thinking as reflected in De occulta philosophia passed through several stages. The book has been called “a neoplatonic credo”: the influence of Ficino and Pico is evident, but less famous authors such as →Lazzarelli play a significant role as well. The first version – an encyclopaedic review rather than a treatise – most clearly reveals Agrippa’s profound dependence on his predecessors, Reuchlin in particular. The final draft, as pointed out by Perrone Compagni, reveals a more mature grasp of the subject and of his claims about spiritual rebirth as necessary for religious reform. The latter should take place step by step: one must progressively remove one’s ties to the blinding theology (scholasticism in particular) that conceals the real meaning of the Holy Scriptures. Through continuous contemplation of divine things, the soul may free itself from the lure of the senses. In his dedicatory letter to Trithemius, Agrippa seeks to explain how magic, which the ancient philosophers considered the highest science, could have fallen into such disrepute; he argues that ‘by a certain corruption of times and men’, many dangerous errors and superstitions crept in, and false philosophers prefixed the title of “magic” to their heresies and wicked practices. It is now necessary to restore magic to its former state of the purest kind of religion; and from the Third Book one can deduce that Agrippa conceived of the latter largely in terms of Christian kabbalah.
body.zh: 阿格里帕最著名的著作、他的代表作，也是使他蒙受黑魔法师这一不当名声的作品，便是《论秘传哲学》；其最终的三卷本于1533年出版。此书是对“秘传哲学”或“魔法”的系统综合（阿格里帕最初想把它命名为《论魔法》De magia）：第一卷讨论与月下界或元素界相关的自然魔法；第二卷讨论与天界相关的→数字象征、数学、→音乐与→占星学；第三卷则大体上是基督教卡巴拉式的，聚焦于与最高界或理智界相关的天使学与预言。在阿格里帕这部巨著中，魔法显现为最完善的科学，凭借它可以认识自然与上帝二者。在1533年的最终版本之前，《论秘传哲学》所反映的阿格里帕思想经历过数个阶段。此书曾被称为“一份新柏拉图主义的信条”：费奇诺与皮科的影响显而易见，但一些不那么著名的作者，如→拉扎雷利（Lazzarelli），也发挥了重要作用。第一个版本——与其说是一部论著，不如说是一篇百科式的综述——最清楚地显示出阿格里帕对其前辈、尤其是罗伊希林的深刻依赖。正如佩罗内·孔帕尼（Perrone Compagni）所指出的，最终稿显示出他对该主题更为成熟的把握，也显示出他关于精神重生为宗教改革所必需的主张更为成熟。后者应当逐步进行：人必须逐渐摆脱与那种遮蔽《圣经》真正含义的致盲神学（尤其是经院哲学）的束缚。通过对神圣之物的持续沉思，灵魂可以摆脱感官的诱惑。在致特里特米乌斯的题献信中，阿格里帕试图解释，为何古代哲学家视为最高科学的魔法竟会沦落到如此声名狼藉的地步；他主张，“由于时代与人的某种败坏”，许多危险的谬误与迷信悄然渗入，虚假的哲学家们把“魔法”之名加在自己的异端与邪恶行径之前。如今必须把魔法恢复到它昔日作为最纯粹宗教的状态；从第三卷可以推知，阿格里帕在很大程度上是以基督教卡巴拉来构想这种宗教的。

body.text: In his other great work, De incertitudine, Agrippa seeks to show the relativity of all human knowledge, as compared to God’s word as the only foundation of true certainty, by means of an incisive attack on all the sciences and arts. Echoing Erasmus’ Encomium Moriae, Agrippa satiricizes various beliefs, deploring the superstitions that have ruined the original purity of the Christian Church. The work has been incorrectly interpreted as a revival of Greek scepticism; but actually, Agrippa’s aim was to build a new concept of faith, based on divine revelation more than on Church interpretation, and to expose the blindness and arrogance of the school-theologians. The Bible should be restored to a leading role in Christian belief and practice. Marc van der Poel has located Agrippa within the Ciceronian tradition, and shows how De incertitudine can be considered the culmination of Agrippa’s battle against the scholastic theologians.
body.zh: 在另一部巨著《论不确定性与虚妄》中，阿格里帕通过对一切科学与技艺的犀利攻击，力图表明一切人类知识都是相对的，唯有上帝之言才是真正确定性的唯一基础。阿格里帕呼应伊拉斯谟的《愚人颂》（Encomium Moriae），讽刺种种信仰，痛惜那些破坏了基督教会原初纯洁性的迷信。此书曾被错误地解释为希腊怀疑主义的复兴；但实际上，阿格里帕的目的是建立一种新的信仰概念，它更多地基于神的启示而非教会的解释，同时揭露学院派神学家的盲目与傲慢。《圣经》应当在基督教的信仰与实践中重新占据主导地位。马克·范德普尔（Marc van der Poel）将阿格里帕置于西塞罗传统之中，并说明《论不确定性与虚妄》如何可被视为阿格里帕与经院神学家论战的顶峰。

body.text: There has been much scholarly debate about what might seem to be a contradiction between Agrippa’s defense of the occult sciences in De occulta philosophia, and his description of all human sciences as “vain and uncertain” in De incertitudine. However, the contradiction can be largely resolved by recognizing how sharply Agrippa distinguished between reason and faith: he criticized the scholastics for ignoring this distinction and thereby confusing the study of created things with the study of divine things. The authority of God’s revelation in the holy Scriptures ‘cannot be grasped by any judgment of our senses, by any reasoning of our mind, by any syllogism delivering proof, by any science, by any speculation, by any contemplation, in short, by any human powers, but only by faith in Jesus Christ, poured into our soul by God the Father through the intermediary of the Holy Spirit’ (De incertitudine, in Opera, 299). Divine matters are not a matter for debate but an object of faith; in contrast, we are permitted ‘to philosophize, dispute, and formulate deductions by means of our intellect concerning all created things’, as long as we do not put our faith and hope in them (De originale peccato, in Opera, 553). From that perspective, one understands how the occult sciences can be a legitimate object of study, even though they must be considered “vain and uncertain” as a basis for absolute religious certainty. Accordingly, De occulta philosophia ended with a discussion of how to live a religious life that may make one worthy of receiving divine revelations.
body.zh: 学界曾有大量讨论，涉及一个看似矛盾之处：阿格里帕在《论秘传哲学》中为秘传科学辩护，却在《论不确定性与虚妄》中把一切人类科学都描述为“虚妄而不可靠”。然而，只要认识到阿格里帕如何严格区分理性与信仰，这一矛盾大体上便可化解：他批评经院学者忽视这一区分，从而把对受造之物的研究同对神圣之物的研究混为一谈。《圣经》中上帝启示的权威“不能凭我们感官的任何判断、我们心智的任何推理、任何提供证明的三段论、任何科学、任何思辨、任何沉思，简言之，不能凭任何人的能力去把握，而只能凭对耶稣基督的信仰；这信仰由圣父藉圣灵的中介倾注于我们的灵魂”（《论不确定性与虚妄》，见 Opera, 299）。神圣之事不是辩论的对象，而是信仰的对象；相反，我们被允许“就一切受造之物进行哲学思考、辩论并凭理智作出推论”，只要我们不把信仰与希望寄托于其中（《论原罪》，见 Opera, 553）。由此视角便可理解，秘传科学何以能够成为合法研究对象，尽管作为绝对宗教确定性的基础，它们必须被视为“虚妄而不可靠”。因此，《论秘传哲学》以讨论如何过一种宗教生活作结，这种生活或可使人配得接受神的启示。

body.text: Many unsubstantiated rumours began to circulate about Agrippa already during his life. The most influential portrait was presented by Paolo Giovio (1483-1552) in his Elogia virorum illustrium, which describes him as a man with a powerful mind, through which he tried to destroy the République des lettres. The most enduring part of Giovio’s portrayal concerns Agrippa’s death and the legend of his black dog. Agrippa’s love for animals and his passion for his dog (whom he called “monsieur”) was interpreted by the Italian humanist as proof that the dog was no one else than the devil. Two later authors, Andreas Hondorff and André Thevet, accepted the story and contributed to its diffusion. The legend was disputed by Agrippa’s pupil Johann Wier, in his De praestigiis daemonum ac incantationibus (1563). Wier also attacked the attribution to Agrippa of a magical text known as the “Fourth Book of Occult Philosophy”, the contents of which seemed to confirm his reputation as a black magician. A different literary tradition, influenced by several thinkers from Rabelais to Apollinaire and Thomas Mann, and including →Goethe, looks at Agrippa as an archetype of the Faust figure.
body.zh: 早在阿格里帕生前，关于他的许多无稽传闻便开始流传。最具影响力的刻画出自保罗·焦维奥（Paolo Giovio，1483-1552）的《名人赞辞》（Elogia virorum illustrium），书中称他心智强健，并借以试图摧毁“文人共和国”（République des lettres）。焦维奥这一刻画中流传最久的部分，涉及阿格里帕之死以及他那条黑狗的传说。阿格里帕对动物的喜爱以及对那条狗（他称之为“先生”）的钟爱，被这位意大利人文主义者解释为证据，证明那条狗不是别人，正是魔鬼。后来的两位作者安德烈亚斯·洪多夫（Andreas Hondorff）与安德烈·泰韦（André Thevet）接受了这一说法，并促使其流传。阿格里帕的学生约翰·维尔在《魔鬼的幻术与咒术》（De praestigiis daemonum ac incantationibus，1563）中反驳了这一传说。维尔还抨击了把一部名为《秘传哲学第四卷》的魔法文本归于阿格里帕名下的做法，因为该书内容似乎印证了他作为黑魔法师的名声。另一条文学传统则把阿格里帕视为浮士德式人物的原型；这一传统受到从拉伯雷到阿波利奈尔、托马斯·曼等数位思想家的影响，也包括→歌德在内。

body.text: As Pierre Bayle wrote in his Dictionnaire, despite his great knowledge Agrippa was considered malheureux because of his great curiosity, his all too free spirit, and his unstable mood. With his restless journeys, he indeed seems to embody the spirit of the Renaissance. It is regrettable, although perhaps not surprising, that this outstanding thinker has gone down in history as little more than a magician, for precisely Agrippa’s ambivalent position with respect to various religious and intellectual issues central to his time, and the very ambiguity of his combination of magic and skepsis in the search for truth, make him a fascinating representative of Renaissance culture. In any case, his De occulta philosophia is considered the standard summa of Renaissance magic, and has exerted an incalculable influence on later magical and esoteric traditions.
body.zh: 正如皮埃尔·培尔（Pierre Bayle）在《历史与批判辞典》（Dictionnaire）中所写，尽管阿格里帕学识渊博，他却因其过盛的好奇心、过于自由的精神以及不稳定的性情而被视为 malheureux（不幸之人）。他马不停蹄的漫游，确实似乎体现了文艺复兴的精神。这位杰出的思想家在历史上留下的形象几乎只是一位魔法师，这令人遗憾，尽管也许并不令人意外；因为恰恰是阿格里帕在同时代诸多核心宗教与思想问题上的模棱两可立场，以及他在探求真理时把魔法与 skepsis（怀疑）结合起来的那种含混性本身，使他成为文艺复兴文化一个引人入胜的代表。无论如何，他的《论秘传哲学》被视为文艺复兴魔法的标准大全，并对后世魔法与秘传主义传统产生了不可估量的影响。

entries.title: Albertus Magnus
entries.heading: Albertus Magnus, * ca. 1200 near Lauingen, † 15.11.1280 Cologne
entries.author: claire fanger

body.text: 1. Life 2. Works 3. Works of Questionable Authenticity 4. Saint and Magician
body.zh: 1. 生平 2. 著作 3. 真伪存疑的著作 4. 圣人与魔法师

body.text: 1. Life
body.zh: 1. 生平

body.text: German philosopher and theologian, one of the most influential Aristotelian [→Aristotelianism] synthesizers of the 13th century, Dominican friar, teacher of Thomas Aquinas (c. 1225-1274). Albert was born into a Swabian family of knights and joined the Dominican order when he was a student at Padua, receiving the habit from Jordan of Saxony in 1223. It seems likely that he was sent to Cologne to make his novitiate and study theology from the local lector. Later, probably in the early 1240s, he was sent to Paris to lecture on the Sentences under the Dominican Master Guéric of St.- Quentin (Dominican Master 1233-1245). In 1245, Albert succeeded Guéric as Dominican Regent Master, a position he held until 1248. During this period Albert met Thomas Aquinas, who arrived in Paris in 1245 during Albert’s first year as Regent Master. In 1248 Albert returned to Cologne with Thomas to establish the first Studium Generale in Germany in association with the new Dominican cloister of Heilige Kreuz. He remained in Cologne as Regent Master of the Studium Generale from 1248-1254 (Thomas returned to Paris in the fall of 1252, becoming Regent Master there in 1256).
body.zh: 德意志哲学家与神学家，十三世纪最有影响的亚里士多德主义[→亚里士多德主义]综合者之一，多明我会修士，托马斯·阿奎那（Thomas Aquinas，约1225-1274）的老师。阿尔伯特出身于施瓦本的一个骑士家族，在帕多瓦求学期间加入多明我会，1223年从萨克森的约尔丹（Jordan of Saxony）手中接受了会衣。他很可能被派往科隆完成初学期，并随当地的讲师（lector）学习神学。后来，大约在1240年代初，他被派往巴黎，在多明我会导师圣康坦的盖里克（Guéric of St.- Quentin，任多明我会导师1233-1245）门下讲授《箴言四书》。1245年，阿尔伯特接替盖里克出任多明我会摄政导师（Regent Master），任职至1248年。在此期间，阿尔伯特结识了托马斯·阿奎那；阿奎那于1245年、即阿尔伯特就任摄政导师的第一年抵达巴黎。1248年，阿尔伯特与托马斯一同返回科隆，依托新建的多明我会圣十字（Heilige Kreuz）修道院，建立了德意志第一所总学馆（Studium Generale）。1248年至1254年，他留在科隆担任总学馆的摄政导师（托马斯于1252年秋返回巴黎，1256年在那里出任摄政导师）。

body.text: Among the earliest works certainly known to have come from Albert’s hand are public lectures he delivered during this period as Master at Cologne on →Pseudo-Dionysius Areopagita’s De divinis nominibus and (although he was engaged to teach theology, not philosophy) on Aristotle’s Ethics, a work lately made available in translation by Robert Grosseteste (c. 1175-1253). Albert appears to have been unworried by the Parisian bans on Aristotle early in the century and the papal reiteration of the need to purge the Aristotelian corpus of error in 1231. An independent thinker whose interest in the natural sciences and Aristotelian philosophy were lifelong, Albert saw no essential conflict between science and theology, believing that philosophical truth, faithfully sought, could only support, not detract from, the truth of theology. By the mid-1250s, the acceptance of at least some of Aristotle’s works into the official Parisian curriculum was likely influenced by the interest shown in the Aristotelian corpus by Albert, Thomas, and others of their contemporaries who had taught at Paris and shared similar views on the need to maintain a productive relationship between philosophy and revealed truth.
body.zh: 可以确知出自阿尔伯特手笔的最早作品之一，是他在科隆任导师期间所作的公开讲座，分别讲→伪狄奥尼修斯·阿雷奥帕吉塔（Pseudo-Dionysius Areopagita）的《论神名》（De divinis nominibus），以及（尽管他受聘讲授的是神学而非哲学）亚里士多德的《伦理学》——该书不久前由罗伯特·格罗斯泰斯特（Robert Grosseteste，约1175-1253）译出。阿尔伯特似乎并不为本世纪初巴黎对亚里士多德的禁令，以及1231年教宗重申必须清除亚里士多德著作中的错误而担忧。阿尔伯特是一位独立的思想家，对自然科学与亚里士多德哲学的兴趣终身不衰；他并不认为科学与神学之间存在本质冲突，相信只要忠实探求，哲学真理只会支持、而不会减损神学真理。到1250年代中期，至少部分亚里士多德著作被纳入巴黎的正式课程，这很可能受到阿尔伯特、托马斯以及他们那些曾在巴黎任教、并在哲学与启示真理之间应保持富有成效之关系这一点上持相似看法的同时代人的影响。

body.text: In 1254, Albert was elected Prior Provincial of the Province of Teutonia. The province at that time included something over 50 priories, all of which Albert engaged to visit personally on foot (Dominicans being forbidden the use of horses or wagons). He resigned from this job in June of 1257 in Florence and by 1258 he had returned to Cologne to resume his position as lector at Heilige Kreuz. It was not long, however, before another set of arduous administrative duties imposed themselves. In 1259 Albert was requested by the Papal Curia to fill the position of Bishop of Regensburg (also called Ratisbon). Albert had already shown skill as a mediator of conflicts, and a diplomatic touch was needed for this post, since the unpopularity of the previous Bishop had resulted in a forced resignation, and the acephalous diocese was now torn by strife and bankrupt. After consideration Albert decided to accept the position against the advice of the Master General of his order, putting himself under direct obedience to the Pope. Though technically this move released him from obedience to the Master General, it is clear that Albert never ceased to regard himself as a Dominican, obeying the rules of the order so far as it was in his power to do so, and also that the order did not cease to consider him one of their own.
body.zh: 1254年，阿尔伯特当选条顿尼亚省（Province of Teutonia）省会长。当时该省辖有五十余所会院，阿尔伯特承诺亲自徒步巡视所有这些会院（多明我会士被禁止骑马或乘车）。1257年6月，他在佛罗伦萨辞去这一职务；到1258年，他已返回科隆，重新担任圣十字修道院的讲师。然而不久，另一批繁重的管理职责又落在了他身上。1259年，教廷要求阿尔伯特出任雷根斯堡（Regensburg，又称拉蒂斯本 Ratisbon）主教。阿尔伯特此前已显示出调解冲突的才能，而这一职位正需要外交手腕：前任主教因不得人心而被迫辞职，失去首牧的教区此时纷争不断、财政破产。经过考虑，阿尔伯特不顾本会总会长的劝告，决定接受这一职位，将自己置于对教宗的直接服从之下。尽管从法理上说，此举使他不再受总会长管辖，但显然阿尔伯特从未停止将自己视为多明我会士，凡力所能及之处都遵守会规；而修会也从未停止视他为自己的一员。

body.text: By 1261 the affairs of the Regensburg diocese had been sufficiently organized for Albert to feel able to hand his duties over to a locally chosen bishop. He headed toward Italy to deliver his resignation to the Pope, whose unexpected death resulted in a year’s delay before the election of a new bishop could be confirmed under the auspices of the new Pope, Urban IV (1216-1264). Nothing is known with certainty of Albert’s activities during the remainder of 1261 and 1262, though it is presumed likely that he remained in Viterbo to wait for the outcome of the election, renewing his acquaintance with Thomas Aquinas and others he had known in Paris. In 1263, Pope Urban IV appointed Albert Preacher of the Crusade in Germany, Bohemia and all German speaking lands. Dutifully undertaking the commission, Albert traveled through Germany and the Netherlands, laying down (one imagines with relief) his peripatetic preaching office on the death of Urban IV in October of 1264.
body.zh: 到1261年，雷根斯堡教区的事务已整顿得足以让阿尔伯特感到可以将职责移交给一位当地选出的主教。他前往意大利向教宗呈递辞呈，而教宗的意外去世使新主教的选举在新教宗乌尔班四世（Urban IV，1216-1264）主持下获得确认之前，拖延了一年。关于阿尔伯特在1261年余下时间及1262年的活动，没有确切记载，但一般认为他很可能留在维泰博等待选举结果，并重叙与托马斯·阿奎那以及他在巴黎认识的其他人物的旧谊。1263年，教宗乌尔班四世任命阿尔伯特为德意志、波希米亚及所有德语地区的十字军布道者。阿尔伯特尽职地接受了这一委任，遍历德意志与尼德兰；1264年10月乌尔班四世去世后，他便卸下了这一四处奔波的布道职务（可以想象他是如释重负的）。

body.text: From 1264-1267 Albert retired to the Dominican cloister in Würzburg. There is evidence that he took part in mediation of local disputes while working to finish the corpus of Aristotelian paraphrases. In 1268 Albert was in Strasbourg resolving a dispute at the request of Pope Clement IV (Pope 1265-1268), and in 1269 he was called back to Cologne by the Dominican Master to reside there as lector emeritus. In the last years of his life in Cologne he worked on his paraphrase of the pseudo-Aristotelian Liber de causis and several late theological works while being called upon at intervals to act as mediator and to consecrate churches and other ecclesiastical structures. The legend that he went to Paris in 1277 to register his protest against the rumored condemnation of the ideas of his disciple Thomas Aquinas (who predeceased him in 1274) is probably unfounded. Albert was over eighty years old when he died in Cologne on November 15th, 1280.
body.zh: 1264年至1267年，阿尔伯特退居于维尔茨堡的多明我会修道院。有证据表明，他在致力于完成亚里士多德著作释义全集的同时，也参与了当地纠纷的调解。1268年，阿尔伯特应教宗克雷芒四世（Clement IV，教宗1265-1268）之请，在斯特拉斯堡解决一桩争端；1269年，多明我会总会长召他回科隆，以荣休讲师（lector emeritus）的身份居住。在科隆的晚年，他撰写了伪亚里士多德著作《论原因》（Liber de causis）的释义以及若干晚期的神学著作，同时不时被请去充当调停人，并为教堂及其他教会建筑祝圣。传说他于1277年前往巴黎，对传闻中将谴责其弟子托马斯·阿奎那（Thomas Aquinas，1274年先于他去世）思想的举动提出抗议；这一传说大概没有根据。1280年11月15日，阿尔伯特在科隆去世，享年八十余岁。

body.text: 2. Works
body.zh: 2. 著作

body.text: Albert’s corpus is substantial (his Opera omnia takes up 38 volumes in the Borgnet edition) and contains a roughly equal quantity of theological and philosophical writing, including lectures and commentaries on the Bible, on Lombard’s Sentences, on the Pseudo-Dionysius, and a large and important body of commentaries on or “paraphrases” of Aristotelian works. In addition to the writings definitely known to belong to Albert, there are several treatises which were attributed to him through the later Middle Ages and Early Modern period, but which are now considered to be of questionable authenticity. The questions surrounding attribution are not straightforward, since in some cases works unlikely to have been composed by Albert still seem to be under his influence. In one case (that of the Speculum astronomiae) the attribution to Albert is still a matter of active scholarly debate. These works will be dealt with in a separate section.
body.zh: 阿尔伯特的著作数量可观（其《全集》在博尔涅版中多达38卷），神学与哲学写作的分量大致相当，包括对《圣经》、伦巴德《箴言四书》、伪狄奥尼修斯的讲授与注释，以及一大批重要而卷帙浩繁的亚里士多德著作注释或“释义”。除确知属于阿尔伯特的著作外，还有若干论著在中世纪后期与近代早期被归在他名下，如今则被认为真伪存疑。归名问题并不简单，因为在某些情况下，那些不太可能出自阿尔伯特之手的作品似乎仍受其影响。有一种情况（即《天文学之镜》Speculum astronomiae），其归属于阿尔伯特仍是学界激烈争论的问题。这些作品将在单独一节中讨论。

body.text: Of the authentic works of Albert, the Aristotelian paraphrases are probably the most important, not only to subsequent natural philosophy, but also to the history of Western Esotericism. As Albert explains at the opening of the Physica, these works were undertaken at the request of his Dominican brothers who wished to have all of Aristotelian natural philosophy laid out for them in an accessible way. Albert tried to follow the order of Aristotle’s works, using the Aristotelian titles but paraphrasing (rather than citing and commenting on) Aristotle’s words, presenting additional information at appropriate points to clarify and supplement the Philosopher’s ideas, and adding in new material where discussions of topics appeared to be left incomplete. The paraphrases thus adhered to the spirit of Aristotle (as Albert understood it) more than to the letter, not only because Albert freely included new material, but also because he was not shy about contradicting Aristotle’s opinions when he felt they were inconsistent either with his personal experience or with facts he had learned from other sources.
body.zh: 在阿尔伯特确凿无疑的著作中，亚里士多德释义大概是最重要的，不仅对此后的自然哲学而言，对西方秘传主义的历史而言也是如此。正如阿尔伯特在《物理学》（Physica）开篇所说明的，这些著作是应其多明我会弟兄之请而作的，他们希望有人以浅显易懂的方式为他们把亚里士多德的全部自然哲学条理化地呈现出来。阿尔伯特力求依循亚里士多德著作的顺序，沿用其标题，但对亚里士多德的话采取释义（而非引用并注释）的方式，在适当之处提供补充材料以澄清和补充“那位哲学家”（the Philosopher）的观点，并在某些论题的讨论似有未竟之处增添新内容。因此，这些释义忠于亚里士多德的精神（就阿尔伯特所理解的精神而言）甚于其字句；这不仅因为阿尔伯特自由地加入新材料，也因为他感到亚里士多德的某些意见与自己的亲身经验或从其他来源获知的事实不合时，并不讳言反驳。

body.text: In his understanding of the natural sciences, Albert drew on a broad range of material extending from the Church Fathers to the works of Arabic philosophers, and including not only the major commentators on Aristotle, but also anonymous treatises on various natural subjects, works of image →magic, →alchemy, and other medieval Hermetica [→Hermetic Literature II]. While skeptical of the extraordinary claims of magical and alchemical texts, Albert’s quest for information about the natural world included perusal of many such works, and he respected the facts they reported when these seemed consistent with his own general or experiential knowledge. He refers to alchemy and alchemical operations repeatedly in the De caelo et mundo, the Meteora, and in the Mineralium libri V, where Book IV is particularly concerned with alchemical categories, and →Hermes Trismegistus is a frequently cited authority. In Book II of the same work, he discusses sigils and image magic, calling it ‘that part of necromancy which is dependent on astrology’ (Wyckoff, 127) (here and elsewhere in his philosophical writings Albert uses the word “necromancy” in the benign sense indicated by Charles Burnett). Consistent with the practice of many who compiled herbals and books of remedies, Albert included in his De vegetabilibus a final section (part VI) devoted to uses of plants less theoretically plausible, but presumably empirically attested, which contains over a dozen references to magic arts and incantatores. Albert’s works generally bear the stamp of a wide-ranging mind which enjoyed taxonomy and systems of classification. He rejected no plausible source of information out of hand, and preferred, where he could, to reconcile attractive philosophical systems rather than champion one at the expense of another.
body.zh: 在对自然科学的理解上，阿尔伯特取材广博，从教父著作直到阿拉伯哲学家的作品，不仅包括亚里士多德的主要注释者，也包括论各种自然主题的佚名论著、图像→魔法之作、→炼金术以及中世纪的其他赫尔墨斯文献[→赫尔墨斯文献 II]。阿尔伯特虽对魔法与炼金术文本的离奇主张持怀疑态度，但他在探求关于自然世界的信息时仍研读了许多这类著作；当其中所报告的事实与他自己的普遍知识或经验知识看来相符时，他便予以尊重。他在《论天与地》（De caelo et mundo）、《气象学》（Meteora）以及《矿物志》五卷（Mineralium libri V）中屡次提及炼金术与炼金操作；其中第四卷尤其关注炼金术的范畴，→赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯则是频繁被引用的权威。在同一著作的第二卷中，他讨论印记（sigils）与图像魔法，称之为“依附于占星学的那一部分亡灵术（necromancy）”（Wyckoff, 127）（在此处以及其哲学著作的其他地方，阿尔伯特都是在查尔斯·伯内特（Charles Burnett）所指出的那种无害意义上使用“necromancy”一词的）。与许多编纂本草书与药方集者的做法一致，阿尔伯特在《论植物》（De vegetabilibus）中收入了最后一节（第六部分），专门讨论那些理论上不那么可信、但想必有经验依据的植物用途；其中十余次提到魔法技艺与吟咒者（incantatores）。阿尔伯特的著作总体上带有一种视野开阔的心灵的印记，这种心灵喜爱分类与分类体系。他从不轻率否定任何看似可信的信息来源；在可能之处，他宁愿调和有吸引力的哲学体系，而不愿拥护其一而贬抑其他。

body.text: For all these reasons Albert’s paraphrases played an important part in putting the Aristotelian cosmos together for subsequent thinkers. He was one of the earliest and most important writers to integrate Arabic Aristotelianism into Christian natural philosophy, and his influence on medieval and Renaissance thinkers following him was profound. Less idiosyncratic than friar →Roger Bacon, less of a rigorous Augustinian than Thomas Aquinas, his natural universe remains wide open to influences from the heavens. No doubt in part for this reason he is something of a favorite among the medieval auctoritates in the Early Modern period, praised by →Ficino, relied upon by Pomponazzi, an Aristotelian cornerstone of →Pico della Mirandola’s 900 Conclusiones, and cited as an authority in over a dozen places in →Agrippa’s De occulta philosophia (where, to give comparative examples, Thomas is cited in six loci and Roger Bacon only in three – not that the influence of any of these thinkers should be considered as strictly confined to loci where they receive citations). It was probably advantageous that Albert’s diplomatic gifts, Christian life of service, and reputation for saintliness conspired to make his name eminently citable; there were few other medieval philosophers so friendly to Hermetic thinking whose names could so unimpeachably be used to adorn the esoteric claims of Renaissance philosophers.
body.zh: 由于上述种种原因，阿尔伯特的释义在为此后的思想家整合亚里士多德式宇宙图景方面发挥了重要作用。他是最早也最重要的将阿拉伯亚里士多德主义融入基督教自然哲学的作家之一，对后世中世纪与文艺复兴思想家的影响至为深远。与修士→罗吉尔·培根（Roger Bacon）相比，他不那么特异；与托马斯·阿奎那相比，他也不那么严格恪守奥古斯丁主义；他的自然宇宙始终向来自天界的影响敞开。无疑部分因此之故，他在近代早期是中世纪权威（auctoritates）中颇受青睐的一位：受到→费奇诺的称赞，为蓬波纳齐（Pomponazzi）所倚重，是→皮科·德拉·米兰多拉《九百论题》（900 Conclusiones）的亚里士多德式基石，并在→阿格里帕《论秘传哲学》（De occulta philosophia）中十余处被引为权威（作为比较：托马斯在六处被引用，罗吉尔·培根仅在三处——这并不是说这些思想家的影响应被严格限定于他们被引用的段落）。阿尔伯特的外交才能、基督徒的服事生涯与圣洁的名声共同使他的名字极宜于征引，这大概对他颇为有利；中世纪哲学家中，对赫尔墨斯式思想如此友好、而其名字又能如此无可指摘地被用来装点文艺复兴哲学家秘传主张的人，实不多见。

body.text: 3. Works of Questionable Authenticity
body.zh: 3. 真伪存疑的著作

body.text: Works attributed to Albert but of doubtful or questionable authenticity include two Books of Secrets (the De secretis mulierum and the Secreta or Experimenta Alberti also called the Liber aggregationis), a De mirabilibus mundi, around thirty alchemical treatises, and the important bibliographic work known as the Speculum astronomiae which categorizes texts of image magic according to their dependence on astral influence. Some of these works have been shown to be dependent in whole or in part on Albert’s authentic writings. Lynn Thorndike demonstrated that the De secretis mulierum – a gynecological manual that was used as a medical textbook – is in part a compilation of medical information extracted from Albert’s paraphrase the De animalibus (possibly by a student or disciple of Albert’s), and the Experimenta Alberti lifts some of its material from Albert’s Mineralium libri V in its section on the uses of stones (though other sections of the work do not depend on Albert’s authentic writings).
body.zh: 归于阿尔伯特而真伪可疑的著作，包括两部《秘密之书》（《论妇女的秘密》De secretis mulierum，以及《阿尔伯特的秘密》或《阿尔伯特的实验》Secreta／Experimenta Alberti，又称《汇编》Liber aggregationis）、一部《论世界奇事》（De mirabilibus mundi）、约三十篇炼金术论著，以及那部名为《天文学之镜》的重要书志学著作——后者依据图像魔法文本对星辰影响的依赖程度对其加以分类。其中一些作品已被证明整体或部分地依赖于阿尔伯特确凿无疑的著作。林恩·桑代克（Lynn Thorndike）证明，《论妇女的秘密》——一部曾被用作医学教科书的妇科手册——部分是从阿尔伯特的释义著作《论动物》（De animalibus）中摘取医学信息汇编而成（可能出自阿尔伯特的学生或弟子之手）；而《阿尔伯特的实验》在论石头用途的部分，从阿尔伯特的《矿物志》五卷中取用了一些材料（不过该著作的其他部分并不依赖阿尔伯特确凿无疑的著作）。

body.text: Concerning the treatises on alchemy, the most important both in terms of manuscript count and potential likelihood of correct attribution is the Semita recta or Libellus de alchimia, a version of which was included in the Borgnet edition of Albert’s Opera. Concerning its attribution, Pearl Kibre suggests that ‘its clear, concise, and well ordered account of the subject resembles Albert’s treatment of other topics of natural science in his authentic compositions’ (Kibre 1942, 500). It is a feature of all the earliest alchemical texts attributed to Albert (including the Semita recta, the Alkimia minor, the De occultis naturae, and the Compositum de compositis), that they show a deference to his style, many of these works putatively composed (like the Aristotelian paraphrases) at the request of Albert’s Dominican brothers who wish to have the scientific elements of alchemy explained to them in an accessible way.
body.zh: 就炼金术论著而言，无论从抄本数量还是从正确归名的可能性来看，最重要的都是《正道》（Semita recta）或《炼金术小书》（Libellus de alchimia）；博尔涅版《阿尔伯特全集》收录了其中的一个版本。关于其归名，珀尔·基布雷（Pearl Kibre）提出，“该书对这一主题清晰、简明而条理井然的论述，与阿尔伯特在确凿无疑的著作中处理其他自然科学主题的方式相似”（Kibre 1942, 500）。所有归于阿尔伯特的最早炼金术文本（包括《正道》、《小炼金术》Alkimia minor、《论自然之隐秘》De occultis naturae 与《复合之复合》Compositum de compositis）都有一个共同特点：它们都表现出对其文风的遵从；这些作品据称大多（像亚里士多德释义一样）是应阿尔伯特的多明我会弟兄之请而作，他们希望有人以浅显易懂的方式为他们解释炼金术中的科学要素。

body.text: The question of attribution of the Speculum astronomie is so difficult to resolve with any certainty that it is worth briefly summarizing the issues at stake. While objections have been raised concerning the work’s attribution to Albert from the early part of the 20th century, some suggesting that it might have been composed by Roger Bacon, these objections were countered by convincing arguments in favour of Albert’s authorship by Lynn Thorndike and subsequently by Paola Zambelli. In brief, the Speculum resembles Albert’s thinking; it shows the same style of preoccupation with taxonomy; it refers to works he is known to have read. It is impossible to nail the attribution down as firmly as might be wished, however, because the manuscript tradition does not begin to attribute the Speculum to Albert until the mid-14th century, nor is it mentioned as Albert’s work in any texts dating from prior to that time (though attributions after the mid-14th century are consistent; that is, no manuscripts of any period are known which attribute the text to anyone else). From the earliest period of the controversy it has been pointed out that certain statements in it are inconsistent with Albert’s views as expressed elsewhere in his writings, but arguments from attitude can go both ways. As Thorndike pointed out early on, there is considerable inconsistency in any case between Albert’s views as expressed in his authentic works; in general he tends to express himself more conservatively in his theological mode than he does in his philosophical mode (Thorndike 1955, 426).
body.zh: 《天文学之镜》的归名问题极难有确切结论，因此值得简要概述其中的关键问题。20世纪初以来，一直有学者对该书归于阿尔伯特提出异议，有人甚至认为它可能出自罗吉尔·培根之手；但林恩·桑代克以及其后的保拉·赞贝利（Paola Zambelli）以有说服力的论证支持阿尔伯特的著作权，反驳了这些异议。简言之，《天文学之镜》与阿尔伯特的思想相似；它表现出同样热衷于分类的风格；它提及了他确曾读过的一些著作。然而，要像人们所希望的那样牢固地确定其归属是不可能的，因为抄本传统直到14世纪中叶才开始将《天文学之镜》归于阿尔伯特，在此之前成书的任何文本也未曾提及它是阿尔伯特的作品（尽管14世纪中叶以后的归名颇为一致；也就是说，尚不知有任何时期的抄本将该文本归于他人）。自争论之初，就有人指出书中某些说法与阿尔伯特在其他著作中所表达的观点不一致，但依据态度立论可以正反两说。正如桑代克早已指出的，无论如何，阿尔伯特在其确凿无疑的著作中所表达的观点本身就存在相当多的不一致；总体而言，他在神学模式下的表述往往比在哲学模式下更为保守（Thorndike 1955, 426）。

body.text: More recently it has been argued by Bruno Roy that the Speculum is the work of Richard of Fournival – a suggestion more plausible than the arguments in favor of Roger Bacon (since it is known that the author of the Speculum consulted Richard of Fournival’s library), but suffering from the same lack of certitude in the area of manuscript attribution as trouble the arguments in favor of Albert’s authorship. Roy suggests that if Albert did not write the work, he may well have read it – something which is almost a necessary postulate for those who do not believe that Albert wrote it, given the fact that Albert mentions so many of the works that are listed in it. The debate cannot be conclusively settled except by the discovery of further manuscript evidence, but in the meantime, it remains as difficult to dismiss the idea of Albertine attribution as to prove it. The Speculum was an important touchstone for Renaissance Esotericism; many of the Albertine citations in Agrippa’s De Occulta Philosophia Libri Tres are to this work.
body.zh: 晚近，布鲁诺·鲁瓦（Bruno Roy）提出，《天文学之镜》乃富尔尼瓦尔的理查（Richard of Fournival）之作——这一说法比支持罗吉尔·培根的论据更为可信（因为已知《天文学之镜》的作者曾查阅富尔尼瓦尔的理查的藏书），但它与支持阿尔伯特著作权的论据一样，在抄本归名方面缺乏确定性。鲁瓦提出，即使该书非阿尔伯特所撰，他也很可能读过它——鉴于阿尔伯特提及了书中列出的如此之多的著作，对于那些不相信该书为阿尔伯特所撰的人来说，这几乎是一个必要的假定。除非发现更多抄本证据，这场争论无法得到最终解决；但就目前而言，否定阿尔伯特归名之说与证明它同样困难。《天文学之镜》是文艺复兴秘传主义的重要试金石；阿格里帕《论秘传哲学三卷》（De Occulta Philosophia Libri Tres）中许多归于阿尔伯特的引文都出自此书。

body.text: 4. Saint and Magician
body.zh: 4. 圣人与魔法师

body.text: Like other natural philosophers of his era, Albert was the subject of numerous posthumous legends which made him into a magical and alchemical adept. If all that was said of his reputation in this regard was not strictly justified by the facts, nevertheless there is some continuity between his real life and his reputation, just as some continuity is observable between his questionable works and his authentic writings. Albert had perused volumes of magical and hermetic writings as already noted, and had also observed alchemical procedures in laboratory conditions, as he mentions in several places in the Book of Minerals, though it is probably not true (as one manuscript suggests) that he was a teacher of alchemy who took Roger Bacon as a disciple. Albert was also known for working miracles of another sort, and in the end the growth of his reputation for sanctity outstripped the growth of his reputation for magic. It is interesting that a Vita composed in the mid 1480s with a view to his eventual canonization devotes about a quarter of its pages to the refutation of the exaggerated magical claims laid upon him. In 1484, the Pope gave permission to the Dominicans of Cologne to celebrate Albert’s Feast on November 15 – a gesture that was equivalent to beatification, though Albert was not finally canonized until 1931.
body.zh: 与他那个时代的其他自然哲学家一样，阿尔伯特身后成为众多传说的对象，这些传说把他塑造成一位魔法与炼金术的大师。如果说关于他这方面声誉的种种说法并不完全符合事实，那么他的真实生平与他的名声之间仍存在某种连续性，正如在他那些真伪存疑的著作与确凿无疑的著作之间也可观察到某种连续性。如前所述，阿尔伯特曾研读魔法与赫尔墨斯著作，也曾在实验室条件下观察炼金操作——他在《矿物志》（Book of Minerals）中数处提及此事；不过，说他是炼金术教师并收罗吉尔·培根为弟子，大概并非事实（尽管有一份抄本如此暗示）。阿尔伯特也以施行另一类奇迹而闻名；最终，他圣洁名声的增长超过了他魔法名声的增长。有趣的是，一部为日后封圣而于1480年代中期撰写的《传记》（Vita），将约四分之一的篇幅用于驳斥加在他身上的那些夸大的魔法说法。1484年，教宗准许科隆的多明我会士于11月15日庆祝阿尔伯特的瞻礼——这一举措相当于宣福，不过阿尔伯特直到1931年才最终被封圣。
