body.text: 1. From Alchemy to Alchemies 2. The “Spiritual” Interpretation 3. Alchemy and the Scientific Revolution 4. Alchemy and Chemistry
body.zh: 1. 从炼金术到诸种炼金术 2. “灵性”解释 3. 炼金术与科学革命 4. 炼金术与化学

body.text: Alchemy is a subject of enormous intrinsic interest but one which has long proven difficult to grasp properly. The last thirty years, however, have witnessed a remarkable florescence of scholarly work on the subject, which has shed much new light on this obscure subject and brought forth significant revisions and advances in our understanding of it.
body.zh: 炼金术是一个本身具有极大趣味的题目，但长期以来一直难以被恰当把握。然而，过去三十年间，围绕这一题目的学术研究出现了引人注目的繁荣，为这一晦暗不明的题目带来了许多新的启示，并促成了我们对其理解的重要修正与推进。

body.text: Whereas it was common just half a century ago for historians of science to dismiss alchemy out-of-hand as a “pseudo-science” or to deploy it merely as a foil against which to set the origins of modern science, the unsuitability of such attitudes has now become apparent among serious scholars, and such prejudiced readings of alchemy are in the process of passing away. An enormous amount of work, nevertheless, remains to be done in the field, for many aspects and developments of alchemy remain very incompletely understood. One important part of the remaining work is the continued dismantling of erroneous views of alchemy promulgated since the Enlightenment which have, despite their dubious qualifications and origins, deeply tinctured a major part of the literature on alchemy written during the 19th and 20th centuries. Four interrelated, and now increasingly rejected, features of these earlier treatments are identifiable: first, the notion or assumption that alchemy is a largely monolithic tradition, bearing little significant internal articulation or dynamic development over time or cultures; second, the concept of alchemy as an essentially or primarily spiritual, psychic, or self-transformative endeavor; third, the idea that alchemy ran counter to, was a non-participant in, or non-contributor to the scientific developments of the period characterized as the Scientific Revolution; and fourth, the belief that alchemy was something clearly distinguishable (in terms of goals, practices, and practitioners) from chemistry prior to the 18th century.
body.zh: 仅仅半个世纪之前，科学史家还常常把炼金术一概斥为“伪科学”，或仅仅把它当作衬托现代科学起源的对照物；而如今，严肃的学者已经认识到这类态度并不恰当，这类带有偏见的炼金术解读也正在逐渐消逝。然而，这一领域仍有大量工作有待完成，因为炼金术的许多方面及其发展仍然被理解得很不充分。余下工作中的一项重要内容，是继续拆解自启蒙运动以来流传的错误炼金术观念；这些观念尽管来路与资格都颇为可疑，却深深浸染了19世纪与20世纪写就的很大一部分炼金术文献。这些较早的论述有四个相互关联、如今日益遭到摒弃的特征可以辨识：第一，认为或假定炼金术大体上是一种单一整全的传统，在时间与文化中几乎没有重要的内部分化或动态发展；第二，把炼金术视为本质上或主要是灵性的、心灵的或自我转化的追求；第三，认为炼金术与被称为科学革命的那个时期的科学发展相抵触，未曾参与其中，也无所贡献；第四，相信在18世纪之前，炼金术在目标、实践与从业者方面都可以与化学清楚地区分开来。

body.text: 1. From Alchemy to Alchemies
body.zh: 1. 从炼金术到诸种炼金术

body.text: The idea of alchemy as largely monolithic in character comes partly from the rhetoric of early modern alchemical writers themselves. Oft-repeated mottoes such as “the Sages all say one thing”, the drawing of mythic histories and genealogies of alchemy to stress its supposed antiquity, and the desire of aspiring alchemists to uncover the secret knowledge known to and hidden by their predecessors (for example, preparing the Philosophers’ Stone) conspire to give the impression of a tradition that remained largely constant over time, cultures, and practitioners. The ambiguity of alchemical writings, moreover, allowed for their broad reinterpretation by subsequent alchemists (and others) to create the appearance of a harmony of views among authors who, when treated critically, show very little actual agreement. In fact, the diversity and dynamism within historical alchemy is sufficiently extensive that historians have now begun to group individual authors and practitioners within “schools” and to see the differences among their practices and goals. Many alchemists, for example, were interested predominantly in bringing about metallic transmutation, generally by means of the Philosophers’ Stone. Others, like →Paracelsus or Alexander von Such-ten, downplayed this aspect of alchemy in favor of medicinal applications. Some emphasized productive processes of all sorts – distillation, refining, salt or pigment manufacture, etc. – along the lines of an early chemical industry. Some emphasized the theological implications of alchemical work, while others ignored this dimension entirely. Many writers and practitioners pursued several or even all of these goals, and this brief catalogue does not even mention the important intersections of alchemy over its long history with fine art, theatre, literature, religion, political and social movements, and many other areas of culture and society.
body.zh: 炼金术在性质上大体单一整全的观念，部分来自近代早期炼金术作者自身的修辞。诸如“智者所言皆一事”这类屡屡重复的箴言、为强调炼金术所谓古老渊源而勾勒的神话式历史与谱系，以及有志于炼金术者渴望揭示其前辈所知晓并隐藏起来的秘密知识（例如制备贤者之石）的愿望，共同造成了一种印象：这是一个在时间、文化与从业者之间大体保持不变的传统。此外，炼金术著作的含混性使得后来的炼金术士（以及其他人士）可以对其作宽泛的重新诠释，从而营造出一种诸家观点和谐一致的假象——而这些作者若受到批判性的考察，实际上几乎没有什么共识。事实上，历史上的炼金术内部所具的多样性与动态性如此广泛，以致史家如今已开始把个别作者与从业者归入不同的“流派”，并辨识其各自实践与目标之间的差异。例如，许多炼金术士主要关心的是实现金属转化，通常借助贤者之石。另一些人，如→帕拉塞尔苏斯（Paracelsus）或亚历山大·冯·祖赫滕（Alexander von Suchten），则淡化炼金术的这一方面，而偏重其医药应用。还有些人强调各种各样的生产性工艺——蒸馏、精炼、盐或颜料的制造等等——其路数近似于早期的化学工业。有些人强调炼金工作的神学意涵，另一些人则完全忽视这一维度。许多作者与从业者追求其中数项乃至全部目标；而这份简短的清单甚至还未提及炼金术在其漫长历史中与美术、戏剧、文学、宗教、政治与社会运动，以及文化与社会许多其他领域的重要交汇。

body.text: Even within any one of just the early modern European groups there exist diversities of theoretical, philosophical, or operational frameworks. We can speak of, for example, Mercurialists, who sought the matter for the Stone in common mercury, and contrast these with Sendivogians who sought for it in some sort of niter. Likewise,
body.zh: 即便在近代早期欧洲的任何一个群体内部，也存在着理论、哲学或操作框架上的差异。例如，我们可以谈到水银派（Mercurialists），他们在普通水银中寻找制造贤者之石的材料；并可将其与塞迪沃吉乌斯派（Sendivogians）相对照，后者则在某种硝石中寻找这一材料。同样地，

body.text: Scholastic →Aristotelianism appealed as a system to some alchemists – like Geber and Gaston Duclo – while Neoplatonic [→Neoplatonism] or other notions appealed to others. Some alchemists took a rigidly mechanistic view of their processes, while others adopted non-mechanical or vitalistic views, with yet others falling at all the possible gradations in-between. The critical point is that we cannot blithely extend the example of a single individual or group of individuals to make claims broadly about alchemy as a whole. While this situation renders a comprehensive understanding of alchemy far more difficult, it also makes it a far more interesting subject of study, and in fact, one less alien from other branches of human inquiry.
body.zh: 经院式→亚里士多德主义作为一个体系吸引了一些炼金术士——如盖伯（Geber）与加斯东·杜克洛（Gaston Duclo）——而新柏拉图主义［→新柏拉图主义］或其他观念则吸引了另一些人。有些炼金术士对其操作过程持严格的机械论看法，另一些人则采取非机械论或活力论的观点，还有人则落在两者之间一切可能的渐变层级上。关键的一点在于，我们不能轻率地把某一个人或某一群人的例子推而广之，从而对整个炼金术作出笼统的论断。这种情形固然使对炼金术的全面理解变得困难得多，但也使它成为一个有趣得多的研究对象，而且事实上，它与人类探究的其他分支也并不那么隔膜。

body.text: 2. The “Spiritual” Interpretation
body.zh: 2. “灵性”解释

body.text: The idea of a monolithic, constant, and ancient “tradition” within alchemy received a boost from the development of the spiritual interpretation of alchemy in the 19th century. A key event here was the publication of Mary Anne Atwood’s Suggestive Inquiry into the Hermetic Mystery (1850). Atwood reduced all “true” alchemy to a quest for spiritual elevation operating through Mesmeric trances, the knowledge of which, along with →animal magnetism, she believed to be a secret tradition dating back at least to the ancient Greeks. Alchemical writers who apparently busied themselves with actual laboratory operations, were, according to Atwood, mere “literal souls” who failed to perceive the hidden truth of alchemy, and were not “real” alchemists at all; they were in fact, in her words, as “blind” as the chemists and other scientists of her day. Such a division – which plays upon a common rhetorical device employed in early modern alchemical texts where the wise author routinely differentiates himself from imposters and false alchemists – helped give rise to a putative division of alchemy into “esoteric” and “exoteric” aspects. These terms are still encountered today, but when they are applied to early modern alchemy their validity is questionable. There is no evidence that a majority, or even a significant fraction of pre18th century European alchemical writers and practitioners saw their work as anything other than natural philosophical in character, as even the prolific occultist writer →A.E. Waite (1857-1942) was forced to admit toward the end of his career in 1926. Nonetheless, Atwood’s treatise touched off a surge of interest in alchemy within the context of Victorian occultism [→occult/occultism]. Although Victorian and subsequent alchemy is extremely interesting in its own right, its popularity has become an obstacle to understanding earlier alchemy because the spiritual interpretation’s universal historical claims about the intent and content of pre-18th century alchemy are untenable.
body.zh: 炼金术内部存在一种单一整全、恒定不变的古老“传统”这一观念，因19世纪炼金术灵性解释的发展而得到推动。此处的关键事件是玛丽·安妮·阿特伍德（Mary Anne Atwood）的《对赫尔墨斯奥秘的提示性探究》（Suggestive Inquiry into the Hermetic Mystery, 1850）出版。阿特伍德把一切“真正的”炼金术化约为一种通过梅斯梅尔式恍惚状态运作的灵性提升追求；她相信，关于此道的知识连同→动物磁力（animal magnetism）一起，是一种至少可上溯至古希腊人的秘密传统。在阿特伍德看来，那些显然忙于实际实验室操作的炼金术作者不过是“拘泥字面的灵魂”，未能领会炼金术隐藏的真理，根本算不上“真正的”炼金术士；用她的话说，他们实际上与她那个时代的化学家及其他科学家一样“盲目”。这样一种区分——它借用了近代早期炼金术文本中常见的一种修辞手法，即明智的作者惯常把自己与冒牌货和假炼金术士区分开来——促成了所谓炼金术分为“秘传”与“外传”两个方面的说法。这些术语至今仍可见到，但当它们被用于近代早期炼金术时，其有效性颇可置疑。没有证据表明，18世纪以前欧洲炼金术作者与从业者中的多数、甚至相当一部分，曾把自己的工作视为自然哲学性质之外的任何东西——就连著述宏富的秘传学作家→A. E. 韦特（A. E. Waite, 1857–1942）也在1926年其生涯末期不得不承认这一点。尽管如此，阿特伍德的论著在维多利亚时代秘传主义［→秘传／秘传主义］的语境中引发了一阵对炼金术的兴趣热潮。维多利亚时代及其后的炼金术本身固然极有意思，但它的流行却成了理解更早炼金术的障碍，因为灵性解释就18世纪以前炼金术的意图与内容所作的那些普泛的历史论断是站不住脚的。

body.text: It is important to clarify the distinction between 19th century occultist views of a self-transforma-tive “spiritual” alchemy and the actual religious dimensions of pre-18th century alchemy. Many early modern alchemists stressed how alchemical truths and religious truths support and reveal one another. Likewise, the language of alchemy is full of religious terminology such as death and resurrection, glorification, and extensive parallels with Biblical texts, the life of Christ, and even the sacred liturgy. The power of fire or the Stone to purify metals is sometimes related to Christ’s freeing men from sin. And of course, early alchemists frequently stressed the sanctity and divine favor needed for success. Yet such expressions of piety, as well as the synoptic, analogical view of the truths of the universe (whether natural or supernatural) typical of early modern thought (not just of alchemy) and the extensive use of religious imagery as a source of metaphor is widely different from the 19th century’s identification of alchemy with Mesmerism, self-illumination, and psychic transformation. Indeed, the majority of alchemists (though not all) were at pains to stress that their art operated naturally upon natural substances. Even if among the broad diversity of alchemists one could identify a few who seem to promote a view more or less akin to the 19th-century interpretation, this feature could not be proposed as characteristic of alchemy since the majority of alchemists clearly did not hold it.
body.zh: 有必要澄清19世纪秘传主义者关于自我转化的“灵性”炼金术的看法，与18世纪以前炼金术实际的宗教维度之间的区别。许多近代早期炼金术士强调，炼金术真理与宗教真理相互支撑、相互揭示。同样，炼金术的语言充满了死亡与复活、荣耀化之类的宗教术语，并与《圣经》文本、基督生平乃至神圣礼仪有着广泛的平行对应。火或贤者之石净化金属的力量，有时被联系于基督将人从罪中解放出来。当然，早期炼金术士常常强调成功所需的圣洁与神的恩宠。然而，此类虔敬表达，连同近代早期思想（不止是炼金术）所典型的对宇宙真理（无论自然的还是超自然的）作统观式、类比式观照的取向，以及广泛使用宗教意象作为隐喻来源的做法，与19世纪把炼金术等同于梅斯梅尔主义、自我启明与心灵转化的做法大相径庭。的确，多数炼金术士（虽非全部）都竭力强调，他们的技艺是自然地作用于自然物质的。即便在形形色色的炼金术士中能够找出少数人，似乎主张某种与19世纪解释大致相近的观点，这一特征也不能被提出来作为炼金术的典型特征，因为多数炼金术士显然并不持此说。

body.text: A major (and, in a critical historical sense, deleterious) outgrowth of the Victorian occultist fascination with alchemy is the psychological interpretation put forth by →Carl Gustav Jung. According to Jung, alchemy is not about physical (chemical) processes at all but rather about psychological developments occurring within the practitioner. The metaphorical language and strange phenomena filling alchemical tomes actually record hallucinatory ‘irruptions of the unconscious’ which are ‘projected’ from the alchemist’s psyche onto the contents of his flasks. Despite the inherently unlikely character of this notion, it has had enormous influence on the understanding of alchemy even among otherwise sober historians of science. Besides the fact that there are few outside the ranks of avowedly Jungian analytical psychologists who continue to assent to Jung’s views, recent scholarly investigations of alchemy have undermined Jung’s construct. In the first place, there is now no question that the vast majority of early modern alchemists were deeply involved in practical pursuits, which they carried out and interpreted with clear-headed, conscious thought. Studies of obscure alchemical language show how even some of the most bizarre metaphorical expressions and emblems can be comprehensively “decoded” into chemical operations. Some of these decoded processes have even been reproduced in modern chemical laboratories, providing occasionally evocative visual results – such as the growing of a spectacular “Philosophical Tree” from gold. The physical appearance of such results, taken together with the delight and fertility of early modern culture in drawing analogies and similitudes affords more immediate and more likely explanations for the origins of at least some alchemical imagery than the invocation of so shaky a construct as irruptions of a collective unconscious. Moreover, the inspection of private manuscript materials, for example the laboratory notebooks of George Starkey (1628- 1665, alias Eirenaeus Philalethes, a favorite example for Jung), indicate clearly how he consciously encoded laboratory results in extravagant allegorical guise for public view while he maintained clear, precise expressions for private circulation, and even how he went about deciphering the metaphorical texts of his predecessors into chemical operations he could test practically in the laboratory. The affinity of Jung’s interpretation with the 19th-cen-tury occultists’ spiritual interpretation is clear in their common sundering of alchemy from practical chemical processes and their description of alchemical transformation as taking place within the practitioner; neither has withstood critical historical scrutiny.
body.zh: 维多利亚时代秘传主义者对炼金术的迷恋所产生的一个重大（而且从批判性史学的意义上说是有害的）衍生结果，就是→卡尔·古斯塔夫·荣格（Carl Gustav Jung）提出的心理学解释。按照荣格的说法，炼金术根本不关乎物理的（化学的）过程，而是关乎从业者内部发生的心理发展。充斥炼金术典籍的隐喻语言与奇异现象，实际上记录了幻觉性的“无意识突入”，它们从炼金术士的心灵“投射”到其烧瓶中的内容物上。尽管这一观念本身极不可能成立，它却对炼金术的理解产生了巨大影响，甚至在原本审慎的科学史家当中也是如此。除了在公开的荣格派分析心理学家行列之外，如今很少有人仍赞同荣格的看法；此外，晚近的炼金术学术研究已经动摇了荣格的建构。首先，如今已毫无疑问的是，绝大多数近代早期炼金术士都深深投身于实际事务，他们以清醒而有意识的思考来从事并解释这些事务。对晦涩炼金术语言的研究表明，即便是一些最为怪诞的隐喻表达与图徽，也能够被全面地“解码”为化学操作。其中一些被解码的过程甚至已在现代化学实验室中得到再现，偶尔还产生颇具感染力的视觉效果——例如从黄金中生长出一棵壮观的“哲学树”。此类结果的物理外观，加上近代早期文化在援引类比与相似之物方面的兴致与丰饶，为至少某些炼金术意象的起源提供了比诉诸“集体无意识突入”这样摇摇欲坠的建构更为直接、也更为可能的解释。此外，对私人手稿材料——例如乔治·斯塔基（George Starkey, 1628–1665，别名埃瑞奈乌斯·菲拉勒忒斯［Eirenaeus Philalethes］，荣格最爱举的例子之一）的实验室笔记——的检视清楚地表明，他如何有意识地把实验结果以夸饰的寓言外衣编码以供公众观看，而在私下流通中则保持清晰精确的表述；甚至表明他如何着手把前人的隐喻文本解读为可在实验室中实际检验的化学操作。荣格的解释与19世纪秘传主义者的灵性解释之间的亲缘性十分明显：两者都把炼金术与实际化学过程割裂开来，都把炼金术的转化描述为发生在从业者内部；而两者都未能经受住批判性的历史审视。

body.text: 3. Alchemy and the Scientific Revolution
body.zh: 3. 炼金术与科学革命

body.text: Given the currency of spiritual and psychological interpretations of alchemy, it is not surprising that many in the early generation of 20th-century professional historians of science, especially those most influenced by positivist tendencies, denied to alchemy any place in the history or origins of modern science save perhaps as a counter-example. Their dismissal of alchemy often echoed sentiments voiced against alchemy in the 18th century, e.g. that it was entirely fraudulent, or that it was simply part of the “occult” (a word poorly defined in this context) which was supplanted by the progress of reason. Thus, influential figures like George Sarton cast alchemy into the scorned bin of “pseudo-sciences” alongside →witchcraft, black →magic, and necromancy, bedfellows alchemy had acquired predominantly by the writings of the 18th-century philosophes.
body.zh: 鉴于炼金术的灵性与心理学解释颇为流行，20世纪早期职业科学史家中的许多人——尤其是那些最受实证主义倾向影响的人——不承认炼金术在现代科学的历史或起源中拥有任何位置，除非或许作为反例，这并不令人意外。他们对炼金术的摒弃，常常呼应18世纪反对炼金术的论调，例如说它完全是欺诈，或说它不过是“秘术”（occult，该词在此语境中定义含混）的一部分，而秘术已被理性的进步所取代。于是，像乔治·萨顿（George Sarton）这样的有影响力的人物，把炼金术与→巫术、黑→魔法和通灵术一起扔进了遭人鄙弃的“伪科学”垃圾箱——炼金术的这些同伴，主要是通过18世纪哲人（philosophes）的著述才与之结缘的。

body.text: Yet the last three decades of the 20th century have witnessed a major shift in this perception. First, the profound alchemical interests and commitments of several thinkers recognized as key to the development of the physico-mathematical sciences central to master narratives of the Scientific Revolution were revealed. →Isaac Newton, → Robert Boyle, John Locke, and others were shown to have invested enormous time and energy in traditional alchemical pursuits. Other notable scholars such as Daniel Georg Morhof, Pierre Gassendi, and Olaus Borrichius are now known to have taken alchemy seriously and seen it as no less a part of natural philosophy than astronomy or natural history. Second, a closer, more contextualized study of individual alchemists has shown not only the inadequate – indeed, sometimes caricatured – portrayals of them current in the secondary literature, but also the significant contributions which alchemy has brought to the development of early modern science. For example, alchemy brought forth such principles as an emphasis on the determination and conservation of weight in chemical processes, well-developed and explanatory particulate matter theories, analysis and synthesis as tools for understanding nature, the power of human artifice to create new or improved products over natural ones, and perhaps even the notions of force key to Newton’s physics.
body.zh: 然而，20世纪最后三十年见证了这种看法的一次重大转变。首先，一些思想家被公认为对物理—数学科学的发展至关重要，而物理—数学科学正是科学革命主导叙事的核心；这些人对炼金术的深厚兴趣与投入被揭示了出来。→艾萨克·牛顿（Isaac Newton）、→罗伯特·波义耳（Robert Boyle）、约翰·洛克（John Locke）等人被证明曾在传统炼金术的追求上投入了大量时间与精力。其他著名学者，如丹尼尔·格奥尔格·莫尔霍夫（Daniel Georg Morhof）、皮埃尔·伽桑狄（Pierre Gassendi）与奥劳斯·博里希乌斯（Olaus Borrichius），如今已知都认真对待炼金术，并视之为自然哲学中与天文学或自然史同等的一部分。其次，对个别炼金术士更为细致、更具语境化的研究，不仅揭示了二手文献中流行的那种不充分——有时甚至是漫画化——的形象，也揭示了炼金术对近代早期科学发展的重大贡献。例如，炼金术提出了这样一些原则：强调化学过程中重量的测定与守恒，发展完备且具解释力的微粒物质理论，把分析与合成作为理解自然的工具，人类技艺能够创造出新的或更优良的产品，胜于自然产物，或许甚至还包括对牛顿物理学至关重要的力的概念。

body.text: 4. Alchemy and Chemistry
body.zh: 4. 炼金术与化学

body.text: The last of the obstacles to understanding alchemy which were mentioned at the outset can be seen as a parallel to the segregation of alchemy from the scientific mainstream (both in the 18th and the 19th to 20th centuries). This is the frequent division of alchemy from chemistry as if the two were only marginally contiguous. This division was made quite clearly by the work of Hélène Metzger in the 1920s, with alchemy as vitalistic and inherently “primitive” on the one side, and chemistry as mechanistic and “scientific” on the other. The division was recapitulated in Marie Boas’ studies of Boyle and in quite a bit of historical writing down to the present. Yet until about the end of the 17th century, the terms alchemy and chemistry were used largely interchangeably, and did not carry their modern definitions and distinctions. The division between the two terms dates from around 1700, and is tied up with a number of issues, including the professionalization and institutionalization of chemistry at this time and the desire to insulate the newly professionalizing field from the criticisms to which earlier transmutational endeavors had been prone. Thus “alchemy” then became equated with gold-making (and generally fraud), while “chemistry” encompassed most everything else which could previously have been called either alchemy or chemistry. The important point is that it is distorting and historically inaccurate to read our current distinction between the terms back into the 17th century and earlier, and thus to imagine the existence of “chemists” and “alchemists” as distinct groups at that time. Use of the archaic (and inclusive) term chymistry for speaking comprehensively about the undifferentiated alchemy/chemistry of the early modern period has been suggested as a solution. Likewise, for the sake of greater clarity, a revival of archaic, but more precise, terminology has also been advocated, for example, chrysopoeia (gold-making) and less commonly argyropoeia (silvermaking) to describe metallic transmutational chymistry, iatrochemistry or chemiatria to describe medicinal applications, spagyria to label Paracelsian-inspired attempts to create more potent substances by analysis and resynthesis, and so forth.
body.zh: 开头提到的理解炼金术的最后一项障碍，可以看作与把炼金术从科学主流中隔离出去（无论在18世纪还是在19至20世纪）的做法相平行。这就是常把炼金术与化学分割开来，仿佛二者仅在边缘上相邻。这一分割在埃莱娜·梅茨格（Hélène Metzger）20世纪20年代的著作中被划分得相当清楚：一边是活力论的、本质上“原始”的炼金术，另一边是机械论的、“科学的”化学。这一分割在玛丽·博厄斯（Marie Boas）关于波义耳的研究中，以及在直至今日的相当一部分历史著述中，都被重述。然而，直到大约17世纪末，炼金术与化学这两个术语在很大程度上是互换使用的，并不带有它们现代的界定与区分。两个术语之间的区分始于1700年前后，并与一系列问题纠缠在一起，其中包括化学在当时走向职业化与制度化，以及人们希望使这一新近职业化的领域免受早先的转化尝试所易招致的批评。于是，“炼金术”当时被等同于制金（且通常是欺诈），而“化学”则涵盖了此前可能被称为炼金术或化学的几乎所有其他内容。重要的一点在于，把我们当下对这两个术语的区分回溯到17世纪及更早时期，从而想象当时存在“化学家”与“炼金术士”这样两个彼此分明的群体，乃是一种扭曲且有违历史事实的做法。有人建议以古旧（且具包容性）的术语 chymistry（化学—炼金术）来统称近代早期尚未分化的炼金术／化学，以此作为解决办法。同样，为了更加明晰，也有人主张复兴古旧但更为精确的术语，例如以 chrysopoeia（制金）以及较少使用的 argyropoeia（制银）来描述金属转化的 chymistry，以 iatrochemistry 或 chemiatria 来描述医药应用，以 spagyria 来标示受帕拉塞尔苏斯派启发、通过分解与再合成来制造更强效物质的尝试，等等。

body.text: Much work is still required (and on-going) to fill out our understanding of so difficult and diverse a field as alchemy. Such fresh understanding will be advanced when we avoid making unnecessarily broad statements about the intent and content of alchemy as a whole, and instead carry out studies which adequately localize alchemical thought – of whatever century – in its due context of time and place. In particular, the new understanding now being gained of pre-18th century alchemy (or “chymistry”) requires the recognition and rejection of preconceptions arising from anachronistic and untenable interpretations which date from the 19th and 20th centuries.
body.zh: 要充分理解炼金术这样一个困难而多样的领域，仍需（并且正在进行）大量工作。当我们避免就炼金术整体的意图与内容作出不必要地宽泛的论断，转而开展研究，把无论哪个世纪的炼金术思想充分置于其应得的时间与地点语境之中时，这种新的理解便会得到推进。尤其是，目前正在形成的对18世纪以前炼金术（或“chymistry”）的新理解，要求我们辨识并摒弃那些源自19世纪与20世纪、时代错置且站不住脚的解释所带来的先入之见。
