body.text: An engraver by trade, Blake was primarily a self-educated graphic and literary artist whose work reflects the attempt to confront contemporary political and social problems through a philosophically based spiritualism. Although baptized and buried in the Anglican Church, Blake was born into a family of freethinkers, and himself attempted to get back to the pure form of Christianity he believed to have existed before it was corrupted by organized religion.
body.zh: 威廉·布莱克（William Blake）以铜版雕刻为业，但主要是一位自学成才的版画与文学艺术家，其作品体现出一种尝试：以有哲学根基的唯灵论去直面当时的政治与社会问题。他虽在英国国教会受洗、亦葬于其墓地，却出身于一个自由思想者家庭，本人则力图回到他所相信的那种纯粹基督教形态——在它被组织化宗教败坏之前曾经存在。

body.text: Blake’s life reflects the conflict between corporeal and spiritual needs. He worked as a commercial artist, engraving illustrations for popular books, including some by Mary Wollstonecraft (1759-1797), Erasmus Darwin (1731-1802), and, notably, the account of John Gabriel Stedman (1744-1797), Narrative of a Five Years Expedition against the Revolted Negroes of Surinam (1796). Yet, he was always more interested in executing his own illuminated books, which reflect an increasingly strong influence by the prisca theologia [→tradition], a pure form of theology that had developed as a counterpoint to conventional religion. Attempting to address the sometimes contradictory obligations of his materialistic and idealistic needs, Blake experimented with novel paint formulæ and engraving methods (explained to him, in a dream, by his deceased brother Robert), all designed to make his visions commercially viable. Unfortunately, none of the innovations proved financially successful.
body.zh: 布莱克的一生体现出肉体需要与精神需要之间的冲突。他以商业艺术家的身份谋生，为流行书籍雕制插图，其中包括玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特（Mary Wollstonecraft，1759-1797）、伊拉斯谟·达尔文（Erasmus Darwin，1731-1802）的某些著作，尤其还有约翰·加布里埃尔·斯特德曼（John Gabriel Stedman，1744-1797）的记述《苏里南起义黑奴五年远征记》（Narrative of a Five Years Expedition against the Revolted Negroes of Surinam，1796）。然而，他始终更倾心于制作自己的彩饰书（illuminated books）；这些作品反映出上古神学（prisca theologia）[→传统]日益强烈的影响，而这是一种纯粹的神学形态，作为常规宗教的对立面发展起来。为了兼顾自己在物质与理想两方面时或相互矛盾的需要，布莱克尝试了新的颜料配方与雕版方法（据他说，这是已故的弟弟罗伯特在梦中传授给他的），凡此都是为了让他的幻象在商业上可行。不幸的是，这些革新在财务上无一成功。

body.text: Throughout his life, Blake evinced a strong interest in spiritualism. As a child, he experienced religious visions, and as a young man, he circulated among the mystics who frequented London in the 1780s. He met the neoplatonist Thomas Taylor (1758-1835), as well as the artist Henry Füseli (1741-1825); and he engraved the frontispiece for Füseli’s English translation of →Johann Kaspar Lavater’s Aphorisms on Man (1788). Intellectually, he was attracted to the writings of →Emanuel Swedenborg, owning and annotating at least three of Swedenborg’s books – Heaven and Hell, Divine Love and Divine Wisdom, and Divine Providence – and was likely familiar with two others – Earths in the Universe and True Christian Religion. In addition, Blake and his wife both signed the register for the first General Conference of the New Jerusalem Church in 1789. There is no clear evidence, however, that they attended any subsequent meetings, and Blake was eventually disillusioned enough to satirize Swedenborg’s Heaven and Hell in his own The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (1790-1793), transforming Swedenborg’s Memorable Relations into his own Memorable Fancies. Renouncing, for a time, Swedenborg’s influence, Blake claimed that ‘Swedenborgs writings are a recapitulation of all superficial opinions, and an analysis of the more sublime, but no further’ (pl. 22, E 43).
body.zh: 布莱克终生对唯灵论表现出浓厚的兴趣。他幼年时就有宗教异象，青年时代则与1780年代出入伦敦的各位神秘主义者往来。他会见过新柏拉图主义者托马斯·泰勒（Thomas Taylor，1758-1835）以及画家亨利·富塞利（Henry Füseli，1741-1825）；还为富塞利英译的→约翰·卡斯帕·拉瓦特（Johann Kaspar Lavater）《论人箴言》（Aphorisms on Man，1788）雕制了卷首插图。在思想上，他倾心于→伊曼纽尔·斯威登堡（Emanuel Swedenborg）的著作，至少藏有并批注过斯威登堡的三部书——《天堂与地狱》（Heaven and Hell）、《神的爱与神的智慧》（Divine Love and Divine Wisdom）与《神意》（Divine Providence）——并且很可能熟悉另外两部：《宇宙中的大地》（Earths in the Universe）与《真正的基督教》（True Christian Religion）。此外，布莱克夫妇都在1789年新耶路撒冷教会第一次全体会议的登记簿上签了名。然而，没有明确证据表明他们参加过此后的任何集会；布莱克最终失望之至，在自己的《天堂与地狱的婚姻》（The Marriage of Heaven and Hell，1790-1793）中讽刺了斯威登堡的《天堂与地狱》，把斯威登堡的“可纪念之事”（Memorable Relations）改写成自己的“可纪念的幻想”（Memorable Fancies）。布莱克一度弃绝斯威登堡的影响，声称“斯威登堡的著作是对一切肤浅意见的复述，并且是对较为崇高之事的分析，但仅止于此”（pl. 22, E 43）。

body.text: From Swedenborg Blake turned to →Paracelsus, the 16th-century Swiss alchemist, and →Jacob Boehme, the 17th-century German visionary, whose works had been translated by the 18th-cen-tury English mystic, →William Law. Although Blake spent his entire life in England, he did leave London for a few years, spending 1800-1803 in Felpham, as a guest of minor poet William Hayley (1745-1820). Although the relationship with the practical-minded Hayley quickly deteriorated, the stay in the country afforded Blake access to an extensive library. More successful was the relationship with Thomas Butts, a minor bureaucrat whose patronage during the first decade of the 19th century enabled Blake to illustrate parts of the Bible and Milton, among other things. Later in life, in 1818, Blake was discovered by John Linnell (1792- 1882) and John Varley (1778-1842), two young artists whose own interests in the occult helped reinvigorate Blake’s final works.
body.zh: 布莱克从斯威登堡转向16世纪瑞士炼金术士→帕拉塞尔苏斯（Paracelsus），又转向17世纪德国灵视者→雅各布·波墨（Jacob Boehme）；后者的著作曾由18世纪英国神秘主义者→威廉·劳（William Law）译成英文。布莱克虽终生都在英格兰度过，却确实离开伦敦数年，1800至1803年客居费尔珀姆（Felpham），是小诗人威廉·海利（William Hayley，1745-1820）的座上客。尽管与讲求实际的海利之间的关系很快恶化，乡居生活仍使布莱克得以利用一座藏书丰富的图书馆。更为成功的是他与托马斯·巴茨（Thomas Butts）的关系；这位小官吏在19世纪头十年的赞助，使布莱克得以绘制《圣经》与弥尔顿作品的部分插图，此外还有其他工作。晚年，1818年，布莱克被约翰·林内尔（John Linnell，1792-1882）与约翰·瓦利（John Varley，1778-1842）发现；这两位年轻艺术家自身对秘术的兴趣，有助于重新激发布莱克最后一批作品的活力。

body.text: These disparate interests all converge in Blake’s own form of a prisca theologia, in which he uses a kabbalistic-like myth as the basis for unifying all of his spiritual interests. His thesis in the early tract, All Religions are One (1788), that ‘The Religions of all Nations are derived from each Nation’s different reception of the Poetic Genius which is every where call’d the Spirit of Prophecy’, would lead inexorably to a rejection of any particular religious organization, the Swedenborgian New Church included. As he explained in The Marriage of Heaven and Hell: ‘Till a system was formed, which some took advantage of & enslav’d the vulgar by attempting to realize or abstract the mental dieties from their objects: thus began Priesthood. / Choosing forms of worship from poetic tales. / And at length they pronounced that the Gods had orderd such things. / Thus men forgot that All deities reside in the human breast’ (pl. 11).
body.zh: 这些彼此不同的旨趣，全都汇入布莱克自己形态的上古神学：他以一种类卡巴拉的神话为基础，把他所有的精神关怀统一起来。他在早期短文《一切宗教皆为一体》（All Religions are One，1788）中提出：“所有民族的宗教，都源于每个民族对‘诗性天才’（Poetic Genius）的不同接受，而此天才到处被称为‘预言的精神’”；这一论点势必导致对任何特定宗教组织的拒斥，斯威登堡派的新教会亦在其中。正如他在《天堂与地狱的婚姻》中所解释的：“直到一个体系形成，有人利用它，试图把精神诸神从其所附之物中抽离或实现出来，从而奴役庸众：祭司制度由此开始。/ 从诗性的故事中挑选崇拜的形式。/ 最终他们宣称，诸神已命定了这些事。/ 于是人们忘记了，一切神明都居于人心之中”（pl. 11）。

body.text: Intellectually, Blake agreed with the basic assumptions of →Francis Mercurius van Helmont’s delineation of the prisca theologia, that the universe is an organic, vital, evolving whole, and that humans, having been made in God’s image, are to use their imagination to help restore the post-lapsarian world to its original perfection, through the exercise of their intellect and imagination. In the works leading up to The Marriage of Heaven and Hell, Blake applies his spiritual principles to contemporary problems. The early unpublished poem, The French Revolution (1791), focuses on the war in Europe; Visions of the Daughters of Albion (1793) considers English participation in the slave trade; and various lyrics in the collected Songs of Innocence (1789), and later, the combined Songs of
body.zh: 在思想上，布莱克赞同→弗朗西斯·墨丘利·范·海尔蒙特（Francis Mercurius van Helmont）对上古神学的阐述所依据的基本假设：宇宙是一个有机的、有生命的、演化着的整体；人既按上帝的形象受造，就应当运用理智与想象力，帮助堕落之后的世界恢复其原初的完善。在《天堂与地狱的婚姻》之前的那些作品中，布莱克把自己的精神原则应用于当代问题。早期未发表的长诗《法国大革命》（The French Revolution，1791）聚焦于欧洲的战争；《阿尔比恩女儿们的幻象》（Visions of the Daughters of Albion，1793）审视英国参与奴隶贸易一事；而诗集《天真之歌》（Songs of Innocence，1789）中的各首诗，以及后来合刊的《天真与

body.text: Innocence and of Experience (1794) explore different forms of social, religious, political and moral hypocrisy.
body.zh: 经验之歌》（Songs of Innocence and of Experience，1794）则探讨了各种形式的社会、宗教、政治与道德虚伪。

body.text: At the same time that he worked on these exoteric works, Blake also began exploring esoteric themes. There is No Natural Religion, the companion to All Religions are One, is a series of aphorisms that conclude with the Application: ‘He who sees the Infinite in all things sees God. He who sees the Ratio only sees himself only. Therefore God becomes as we are, that we may be as he is’. He also began exploring the dimensions of gnosis in The Book of Thel (1789), a neoplatonic poem in which the soul ultimately chooses to stay in the ‘vales of Har’, Blake’s name for what he sees as the debilitation inherent in pre-lapsarian Eden, rather than become part of the corporeal cosmos where, though contributing to the life cycle, she will die. Similarly, in the unengraved Tiriel (c. 1789), Blake merges exoteric and esoteric themes, condemning contemporary politics for being a function of the erroneous use of reason, as opposed to intellect. To complete this phase of his artistic development, Blake wrote two prophecies – America (1793) and Europe (1794) – in which he presents an apocalyptic interpretation of the American and French Revolutions.
body.zh: 在创作这些显白（exoteric）作品的同时，布莱克也开始探索隐微（esoteric）主题。《没有自然宗教》（There is No Natural Religion）是《一切宗教皆为一体》的姊妹篇，由一系列箴言组成，末尾的“应用”（Application）写道：“在一切事物中看见无限的人，就看见了上帝。只看见‘比率’（Ratio）的人，只看见他自己。因此，上帝成为我们之所是，使我们得以成为他之所是。”他也在《塞尔书》（The Book of Thel，1789）中开始探索灵知（gnosis）的诸维度；这是一首新柏拉图主义的长诗，其中的灵魂最终选择留在“哈耳之谷”（vales of Har）——布莱克以此名称指他所理解的、堕落前伊甸园所固有的那种萎弱状态——而不愿进入有形的宇宙；在那里，她虽参与生命循环，却终将死去。同样，在未雕版印行的《提利尔》（Tiriel，约1789）中，布莱克融合了显白与隐微两种主题，谴责当时的政治乃是错误运用理性（reason）而非智性（intellect）的结果。为完成其艺术发展的这一阶段，布莱克写了两部“预言书”——《美洲》（America，1793）与《欧洲》（Europe，1794）——在其中对美国和法国革命作出了启示录式的解释。

body.text: In the mid-1790s, Blake began the decades-long process of rendering his kabbalistic prisca theologia into mythic form. During this period he completed the four “minor prophecies”, in which he worked out specific details of his developing myth. In the first, The Song of Los (1795), Blake traces the progress of organized religion, attributed, in The Book of Urizen (1794), to the consolidation of the rational factor. The problem, as analyzed in The Book of Ahania (1795), is that once consolidated, reason became cut off from its spiritual component. Therefore, as suggested in The Book of Los (1795), the relationship between reason and vision had to be reconfigured. Of key importance to Blake’s thought process at this stage was the commission, worked on in 1795-1796, to help illustrate the popular poem by Edward Young (1683-1765), The Complaint, or Night Thoughts on Life, Death, and Immortality (1742-45), an extensive meditation based on conventional Christian theology. Even though the commission eventually fell through, the detailed analysis required for the project forced Blake to confront point by point his own attitude towards exoteric theology.
body.zh: 1790年代中期，布莱克开始了一项历时数十年的工作：把他那带有卡巴拉色彩的上古神学转化为神话形式。这一时期，他完成了四部“小预言书”，在其中把他正在形成的神话的具体细节推演出来。在第一部《洛斯之歌》（The Song of Los，1795）中，布莱克追溯了组织化宗教的进展，而《乌里森之书》（The Book of Urizen，1794）则把这一进展归因于理性因素的固化。正如《阿哈尼娅之书》（The Book of Ahania，1795）所分析的，问题在于：理性一旦固化，便与其精神成分割裂开来。因此，正如《洛斯之书》（The Book of Los，1795）所暗示的，理性与灵视之间的关系必须重新配置。在布莱克这一阶段的思想进程中，关键的一件事是1795至1796年间接受的一项委托：为爱德华·扬（Edward Young，1683-1765）的流行长诗《怨诉，或关于生命、死亡与不朽的夜思》（The Complaint, or Night Thoughts on Life, Death, and Immortality，1742-45）绘制部分插图；这部作品是以常规基督教神学为基础的长篇沉思。尽管这项委托最终未能成事，但项目所需的细致分析迫使布莱克逐点面对自己对显白神学的态度。

body.text: During the next ten years, intermittently from 1796 until 1807, Blake attempted to consolidate his criticism into a full-scale epic that would counter the errors propagated by Young’s Night Thoughts.
body.zh: 此后十年间，自1796年至1807年断断续续地，布莱克试图把自己的批评整合为一部规模宏大的史诗，以抗衡扬《夜思》所传播的错误。

body.text: The Four Zoas – or Vala, as it was originally called – is the first major attempt to transform his prisca theologia into narrative form. Written, in many cases, on proof sheets from the Young project, The Four Zoas is an early revision and re-presentation of exoteric Christianity in an esoteric form, its nine “nights” corresponding respectively to the kabbalistic sefirot (emanations) from Malkhut (Kingdom) through Hokhmah (Divine Wisdom), tracing the via mystica back to Keter Elyon, the Supreme Crown. Even though the myth is populated by unique allegorical figures with originally coined names, its structure resembles Francis Mercurius van Helmont’s system of Christian Kabbalism. A major collaborator with →Christian Knorr von Rosenroth (1636-1689) on the Kabbala Denudata (2 vols., Sulzbach, 1677-1684), van Helmont contributed the Adumbratio Kabbalæ Christianæ, a full-length Platonic dialogue between a Kabbalist and a Christian Philosopher, designed to demonstrate the congruence between the myth generated by Jewish mystic Isaac Luria (1534-1572) and Christianity. According to kabbalistic tradition, our existence is part of a larger cycle of creation, the purpose of which is to provide the opportunity for all souls to be purified. In the Adumbratio, van Helmont christianizes the myth, using the Bible to justify his transformation of the Jewish system. In order to add a specifically christological function, he expands what was originally a three-part structure – “Contraction”, “the Breaking of the Vessels”, and “Restoration” – into four phases: “The Primordial Institution”, the Godhead’s original intention for creation; “The State of Destitution”, the fall, as caused by the breaking of the vessels, and the ensuing contamination of souls; “The Modern Constitution”, corporeal existence in which both macrocosm (Christ) and microcosm (man) work, each on his own level, to effect the form of restoration; so that, finally, in “The Supreme Restitution”, Christ can defeat the forces of evil and man can rise.
body.zh: 《四佐亚》（The Four Zoas）——最初名为《瓦拉》（Vala）——是把他的上古神学转化为叙事形式的第一次重大尝试。这部作品许多部分写在扬项目留下的校样纸上；《四佐亚》是对显白基督教的早期改写，并以隐微形式重新呈现，其九个“夜晚”分别对应卡巴拉的生命树十辉（sefirot，流溢）中从玛尔库特（Malkhut，王国）到霍克玛（Hokhmah，神圣智慧）的诸级，沿着神秘之路（via mystica）回溯至“至高冠冕”（Keter Elyon）。尽管这部神话中充斥着名称自创的独特寓意人物，其结构却近似于弗朗西斯·墨丘利·范·海尔蒙特的基督教卡巴拉体系。范·海尔蒙特曾与→克里斯蒂安·克诺尔·冯·罗森罗特（Christian Knorr von Rosenroth，1636-1689）密切合作，编纂《揭去面纱的卡巴拉》（Kabbala Denudata，2卷，苏尔茨巴赫，1677-1684），并撰写了《基督教卡巴拉概要》（Adumbratio Kabbalæ Christianæ）：这是一篇完整的柏拉图式对话，在一位卡巴拉学者与一位基督教哲学家之间展开，旨在证明犹太神秘主义者以撒·卢里亚（Isaac Luria，1534-1572）所生成的神话与基督教彼此契合。按卡巴拉传统，我们的存在是更大创造循环的一部分，其目的在于为一切灵魂提供净化的机会。在《概要》中，范·海尔蒙特把这一神话基督教化，借《圣经》为他改造犹太体系作辩护。为了加入一个明确的基督论功能，他把原本三阶段的结构——“收缩”（Contraction）、“器皿破裂”（the Breaking of the Vessels）与“复原”（Restoration）——扩展为四个阶段：“原初建制”（The Primordial Institution），即神性对创造的原始意图；“匮乏状态”（The State of Destitution），即由器皿破裂所导致的堕落，以及随之而来的灵魂污染；“现代构造”（The Modern Constitution），即有形存在，在其中大宇宙（基督）与小宇宙（人）各自在自己的层面上运作，以实现复原的形式；最后，在“至高复归”（The Supreme Restitution）中，基督得以战胜恶的势力，人得以升起。

body.text: We do not know Blake’s specific source for Kabbalism. However, in his major prophecies, he generated a universal prisca theologia which incorporates into a Lurianic/van Helmontian base all of his esoteric reading, including the neoplatonists, Boehme and even Swedenborg. The result was a four-fold myth about the nationalistic hero, Albion – ‘His fall into Division & his Resurrection to Unity / His fall into the Generation of Decay & Death & his Regeneration by the Resurrection from the dead’ (n. 1, 4:4-5). In this first attempt at an epic narrative, Blake seems incapable of delineating a non-conventional role for the Saviour.
body.zh: 我们并不知道布莱克卡巴拉思想的具体来源。然而，在他的主要预言书中，他生成了一种普遍的上古神学，以卢里亚／范·海尔蒙特式的体系为基础，把他所读的一切隐微著作都纳入其中，包括新柏拉图主义者、波墨，甚至斯威登堡。其结果是一个关于民族性英雄阿尔比恩（Albion）的四重神话——“他堕落而分裂，又复活而归于统一／他堕落而生成腐朽与死亡，又借从死者中的复活而重生”（n. 1, 4:4-5）。在这第一次史诗叙事的尝试中，布莱克似乎无力为救主勾画一个非常规的角色。

body.text: Available only in a heavily revised manuscript, The Four Zoas reflects the creative process involved in the attempt to transform abstract theory into a fully realized myth. In its earliest form, originally entitled Vala, the epic was apparently intended to focus on the emanation of the spiritual component, her individuation signifying the consolidation of the force that would oppose true vision, and therefore lead inevitably to organized religion. As the poem evolved, however, Blake shifted his focus from the effect to the cause, from Vala to the four zoas, his name for the four psychological components that correspond to the four kabbalistic souls. In its final form, The Four Zoas depicts the initial disorganization of the four zoas, as Urizen (the Rational Soul) usurps the function of vision, causing Urthona (the Immortal Soul) to grow dark and to limp. Throughout the poem, the action delineates the process by which the zoas are ultimately realigned so that Albion can be regenerated. The problem is that at this point, the action leads almost inexorably to an external catalyst – Christian ransom – for its resolution. Although Blake would work on the poem for at least a decade, and would even complete its apocalyptic vision – ‘The war of swords departed now / The dark Religions are departed & sweet Science reigns’ (n. 9, 139:9-10) – he could never integrate within its action a christological function that was not inimical to the concept of free will.
body.zh: 《四佐亚》仅以一份经过大幅修改的手稿存世，它反映出把抽象理论转化为完整神话这一尝试所涉及的创作过程。在其最早形态（原题《瓦拉》）中，这部长诗显然意在聚焦于精神成分的流溢：她的个体化标志着那股将对抗真正灵视的力量得以固化，从而不可避免地导向组织化宗教。然而，随着诗作的发展，布莱克把焦点从结果转向原因，从瓦拉转向四位佐亚——他用以称呼与卡巴拉四重灵魂相对应的四种心理成分的名称。在最终形态中，《四佐亚》描绘了四位佐亚最初的失序：乌里森（Urizen，理性灵魂）篡夺了灵视的职能，致使乌尔托纳（Urthona，不朽灵魂）变得晦暗而跛行。全诗的动作勾勒出佐亚们最终重新排列、从而使阿尔比恩得以重生的过程。问题在于，至此情节几乎不可避免地引向一个外部催化剂——基督的救赎——才能解决。尽管布莱克为这部诗至少工作了十年，甚至完成了它的启示录式幻象——“刀剑的战争如今已逝去／黑暗的诸宗教已逝去，甜美的科学掌权”（n. 9, 139:9-10）——他却始终无法在情节中纳入一个不与自由意志概念相抵触的基督论功能。

body.text: Blake confronts that specific problem in Milton, a brief epic in which the historical John Milton – whose doctrine in Paradise Lost was the source, Blake believed, of subsequent theological misapprehensions – returns to correct his error. As a transmigrating soul, Milton has wandered in heaven for one hundred years, unhappy at the legacy he left on earth. Hearing, in the Bard’s Song, the esoteric account of creation and fall, he identifies himself as the source of the exoteric misconception that has been promulgated on earth – ‘I in my Selfhood am that Satan: I am that Evil One!’ – and returns to correct his error: ‘I go to Eternal Death’ (14[15]:30, 32). Once there, he literally reforms Urizen so that Albion can rise, and all of creation can prepare for ‘the Great Harvest & Vintage of the Nations’.
body.zh: 布莱克在《弥尔顿》（Milton）中直面这一具体问题。这部小型史诗让历史上的约翰·弥尔顿（John Milton）归来纠正自己的错误——布莱克相信，《失乐园》（Paradise Lost）中的教义正是此后种种神学误解的源头。作为一个转世的灵魂，弥尔顿在天堂漂泊了一百年，为自己在人间留下的遗产而郁郁不乐。他在吟游诗人的歌中听到关于创造与堕落的隐微叙述，便认明自己正是那在人间流传的显白谬见的源头——“我，在我的自我性（Selfhood）中，就是那撒旦：我就是那恶者！”——于是归来纠正自己的错误：“我走向永恒之死”（14[15]:30, 32）。到了那里，他实实在在地改造了乌里森，使阿尔比恩得以升起，整个创造得以预备“万民的大收割与采收”。

body.text: In delineating gilgul, the process by which the transmigrating soul returns to correct its error, Blake, like van Helmont before him, associates the kabbalistic Adam Kadmon (primordial man) with the christological function, though not as an external Saviour. Instead, he reconfigures Los, the personification that had been associated with the → imagination, into an internal Christ. Becoming what Blake will call ‘the vehicular form’ of Urthona (the Immortal Soul), Los is now depicted as having forgotten his originally intended function. But when Milton reforms Urizen, Los ‘recollect[s] an old Prophecy in Eden recorded’ (20[22]:57), and devotes himself to constructing Golgonooza, the lower Eden where transmigrating souls will be purified in preparation for the apocalypse. Instead of sacrificing himself for the sake of mankind, Los creates the structure through which the individual can, of his own free will, save himself.
body.zh: 在阐述“吉尔古尔”（gilgul）——即转世灵魂归来纠正其错误的过程——时，布莱克一如先前的范·海尔蒙特，把卡巴拉的“原人”亚当·卡德蒙（Adam Kadmon）与基督论功能联系起来，但并不将其视为外在的救主。相反，他把原本与→想象力相联系的人格化形象洛斯（Los）重塑为内在的基督。洛斯成为布莱克后来所称的乌尔托纳（不朽灵魂）的“载具形式”（vehicular form），此时被描绘为已经遗忘自己原初被指定的职能。但当弥尔顿改造乌里森时，洛斯“回想起一个记于伊甸的古老预言”（20[22]:57），并致力于建造戈尔戈诺扎（Golgonooza）——那较低层的伊甸，转世的灵魂将在那里得到净化，为启示录作准备。洛斯不是为人类牺牲自己，而是创造出一种结构，使个体得以凭自己的自由意志拯救自己。

body.text: If Milton creates the form of restoration, Jerusalem, Blake’s final prophecy, enacts the process in the fullest sense. Consistent with the four-part structure delineated by van Helmont, Blake divides the action of Jerusalem into the four-part process ‘Of the Sleep of Ulro! and of the passage through / Eternal Death! and of the awaking to Eternal Life’(4:1-2). Juxtaposing the corresponding actions of the macrocosm (Adam Kadmon/Los) and the microcosm (Adam Rishon/Albion), Blake divides his epic into four chapters, corresponding respectively to van Helmont’s four sections. In his first chapter, Blake conveys the inverse of van Helmont’s “Primordial Institution”, portraying the prelapsarian state in terms of what was lost as a result of the fall, when Albion chose ‘demonstration’ over ‘faith’. At the same time that Albion lapses into despair, the psychological state that prevents restoration of the microcosm, Los confronts his Spectre, the force of negation that attempts to deter him from effecting restoration on the macrocosmic level. In the second chapter, Blake depicts van Helmont’s “State of Destitution”, when ‘Every ornament of perfection, and every labour of love, / In all the Garden of Eden, & in all the golden mountains / Was become an envied horror’ (28: 1-3). Even though, in his spiritual blindness, Albion turns his back on the Divine Vision, still, Los labors at his furnace, renovating the form of religion so that Albion will be able to rise. Next, corresponding to van Helmont’s “Modern Constitution”, Albion, the microcosm, confronts the perversions of Christianity that were produced as a result of the fall, while simultaneously, Los, on the macrocosmic level, attempts to align the biblical tribes with Albion’s sons, to prepare for the “Supreme Restitution”, when Los will confront negation at its very source, as he ‘alterd his Spectre & every Ratio of his Reason / . . . Till he had completely divided him into a separate space’ (91:50, 52). Finally, ‘Time was Finished! The Breath Divine Breathed over Albion’ (94:18).
body.zh: 如果说《弥尔顿》创造了复原的形式，那么布莱克的最后一部预言书《耶路撒冷》（Jerusalem）则最充分地践行了这一过程。与范·海尔蒙特所勾画的四部分结构相一致，布莱克把《耶路撒冷》的情节分为四个部分的过程：“关于乌尔罗的沉睡！以及穿越／永恒之死的经过！以及觉醒于永恒生命”（4:1-2）。他把大宇宙（亚当·卡德蒙／洛斯）与小宇宙（亚当·里雄／阿尔比恩）的相应行动并置，把自己的史诗分为四章，分别对应范·海尔蒙特的四个部分。在第一章中，布莱克传达的是范·海尔蒙特“原初建制”的倒转：他以堕落所丧失之物的角度描绘堕落前的状态——当时阿尔比恩选择了“论证”而非“信仰”。就在阿尔比恩陷入绝望（这种心理状态阻碍小宇宙的复原）之际，洛斯直面他的“幽灵”（Spectre），即那股试图阻止他在大宇宙层面实现复原的否定力量。在第二章中，布莱克描绘范·海尔蒙特的“匮乏状态”：“完美的一切装饰，以及爱的一切劳作，／在整个伊甸园中，在一切金色的山峦上／都变成了为人所妒的恐怖”（28:1-3）。尽管阿尔比恩在其精神上的盲目中背弃了神圣幻象，洛斯仍在炉边劳作，更新宗教的形式，使阿尔比恩终能升起。接着，对应于范·海尔蒙特的“现代构造”，小宇宙阿尔比恩直面堕落所导致的基督教种种败坏；与此同时，在大宇宙层面上，洛斯试图使《圣经》中的各支派与阿尔比恩的众子相配列，为“至高复归”作准备——届时洛斯将在否定的源头处与之对峙，他“改变了他的幽灵，以及他理性中的每一‘比率’／……直到他把他完全分割到一个独立的空间”（91:50, 52）。最后，“时间已完结！神的气息吹拂过阿尔比恩”（94:18）。

body.text: Through Jerusalem, which he worked on intermittently from 1804 until the 1820s, Blake was able to conceive a kabbalistic version of Christianity, one that enabled Albion to exercise the free will necessary to save himself, but without sacrificing the christological function of Los, who on the one hand, manipulated the form that Albion would actualize, and on the other, confronted the shards of negation that exist as an obstacle to cosmic restoration. Thus, it was through his verbal art that Blake was able to articulate his system. From that point on, however, he would focus on the visual art for its ultimate expression.
body.zh: 通过《耶路撒冷》——他自1804年起断断续续写作至1820年代——布莱克得以构想出一种卡巴拉式的基督教，这种基督教使阿尔比恩能够行使拯救自己所必需的自由意志，同时又不牺牲洛斯的基督论功能：洛斯一方面操控阿尔比恩将要实现的形式，另一方面直面那些作为宇宙复原之障碍而存在的否定碎片。因此，布莱克正是通过他的语言艺术才得以表述自己的体系。然而自此以后，他将专注于视觉艺术，以之作为其体系的终极表达。

body.text: In his last works, Blake used the myth he had developed in the composite art as the standard against which to criticize and artistically revise the Bible and other religious works. He returned to the Book of Job, which he had worked on sporadically throughout his life, this time engraving plates that inverted the focus of the composite books. There, the pictures had been used to illustrate the verbal text; now, he uses words to illuminate what is primarily a visual text. In its completed form, Blake faults Job for constructing a rationalistic interpretation of religion, rather than experiencing God directly through the imagination. The Ghost of Abel (1822), a two-plate response to Byron’s Cain: A Mystery, published in December 1821, is subtitled ‘A Revelation In the Visions of Jehovah / Seen by William Blake’. For Laocoön (c. 1826-1827), his last illuminated work, Blake arranges a vast collection of aphorisms, using Hebrew and Greek, as well as English, all around a statue of Laocoön and his two sons, to convey the disparity between that which is taught and that which is true. Finally, on his deathbed, Blake worked on the 102-water color drawings that criticize and correct →Dante’s Divine Comedy, demonstrating how organized religion had occluded the medieval Italian poet’s true vision.
body.zh: 在最后一批作品中，布莱克以自己在“综合艺术”（composite art）中发展出的神话为标准，据以批评并在艺术上修订《圣经》及其他宗教作品。他重新回到《约伯记》（Book of Job）——这是他一生中零星处理过的题材——这一次雕制了若干版画，颠倒了那些综合艺术书籍的侧重。在那些书中，图像曾被用来图解文字；如今，他则用文字来照亮一部主要是视觉性的文本。在完成的版本中，布莱克责难约伯，认为他建构了一种对宗教的理性主义解释，而不是通过想象力直接体验上帝。《亚伯的幽灵》（The Ghost of Abel，1822）是对拜伦（Byron）《该隐：一个谜》（Cain: A Mystery，1821年12月出版）的回应，由两块版组成，副标题为“在耶和华的异象中的一则启示／由威廉·布莱克所见”（A Revelation In the Visions of Jehovah / Seen by William Blake）。在《拉奥孔》（Laocoön，约1826-1827）——他最后一部彩饰作品——中，布莱克把大量箴言安排在一座拉奥孔及其两个儿子的雕像周围，使用希伯来文、希腊文以及英文，以传达所教之物与真实之物之间的差距。最后，在临终的床上，布莱克仍在处理那102幅水彩画，它们批评并纠正→但丁（Dante）的《神曲》（Divine Comedy），表明组织化宗教如何遮蔽了这位中世纪意大利诗人的真正灵视。
