entries.title: Blavatsky, Helena Petrovna
entries.heading: Blavatsky, Helena Petrovna, * 12.8.1831 Ekaterinoslav, † 8.5.1891 London
entries.title_zh: 布拉瓦茨基，海伦娜·彼得罗夫娜
entries.author: james a. santucci

body.text: Undoubtedly one of the most fascinating, controversial, and influential women in the 19th century writing on the ancient wisdom tradition, Blavatsky was born in the von Hahn family on August 12, 1831 (or on July 31, according to the old Julian calendar that was still current in Russia) in Ekaterinoslav (Dnepropetrovsk), the Ukraine. Descended from a prominent family of Russian, French Huguenot, and German background, her father, Col. Peter Alexeyevich von Hahn (1798- 1873), was a descendant of the medieval crusader Count Rottenstern and a Captain of Artillery. Her mother, Helena Andreyevna, née de Fadeyev (1814- 1842), was a woman of great literary talent who wrote novels under the pseudonym of Zeneida R__va. Because of her husband’s position, the family traveled constantly. During an interlude in the early 1840s following the death of her mother in Odessa, young Helena was sent to live with her grandparents (Andrey Mihailovitch de Fedeyev and Helena Pavlovna Delgorukova) in Saratov, where she remained until 1845. According to accounts of this period, Helena already exhibited traits of mediumship.
body.zh: 毫无疑问，布拉瓦茨基（Blavatsky）是19世纪论述古代智慧传统的女性中最引人入胜、最具争议也最具影响力的人物之一。她于1831年8月12日（若按当时俄国仍在通行的旧儒略历，则为7月31日）出生于乌克兰的叶卡捷琳诺斯拉夫（Ekaterinoslav，即第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克〔Dnepropetrovsk〕），出身冯·哈恩（von Hahn）家族。她出自一个兼具俄罗斯、法国胡格诺派与德国血统的名门；父亲彼得·阿列克谢耶维奇·冯·哈恩上校（Col. Peter Alexeyevich von Hahn，1798-1873）是中世纪十字军骑士罗滕施特恩伯爵（Count Rottenstern）的后裔，官至炮兵上尉。母亲海伦娜·安德烈耶夫娜（Helena Andreyevna，娘家姓德·法捷耶夫〔de Fadeyev〕，1814-1842）是一位极富文学才华的女性，曾以“Zeneida R__va”为笔名撰写小说。由于丈夫的职位，全家频频迁徙。1840年代初，母亲在敖德萨去世后的一段间歇期里，年幼的海伦娜被送到萨拉托夫（Saratov）与外祖父母（安德烈·米哈伊洛维奇·德·费杰耶夫〔Andrey Mihailovitch de Fedeyev〕与海伦娜·帕夫洛夫娜·德尔戈鲁科娃〔Helena Pavlovna Delgorukova〕）同住，直至1845年。据这一时期的记载，海伦娜此时已显露出通灵（mediumship）的特质。

body.text: By age eighteen (1849) she married Nikofor Blavatsky (1809-?), a man for whom she obviously had little attachment, given that she left him after only three months. From that time on she embarked on years of wandering, presumably in search of esoteric truths and occult training, traveling to a number of destinations, including Constantinople – where the greatest concentration of Sufi mystics resided – Greece, Egypt, and Eastern Europe. While in Egypt (1849-1850), she met the Copt occultist Paulos Metamon, a so-called magician who many years later (1871) was said to have assisted Blavatsky in the establishment of the “Société Spirite” in Cairo. It has been claimed that Metamon was her occult teacher during these early years of her travels. From Egypt, Blavatsky left for Europe, traveling to Paris and London, where she later claimed to have met her Master for the first time in Hyde Park during the summer of 1850.
body.zh: 十八岁那年（1849），她嫁给了尼基福尔·布拉瓦茨基（Nikofor Blavatsky，1809-？）。显然她对他并无多少感情，因为仅三个月后她便离他而去。自此她开始了多年的漂泊，据推测是为寻求秘传真理与秘术训练，足迹遍及君士坦丁堡（当时苏菲神秘主义者聚居最密之地）、希腊、埃及与东欧。在埃及期间（1849-1850），她结识了科普特秘术师保罗·梅塔蒙（Paulos Metamon）——一位所谓的“魔法师”；据说多年之后（1871），此人曾协助布拉瓦茨基在开罗创立“灵学会”（Société Spirite）。有人称梅塔蒙是她早年游历时期的秘术导师。布拉瓦茨基从埃及前往欧洲，游历巴黎与伦敦；她后来声称，1850年夏天在伦敦海德公园（Hyde Park）首次遇见了她的“大师”（Master）。

body.text: From Paris, Blavatsky left for North America, inspired by the novels of James Fenimore Cooper and his descriptions of the Native Americans and the promise of secrets possessed by the medicine men or shamans. She arrived in Quebec, but was ultimately disappointed with the group of Native Americans with whom she met. After this meeting, she commenced on a new plan, leaving for New Orleans to investigate Voudouism, then on to Texas, Mexico, and – for much of 1852 – to Central and South America. She then decided to go to India, and together with two other companions – one of them a Hindu she had originally met in Honduras and whom she had selected to be her guru or Master – they sailed first to Ceylon (Sri Lanka) and then on to Bombay (Mumbai) sometime during the latter part of 1852. During the same year she attempted to enter Tibet through Nepal but failed in her attempt. She then journeyed to south India, Java, and Singapore and ultimately back to England. Her probable arrival there was in 1853, and she remained until 1854. Sometime in the second part of the year, she set out once again for the United States, landing in New York, journeying across country through Chicago to her final destination in San Francisco – traveling for part of the journey in a covered wagon caravan – where she remained until 1855.
body.zh: 受詹姆斯·费尼莫尔·库珀（James Fenimore Cooper）小说中对美洲原住民的描写以及巫医或萨满据说掌握的秘密所吸引，布拉瓦茨基从巴黎前往北美。她抵达魁北克，但最终对所遇见的那群美洲原住民深感失望。此次会面之后，她另作打算，前往新奥尔良考察伏都教（Voudouism），随后又去往得克萨斯、墨西哥，并在1852年的大部分时间里辗转于中美洲与南美洲。之后她决定前往印度，并与另外两名同伴——其中一位是她在洪都拉斯初次结识的印度教徒，她选定此人为自己的古鲁（guru）或大师——一同先航行至锡兰（斯里兰卡），继而在1852年下半年某时抵达孟买（Bombay，今称 Mumbai）。同年，她试图经尼泊尔进入西藏，但未获成功。随后她游历南印度、爪哇与新加坡，最终返回英格兰。她大概于1853年抵达那里，并一直逗留到1854年。该年下半年某时，她再度启程前往美国，在纽约登岸，横穿全国，经芝加哥抵达最终目的地旧金山——其中一段旅程是随大篷车队同行——并在那里待到1855年。

body.text: Her next destination was India (Calcutta), which she reached via Japan. During her second visit there, from 1855 to 1856, she met with a German acquaintance of her father (an ex-Lutheran minister by the name of Kühlwein) and two other companions, all of whom attempted to enter western Tibet through Kashmir to Ladakh. If we trust the account in A.P. Sinnett’s (1840-1921) Incidents in the Life of Madame Blavatsky, she alone among her traveling companions was taken into Tibetan territory by a Tatar shaman guide, albeit for only a short time.
body.zh: 她的下一站是印度（加尔各答），取道日本抵达。1855至1856年第二次访印期间，她与父亲的一位德国旧识（一位名叫库尔韦因〔Kühlwein〕的前路德宗牧师）及另外两名同伴会合，众人试图经克什米尔前往拉达克，从而进入西藏西部。倘若辛尼特（A.P. Sinnett，1840-1921）《布拉瓦茨基夫人行状录》（Incidents in the Life of Madame Blavatsky）的记述可信，那么同行者中唯有她由一名鞑靼萨满向导带入西藏境内，尽管为时短暂。

body.text: Blavatsky left India in 1857 for Europe (France and Germany) by way of Java, and finally ended up in Russia. The period from 1858 to 1863 she spent primarily with her family; and during a period of about a year she stayed with her husband, General Blavatsky, in Tiflis. We know that sometime around 1859 she became very ill and came close to death. This period in Russia is significant because the mediumistic or psychic powers she was said to have displayed since childhood now became particularly prominent; this, at least, is what we can deduce from the account of her sister, Vera Petrovna de Jelihowsky (or de Zhelihovsky, 1835-1895), who, when questioned on the subject, replied: ‘I remember that when addressed as a medium, she (Mme. Blavatsky) used to laugh and assure us she was no medium, but only a mediator between mortals and beings we knew nothing about’. The types of phenomena that were produced during the time of Blavatsky’s stay in Pskov are classified and described by Madame de Zhelihovsky as follows: ‘1) direct and perfectly clear written and verbal answers to mental questions – or “thought-read-ing”; 2) prescriptions for various diseases, written in Latin, and subsequent cures; 3) private secrets, unknown to all but the interested party, divulged, especially in the case of those persons who mentioned insulting doubts; 4) change of weight in furniture and of persons at will; 5) letters from unknown correspondents, and immediate answers written to queries made and found in the most out-of-the-way mysterious places; 6) appearance and apport of objects unclaimed by any one present; 7) sounds as of musical notes in the air wherever Mme. Blavatsky desired they should resound’ (Sinnett, Incidents, 86). Blavatsky’s exact whereabouts between 1863 and 1867 are not altogether certain, but it is reasonable to assume that she left her family and Russia around 1863 and traveled to Italy, the Balkans, Serbia, Egypt, and Persia (Iran). It was an eventful period because of her association with a revolutionary Italian society, the Carbonari, on the one hand, and a controversy surrounding her relationship to her adolescent ward, Yury, on the other. The child was apparently in her care since 1862, when she resided in Tiflis. Although he was the son of Baron Nicholas Meyendorff and an unknown mother, suspicion was placed on Blavatsky as being the actual mother by the sisterin-law of the Baron, who claimed that the latter had an ongoing affair with Blavatsky since she arrived in Russia in 1858. Yet, a medical examination in 1885 revealed that Blavatsky suffered from Anteflexio Uteri, ‘most probably from the day of her birth’, so it is unlikely that the child was hers.
body.zh: 布拉瓦茨基于1857年离开印度，取道爪哇前往欧洲（法国与德国），最后回到俄国。1858至1863年间，她主要与家人同住；其中约有一年时间，她与丈夫布拉瓦茨基将军（General Blavatsky）住在第比利斯（Tiflis）。我们确知，大约在1859年某时，她曾病重濒死。她在俄国的这段时期之所以重要，是因为据说她自幼便表现出的通灵或灵媒能力此时变得格外突出；至少，从她妹妹薇拉·彼得罗夫娜·德·叶利霍夫斯基（Vera Petrovna de Jelihowsky，又称 de Zhelihovsky，1835-1895）的记述中可以推知这一点。当被问及此事时，她答道：“我记得，每当有人称她（布拉瓦茨基夫人）为灵媒，她总是发笑，并向我们保证她不是灵媒，而只是凡人与我们一无所知的生灵之间的中介。”布拉瓦茨基逗留普斯科夫（Pskov）期间所产生的现象，被热利霍夫斯基夫人分类描述如下：“1）对心中所想的问题给出直接而完全清晰的书面与口头回答——即‘读心术’；2）以拉丁文写成的各种病症处方，以及随后的痊愈；3）泄露除当事人外无人知晓的私密，尤其是在那些表示过侮辱性怀疑的人身上；4）家具与人依其意愿改变重量；5）来自不知名通信者的信件，以及对当场提出、并在最偏僻神秘之处发现的询问所作的即时答复；6）出现并无任何在场者认领的物品，以及此类物品的移现；7）空气中响起乐音般的声响，凡布拉瓦茨基夫人希望其鸣响之处皆然”（Sinnett, Incidents, 86）。布拉瓦茨基1863至1867年间的确切行踪并不完全确定，但可以合理推断，她约于1863年离开家人与俄国，前往意大利、巴尔干、塞尔维亚、埃及与波斯（伊朗）。这段时期事件迭出：一方面是她与意大利革命团体烧炭党（Carbonari）的联系，另一方面则是围绕她与其少年被监护人尤里（Yury）之关系的争议。这孩子显然自1862年她居于第比利斯时起便由她照料。尽管他是尼古拉·梅延多夫男爵（Baron Nicholas Meyendorff）与一位身份不明女子之子，男爵的姻亲却怀疑布拉瓦茨基才是生母，声称男爵自她1858年回到俄国后便一直与她有染。然而，1885年的一次医学检查显示，布拉瓦茨基患有子宫前倾（Anteflexio Uteri），“很可能自出生之日起便是如此”，因此这孩子不太可能是她所生。

body.text: When the boy died in 1867, she arranged, with the assistance of her long-time friend, Agardi Metrovitch, to have him buried in Russia. It was apparently this same Metrovitch who introduced Blavatsky to the cause of the Carbonari, but his identity and his relationship to Blavatsky remain unclear. According to Blavatsky herself, the two had been acquainted since 1850, and she probably knew that this revolutionary half-Italian had ties to the society that included among its membership Giuseppe Garibaldi (1807-1882) and Giuseppe Mazzini (1805-1872), and whose purpose was to break the hold of the Papacy over Italy. Blavatsky actively supported Metrovitch’s cause, even to the extent of participating in the battle of Mentana (November 3, 1867). This battle was lost to the Papists and the French, and Blavatsky received multiple wounds, including being shot in the leg and right shoulder and stabbed near her heart.
body.zh: 1867年男孩去世后，她在多年好友阿加尔迪·梅特罗维奇（Agardi Metrovitch）的协助下，安排将其安葬于俄国。似乎正是这位梅特罗维奇把布拉瓦茨基引向了烧炭党的事业，但他的身份及其与布拉瓦茨基的关系至今仍不清楚。据布拉瓦茨基自己说，两人自1850年起便已相识；她大概知道，这位有一半意大利血统的革命者与该团体有联系，其成员包括朱塞佩·加里波第（Giuseppe Garibaldi，1807-1882）与朱塞佩·马志尼（Giuseppe Mazzini，1805-1872），而该团体的宗旨是打破教廷对意大利的控制。布拉瓦茨基积极支持梅特罗维奇的事业，甚至参与了门塔纳战役（battle of Mentana，1867年11月3日）。此役以教廷派与法国人一方战败告终，布拉瓦茨基身负多处创伤，腿部与右肩中弹，心脏附近亦被刺伤。

body.text: Blavatsky’s travels resumed in early 1868. She left Italy, traveling to India by way of Constantinople; this time she claimed that she was accompanied by her Master. After having reached India later in the year, she claims to have entered Tibet and resided both in Greater and Little Tibet, even staying at the home of the Master Koot Hoomi in Little Tibet and in Shigatse in southern Tibet, the latter close to Tashilhumpo, the residence of the Panchen Lama.
body.zh: 1868年初，布拉瓦茨基重又踏上旅途。她离开意大利，取道君士坦丁堡前往印度；这一次她声称有大师同行。同年晚些时候抵达印度后，她声称曾进入西藏，先后居于大西藏与小西藏，甚至住在小西藏库特·胡米大师（Master Koot Hoomi）的家中，以及藏南日喀则（Shigatse）——后者靠近扎什伦布寺（Tashilhumpo），即班禅喇嘛（Panchen Lama）的驻锡之地。

body.text: The first so-called Mahatma letter, or letter from the Master KH (Koot Hoomi), arrived at the home of Blavatsky’s aunt, Nadyezhda Andreyevna de Fadeyev in 1870. It stated that Helena would be returning shortly to her family. This she did after journeying to Greece and Cyprus at the end of 1870, where she claimed to have met the Master Hilarion (Illarion). From Piraeus (Greece) she boarded the SS Eunomia for Cairo in July 1871. On route, the gunpowder magazine in the cargo hold blew up, causing many deaths. Blavatsky was rescued and brought to Alexandria, arriving in Cairo toward the end of the year. Here she made the acquaintance of Emma Cutting, who is known to Theosophists by her married name, Mme. Alexis Coulomb, and who would cause untold grief to Blavatsky thirteen years later.
body.zh: 1870年，第一封所谓的“圣雄书信”（Mahatma letter），即来自库特·胡米大师（Master KH）的信，寄到了布拉瓦茨基姑母娜杰日达·安德烈耶夫娜·德·法捷耶夫（Nadyezhda Andreyevna de Fadeyev）家中。信中称海伦娜不久将返家。她果然在1870年底游历希腊与塞浦路斯之后归来；她声称在那里遇见了希拉里昂大师（Master Hilarion，Illarion）。1871年7月，她从希腊比雷埃夫斯（Piraeus）乘“欧诺米亚号”（SS Eunomia）前往开罗。途中，货舱内的火药库爆炸，造成多人死亡。布拉瓦茨基获救并被送往亚历山大港（Alexandria），于该年年底抵达开罗。她在那里结识了埃玛·卡廷（Emma Cutting），神智学者以她的夫姓称她为亚历克西·库隆夫人（Mme. Alexis Coulomb）；十三年后，正是此人给布拉瓦茨基带来了无尽的痛苦。

body.text: While in Cairo, Blavatsky founded the “Société Spirite”, a society that seems to have had a double agenda: a public and a private one. The first involved the public investigation of passive reception by mediums of spirit communications – a reflection of the →spiritualism that was practiced in the United States since 1848. There appears to have been another agenda, however, that was known only to certain individuals in the society
body.zh: 在开罗期间，布拉瓦茨基创立了“灵学会”（Société Spirite）。该会似乎有双重议程：一为公开，一为秘密。公开的一面涉及对灵媒被动接收亡灵讯息这一现象的公开调查——这反映了自1848年以来在美国盛行的→唯灵论（spiritualism）。然而，该会似乎还有另一重议程，仅为会中某些人士所知

body.text: (including Blavatsky and Metamon, the same Copt magician whom Blavatsky met in 1850). It involved conducting undisclosed occult practices that may very well have been similar to those practiced in the early →Theosophical Society. As far as Blavatsky was concerned, the importance of the “Société Spirite” lay in its private aspect. Within a few months, perhaps weeks, the formal society all but disappeared.
body.zh: （包括布拉瓦茨基与梅塔蒙，即她1850年结识的那位科普特魔法师）。这一议程涉及进行不公开的秘术实践，其实践方式很可能与早期→神智学会中所行者相似。就布拉瓦茨基而言，“灵学会”的重要性正在于其秘密的一面。不出数月——或许不出数周——这个正式团体便几乎销声匿迹了。

body.text: By April 1872, Blavatsky again left Egypt, traveling to Odessa to reunite with her family, but making a number of stops on the way. In March or April 1873 she traveled to Paris via Bucharest before finally taking a passenger liner to the United States, where she arrived on July 7, 1873. This journey marks the conclusion to her earlier life of travel and the beginning of the next major period of her life.
body.zh: 到1872年4月，布拉瓦茨基再度离开埃及，前往敖德萨与家人团聚，途中多次停留。1873年3月或4月，她经布加勒斯特前往巴黎，随后终于搭乘一艘客轮前往美国，于1873年7月7日抵达。这段旅程标志着其早年漂泊生活的结束，也标志着她生命中下一个重要时期的开始。

body.text: What are we to make of this extended period of travel by a girl who began her journeys as a recently married teenager and who later claimed to have resided in many of the most inaccessible places on earth, sometimes disguising herself as a man, once involved in a battle, meeting with practitioners of magic and the occult arts, and spending the better part of twenty years as a veritable gypsy? In psychological terms one might speak of travel compulsiveness, but if we take Blavatsky’s own words seriously, this compulsion had a purpose. Most of what we know about this period originates from her own reminiscences, from the accounts of acquaintances who affirm having met her during the course of her travels, and from family members who left their own written recollections of her activities. Even if we assume an attitude of healthy skepticism regarding the question of whether all these accounts are to be trusted, it remains that much of it appears to have a basis in fact. Some of Blavatsky’s adventures have been embellished by her, but it seems certain that she met many unusual people and acquired a vast store of esoteric and occult knowledge. Already as a child of fifteen, she claims to have been exposed to an occult library, consisting of several hundred volumes, belonging to her maternal great-grandfather, Prince Paul Vassilyevich Dolgorukov (1755-1837). In all likelihood, this was her first exposure to →alchemy, → magic, and kabbalah [→Jewish Influences]. Combine this with the psychic abilities that her family claimed she exhibited, and we have the basic conditions for a theoretical as well as practical occultist. Blavatsky’s interests appear to have driven her to seek more knowledge of esotericism and occultism, not just from written sources but also from living teachers. Who these teachers were, and how they were related to the Theosophical “Masters” who were to play a highly important role in her life, remains a mystery to this day.
body.zh: 一个刚结婚不久的少女便踏上旅程，后来声称曾居住于地球上许多最难抵达之地，有时女扮男装，曾投身战阵，与魔法及秘术的实践者往来，并作为名副其实的流浪者度过近二十年光阴——对于这样一段漫长的旅行岁月，我们该如何理解？从心理学角度，人们或许会称之为旅行强迫症；但若认真对待布拉瓦茨基自己的说法，这种强迫是有其目的的。我们对这一时期所知的大部分，源自她本人的回忆，源自那些确认曾在旅途中与她相遇的熟人的记述，也源自留下关于她活动之书面回忆的家人。即便我们对这些记述是否全都可信持一种健康的怀疑态度，其中许多仍显然有事实依据。布拉瓦茨基的一些冒险经历确经她渲染，但可以确定的是，她结识了许多不寻常的人物，并积累了大量的秘传与秘术知识。她声称，早在十五岁时，她便接触到一座秘传藏书室，其中藏有数百卷书，属于她的外曾祖父保罗·瓦西里耶维奇·多尔戈鲁科夫公爵（Prince Paul Vassilyevich Dolgorukov，1755-1837）。这极可能是她首次接触→炼金术、→魔法与卡巴拉〔→犹太影响〕。将这一点与她家人所称她表现出的灵媒能力结合起来，便具备了造就一位理论兼实践秘术师的基本条件。布拉瓦茨基的兴趣似乎驱使她去寻求更多关于秘传主义与秘术主义的知识，不仅从文字资料中，也从活生生的导师那里。这些导师究竟是谁，他们与后来在她生命中扮演极重要角色的神智学“大师”们有何关系，至今仍是一个谜。

body.text: Why Madame Blavatsky came to the United States is open to speculation, but in keeping with her propensity for the mysterious, she claimed that she had been sent by her Lodge either to reveal the truth about modern spiritualism or to form a secret society. The events leading up to the foundation of what would become known as the Theosophical Society begin in 1874, with her introduction to Col. →Henry Steel Olcott (1832-1907). According to Olcott’s account in his Old Diary Leaves (I, 1f.), their meeting took place in Chittenden, Vermont on October 14, 1874, during his investigation of the spirit or phantom phenomena allegedly occurring at the farmhouse of William and Horatio Eddy. Thus began a lifelong collaboration, sometimes rancorous and turbulent but always productive. Their initial interest involved the investigation of spiritualist phenomena, including the phantom forms at the Eddy brothers’ home in Chittenden, and the reappearance (having first appeared as the spirit guide to Florence Cook in England) of the spirit “Katie King” in Philadelphia through the mediums Mr. and Mrs. Nelson Holmes. There is no doubt that Blavatsky defended →spiritualism in her early correspondence to the New York Daily Graphic and spiritualist papers. One example illustrating her high opinion of spiritualism and her belief that the United States was the cradle of that phenomenon appears in the Spiritual Scientist, in which she remarks that she ‘came over here [the U.S.] from France with feelings not unlike those of a Mohammedan approaching the birth-place of his prophet’. Comparing these remarks in support of spiritualism, made in December 1874, to those made in February 1875, one can observe a marked change in attitude. In her correspondence of that month with Hiram Corson (1828-1911), a professor at Cornell University, she writes that for her, spiritualism is based not on the modern American variety that began in 1848 but on a much older one, originating ‘from the same source of information that was used by Raymond Lully, Picus della Mirandola, Cornelius Agrippa, Robert Fludd, Henry More, etc. etc. etc.’. Thus she expressed for the first time her concept of an “ancient Spiritualism” or “occultism” [→occult / occultism] that was later to become the foundation of her theosophy. To Blavatsky, American spiritualism was devoid of ancient wisdom, whereas “ancient Spiritualism” or occultism comprised ‘a system that should disclose . . . the “deepest depths” of the Divine Nature, and show . . . the real tie which binds all things together’. In other words, what we see here is a shift from a form of spiritualism based merely upon investigation of “phenomena” but devoid of doctrinal content, towards one that claims to be rooted in the ancient wisdom of the Western esoteric tradition. Henceforth Blavatsky would continue to emphasize this tradition, while increasingly including Eastern (primarily South Asian) occult teachings as well. By July 1875 the first public statement of her views appears in a response to an article by HIRAF (an acronym for five authors) entitled “Rosicrucianism”, which had appeared in the July 1 and 8 issues of the Spiritual Scientist. Blavatsky’s response, entitled “A Few Questions to ‘HIRAF’”, appeared in the following two issues (July 15 and 22). For the first time, she presents a rather detailed exposition of her views on occultism and magic – presented by her as the practical and theoretical sides of the Ancient Wisdom. Because it is a response to →Rosicrucianism as interpreted by HIRAF, one important idea evident from this article is her acknowledgement of the existence of a number of “Brotherhoods” devoted to the “Wisdom or Occult tradition”, going back as far as the Egyptian →Ophites and persisting through the “Fire-Philosophers” or Paracelsists and European alchemists.
body.zh: 布拉瓦茨基夫人为何来到美国，众说纷纭；但以她喜好神秘的一贯作风，她声称自己是被其“会所”（Lodge）派来的，目的或是揭示现代唯灵论的真相，或是组建一个秘密社团。导致后来所谓神智学会之创立的一系列事件，始于1874年她与→亨利·斯蒂尔·奥尔科特上校（Col. Henry Steel Olcott，1832-1907）的相识。据奥尔科特《旧日记页》（Old Diary Leaves，第1卷，第1页及以下）所述，两人于1874年10月14日在佛蒙特州奇滕登（Chittenden）相遇，当时他正在调查据称发生在威廉·埃迪与霍雷肖·埃迪（William and Horatio Eddy）农舍的幽灵或幻影现象。由此开始了一段终生的合作——时而怨怼、动荡，却始终富有成果。他们最初的兴趣在于调查唯灵论现象，包括埃迪兄弟在奇滕登家中的幻影形态，以及幽灵“凯蒂·金”（Katie King）在费城通过灵媒纳尔逊·霍姆斯夫妇（Mr. and Mrs. Nelson Holmes）再度显现（她最初曾作为幽灵向导出现在英格兰的弗洛伦斯·库克〔Florence Cook〕面前）。毫无疑问，布拉瓦茨基在早期致《纽约每日写真报》（New York Daily Graphic）及唯灵论报刊的通信中为→唯灵论辩护。有一例可说明她对唯灵论的高度评价以及她认为美国是这一现象之摇篮的信念，见于《唯灵论科学家》（Spiritual Scientist）：她在其中写道，她“从法国来到这里〔美国〕时，心情与一个即将走近其先知诞生之地的穆斯林并无二致”。将1874年12月这些支持唯灵论的言论与1875年2月的言论相比较，便可见其态度发生了显著变化。在当月致康奈尔大学教授海勒姆·科森（Hiram Corson，1828-1911）的通信中，她写道，对她而言，唯灵论并非建立在始于1848年的现代美国变体之上，而是建立在一种古老得多的唯灵论之上，其源头“与雷蒙德·卢利（Raymond Lully）、皮科·德拉·米兰多拉（Picus della Mirandola）、科尼利厄斯·阿格里帕（Cornelius Agrippa）、罗伯特·弗卢德（Robert Fludd）、亨利·莫尔（Henry More）等人所用者同出一源”。她由此首次表达了她那“古代唯灵论”或“秘术主义”（occultism）〔→秘术／秘术主义〕的观念，这一观念后来成为其神智学的基础。在布拉瓦茨基看来，美国的唯灵论缺乏古代智慧，而“古代唯灵论”或秘术主义则包含“一套应当揭示……神性本质之‘最深幽处’，并显示……将万物联结为一体的真正纽带的体系”。换言之，我们在此看到一种转变：从仅仅基于对“现象”之调查、却缺乏教义内容的唯灵论形式，转向一种自称植根于西方秘传传统之古代智慧的唯灵论。此后，布拉瓦茨基继续强调这一传统，同时日益纳入东方（主要是南亚）的秘术教义。到1875年7月，她首次公开陈述自己的观点，是对HIRAF（五位作者合用的缩略名）一篇题为《玫瑰十字会主义》（“Rosicrucianism”）的文章的回应；该文发表于《唯灵论科学家》7月1日与8日两期。布拉瓦茨基的回应题为《向“HIRAF”提出的几个问题》（“A Few Questions to ‘HIRAF’”），刊于随后两期（7月15日与22日）。她首次相当详尽地阐述了自己关于秘术主义与魔法的观点——在她看来，这两者是古代智慧的理论与实践两面。由于此文是对HIRAF所解释的→玫瑰十字会主义的回应，文中体现出的一个重要观念，是她承认存在若干“兄弟会”（Brotherhoods），专事“智慧或秘术传统”，其源可上溯至埃及的→俄斐特派（Ophites），并经由“火哲学家”（Fire-Philosophers）即帕拉塞尔苏斯派与欧洲炼金术士而延续不绝。

body.text: Staying at 46 Irving Place in New York during much of 1875, Blavatsky attracted to her apartment a number of interested individuals curious to hear her views on occultism. From the early months of 1875, she was also involved in the writing of her first major work, Isis Unveiled. In addition to this creative activity, she experienced a rather tumultuous period involving domestic problems (her marriage with and divorce from a Russian citizen, Michael Betanelly, within the space of a few months) and a serious leg injury caused by a fall.
body.zh: 1875年的大部分时间，布拉瓦茨基住在纽约欧文坊46号（46 Irving Place）；她的寓所吸引了一批有兴趣的人士前来，渴望听她谈论秘术主义。自1875年初起，她还投身于第一部重要著作《揭开伊西斯的面纱》（Isis Unveiled）的写作。除这一创作活动外，她还经历了一段颇为动荡的时期，既有家庭纠纷（她与俄国公民迈克尔·贝塔内利〔Michael Betanelly〕结婚又离婚，前后不过数月），也有一次跌倒造成的腿部重伤。

body.text: The meetings at her apartment led to the formation of the Theosophical Society later in 1875. On September 7, a lecture was given here by George Henry Felt (1831-1906) entitled “The Lost Canon of Proportion of the Egyptians”. According to Felt’s own account, he successfully proved the existence of ‘elementals or intermediates, or elementary or original spirits’ existing on various levels from ‘inanimate nature through the animal kingdom to man’; furthermore, Felt affirmed that these beings were represented in the Egyptian zodiacs (i.e. the forms appearing there were not figments of the imagination but real creatures), and that they could be evoked by chemical means. This lecture incited Col. Olcott to suggest, in a note passed to Blavatsky during the meeting, whether it would ‘not be a good thing to form a Society for this kind of study?’ Blavatsky agreed to the proposal, and the other members of the audience concurred, thus initiating the process of formally establishing a society which would soon come to be known as the Theosophical Society, which was to be organized on October 30 and ‘constitutionally perfected’ on November 17, 1875.
body.zh: 她寓所中的聚会促成了1875年晚些时候神智学会的成立。9月7日，乔治·亨利·费尔特（George Henry Felt，1831-1906）在此作了一场题为《埃及人失传的比例法则》（“The Lost Canon of Proportion of the Egyptians”）的演讲。据费尔特自述，他成功证明了“精灵或中介物，即元素精灵或原初精灵”的存在，这些存在居于从“无生命自然界经动物界直至人”的各个层级；此外，费尔特断言，这些存在在埃及黄道十二宫图中有所表现（即图中出现的形态并非想象之物，而是真实的造物），并且可以通过化学手段将其召唤出来。这场演讲促使奥尔科特上校在会间递给布拉瓦茨基的一张字条中提议：是否“成立一个学会来从事这类研究，岂非好事？”布拉瓦茨基同意此议，在场其他成员亦表赞同，于是正式建立学会的进程由此启动；该会不久便以神智学会之名行世，于10月30日着手组织，并于1875年11月17日“在章程上臻于完备”。

body.text: The second significant event that occurred during the New York years (1873-1878) was the publication of Isis Unveiled on September 29, 1877. A monumental work in scope, the text extended over 1268 pages in two volumes: the first volume called “The ‘Infallibility’ of Modern Science” and the second called “Theology”. Originally entitled The Veil of Isis (which remains on the heading of each page), it had to be renamed once it was discovered that this title had already been used for an 1861 Rosicrucian work by W.W. Reade. Many years later, within a month of her death, Blavatsky revealed that the text was not written primarily for the general public but rather for the members of the Theosophical Society; and she added that much of the work was edited by Col. Olcott and Alexander Wilder (1823-1908) – an old acquaintance of Olcott’s, and a member and later Vice-president of the Theosophical Society. Blavatsky writes in the Preface that Isis Unveiled ‘is a plea for the recognition of the Hermetic philosophy, the anciently universal Wisdom Religion, as the only possible key to the Absolute in science and theology’. This Wisdom Religion is identified with magic, considered in ancient times ‘a divine science which led to a participation in the attributes of Divinity itself’. Volume one is devoted to the hidden and unknown forces of nature, discussing subjects such as phenomena and forces (Chapter 2), elementals and elementaries (Chapter 7), cyclic phenomena (Chapter 9), psychic and physical marvels (Chapter 11), and the Inner and Outer Man (Chapter 10), all accompanied by a vast array of supportive and incidental knowledge – ancient and modern, Western and Eastern, esoteric and exoteric. Volume two discusses similarities of Christian scripture, doctrine, history, and personalities with non-Christian systems such as Buddhism, Hinduism, the Vedas, and Zoroastrianism, all based on the notion that they share a common origin referred to as the ‘primitive “wisdom-religion”’.
body.zh: 纽约岁月（1873-1878）间发生的第二件大事，是《揭开伊西斯的面纱》于1877年9月29日出版。这部著作规模宏大，两卷合计1268页：第一卷题为《现代科学的“无误性”》（“The ‘Infallibility’ of Modern Science”），第二卷题为《神学》（“Theology”）。该书原题《伊西斯的面纱》（The Veil of Isis，此名仍保留于各页页眉），后因发现W.W. 里德（W.W. Reade）1861年的一部玫瑰十字会著作已用过此题，只得改名。多年之后，即在去世前一个月内，布拉瓦茨基透露，此书主要并非为一般公众而写，而是为神智学会会员而写；她还补充说，书中很大一部分经奥尔科特上校与亚历山大·怀尔德（Alexander Wilder，1823-1908）编订——后者是奥尔科特的旧识，也是神智学会会员，后来担任副会长。布拉瓦茨基在序言中写道，《揭开伊西斯的面纱》“是为求承认赫尔墨斯哲学——即古来普世的智慧宗教——为科学与神学中绝对者之唯一可能钥匙的辩护”。这一智慧宗教被等同于魔法；在古代，魔法被视为“一门神圣的科学，可使人参与神性本身的诸属性”。第一卷专论自然界隐秘而未知的力量，讨论现象与力（第2章）、元素精灵与元素魂（第7章）、周期性现象（第9章）、灵性与物质奇观（第11章）以及内在之人与外在之人（第10章）等题目，并附以大量佐证性与旁涉性的知识——古今兼收，东西并蓄，秘传与外传俱备。第二卷讨论基督教经典、教义、历史与人物同非基督教体系（如佛教、印度教、吠陀与琐罗亚斯德教）之间的相似之处，其立论基础是它们共有同一个起源，即所谓“原初‘智慧宗教’”。

body.text: Sometime during the writing of Isis Unveiled the idea came up (probably first in Olcott’s mind) of a move to India, and eventually this plan was confirmed when the Masters’ “Orders to make ready” to leave New York were recorded in his diary on May 24. Shortly thereafter (July 8, 1878) Blavatsky became a naturalized U.S. citizen.
body.zh: 在撰写《揭开伊西斯的面纱》期间的某个时候，迁居印度的想法出现了（最初大概出自奥尔科特）；最终，当大师们“准备启程”离开纽约的“命令”于5月24日被记入他的日记时，这一计划得到确认。此后不久（1878年7月8日），布拉瓦茨基加入美国国籍。

body.text: Toward the end of the year, Blavatsky and Olcott departed from New York harbor to England, arriving from there in Bombay on February 16, 1879. Blavatsky was never to return to the U.S. again.
body.zh: 是年年底，布拉瓦茨基与奥尔科特从纽约港启程前往英格兰，再由那里出发，于1879年2月16日抵达孟买。布拉瓦茨基此后再未重返美国。

body.text: After their arrival in Bombay, accompanied by considerable publicity in the Indian newspapers, Olcott and Blavatsky settled in a home on Girgaum Back Road. One of the newspapers, The Pioneer (Allahabad), gave especially favorable accounts of the Theosophists because its editor, Alfred Percy Sinnett (1840-1921), had had an interest in the Theosophical Society and its founders as a result of his involvement with spiritualism. Sinnett’s interest in Theosophy eventually led to his and Mrs. Sinnett’s meeting the Theosophists for the first time in December 1879, thus resulting in Blavatsky’s short-time involvement with The Pioneer. She contributed a number of letters, unsigned articles on Russian subjects, and an eleven-part translation of “The Travels of Colonel Grodekoff”.
body.zh: 抵达孟买后，在印度报章的大量报道中，奥尔科特与布拉瓦茨基在吉尔冈后路（Girgaum Back Road）的一处住宅安顿下来。其中一家报纸——阿拉哈巴德（Allahabad）的《先驱报》（The Pioneer）——对神智学者尤为称许，因为其主编阿尔弗雷德·珀西·辛尼特（Alfred Percy Sinnett，1840-1921）因参与唯灵论活动，早已对神智学会及其创始人心存兴趣。辛尼特对神智学的兴趣，最终促使其夫妇于1879年12月首次与这些神智学者会面，布拉瓦茨基也因此一度与《先驱报》有所往来。她为该报撰写了若干书信、关于俄国题材的未署名文章，以及《格罗杰科夫上校游记》（“The Travels of Colonel Grodekoff”）的十一部分译文。

body.text: In October 1879, Olcott and Blavatsky initiated a monthly magazine designed as the main organ for the Society, The Theosophist, with an initial circulation of 400 copies. Prior to this event, however, far more ambitious plans were being developed. Olcott records in this diary entry of May 23, 1879, that Blavatsky began work on ‘her new book on Theosophy’, an undertaking that was to culminate in the publication of her greatest work, The Secret Doctrine.
body.zh: 1879年10月，奥尔科特与布拉瓦茨基创办了一份月刊《神智学者》（The Theosophist），作为学会的主要机关刊物，初期印数400份。然而在此事之前，更为宏大的计划已在酝酿之中。奥尔科特在1879年5月23日的日记中记载，布拉瓦茨基已开始撰写“她那部关于神智学的新书”，此项工程最终将结出她最伟大的著作《秘密教义》（The Secret Doctrine）。

body.text: In 1880, two significant events occurred. The first was Blavatsky’s and Olcott’s first tour of Ceylon (Sri Lanka), which resulted in both of them formally accepting the Five Precepts (pansil; Pali: pañcasìla) and presumably the Triple Gem as well. Thus they formally became Buddhists; although in Blavatsky’s case one should perhaps say that she reaffirmed her Buddhism, since she already identified herself as a Buddhist during her New York residency in the 1870s. The outcome of this visit was the establishment of branches of the Theosophical Society in Ceylon and the initiation of a Buddhist revival that, through the sustained efforts of Col. Olcott, would continue to develop throughout the 1880s and 1890s.
body.zh: 1880年发生了两件大事。第一件是布拉瓦茨基与奥尔科特首次巡游锡兰（斯里兰卡），两人由此正式受持五戒（pansil；巴利文：pañcasīla），想必也皈依了三宝。他们于是正式成为佛教徒；不过就布拉瓦茨基而言，或许应当说她是在重申自己的佛教信仰，因为早在1870年代旅居纽约期间，她便已自认是佛教徒。此次访问的成果，是在锡兰建立了神智学会的分会，并开启了一场佛教复兴运动；经由奥尔科特上校的持续努力，这场复兴在1880年代与1890年代不断发展。

body.text: In October 1880, a significant event took place: the receipt of the first of a long succession of letters from the Masters K.H. (Koot Hoomi) and M. (Morya) to Sinnett and others. K.H., M. and other Masters, believed to belong to an “Occult Brotherhood” in the East, were assumed to have given their philosophical and ethical teachings to the world through the medium of the Theosophical Society; they were also believed to have been the teachers of Blavatsky, who had first become their pupil (chela) and who had received training and instruction during her visit to Tibet. From the first letter received by Sinnett on October 15, 1880 to the final letter of the series in 1886, 145 were written. The esoteric teachings contained in these letters were summarized by Sinnett in his book Esoteric Buddhism (1883).
body.zh: 1880年10月，一件大事发生：库特·胡米大师（K.H.）与莫里亚大师（M.）致辛尼特等人的书信开始陆续抵达，此为长长系列中的第一批。K.H.、M. 及其他大师据信属于东方的一个“秘术兄弟会”，人们认为他们通过神智学会这一中介，将其哲学与伦理教诲传给世界；人们还认为他们是布拉瓦茨基的老师，她先是成为他们的弟子（chela），并在访藏期间接受了训练与指导。从1880年10月15日辛尼特收到的第一封信，到1886年该系列的最后一封，共有145封。这些书信所包含的秘传教义，由辛尼特在其《秘传佛教》（Esoteric Buddhism，1883）一书中作了概述。

body.text: The year 1884 was eventful for the Founders and for the Theosophical Society. Early in February Olcott and Blavatsky visited Europe – Blavatsky for medical reasons, Olcott on Society business and as an advocate for the Buddhist cause in Ceylon. While in England, Olcott had to intervene in a struggle that was causing considerable distress within the British Theosophical Society. The latter, formed in 1878, consisted in the early 1880s of a small, intellectual group of individuals whose president, George Wyld (1821-1906), attempted to establish an independent Society more in step with the teachings of Christianity and less with the “atheism” of Blavatsky and her anti-Christian views. Having failed, he resigned in 1882. A similar crisis within the Society developed over the next two years involving Mrs. →Anna Bonus Kingsford (1846-1888) and her close associate, Edward Maitland (1824-1897), resulting in the formation of the Hermetic Society [→Hermeticism and Hermetic Societies]. Early in May, Olcott, Blavatsky and other members of the Theosophical Society assented to a series of meetings with a committee formed by the Society for Psychical Research (established in 1882) on the subject of psychic phenomena, including ‘the phenomenal receipt of written documents’ and ‘the precipitation of Mahatmic writing within closed letters from ordinary correspondents while in transit through the mails’. Blavatsky was questioned in Cambridge in August 9th, and the S.P.R. committee was favorably impressed with her responses. Its ‘preliminary and provisional’ report came out in December 1884.
body.zh: 1884年对两位创始人及神智学会而言是多事之秋。2月初，奥尔科特与布拉瓦茨基访问欧洲——布拉瓦茨基为就医，奥尔科特则为学会事务，并作为锡兰佛教事业的代言人。在英格兰期间，奥尔科特不得不介入一场争斗，这场争斗在英国神智学会内部引起了相当大的困扰。英国神智学会成立于1878年，1880年代初由一小群知识分子组成，其主席乔治·怀尔德（George Wyld，1821-1906）试图建立一个独立学会，使其更契合基督教教义，而较少沾染布拉瓦茨基的“无神论”及其反基督教观点。此举失败后，他于1882年辞职。此后两年间，学会内部又因→安娜·博纳斯·金斯福德夫人（Mrs. Anna Bonus Kingsford，1846-1888）及其密友爱德华·梅特兰（Edward Maitland，1824-1897）而爆发类似危机，结果促成了赫尔墨斯学会的成立〔→赫尔墨斯主义与赫尔墨斯学会〕。5月初，奥尔科特、布拉瓦茨基及神智学会其他成员同意与心灵研究学会（Society for Psychical Research，成立于1882年）所设的一个委员会举行一系列会晤，讨论灵异现象，包括“以超常方式收受书面文件”以及“圣雄笔迹在普通通信者的密封信件于邮递途中时降现其中”。布拉瓦茨基于8月9日在剑桥接受询问，该委员会对她的回答颇有好感。其“初步且暂定”的报告于1884年12月发表。

body.text: In the month following the interview, an explosive event in India lent support to the negative conclusions of a second S.P.R. Report, issued in 1885. These developments were to leave a permanent stain upon the reputations of the Theosophical Society and Blavatsky. Under the title ‘The Collapse of Koot Hoomi’, The Madras Christian College Magazine of September 1884 published the first part of an exposé containing fifteen letters purportedly written by Blavatsky to Emma Coulomb. The letters were intended to be proof of Mme. Coulomb’s charge that Blavatsky had committed fraud. Blavatsky vehemently objected to the allegations, but did not bring charges against Mrs. Coulomb and her husband, Alexis, and the magazine.
body.zh: 会晤之后的那个月，印度发生的一件爆炸性事件，为1885年发表的第二份心灵研究学会报告的负面结论提供了支持。这些事态发展给神智学会与布拉瓦茨基的名誉留下了永久的污点。1884年9月的《马德拉斯基督教学院杂志》（The Madras Christian College Magazine）以《库特·胡米的垮台》（“The Collapse of Koot Hoomi”）为题，刊出了揭发材料的第一部分，内含十五封据称出自布拉瓦茨基之手、写给埃玛·库隆的信。这些信件意在证明库隆夫人关于布拉瓦茨基行骗的指控。布拉瓦茨基激烈反驳这些指控，却未对库隆夫妇及该杂志提出控告。

body.text: This was because Olcott had convinced her to leave the decision to a special Committee comprising, among others, a number of prominent Indian legal experts and government officials. The Committee suggested not prosecuting the defamers due to the inherent legal dangers to plaintiffs in libel cases. This position was also supported by the delegates at the 1884 Annual Convention of the Theosophical Society, held in December.
body.zh: 这是因为奥尔科特说服她将决定权交给一个特别委员会，其成员包括若干印度知名法律专家与政府官员。委员会建议不起诉那些诽谤者，因为诽谤案原告本身在法律上固有风险。这一立场也得到1884年12月神智学会年度大会上代表们的支持。

body.text: Meanwhile, the S.P.R., which had concluded in its first report that there was some evidence that could not be discounted, decided to continue its investigation by sending an observer, Richard Hodgson (1855-1905), to India in November 1884. He remained there for three months, investigating the charges by the Coulombs; his goal was to determine ‘the competency of the witnesses to phenomena, and to ascertain, if possible, the trustworthiness in particular of three primary witnesses, viz., Mr. Damodar K. Mavalankar, Mr. Babajee D. Nath, and Colonel Olcott’. Hodgson’s conclusions, issued in December 1885, could not have been more damaging and devastating to Blavatsky and the Society. They included the following: (a) the letters to the Coulombs were written by Blavatsky, (b) the Coulombs were Blavatsky’s accomplices in the production of fraudulent phenomena, (c) the primary witnesses to the existence of an Occult Brotherhood, including Blavatsky, had made false statements, (d) the Masters Koot Hoomi and Morya must be fictitious, since their handwriting resembled M. Damodar’s and Blavatsky’s, (e) no instance of phenomena was witnessed by Hodgson, (f) the objects of the Theosophical Society were political and Blavatsky was a Russian spy. Hodgson concluded with this statement: ‘But acting in accordance with the principles upon which our Society [the S.P.R.] has proceeded, I must express my unqualified opinion that no genuine psychical phenomena whatever will be found among the pseudo-mysteries of the Russian lady alias Koot Hoomi Lal Sing alias Mahatma Morya alias Madame Blavatsky’. The S.P.R. Committee concluded: ‘For our own part, we regard her neither as the mouthpiece of hidden seers, nor as a mere vulgar adventuress; we think that she has achieved a title to permanent remembrance as one of the most accomplished, ingenious, and interesting impostors in history’.
body.zh: 与此同时，心灵研究学会在其第一份报告中已断定存在某些不可轻忽的证据，此时决定继续调查，于1884年11月派观察员理查德·霍奇森（Richard Hodgson，1855-1905）前往印度。他在那里逗留三个月，调查库隆夫妇的指控；其目标是判定“证人对现象之适格性，并在可能的情况下查明三位主要证人的可信度，即达莫达尔·K. 马瓦兰卡尔先生（Mr. Damodar K. Mavalankar）、巴巴吉·D. 纳特先生（Mr. Babajee D. Nath）与奥尔科特上校”。霍奇森于1885年12月发表的结论，对布拉瓦茨基与学会的打击再没有比这更严厉、更具毁灭性的了。其结论包括：（a）写给库隆夫妇的信出自布拉瓦茨基之手；（b）库隆夫妇是布拉瓦茨基制造假现象的共犯；（c）关于秘术兄弟会存在的主要证人，包括布拉瓦茨基在内，均作了虚假陈述；（d）库特·胡米与莫里亚两位大师必属虚构，因为其笔迹与达莫达尔先生及布拉瓦茨基的笔迹相似；（e）霍奇森未曾亲见任何一例现象；（f）神智学会的目标具有政治性质，而布拉瓦茨基是俄国间谍。霍奇森以下述论断作结：“但依照本会〔心灵研究学会〕所遵循的原则行事，我必须表示我毫无保留的意见：在这位俄国女士——又名库特·胡米·拉尔·辛格（Koot Hoomi Lal Sing），又名圣雄莫里亚，又名布拉瓦茨基夫人——的伪神秘事物之中，绝不会发现任何真正的灵异现象。”心灵研究学会委员会总结道：“就我们而言，我们既不视她为隐秘先见者的代言人，也不视她为单纯的庸俗女冒险家；我们认为，她已赢得在历史上永被铭记的资格，作为有史以来最娴熟、最机巧、也最有趣的骗子之一。”

body.text: Blavatsky returned to India at the end of 1884, but within a month she became gravely ill, causing her to resign from the office of Corresponding Secretary of the Society on March 21. Shortly thereafter, she left India for the last time, traveling to Europe. After a sojourn of three months in Italy, she decided to settle in Würzburg (Bavaria), in August 1885. By the end of the year, she was immersed in the writing of her magnum opus, The Secret Doctrine, aided by the recent arrival in Würzburg of Countess Constance Wachtmeister (1838-1910).
body.zh: 布拉瓦茨基于1884年底返回印度，但不出一个月便病重，遂于3月21日辞去学会通讯书记（Corresponding Secretary）一职。此后不久，她最后一次离开印度，前往欧洲。在意大利逗留三个月后，她于1885年8月决定定居巴伐利亚的维尔茨堡（Würzburg）。到该年年底，她已埋头撰写其代表作《秘密教义》；康斯坦斯·瓦赫特迈斯特伯爵夫人（Countess Constance Wachtmeister，1838-1910）新近抵达维尔茨堡，从旁协助。

body.text: For the next two years, The Secret Doctrine was to be Blavatsky’s major project. From Würzburg she moved to Ostend (Belgium) in July before being persuaded by some English Theosophists to settle in London. This she did in May 1887, residing first at the home (“Maycot”) of Mabel Collins (1851- 1927), the author of Light on the Path. Within a few days (on May 19), the Blavatsky Lodge was established, and within a few months (September), the magazine Lucifer was founded to provide ‘some sort of public propaganda’ before the publication of The Secret Doctrine, which took place a year later. If the contents of the magazine did not excite the general public, the title certainly did.
body.zh: 此后两年，《秘密教义》成为布拉瓦茨基的主要工程。她于7月从维尔茨堡迁往比利时的奥斯坦德（Ostend），随后被几位英国神智学者说服，定居伦敦。她于1887年5月迁往伦敦，起初住在《道路之光》（Light on the Path）的作者梅布尔·柯林斯（Mabel Collins，1851-1927）的宅邸（“梅科特”〔Maycot〕）。数日之内（5月19日），布拉瓦茨基会所（Blavatsky Lodge）成立；数月之内（9月），《路西法》（Lucifer）杂志创刊，以便在《秘密教义》出版之前进行“某种形式的公开宣传”；该书于一年后问世。如果说杂志的内容未能激起一般公众的兴趣，那么其刊名则无疑做到了这一点。

body.text: In September of 1887, Blavatsky and the Blavatsky Lodge moved to 17 Lansdowne Road, the focal point of Blavatsky’s activities for the next two-and-one-half years before she relocated to 19 Avenue Road, St. John’s Wood, London in 1890, which became the new headquarters of the Blavatsky Lodge as well as of the British Section and of European headquarters. The headquarters incidentally was the home of →Annie Besant (1847-1933), a recently recruited member (May 1889) and rising star of the Theosophical Society. Thirteen months after the establishment of the Lansdowne Road residence as headquarters of the Blavatsky Lodge (October 9, 1888), a second significant event occurred: the establishment of a new organization that was closely affiliated with the Theosophical Society. This organization, the “Esoteric Section of the Theosophical Society” (E.S.), had as its goal the promotion of ‘the esoteric interests of the Theosophical Society’. Blavatsky became Outer Head (the Inner Heads were the Masters or Mahatmas), with the responsibility of giving esoteric teachings to a small group of students who desired chelaship. The E.S. was independent of the administration of the Theosophical Society, or in the words of Olcott, it was ‘not the T.S.; nor that its rules are binding only upon members belonging to that special school; nor that it would be violation of the T.S. constitution for it to interfere with their rights of private judgment; nor that the President-Founder is compelled to guarantee to every individual member, of whatsoever religion, race, sex, or color, his or her personal liberty of belief and speech’.
body.zh: 1887年9月，布拉瓦茨基与布拉瓦茨基会所迁至兰斯当路17号（17 Lansdowne Road）；此后两年半，这里一直是布拉瓦茨基活动的中心，直到1890年她迁往伦敦圣约翰伍德（St. John’s Wood）大道19号（19 Avenue Road）。新址成为布拉瓦茨基会所、英国分会以及欧洲总部的新总部。顺带一提，这处总部正是→安妮·贝赞特（Annie Besant，1847-1933）的住所；她新近入会（1889年5月），是神智学会中一颗冉冉升起的新星。兰斯当路宅邸被确立为布拉瓦茨基会所总部（1888年10月9日）十三个月后，又一件大事发生：一个与神智学会关系密切的新组织成立。这个名为“神智学会秘传部”（Esoteric Section of the Theosophical Society，E.S.）的组织，其宗旨是促进“神智学会的秘传利益”。布拉瓦茨基出任外首（Outer Head；内首〔Inner Heads〕为诸位大师或圣雄），负责向一小群渴望成为弟子（chelaship）的学生传授秘传教义。秘传部独立于神智学会的行政体系；用奥尔科特的话说，“它并不是神智学会；其规则只对该特殊学派的成员具有约束力；它干预这些成员私人判断的权利，并不构成对神智学会章程的违反；会长兼创始人也没有义务向每一位成员——无论其宗教、种族、性别或肤色——保证其信仰与言论的个人自由”。

body.text: A few days after the founding of the Esoteric Section came the publication of The Secret Doctrine, consisting of two volumes with a total of 1474 pages. The first volume, Cosmogenesis, discusses cosmic evolution, expanding upon the contents of Isis Unveiled, while the second volume, Anthropogenesis, discusses the evolution of Humanity through a succession of Root Races, five of which have already appeared. Based on stanzas taken from The Book of Dzyan (seven in volume I and twelve in volume II), a work unknown to modern scholarship, said to be composed by an unattested people and in a language unknown to philosophy, The Secret Doctrine (SD) contains the following ideas: 1) There exists a single, Supreme, Eternal, Immutable, Unknown and Unknowable, Infinite Principle or Reality (SD 1:14); 2) There is a fundamental unity to all existence (SD I:120, 276); 3) The eternal, manifested Universe and everything within it is subject to the ‘law of periodicity, of flux and reflux, ebb and flow’ (SD I:17); 4) The evolution of nature – material and spiritual – reflects progressive development and not merely repetitive action (SD I:43, 277-78; II:653); 5) The evolution of the individual is not limited to one life but continues through innumerable lives made possible by the process of →reincarnation, i.e. the entrance of Self – the trinity of Spirit, Soul, and Mind – into another (human) body (SD II:302-306); 6) This evolution is brought about by the Law of Cause and Effect, or Karma – good actions leading to good consequences, bad actions to bad consequences – thus assigning full responsibility to the individual who performs the actions (SD I:639, 642-47; 7). The structural framework of the universe, humanity included, is by nature septenary in composition (SD II:605-41; 8). The cyclic, evolving universe is hierarchical in constitution, each component – for instance, the planets and the sun in our Solar System – consisting of seven constituents or globes, thus illustrating the correspondence between the microcosm of the human being and the macrocosm of the universe (SD II:68f., 434f.; 9). Human evolution on the Earth is taking place within seven Root Races, each of which is divided into seven sub-races. In our present state of evolution, we belong to the fifth sub-race (the Anglo-Saxon) of the fifth Root Race (SD I:610; II:1f., 86f., 300f., 434f., 688f.); 10) The individual is a microcosm, a ‘miniature copy of the macrocosm’ (SD I:274; 11). The universe is guided and animated by a cosmic Hierarchy of sentient beings, each having a specific mission (SD I:274-77).
body.zh: 秘传部成立数日后，《秘密教义》出版。该书共两卷，合计1474页。第一卷《宇宙生成论》（Cosmogenesis）讨论宇宙演化，在《揭开伊西斯的面纱》的内容基础上加以展开；第二卷《人类生成论》（Anthropogenesis）则讨论人类经由一系列根种族（Root Races）的演化，其中五个根种族已经出现。此书以取自《济恩之书》（The Book of Dzyan）的偈颂为据（第一卷七首，第二卷十二首）；该书为现代学界所未知，据说由一个无从考证的民族以哲学所不知的语言写成。《秘密教义》（SD）包含以下观念：1）存在一个唯一的、至高的、永恒的、不变的、未知且不可知的、无限的本原或实在（SD 1:14）；2）一切存在具有根本的统一性（SD I:120, 276）；3）永恒的、显现的宇宙及其中的一切，都服从“周期性的法则，即涨落、消长、潮汐往复的法则”（SD I:17）；4）自然——物质与精神——的演化体现的是渐进的发展，而不只是重复的作用（SD I:43, 277-78; II:653）；5）个体的演化并不限于一生，而是通过→转世（reincarnation）过程所开启的无量生世延续下去，即自我——由灵、魂、意构成的三位一体——进入另一个（人的）身体（SD II:302-306）；6）这一演化由因果法则即业（Karma）所促成——善行导致善果，恶行导致恶果——从而将全部责任归于行动者本人（SD I:639, 642-47）；7）宇宙（包括人在内）的结构框架在性质上由七重构成（SD II:605-41）；8）周期性演化的宇宙在构造上是层级式的，每一组成部分——例如我们太阳系中的行星与太阳——都由七个成分或球体构成，从而显示出人的微观宇宙与宇宙的宏观宇宙之间的对应（SD II:68f., 434f.）；9）地球上的人类演化在七个根种族之内进行，每一根种族又分为七个亚种。在我们目前的演化阶段，我们属于第五根种族的第五亚种（盎格鲁-撒克逊人）（SD I:610; II:1f., 86f., 300f., 434f., 688f.）；10）个体是一个微观宇宙，是“宏观宇宙的微型复制品”（SD I:274）；11）宇宙由一个有知觉的存在者所构成的宇宙层级体系引导并赋予生命，每一存在者皆有其特定使命（SD I:274-77）。

body.text: Students of The Secret Doctrine soon began to ask questions about its contents. Blavatsky’s responses during meetings of the Blavatsky Lodge in the first half of 1889 led to the publication, in two parts, of the Transactions of The Blavatsky Lodge of the Theosophical Society in 1890 and 1891. They cover issues concerning the heart of The Secret Doctrine: the “stanzas of Dzyan” included in the first volume.
body.zh: 《秘密教义》的读者不久便开始就书中内容提问。布拉瓦茨基在1889年上半年布拉瓦茨基会所会议上的答复，促成《神智学会布拉瓦茨基会所会刊》（Transactions of The Blavatsky Lodge of the Theosophical Society）于1890与1891年分两部分出版。这些会刊涵盖的问题涉及《秘密教义》的核心：收入第一卷的“济恩偈颂”。

body.text: In July 1889, Blavatsky, while visiting Fontainebleau for rest and recuperation, wrote or “translated” excerpts from “The Book of the Golden Precepts”, entitled The Voice of the Silence, allegedly part of the same series of texts from which the stanzas of the Book of Dzyan had been derived. Some stanzas she claimed to be pre-Buddhist, others Mahàyàna Buddhist in spirit. The first part, from which the title of the whole work is derived, highlights the progression of knowledge from the ordinary, waking (ignorant) state to the fourth or dreamless state of higher spiritual consciousness, until finally, in Blavatsky’s words, your ‘Self is lost in SELF, thyself unto THYSELF, merged in THAT SELF from which thou first didst radiate’. The second part, “The Two Paths”, refers to the ‘Open PATH’, i.e. the path of the layman or the exoteric path, that ‘leads to the changeless change – Nirvàna, the glorious state of Absoluteness, the Bliss past human thought’; and it distinguishes this from the second Path of ‘RENUNCIATION’, the ‘Path of Woe’, a ‘Secret Path [which] leads the Arhan to mental woe unspeakable’ but which also leads to ‘Paranirvànic’ bliss. The third part, “the Seven Portals”, purports to bring wisdom to the aspirant through ‘a golden key that openeth its gate’, which echoes in part the six pàramitàs or perfections, discussed in great detail in the Bodhicaryâvatàra by the 8th century Buddhist poet Shàntideva.
body.zh: 1889年7月，布拉瓦茨基在枫丹白露（Fontainebleau）休养期间，撰写或“翻译”了《金戒律之书》（“The Book of the Golden Precepts”）的摘录，题为《寂静之声》（The Voice of the Silence）；据称此书与《济恩之书》偈颂所自出的那一系列文本同属一类。她声称其中一些偈颂属于前佛教时期，另一些则在精神上属于大乘佛教。第一部分——整部作品的标题即由此而来——着重描述知识从寻常的清醒（无知）状态，进至第四即无梦的更高灵性意识状态的进程，直至最终，用布拉瓦茨基的话说，你的“自我消融于大我之中，你自身归于你自身，融汇于你最初由之流射而出的那个大我”。第二部分《两条道路》（“The Two Paths”）指的是“公开之路”（‘Open PATH’），即在家人的道路或外传之路，它“通向不变之变——涅槃，那绝对者的荣耀境界，超越人类思想的至福”；并将此与第二条“弃绝”（‘RENUNCIATION’）之路即“忧苦之路”（‘Path of Woe’）相区别，后者是一条“秘密之路，〔它〕引导阿罗汉（Arhan）进入无可言说的精神忧苦”，但也通向“般涅槃”（‘Paranirvànic’）之福。第三部分《七道门》（“the Seven Portals”）意在通过“一把开启其门的金钥匙”将智慧带给求道者；这与八世纪佛教诗人寂天（Shàntideva）在《入菩萨行论》（Bodhicaryâvatàra）中详加论述的六波罗蜜（pàramitàs）或六种圆满部分呼应。

body.text: The same month also witnessed the publication of The Key to Theosophy, a popular introduction to the “Wisdom Religion” or Theosophy. Among other subjects, it discusses the septenary nature of humanity and earth, reincarnation, post-mortem states, mind and ego, and gives information about the Theosophical Society and the Theosophical Masters or Mahatmas.
body.zh: 同月还见证了《神智学之钥》（The Key to Theosophy）的出版，这是一部面向大众的“智慧宗教”即神智学导论。除其他主题外，该书讨论了人与地球的七重本性、转世、死后状态、心智与自我，并介绍了神智学会以及神智学的大师或圣雄。

body.text: Although Blavatsky’s writing career was open to criticism by non-Theosophist theologians, scientists, and academics, by far the most serious challenge to the credibility of her major contributions – Isis Unveiled, The Secret Doctrine, and The Voice of the Silence – came from a spiritualist, William Emmette Coleman (1843-1909), who claimed that she had plagiarized many of her teachings from sources such as Ennemoser’s History of Magic and Demonologia, Dunlap’s Sod: The Son of Man and Sod: The Mysteries of Adoni, King’s Gnostics, and
body.zh: 尽管布拉瓦茨基的写作生涯受到非神智学阵营的神学家、科学家与学者的批评，但对她几部主要著作——《揭开伊西斯的面纱》《秘密教义》与《寂静之声》——之可信度的最严峻挑战，却来自一位唯灵论者威廉·埃米特·科尔曼（William Emmette Coleman，1843-1909）。他声称，布拉瓦茨基的许多教义剽窃自若干来源，如恩内莫泽（Ennemoser）的《魔法史》（History of Magic）与《魔鬼学》（Demonologia）、邓拉普（Dunlap）的《索德：人之子》（Sod: The Son of Man）与《索德：阿多尼的奥秘》（Sod: The Mysteries of Adoni）、金斯（King）的《诺斯替派》（Gnostics），以及

body.text: Jacolliot’s Christna et le Christ and Le Spiritisme dans le monde. Coleman listed a total of about one hundred secondary sources. Plagiarism has been an issue in Theosophy since the charges first appeared in the late 1880s. Blavatsky’s methods of citing sources have been defended by Theosophists, but in all fairness no detailed investigation has even been conducted, nor have criteria been established to prove or disprove the allegations. Interestingly, many of the authors who were allegedly the victims of Blavatsky’s plagiarism were alive when the charges were made, yet none indicted her.
body.zh: 雅科利奥（Jacolliot）的《基督纳与基督》（Christna et le Christ）与《世界中的唯灵论》（Le Spiritisme dans le monde）。科尔曼总共列出了约一百种二手来源。自这些指控于1880年代末首次出现以来，剽窃问题在神智学中便一直存在。神智学者为布拉瓦茨基的征引方法作了辩护，但平心而论，迄今既未进行过任何详细的调查，也未确立任何用以证实或推翻这些指控的标准。耐人寻味的是，被指为布拉瓦茨基剽窃之受害者的许多作者，在指控提出时仍在世，却无一人对她提出控诉。

body.text: A final assault on Blavatsky’s character came from one of the leading American Theosophists, Elliott Coues (1842-1899). Having failed to retain a position of authority within the newly reorganized Theosophical Society in America in 1886, and having failed to enlist Blavatsky’s aid in his efforts to gain control, Coues, in an article written by him appearing in the New York Sun in July 1890, attacked Blavatsky as an imposter and the Society for its teachings. This resulted in a lawsuit initiated in Blavatsky’s name against both Coues and the Sun. The suit was terminated because of Blavatsky’s death on May 8, 1891. Although Coues was unrepentent, the Sun did retract the story in a separate suit that W.Q. Judge, the General Secretary of the Theosophical Society in America, brought against the paper, and agreed to publish Judge’s sketch of Blavatsky’s life, entitled ‘The Esoteric She’, in the September 27, 1892 issue.
body.zh: 对布拉瓦茨基人格的最后一次攻击，来自美国神智学界的领袖之一埃利奥特·库斯（Elliott Coues，1842-1899）。库斯未能在1886年改组后的美国神智学会中保住权威职位，也未能争取到布拉瓦茨基协助其夺取控制权，遂于1890年7月在《纽约太阳报》（New York Sun）发表文章，攻击布拉瓦茨基为骗子，并抨击该学会的教义。此举导致以布拉瓦茨基名义对库斯与《太阳报》提起的诉讼。由于布拉瓦茨基于1891年5月8日去世，诉讼遂告终止。库斯虽毫无悔意，但《太阳报》在由美国神智学会秘书长W.Q. 贾奇（W.Q. Judge）另行提起的诉讼中撤回了该报道，并同意在1892年9月27日一期上发表贾奇所撰的布拉瓦茨基生平素描，题为《秘传的她》（“The Esoteric She”）。

body.text: In the year before her death, Blavatsky took on additional administrative responsibilities when she became President of the newly established European Section. In Lucifer (July 1890), she declared that she would exercise ‘the Presidential authority for the whole of Europe’, thus effectively becoming the co-leader of the Theosophical Society and declaring independence from Adyar.
body.zh: 在去世前一年，布拉瓦茨基承担了更多行政职责，出任新成立的欧洲分会主席。她在《路西法》（1890年7月）中宣称，她将行使“全欧洲的会长权力”，从而实际上成为神智学会的共同领袖，并宣布脱离阿迪亚尔（Adyar）而独立。

body.text: On April 26, symptoms of influenza appeared, and her condition grew steadily worse. Blavatsky’s final days were described by Laura Cooper, who, with Claude Falls Wright and Walter Richard Old, witnessed her passing. Over one hundred notices appeared in the British press, in addition to numerous letters from Theosophists, all attempting to define Blavatsky’s achievements. These achievements, according to the correspondents, were not to be located in her mediumship and psychic abilities, which may or may not have existed; rather, it was in her ability to synthesize with great erudition a vast expanse of knowledge and to articulate the knowledge that she believed to be the Ancient Wisdom of her Masters. Blavatsky’s esoteric synthesis has served as a basic source for later esotericists, literati, scientists, and entire movements, including the →New Age. Unlike most of her contemporaries, she is as visible today as any modern trend-setting guru, and she will most likely remain the most memorable and innovative esotericist of the 19th century.
body.zh: 4月26日，流感症状出现，她的病情持续恶化。劳拉·库珀（Laura Cooper）描述了布拉瓦茨基最后的时日；她与克劳德·福尔斯·赖特（Claude Falls Wright）、沃尔特·理查德·奥尔德（Walter Richard Old）一同见证了她的辞世。英国报章刊出百余则讣告，此外还有神智学者的大量来信，无不试图界定布拉瓦茨基的成就。据这些撰述者所言，她的成就并不在于其通灵与灵媒能力——这些能力或有或无；而在于她能够以渊博的学识综汇广博的知识，并清晰表述她所信奉的、属于其诸位大师的古代智慧。布拉瓦茨基的秘传综汇，后来成为秘传主义者、文人、科学家乃至包括→新时代运动（New Age）在内的若干完整运动的基本思想来源。与同时代的多数人不同，她今天仍如任何一位引领潮流的现代古鲁一样引人注目；她极可能仍将是19世纪最令人难忘、最具创新性的秘传主义者。
