body.zh: 1. 定义问题 “诺斯替主义”一词是学术上的发明，由剑桥柏拉图主义者→亨利·莫尔（Henry More，1614-1687）首创，他是在贬义上使用它的（Layton 1995）。在古代，这一术语所指称的宗教现象只被称为“诺斯”（希腊文 gnòsis，“知识”），或其反对者称之为“那假称为知识的”（已见于《提摩太前书》6:20）。在此语境中，诺斯一词并不指理性的、哲学的知识，而是指基于启示的宗教性、灵性洞见。从一开始，现代词语“诺斯替主义”就尤其被用来指称一种特殊类型的诺斯，它盛行于2、3世纪，并因其“异端的”创造与救赎学说而遭到若干早期基督教作家的激烈抨击。但即便在这种有限的意义上，要确切判定其标志性特征也变得越来越困难，尤其是在拿戈玛第文库（Nag Hammadi Library）发现之后（→ 诺斯替主义 II）。特别是在德语学界，“诺斯”与“诺斯替主义”两词一直被不加区分地用来指称2、3世纪的伟大诺斯替体系以及它们所属的更一般的精神潮流。英语世界则更倾向于使用“Gnosticism”一词。术语上的晦暗还因另一事实而更加复杂：在早期基督教反异端文献的影响下，“诺斯替的”这一形容词——一如今天仍然如此——几乎只被用来指教父们视为异端的那种“诺斯替主义”，这便赋予该词贬义。A.D. 诺克（A.D. Nock）在评论约纳斯（Jonas）如今已成经典的《诺斯与晚期古代精神》（Gnosis und spätantiker Geist）第一卷时，不无道理地感叹：“我陷在术语的迷雾之中”（I, 444）。为在这一点上求得更大的明晰，1966年在墨西拿召开的首届诺斯替主义大型讨论会，其首要目标便是为“诺斯”与“诺斯替主义”二词确立普遍接受的界定。此次会议的最终文件（有意大利文、法文、英文和德文版本）是一份《关于术语与

body.text: Conceptual Agreement with regard to the theme of the Colloquium’ (Bianchi, XXVI-XXIX, English version). It proposed to reserve the term “Gnosticism” for the movement that began ‘with a certain group of systems of the Second Century A.D.’ and to regard “Gnosis” as ‘knowledge of the divine mysteries reserved for an élite’, i.e. of an esoteric kind. The characteristics of Gnosticism ‘can be summarized in the idea of a divine spark in man, deriving from the divine realm, fallen into this world of fate, birth and death, and needing to be awakened by the divine counterpart of the self in order to be finally reintegrated’. The proposal emphasized: ‘Not every Gnosis is Gnosticism, but only that which involves . . . the idea of the divine consubstantiality of the spark that is in need of being awakened and reintegrated. This Gnosis of Gnosticism involves the divine identity of the knower (the Gnostic), the known (the divine substance of one’s transcendent self) and the means by which one knows (Gnosis as an implicit divine faculty that is to be awakened and actualized)’. As was to be expected, the Messina definitions did not receive unanimous scholarly approval, for the description of the Gnosis of Gnosticism could also be applied to currents that certainly did not fit the proposed definition of Gnosticism. To mention only one influential scholar, Kurt Rudolph almost immediately (1967) rejected the separation between Gnosis and Gnosticism. In accordance with the German scholarly tradition, he continued to use both terms for the religion of salvation through Gnosis that flourished in the first centuries of our era, but later on (1985) he preferred the term Gnosis and advised to eliminate the term Gnosticism ‘as far as possible, since it is not only pejorative, but also confusing’ (Rudolph 1996, 34-52 [1985], 144-148 [1967]). The term Gnosticism was completely discredited by Michael Williams in his Rethinking “Gnosticism”: An Argument for Dismantling a Dubious Category (1996). Based on a solid knowledge of the primary and secondary sources, his book contains a massive attack on what is usually understood by the terms “Gnostic”, “Gnosis”, “Gnosticism” and “Gnostic Religion”. He rightly argues that there never existed one clearly definable religious system that could be called Gnosticism. He shows that many texts that are commonly thought to represent the “Gnostic religion” do not contain the characteristics usually ascribed to it (separation between the supreme God and the Creator, protest exegesis, anti-cosmic world rejection, hatred of the body, Gnostic ethics as either libertinist or ascetic, etc.). In his view, terms such as “Gnosis” and “Gnostic” are so vague that they have lost any specific meaning and, therefore, should be avoided. Of course, even Williams could not deny that a number of 2nd-century texts unquestionably show the existence of a group of related and more or less coherent systems that together are usually, as in Messina, labelled “Gnosticism”. The dominant idea in these systems is the assumption that the world has not been created by the supreme transcendent God, but by a lower, imperfect and even bad Demiurge, who is identified with the God of the Jews (see below). Williams proposed to speak in this connection of “biblical demiurgical” texts and traditions; but this new terminology does not bring us much further, for one still needs to specify what kind of biblical demiurgical texts and traditions are meant, that is to say, those that through a specific interpretation of biblical myths proclaim that salvation is only possible through Gnosis, i.e. an esoteric knowledge of the origin and destination of one’s inner self.
body.zh: 概念共识的提案——就讨论会的主题而言》（Bianchi, XXVI-XXIX，英文版）。它提议将“诺斯替主义”一词保留给“随着公元2世纪某一组体系而开始”的运动，并将“诺斯”视为“保留给精英的神圣奥秘的知识”，即一种秘传性质的知识。诺斯替主义的特征“可以概括为：人之中有一神圣火花，它来自神圣领域，堕入这个由命运、生育与死亡支配的世界，需要被自我的神圣对应者唤醒，以便最终重新整合”。该提案强调：“并非所有的诺斯都是诺斯替主义，只有那包含……如下观念的才是：那需要被唤醒并重新整合的火花具有神圣的同体性。诺斯替主义的这种诺斯涉及知者（诺斯替派）、被知者（人那超越性自我的神圣实体）以及认知手段（诺斯作为一种隐含的、有待唤醒并实现的神圣能力）之间的神圣同一性。”不出所料，墨西拿的定义并未获得学界的一致赞同，因为对诺斯替主义之诺斯的描述也可适用于那些显然不符合所提议的诺斯替主义定义的潮流。仅举一位有影响力的学者为例，库尔特·鲁道夫（Kurt Rudolph）几乎立即（1967）就反对将诺斯与诺斯替主义分开。依照德国学术传统，他继续用这两个词来指我们纪元最初几个世纪中那种通过诺斯而得救的宗教，但后来（1985）他更偏好“诺斯”一词，并建议“尽可能”取消“诺斯替主义”一词，“因为它不仅有贬义，而且令人混淆”（Rudolph 1996, 34-52 [1985], 144-148 [1967]）。诺斯替主义一词在迈克尔·威廉斯（Michael Williams）的《重思“诺斯替主义”：为拆解一个可疑范畴的论证》（Rethinking “Gnosticism”: An Argument for Dismantling a Dubious Category, 1996）中被彻底败坏了声誉。该书基于对原始资料与二手资料的扎实知识，对人们通常以“诺斯替的”“诺斯”“诺斯替主义”和“诺斯替宗教”等词所理解的东西发动了大规模攻击。他正确地论证说，从来就不存在一个可以称为诺斯替主义的、清晰可定义的宗教体系。他表明，许多通常被认为代表“诺斯替宗教”的文本，其实并不包含通常归诸它的那些特征（最高神与造物主之间的分离、抗议式解经、反宇宙的弃世态度、对身体的憎恨、诺斯替伦理或是放荡或是禁欲，等等）。在他看来，“诺斯”和“诺斯替的”这类术语如此模糊，以至已失去任何具体含义，因此应当避免使用。当然，就连威廉斯也无法否认，若干2世纪文本确凿地表明存在一组彼此相关、或多或少融贯的体系，它们合在一起通常——如在墨西拿那样——被称为“诺斯替主义”。这些体系中的主导观念是这样一个假设：世界并非由至高的超越之神所创造，而是由一个较低的、不完善的甚至邪恶的造物主（Demiurge）所造，而这位造物主被等同于犹太人的神（见下文）。威廉斯提议在此语境中谈论“圣经造物主论”（biblical demiurgical）文本与传统；但这一新术语并不能使我们前进多少，因为人们仍需说明所指的是何种圣经造物主论文本与传统，也就是说，是那些通过一种对圣经神话的特殊解释而宣告救赎只有通过诺斯——即关于人内在本真自我的起源与归宿的秘传知识——才可能的文本与传统。

body.text: From the above it may have become clear that an unambiguous definition of what is understood by the much-used terms “Gnosis”, “Gnosticism” and “Gnostic” is impossible; but nevertheless some degree of clarification is necessary. It is undeniable that there existed in Antiquity a broad and variegated religious current characterized by a strong emphasis on esoteric knowledge (Gnosis) as the only means of salvation, which implied the return to one’s divine origin. This religious current can best be referred to as the “Gnostic Movement” or “Gnostic religiosity”. The great Gnostic systems of the 2nd and 3rd centuries are integral parts of this broader Gnostic movement and should not be isolated from it. The main characteristic of these systems is that their central ideas are expressed in myths, which may vary from one system to another, but as a whole display strong similarities. For that reason, and to maintain the link with the Gnostic current in general, it is preferable to speak here of mythological Gnostic texts or systems. The term “Gnosticism”, if used at all, should be reserved for these more or less coherent expressions of mythological Gnosis. The people who believed and proclaimed that salvation is possible only through revealed, secret Gnosis should be called “Gnostics”, i.e. “those who know”. There were Gnostics who used this term as a self-designation, for instance the followers of → Prodicus and the people referred to in Irenaeus, Adversus haereses, I, 29 (Smith). The emphasis on secrecy alone is not decisive to label an idea or a system as Gnostic: in Greek philosophy (Pythagoreanism and Platonism) as well as in Alexandrian Christian theology (the Sentences of Sextus, → Clement of Alexandria, Origen, and the Teachings of Silvanus), there was a strong tendency to maintain secrecy about some central doctrines or mysteries (van den Broek 1996, 264-270), but nobody would classify these doctrines as “Gnostic” and their adherents as “Gnostics”. Rather, the decisive criterion for designating an idea or text as Gnostic is whether or not it involves a concept of knowledge that considers Gnosis the indispensable means of salvation, indeed salvation itself. In this sense, the esoteric Gospel of Thomas can be labelled Gnostic, even though it shows no traces of mythological Gnosis. On the other hand, Clement of Alexandria, who always speaks of his ideal Christian as “the true Gnostic”, cannot be called a Gnostic, because he declared simple faith alone sufficient for salvation. The Gnostic knows of his divine origin and destination. According to the second-century Christian Gnostic Theodotus, Gnosis is the knowledge of ‘who we were and what we have become, where we were and into what we have been thrown, whither we hasten and from what we are redeemed, what is birth and what rebirth’ (Clement of Alexandria, Excerpts from Theodotus, 78, 2). The central Gnostic idea of revealed, secret Gnosis as a gift that illuminates and liberates man’s inner self is found in all periods, as is abundantly shown by the present Dictionary. For that reason, the terms “Gnosis” and “Gnostic” are applicable to all ideas and currents, from Antiquity to the present day, that stress the necessity of esoteric knowledge. The term “Gnosticism”, however, should be used with respect to the Gnostic systems of Antiquity only.
body.zh: 由上可见，要对“诺斯”“诺斯替主义”和“诺斯替的”这些被大量使用的词之所指给出一个毫不含糊的定义，是不可能的；但尽管如此，某种程度的澄清仍是必要的。不可否认，古代曾存在一股广泛而多样的宗教潮流，其特征是极力强调秘传知识（诺斯）是得救的唯一手段，而这暗含着回归人神圣本源之意。这股宗教潮流最好称为“诺斯替运动”或“诺斯替式宗教性”。2、3世纪的伟大诺斯替体系是这一更宽广的诺斯替运动的组成部分，不应与之割裂开来。这些体系的主要特征在于，其核心观念以神话形式表达，这些神话因体系不同而有所变化，但作为整体却显示出强烈的相似性。因此，并且为了与一般的诺斯替潮流保持联系，这里最好称之为神话性的诺斯替文本或体系。“诺斯替主义”一词，若终究要用，应保留给这些或多或少融贯的神话性诺斯的表述。那些相信并宣告救赎只有通过被启示的、隐秘的诺斯才可能的人，应被称为“诺斯替派”，即“那些知道的人”。有些诺斯替派将此词用作自我称谓，例如普罗狄库斯（→ Prodicus）的追随者，以及伊里奈乌斯《反异端》I, 29 中所提到的人（Smith）。仅仅强调秘密性并不足以将一种观念或体系标为诺斯替的：在希腊哲学（毕达哥拉斯主义与柏拉图主义）中，以及在亚历山大里亚基督教神学中（《塞克斯图斯箴言》、→ 亚历山大的克莱门、奥利金，以及《西尔瓦努斯教诲》），都有一种对某些核心教义或奥秘保守秘密的强烈倾向（van den Broek 1996, 264-270），但没有人会把这些教义归为“诺斯替的”、把其拥护者归为“诺斯替派”。相反，判定一种观念或文本为诺斯替的决定性标准，在于它是否包含这样一种知识观：认为诺斯是得救不可或缺的手段，甚至就是拯救本身。在这个意义上，那部秘传的《多马福音》可被标为诺斯替的，尽管它丝毫没有神话性诺斯的痕迹。另一方面，亚历山大的克莱门总是把他理想中的基督徒称为“真正的诺斯替派”，却不能被称为诺斯替派，因为他宣称单凭单纯的信仰就足以得救。诺斯替派知道自己神圣的起源与归宿。据2世纪基督教诺斯替派提奥多托斯（Theodotus）所说，诺斯是关于“我们曾是谁、我们成了什么，我们曾在何处、我们被抛入何处，我们正奔向何方、我们从什么中被赎回，什么是生育、什么是重生”的知识（亚历山大的克莱门《提奥多托斯摘录》78, 2）。诺斯替派关于被启示的、隐秘的诺斯是照亮并解放人内在本真自我的恩赐这一核心观念，在各个时代都可找到，本词典便充分表明了这一点。因此，“诺斯”与“诺斯替的”二词可适用于从古代直至今日一切强调秘传知识之必要性的观念与潮流。而“诺斯替主义”一词，则应仅用于古代的诺斯替体系。

body.text: 2. Gnostic Views The Gnostic ideas of Antiquity display such an enormous variety that it is impossible to reduce them to one coherent system. However, there is a certain set of views that can be considered characteristic of the Gnostic movement, even if most of them also occur in contexts that are not Gnostic at all. To this kernel of Gnostic thought belongs the idea of a completely transcendent God, who produces a divine world, to which the human being’s inner self originally belonged. Through a tragic course of events, which is often more implied than openly exposed, man became separated from his divine origin, which made him forget his high descent. Return to his place of origin is only possible though Gnosis, which in some way or another is imparted to him through revelation.
body.zh: 2. 诺斯替派的观点 古代的诺斯替观念呈现出如此巨大的多样性，以至于不可能将它们化约为一个融贯的体系。然而，确实有一组可以被视为诺斯替运动之特征的观念，尽管其中大多数也出现在完全不属于诺斯替的语境中。属于诺斯替思想核心的，是这样一个观念：一位完全超越的神产生了一个神圣世界，人内在本真自我原本属于那个世界。经过一连串悲剧性的事件——这些事件往往更多是暗示而非明言——人与其神圣本源分离，从而忘记了自己高贵的出身。只有通过诺斯，人才可能返回其本源，而诺斯是以某种方式通过启示传授给他的。

body.text: a. God and the Divine World The starting point of all Gnostic theology, both in its mythological and its more speculative form, is the idea of God’s absolute transcendence. In a number of texts, this idea is expressed in the same terminology of negative theology that was also used by pagan philosophers and hermetists as well as by Christian theologians. God is ineffable, invisible, unbegotten, incomprehensible, immeasurable, incorruptible, unnameable, etc. Long enumerations of these negative qualifications of God are, for instance, found at the beginning of the Apocryphon of John (NHC II, 1), the Tractatus Tripartitus (NHC I, 5), and Eugnostus the Blessed (NHC III, 1 and V, 1). The negative theology of the Gnostics went even further than that of the Greek philosophers and most Christian theologians. The latter held that God, although unknowable in his essence, could at least partially be comprehended by the human mind (nous), through philosophical reasoning and contemplation of the cosmic order; but the Gnostics denied this and declared knowledge of God to be possible only through revelation.
body.zh: a. 神与神圣世界 一切诺斯替神学——无论其神话形式还是更具思辨性的形式——的出发点，都是神绝对超越的观念。在一些文本中，这一观念是以否定神学的术语表达的，异教哲学家、赫尔墨斯主义者以及基督教神学家也同样使用这些术语。神是不可言说的、不可见的、非受生的、不可理解的、不可测度的、不可朽坏的、不可命名的，等等。对神之否定性限定语的长篇列举，例如见于《约翰密传》（NHC II, 1）、《三部分论》（NHC I, 5）和《蒙福的欧格诺斯托斯》（NHC III, 1 与 V, 1）的开头。诺斯替派的否定神学甚至比希腊哲学家和大多数基督教神学家走得更远。后者认为，神虽然在其本质上不可知，但至少可以部分地通过哲学推理和对宇宙秩序的沉思而被人心灵（nous）所把握；诺斯替派则否认这一点，宣称对神的认识只有通过启示才可能。

body.text: A central theme of Hellenistic philosophy was the relationship between the One and the Many, the Monad and the infinite Dyad. In these speculations, the One was always identified with the Good, whereas evil somehow arose from the principle of duality and multiplicity, mostly associated with matter. The Middle Platonists preferred a triad of basic principles of the universe, which could be described differently by the individual philosophers (Dillon). The first principle was mostly seen as Mind, but sometimes it was thought to be above Mind and Being; in that case the second principle was considered Mind. The Platonic ideas, which formed the patterns of visible reality, were conceived of as the thoughts of God and, accordingly, located either in the first or the second principle. The third principle was often identified with primal, formless matter, which by receiving the imprints of the ideas became the created world. A detailed discussion of the complicated Middle Platonist views on the first principles of being is impossible in the present context. May it suffice to say that the Gnostic authors, who often show themselves to be rather well educated, almost inevitably made use of these philosophical speculations to express their fundamentally religious ideas. In many Gnostic systems, a triad of divine hypostases constitutes the apex of the divine world. Most of those described by Hippolytus start from three basic principles of the universe, inter alia → Justin the Gnostic, the →
body.zh: 希腊化哲学的一个中心主题是一与多、单子与无限二元的关系。在这些思辨中，一始终被等同于善，而恶则以某种方式源自二元性与多样性的原则，后者多半与物质相关联。中期柏拉图主义者偏好一种由宇宙三个基本本原构成的三重结构，各位哲学家可对其作不同描述（Dillon）。第一本原多被视为心灵，但有时被认为高于心灵与存在；在后一种情形下，第二本原便被视为心灵。柏拉图式的理念构成了可见现实的范型，被设想为神的思想，因而被置于第一或第二本原之中。第三本原常被等同于原初的、无形式的物质，它接受理念的印痕而成为被造的世界。在此语境中不可能详细讨论中期柏拉图主义关于存在之第一本原的复杂观点。只需说，诺斯替作者——他们往往显得颇有教养——几乎不可避免地借用这些哲学思辨来表达其根本上是宗教性的观念。在许多诺斯替体系中，三个神圣本体（hypostases）构成神圣世界的顶点。希波吕托斯所描述的那些体系大多从宇宙的三个基本本原出发，其中包括诺斯替派的查士丁（→ Justin the Gnostic）、

body.text: Naasssenes, the → Perates, and the → Sethians. The Perates distinguished between the Unbegotten (agennèton), the Self-begotten (autogenes) and the Begotten (gennèton), which are also described as the Father, the Son and Matter (Hippolytus, Refutatio V, 17,1). A similar terminology is found in the Discourse on the Ogdoad and the Ennead (NHC VI, 57, 13-18; 63-21-23), in the Naasssene system, and partly also in Eugnostus the Blessed (NHC III, 72, 22; 75, 6-7). The Paraphrase of Shem says of ‘the great powers that were in existence in the beginning’: ‘There was Light and Darkness and there was Spirit between them’(NHC VII, 1, 25-28; the same principles occur in the Sethian system according to Hippolytus, Refutatio V, 19).
body.zh: 纳阿森派（→ Naassenes）、佩拉泰派（→ Perates）和塞特派（→ Sethians）。佩拉泰派区分非受生者（agennèton）、自生者（autogenes）与受生者（gennèton），它们也被描述为父、子与物质（希波吕托斯《驳斥一切异端》V, 17, 1）。类似的术语见于《论八重体与九重体》（NHC VI, 57, 13-18; 63, 21-23）、纳阿森派体系，并部分见于《蒙福的欧格诺斯托斯》（NHC III, 72, 22; 75, 6-7）。《闪的释义》论及“起初就存在的那些伟大权能”时说：“有光与暗，而它们之间有灵”（NHC VII, 1, 25-28；同样的本原也出现在希波吕托斯《驳斥一切异端》V, 19 所记述的塞特派体系中）。

body.text: There is, however, an important difference between the Middle- and Neoplatonist ideas on the principles of the universe and those of the Gnostics. The latter assumed a much greater number of levels of being than the philosophers were prepared to accept. In the middle of the third century, this led to a conflict in the school of Plotinus, which was also frequented by Gnostics. In his Against the Gnostics (Enneads II, 9), Plotinus rejected the Gnostic introduction of a great number of other hypostases within and outside the three basic principles he acknowledged himself (the One, Mind and Soul). This switch from philosophical reasoning to religious mythology is clearly to be seen in Zostrianus (NHC VIII, 1), which Plotinus’ pupil Amelius, at the master’s instigation, refuted in no less than forty books (Porphyry, Life of Plotinus, 16). Especially the mythological Gnostic texts and systems abound in a cascade of divine entities down from the summit of Being, but both the direct and the indirect sources show that there were great differences at this point, which led to quite different pictures of the structure of the divine world. Some Gnostic texts do mention these lower entities, sometimes even by name, but without further information about their origin and mutual relationship.
body.zh: 然而，中期与晚期柏拉图主义者关于宇宙本原的观念与诺斯替派的观念之间，存在一个重要差异。后者设定了远比哲学家所愿接受的更多层次的存在。3世纪中叶，这在普罗提诺（Plotinus）的学派中引发了一场冲突，而诺斯替派也常出入该学派。在《驳诺斯替派》（《九章集》II, 9）中，普罗提诺反对诺斯替派在他本人所承认的三个基本本原（一、心灵与灵魂）之内和之外引入大量其他本体。从哲学推理转向宗教神话的这一转变，在《佐斯特里亚努斯》（NHC VIII, 1）中清晰可见；普罗提诺的学生阿梅利乌斯（Amelius）在老师的授意下，用了不下四十卷书来驳斥它（波菲利《普罗提诺传》16）。尤其是神话性的诺斯替文本与体系，充满了自存在之巅层层倾泻而下的神圣实体，但直接与间接的资料都表明，在这一点上存在巨大差异，从而导致了关于神圣世界结构的大相径庭的图景。有些诺斯替文本确实提到这些较低的实体，有时甚至举出其名，却未提供关于其起源与相互关系的进一步信息。

body.text: The divine realm as a whole is mostly called the Pleroma (“Fullness”), and described as constituted of a variety of divine qualities and attributes, called aeons. These aeons successively develop out of God, which means that the development of the Pleroma in fact represents the self-realization of the ineffable God. The Gnostic mythological texts show a great variety of aeons and their interrelations, but some aeonic systems exerted a particular influence, especially those of the “Gnostics” behind the Apocryphon of John and the Valentinians (→ Valentinus and Valentinians). There were
body.zh: 神圣领域作为整体多半被称为普累若麻（Pleroma，“丰盈”），并被描述为由种种称为移涌（aeons）的神圣品质与属性构成。这些移涌依次从神发展而出，这意味着普累若麻的发展实际上代表着那不可言说之神的自我实现。诺斯替神话文本展示了移涌及其相互关系的极大多样性，但某些移涌体系产生了特别的影响，尤其是《约翰密传》背后的“诺斯替派”与瓦伦廷派（→ 瓦伦廷与瓦伦廷派）的体系。有些

body.text: Gnostics who indulged almost exclusively in endless speculations about the structure of the divine world. The most bewildering example of this is to be found in the Books of Jeû and the Untitled Treatise of the Bruce Codex.
body.zh: 诺斯替派几乎一味沉溺于关于神圣世界结构的无穷思辨。最令人困惑的例子见于《耶乌之书》和布鲁斯抄本中的无题论著。

body.text: Before discussing some aspects of the development of the Pleroma, a clarification of the concept of aeon may be in order. The Greek word aiòn means “(a long space of) time”, “age”, and in plural “eternity” (e.g. Romans 16:27: ‘until the aeons [of aeons]’). In the Hellenistic world, infinite Time was honoured as a God under the name of Aion, especially in Alexandria. From the meaning “age” the word aeon also evolved into another word for “world” (e.g. Matthew 12:32: ‘this aeon’ versus the ‘the coming aeon’). In some early Christian texts, God is called ‘the King of the aeons’ (1 Timothy 1:17), who through his Son has created the aeons (Hebrews 1:2), so that Clement of Rome (ca. 95 A.D.), in his Letter to the Corinthians, 35, 3, could speak about God as ‘the Creator and Father of the aeons’. The exact meaning of these expressions is a matter for dispute, but it will be clear that they could easily be interpreted in a Gnostic sense. For a correct understanding of the Gnostic concept of aeons it should be realized that, just like the Pleroma as a whole, the Gnostic aeons have a distinct spatial aspect. That explains why, for instance, it is said in the Apocryphon of John that the race of Seth and other Gnostics are placed in specific aeons (BG 36, 1-15 parr. = Synopsis 22, 18-23, 12), and also why in the Gospel of Truth the aeons are often called “spaces”, which are emanations of the Father (NHC I, 27, 11). The aeons are aspects of the ineffable God, but at the same time they are also forms of time and space. There may be an influence here of Greek interpretations of the Persian Zervan Akarana, the Unbegotten Time, from which the opposed gods Ormuzd and Ahriman have come forth: according to Eudemus of Rhodos (4th century B.C.) this primal principle was called both “Place” and “Time” (Frg. 150, ed. Wehrli, VIII, 71). Although there are clear similarities, the aeons differ from other → intermediary beings because of their often artificial nature (personified abstract concepts) and their functions.
body.zh: 在讨论普累若麻发展的一些方面之前，先澄清移涌的概念或许是合宜的。希腊词 aiòn 意为“（一段长久的）时间”“时代”，复数则为“永恒”（例如《罗马书》16:27：“直到诸世代［的世代］”）。在希腊化世界，尤其是在亚历山大里亚，无限的时间作为一个神以埃翁（Aion）之名受到崇奉。由“时代”之义，移涌一词也演变为“世界”的另一种说法（例如《马太福音》12:32：“今世”对“来世”）。在一些早期基督教文本中，神被称为“万世的君王”（《提摩太前书》1:17），他藉其子创造了诸世代（《希伯来书》1:2），因此罗马的克莱门（约公元95年）在其《致哥林多人书》35, 3 中可以说神是“诸世代的创造者与父”。这些表述的确切含义尚有争议，但显然它们很容易作诺斯替式的解释。要正确理解诺斯替的移涌概念，就应意识到，正如普累若麻整体一样，诺斯替的移涌也具有明显的空间维度。这解释了为何例如《约翰密传》说塞特的族类和其他诺斯替派被安置在特定的移涌之中（BG 36, 1-15 及其平行文本 = Synopsis 22, 18-23, 12），也解释了为何在《真理福音》中移涌常被称为“空间”，它们是父的流溢（NHC I, 27, 11）。移涌是那不可言说之神的诸方面，但同时它们也是时间与空间的形式。这里可能受到希腊人对波斯祖尔万·阿卡拉纳（Zervan Akarana，非受生的时间）之解释的影响，对立的神奥尔穆兹德与阿里曼即由此而出：据罗德岛的欧德摩斯（公元前4世纪），这一原初本原既被称为“处所”又被称为“时间”（Frg. 150, ed. Wehrli, VIII, 71）。尽管有明确的相似之处，移涌仍不同于其他→ 中介性存在，因为其往往具有人工的性质（人格化的抽象概念）及其功能。

body.text: As said above, the development of the Pleroma is the self-realization of God: the Unknown Father becomes conscious of himself. A well-known description of this development is that of the Apocryphon of John, which has a close and more original parallel in Irenaeus, Adversus haereses I, 29, and partly also in the Gospel of the Egyptians.
body.zh: 如上所述，普累若麻的发展就是神的自我实现：未知的父意识到自身。《约翰密传》对这一发展有著名的描述，它在伊里奈乌斯《反异端》I, 29 中有一个相近而更为原始的平行版本，并部分见于《埃及人福音》。

body.text: Other interesting pleromatic structures are those of Eugnostus the Blessed and the Valentinians (Irenaeus, AH I, 1). According to the Apocryphon, the Unknown Father saw himself reflected in the light-water that surrounded him, he recognized himself, and immediately his thought became an independent female entity, called Ennoia (“Thought”), who is also called Barbelo. The Father and Barbelo generate the Light, who is also called Autogenes and identified with Christ (probably a secondary addition). Then this original trinity of Father, Mother and Son expands into the spiritual, divine world of the Pleroma. The Father adds to Barbelo the aeons Prognòsis (“Foreknowledge”), Aphtharsia (“Incorruptibility”) and Aeònia Zòè (“Eternal Life”), and to the Light (Christ) he adds the aeons Nous (“Mind”), Thelèma (“Will”), and Logos (“Word”). These two tetrads are then combined into an ogdoad that consists of four pairs, which generate a number of other aeons, which in their turn do the same. The identification of the aeons with abstract concepts that together form the Fullness of God shows that this myth of the development of the Pleroma is of a clearly artificial character. Just as in the Apocryphon of John, the top of the Valentinian Pleroma is formed by an ogdoad that also consists of four pairs of aeons. The first pair consists of the Unknown Father, called Bythos (“Depth”), and his Ennoia (“Thought”), also called Charis (“Grace”) and Sigè (“Silence”). They generate the second level of divine being: Nous (“Mind”) and Aletheia (“Truth”), which produce the third level: Logos (“Word”) and Zoè (“Life”), which in their turn bring forth Anthropos (“Man”) and Ecclesia (“Church”). In the myth of the Apocryphon of John and Irenaeus, AH I, 29, the coming forth of the Anthropos, ‘the perfect and true Man’, also called Adamas, is narrated at the end of the section on the Pleroma. But in both texts the last aeon is called Sophia (“Wisdom”), who becomes responsible for the split in the Pleroma and the origin of evil and, as a corollary, the creation of the world. The insertion of many aeons between the Unknown Father and Sophia was apparently intended to make the distance between the transcendent God and the cause of evil as great as possible.
body.zh: 其他有趣的普累若麻结构见于《蒙福的欧格诺斯托斯》与瓦伦廷派（伊里奈乌斯《反异端》I, 1）。根据《约翰密传》，未知的父在环绕他的光-水中看见自己的映像，他认识了自己，他的思想立刻成为一个独立的女性实体，名为恩诺亚（Ennoia，“思想”），她又被称为芭比洛（Barbelo）。父与芭比洛生出光，光又被称为自生者，并被等同于基督（这大概是次要的增补）。于是这个父、母、子的原初三位一体扩展为普累若麻的灵性神圣世界。父给芭比洛增添了移涌普罗格诺西斯（Prognòsis，“预知”）、阿弗塔西亚（Aphtharsia，“不朽坏”）与埃奥尼亚·佐埃（Aeònia Zòè，“永恒生命”），又给光（基督）增添了移涌努斯（Nous，“心灵”）、特莱玛（Thelèma，“意志”）与逻各斯（Logos，“言”）。这两个四元组随后结合成一个由四对构成的八元组，它们又生出若干其他移涌，后者依次类推。将移涌等同于共同构成神之丰盈的抽象概念，表明这一关于普累若麻发展的神话具有明显的人工性质。正如在《约翰密传》中一样，瓦伦廷派普累若麻的顶端由一个同样由四对移涌构成的八元组组成。第一对由被称为比托斯（Bythos，“深渊”）的未知之父及其恩诺亚（“思想”）组成，后者又被称为卡里斯（Charis，“恩典”）与西格（Sigè，“静默”）。他们生出神圣存在的第二层：努斯（“心灵”）与阿勒忒亚（Aletheia，“真理”），后者产生第三层：逻各斯（“言”）与佐埃（Zoè，“生命”），它们又生出安特罗波斯（Anthropos，“人”）与埃克克莱西亚（Ecclesia，“教会”）。在《约翰密传》与伊里奈乌斯《反异端》I, 29 的神话中，“完美而真实的人”即安特罗波斯（又名阿达玛斯）的出现，被叙述于论普累若麻部分的末尾。但在这两个文本中，最后一个移涌都名为索菲亚（Sophia，“智慧”），她成为普累若麻分裂与恶之起源的负责者，并因此成为世界创造的负责者。在未知之父与索菲亚之间插入众多移涌，显然意在尽可能拉大超越之神与恶之原因之间的距离。

body.text: There are strong indications, however, that the complicated Gnostic myths of the Pleroma developed out of a much simpler model, which was more mythological and presented Anthropos and Sophia as the first manifestations of the transcendent God. According to Eugnostus the Blessed, the ‘self-grown, self-created Father’ conceived the idea of having ‘his likeness come into being’, and ‘immediately the beginning of that Light manifested itself as an immortal androgynous Man’(NHC III, 76, 14-24). His female aspect is inter alia called ‘All-wise Begettress Sophia’ (III, 3-4). Immortal Man and his Sophia put forth another androgynous Man, called the Son of Man, whose female aspect is also called Sophia. This pair generates a third androgynous Man, the Son of the Son of Man, whose female name is again Sophia. In other Gnostic systems, too, the first principles are called Man and the Son of Man, for instance in those of → Monoimus, the Naassenes, and Irenaeus AH, I, 30, which is presupposed in the second part of the Apocryphon of John (see below). In Eugnostus, the addition of the second and third pairs is an obvious amplification of an originally more simple myth that only knew of one Anthropos and Sophia (Schenke 1962 [2]). The figures of Anthropos and Sophia derive from Jewish speculations about the first manifestations of God that were based on biblical texts. Wisdom herself says, in Proverbs 8:22, ‘The Lord created me the beginning of his ways, before all else he made, long ago’, which led to the idea of Wisdom as the creative agent of God: in Genesis 1:1 the words “in the beginning” were accordingly interpreted as “through Wisdom”. In Wisdom of Solomon 7:25, Wisdom is described as an emanation of God, ‘a pure effluence from the glory of the Almighty, . . . the reflection of everlasting light’. Speculations on the manifestation of God as a heavenly Man were triggered off by Ezekiel 1:26- 28, which describes a vision of the Glory of God in ‘the likeness as the appearance of a man’ (King James Version), appearing in fire and light. The figure of a heavenly Man as manifestation of the transcendent God has had an enormous influence in Judaism, → Hermetism (Poimandres), and Gnostic and non-Gnostic Christianity. The attribution of a human shape to the radiant manifestation of God’s Glory caused the heavenly Anthropos to be always associated with Light. The Jewish Alexandrian writer Ezekiel the Dramatist (2nd century B.C.) describes in his Exodus, 66-89, a vision by → Moses of a man (Gr. phòs, with another accentuation also “light”), who sat on a throne, with a diadem on his head and a sceptre in his left hand. Before the man – who is apparently God’s viceregent on earth – disappears, he summons Moses to sit down on the throne and accept the regalia, which makes him a divine being. The association of Heavenly Man with light played an important role in Gnostic speculations about the first manifestation of God.
body.zh: 然而，有强烈的迹象表明，那些复杂的诺斯替普累若麻神话是从一个远为简单的模式发展而来的，该模式更具神话色彩，将安特罗波斯与索菲亚呈现为超越之神的首批显现。根据《蒙福的欧格诺斯托斯》，“自生自创的父”怀有让“其肖似者产生”的意念，“那光的开端立刻显现为一个不死的阴阳同体的人”（NHC III, 76, 14-24）。他的女性方面被称为“全智的生育者索菲亚”等等（III, 3-4）。不死的人及其索菲亚生出另一个阴阳同体的人，称为人子，其女性方面也称为索菲亚。这一对又生出第三个阴阳同体的人，即人子之子，其女性名称同样是索菲亚。在其他诺斯替体系中，第一本原也被称为人与人之子，例如莫诺伊穆斯（→ Monoimus）、纳阿森派的体系，以及伊里奈乌斯《反异端》I, 30，后者是《约翰密传》第二部分的前提（见下文）。在《欧格诺斯托斯》中，第二对与第三对的添加显然是对一个原本更简单的神话的扩充，那个神话只知道一个安特罗波斯与索菲亚（Schenke 1962 [2]）。安特罗波斯与索菲亚的形象源自犹太人关于神之首批显现的思辨，这些思辨基于圣经文本。智慧自己在《箴言》8:22 中说，“在耶和华造化的起头，在太初创造万物之先，就有了我”，这引出了智慧作为神之创造代理者的观念：因此《创世记》1:1 中“起初”一词被解释为“藉着智慧”。《所罗门智慧书》7:25 将智慧描述为神的流溢，“是从全能者荣耀发出的纯流，……是永恒之光的映照”。关于神以天上之人的形象显现的思辨，则由《以西结书》1:26-28 引发，该处描述了在火与光中显现的、“仿佛人的形状”（钦定本）的神之荣耀的异象。天上之人作为超越之神之显现的形象，在犹太教、→ 赫尔墨斯主义（《波伊曼德勒斯》）以及诺斯替与非诺斯替的基督教中产生了巨大影响。将人的形貌赋予神之荣耀的光辉显现，使得天上安特罗波斯始终与光相关联。犹太亚历山大里亚作家、剧作家以西结（公元前2世纪）在其《出埃及记》66-89 中描述了→ 摩西所见的一个异象：一个人（希腊文 phòs，重音不同亦可作“光”）坐在宝座上，头戴冠冕，左手持权杖。在这人——显然就是神在世上的代理人——消失之前，他召摩西坐上宝座并接受王权标识，这使摩西成为一个神圣存在。天上之人与光的关联，在诺斯替派关于神之首批显现的思辨中起了重要作用。

body.text: According to On the Origin of the World, NHC II, 107, 25-108, 14, the Demiurge became aware that ‘an immortal Man of Light had been existing before him’, which refers to the primeval light of Genesis 1:3 (‘Let there be light!’). At the Demiurge’s request, the radiant light manifested itself: ‘As that light appeared, a likeness of Man, which was very marvellous, revealed itself in it’. The association with Genesis 1:3 (Light) and Ezekiel 1:26 (likeness of a man) is clearly visible not only in this text, but also in that of Eugnostus the Blessed (NHC III, 76, 14 ff.), quoted above (Fossum 1985, 266-291).
body.zh: 根据《论世界的起源》NHC II, 107, 25-108, 14，造物主意识到“在他之前已经存在一个不死的光之人”，这指的是《创世记》1:3 的原初之光（“要有光！”）。应造物主之请，那光辉灿烂的光显现出来：“当那光出现时，一个极其奇妙之人的肖似在它里面显露出来”。与《创世记》1:3（光）和《以西结书》1:26（人的形状）的关联，不仅在此文本中清晰可见，也见于上文所引《蒙福的欧格诺斯托斯》（NHC III, 76, 14 以下）（Fossum 1985, 266-291）。

body.text: It is of interest to note that Eugnostus not only describes the apex of the divine world in terms of the Jewish myth of Anthropos and Sophia, but also in those of Platonic philosophy. Immortal Man is identified with Nous (“Mind”; NHC V, 6, 6-7; cf. III, 104, 8) and Sophia with Alètheia (“Truth”; NHC III, 77, 3-10; V, 6, 8-10). According to Plato, Nous and Aletheia are noetic entities produced by the Good (Republic, 517b; cf. also 490b). Plato already placed the Good above Mind and Being and, accordingly, the Middle Platonists identified the Good with the supreme, ineffable God. Read with the eyes of a second-century Platonist, the master himself had taught in the Republic that the unknowable, transcendent God puts forth two noetic entities, Nous and Aletheia. The author of Eugnostus the Blessed apparently knew a tradition that identified the transcendent Jewish God with the Good of Platonism, and the latter’s first products, Nous and Aletheia, with the former’s pre-eminent divine hypostases, Anthropos and Sophia. In the Valentinian myth of the Pleroma, Nous and Aletheia also form the second level of being, but there are some considerable differences with the tradition of Eugnostus, which make it probable that the priority belongs to the latter. In Eugnostus, the supreme, ineffable God is strictly monadic; the principle of androgynous duality is first expressed in Immortal Man and his Sophia. It is to such a conception that Plato’s view of the Good as producing Nous and Aletheia could be applied. In the Valentinian system, the principle of duality and fecundity was transferred to the deepest ground of being itself, by changing its monadic essence into Bythos and Sige, Depth ands Silence (though there were Valentinians who adhered to a more monadic view of the supreme God). The Valentinian Pleroma seems ultimately based on speculations on the structure of the divine world that were closely related to those expressed in Eugnostus the Blessed (van den Broek 1996, 122-129).
body.zh: 值得注意的是，《欧格诺斯托斯》不仅以犹太人的安特罗波斯与索菲亚神话来描述神圣世界的顶点，也以柏拉图哲学的术语来描述。不死的人被等同于努斯（“心灵”；NHC V, 6, 6-7；参 III, 104, 8），索菲亚被等同于阿勒忒亚（“真理”；NHC III, 77, 3-10; V, 6, 8-10）。按照柏拉图，努斯与阿勒忒亚是由善所产生的心智实体（《理想国》517b；参 490b）。柏拉图已将善置于心灵与存在之上，因此中期柏拉图主义者将善等同于至高的、不可言说的神。以2世纪柏拉图主义者的眼光来读，大师本人在《理想国》中已经教导说，不可知的、超越的神产生两个心智实体，努斯与阿勒忒亚。《蒙福的欧格诺斯托斯》的作者显然知道一个传统，它将超越的犹太人的神等同于柏拉图主义的善，并将后者最初的产品努斯与阿勒忒亚等同于前者最卓越的神圣本体安特罗波斯与索菲亚。在瓦伦廷派的普累若麻神话中，努斯与阿勒忒亚也构成存在的第二层，但与《欧格诺斯托斯》的传统有若干相当大的差异，这使后者居于优先地位成为可能。在《欧格诺斯托斯》中，至高的、不可言说的神严格地是单子性的；阴阳同体二元性的原则首先表达于不死的人及其索菲亚之中。正是在这样的构想上，柏拉图关于善产生努斯与阿勒忒亚的观点才得以应用。在瓦伦廷派体系中，二元性与丰产性的原则被转移到存在最深的根基本身，其单子性本质被改变为比托斯与西格，即深渊与静默（尽管也有瓦伦廷派持更为单子性的最高神观）。瓦伦廷派的普累若麻似乎最终基于关于神圣世界结构的思辨，而这些思辨与《蒙福的欧格诺斯托斯》中所表达的思辨密切相关（van den Broek 1996, 122-129）。

body.text: b. Fall and Creation That the human soul, or at least its higher part, was of divine origin, had somehow fallen into its earthly existence, and had to strive for its return to heaven, was a common idea in the Graeco-Roman world. It had been an integral part of Platonic philosophy since Plato’s Phaedrus. While the Gnostic view of the origin and destination of one’s inner self fits this general scheme, its elaboration was not philosophical but religious and mythological, even if use was made of philosophical categories. An important difference between the philosophical and the Gnostic views in this regard is that the Gnostics assumed a pre-cosmic Fall, which had taken place within the divine Pleroma. In many Gnostic texts this Fall is not mentioned or only vaguely hinted at: they concentrate on the bondage of human beings to the evil powers that dominate our world, and on the way to escape from it. The Gnostic, i.e. esoteric, character of these texts is apparent above all from their emphasis on revealed knowledge as the decisive means of salvation. But other writings, especially those that belong to the great systems of the 2nd century, present a full account of how evil originated within the divine Pleroma and eventually led to the creation of the material world and the body as the prison of man’s real self (Dahl, Logan, van der Vliet). However, in this regard too, a clear Gnostic doctrine did not exist; there were only variations on a common theme, namely that of a fatal rupture within the Pleroma.
body.zh: b. 堕落与创造 人的灵魂，或至少其较高部分，具有神圣本源，以某种方式堕入其尘世存在，并须努力返回天上——这在希腊罗马世界是一个常见的观念。自柏拉图的《斐德罗篇》以来，它一直是柏拉图哲学的一个组成部分。诺斯替派关于人内在本真自我之起源与归宿的观点虽符合这一总体图式，但其阐发不是哲学性的，而是宗教性与神话性的，即便借用了哲学范畴。哲学观点与诺斯替观点在此的一个重要差异在于，诺斯替派假定了一次前宇宙的堕落，它发生在神圣的普累若麻之内。在许多诺斯替文本中，这次堕落未被提及，或仅被隐约暗示：它们专注于人类受支配我们世界的邪恶权能奴役的状态，以及逃脱这种状态的道路。这些文本的诺斯替的、即秘传的性质，首先表现于它们强调被启示的知识是得救的决定性手段。但其他著作，尤其是属于2世纪诸大体系的著作，则完整叙述了恶如何在神圣普累若麻之内产生，并最终导致物质世界以及作为人真正自我之牢狱的身体的创造（Dahl, Logan, van der Vliet）。然而，在这一方面同样不存在明确的诺斯替教义；存在的只是对一个共同主题的种种变奏，即普累若麻之内一次致命的破裂。

body.text: According to the basic text of Gnostic mythology, the Apocryphon of John, the split in the deity was caused by the lowest aeon, Sophia (BG 36, 16-47, 13 parr. = Synopsis 24, 1-37, 5). As the Father had brought forth Ennoia out of himself, she wanted to produce her image in the same way, without the consent of the Father and her counterpart. For that reason she is called “lascivious”. As a result of her lewd thought, she produced an ugly, imperfect being: a dragon with a lion’s head and fiery eyes, which she called Jaldabaoth. The etymology of this name is still disputed. For a long time, it was thought to mean “Son of Chaos”; more recent explanations are “Begetter of (S)abaoth” (also interpreted as “Begetter of the Powers”) and “Son of Shame” (Black). Another name given to Jaldabaoth is Saklas, which derives from the Aramaic Saklà± (“Fool”). In order to hide her son, Sophia pushed him out of the Pleroma. However, he had extracted a great power from his mother and created his own world and his own aeons, 360 “angels” in all, among them the twelve signs of the zodiac and the seven planets. Having finished his creation, he said: ‘I am a jealous God, there is no one except me!’ (a combination of Exodus 20:5 and Isaiah 45:5). It is for that reason that he was called Saklas, for only ‘the Fool says in his heart: there is no God’ (Psalm 14:1 and 53:2). The myth of Irenaeus, AH I, 29, which is so closely related to that of the Apocryphon with respect to the constitution of the Pleroma, gives another account of the Fall of Sophia (29, 4). The sect of the Gnostics behind this text denied that Sophia had a pleromatic counterpart. On the contrary, she wanted to have one; and as she did not find it within the Pleroma, she sought it outside the divine realm, but did not find it there either. Realizing that she had acted against the will of the Father, she brought forth a product of herself. She did so with the best intentions, but nevertheless her son was full of ignorance and pride. Sophia repented, but had to remain outside the Pleroma, above the eighth sphere. Though it does not fit its main story, the Apocryphon also knows of her ‘moving to and fro’ outside the Pleroma (which is connected with the moving of the Spirit above the waters of Chaos in Genesis 1:2) and of her repentance and her being placed in the ninth sphere ‘until she has corrected her deficiency’. Related ideas are found in On the Origin of the World and the Hypostasis of the Archons (NHC II, 4 and 5). It is of interest to note that the Valentinians spiritualized the fall of Sophia. According to them, she wanted to have the same union with the Father as Mind had, i.e. to know him, which means that, in fact, she represents the impossible search for knowledge of the depths of the Father. She would have been swallowed up by the sweetness of the Father, had she not been pushed back (Irenaeus, AH I, 2, 2).
body.zh: 按照诺斯替神话的基本文本《约翰密传》，神性中的分裂是由最低的移涌索菲亚引起的（BG 36, 16-47, 13 及其平行文本 = Synopsis 24, 1-37, 5）。正如父从自身生出恩诺亚，她也想以同样方式产生自己的形象，而未得父及其对应者的同意。因此她被称为“淫荡的”。由于其淫邪的思想，她生出一个丑陋、不完善的存在：一条有狮子头与火眼、被她称为雅尔达巴奥特（Jaldabaoth）的龙。这个名字的词源仍有争议。长期以来，人们认为它意为“混沌之子”；较新的解释有“（撒）巴奥特的生育者”（也被解释为“诸权能的生育者”）与“羞耻之子”（Black）。雅尔达巴奥特的另一个名字是萨克拉斯（Saklas），源自阿拉米语 Saklà±（“愚人”）。为藏匿其子，索菲亚将他推出普累若麻。然而他从母亲那里夺取了巨大的权能，创造了自己的世界和自己的移涌，共360个“天使”，其中包括黄道十二宫与七颗行星。完成创造之后，他说：“我是忌邪的神，除我以外没有别神！”（《出埃及记》20:5 与《以赛亚书》45:5 的糅合）。正因如此，他被称为萨克拉斯，因为只有“愚顽人心里说：没有神”（《诗篇》14:1 与 53:2）。与《约翰密传》在普累若麻构造方面关系密切的伊里奈乌斯《反异端》I, 29 的神话，对索菲亚的堕落另有叙述（29, 4）。此文本背后的诺斯替派别否认索菲亚有一个普累若麻中的对应者。相反，她想要有一个；由于她在普累若麻之内找不到，便到神圣领域之外去寻找，但在那里也未找到。她意识到自己违背了父的意志，于是生出自身的一个产物。她此举出于最好的意图，然而她的儿子却充满了无知与傲慢。索菲亚悔改了，但必须留在普累若麻之外、第八重天之上。尽管与主要故事不合，《约翰密传》也知道她在普累若麻之外“来回飘荡”（这与《创世记》1:2 中灵运行在混沌之水面上有关），知道她的悔改，以及她被安置在第九重天“直到她补足了自己的欠缺”。类似观念见于《论世界的起源》与《执政官的本质》（NHC II, 4 与 5）。值得注意的是，瓦伦廷派将索菲亚的堕落灵性化了。据他们说，她想要与父有如同心灵与父那样的结合，即认识他，这意味着她实际上代表着对认识父之深渊的不可能性的追寻。若不是被推回，她本会被父的甜美所吞没（伊里奈乌斯《反异端》I, 2, 2）。

body.text: The Fall of Sophia and the origin of the bad Demiurge serve as a prelude to what the Gnostics were primarily interested in: the explanation of how the divine element had come to reside in man and how it could return to its original state. The story as told by the Apocryphon (BG 47, 14-55,17 parr. = Synopsis 37, 6-56, 10) is not wholly coherent with the preceding section (which indicates a combination of various sources), but it has much in common with the views that Irenaeus, AH I, 30, ascribes to ‘other people’ than the “Gnostics” he described in I, 29. The incoherence is brought out by the sudden introduction of Man and the Son of Man, as the supreme God and his first manifestation. As Jaldabaoth had declared himself the only God, a voice resounded saying: ‘Man exists and the Son of Man!’, and ‘the holy and perfect Father, the first Man’ revealed himself to him in human form. The radiant image of the heavenly Man was reflected in the waters of Chaos and the Demiurge said to the powers that attended him (or they said to themselves): ‘Let us create a man in the image and likeness of God’ (cf. Genesis 1:26). The seven planetary powers of Jaldabaoth made up the components from which the psychic body of man was made, which shows a clear influence of Plato’s Timaeus (van den Broek 1996, 67-85). The long recension of the Apocryphon even assigns the composition of the body to no less than 365 “angels” (demons), who are all mentioned by name. There is little doubt that this list derives from magical sources (van der Vliet, 179-237). The assistants of the Demiurge proved to be incapable of awakening and raising the motionless psychic body of Adam. Then the Father of the All sent his son Autogenes with four great lights to the world of Ialdabaoth and they advised him: ‘Blow into his face something of your spirit and the artefact will arise’ (cf. Genesis 2:7). The Demiurge, who is now identified with the biblical Creator, blew his Spirit, i.e. the divine power of his mother, into the body and it began to move. In this way the divine spirit entered the human being, who because of this spirit was more intelligent than the powers and the Demiurge himself. They realized that he was free from wickedness, and to imprison his divine element they made the material body. This is followed in the Apocryphon by the story of Paradise, which, however, is explained in a Gnostic sense: the Tree of Life is a tree of death and the command not to eat of the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil was meant to prevent Adam from discovering his divine descent.
body.zh: 索菲亚的堕落与邪恶造物主的起源，是诺斯替派主要关切之事的序幕：解释神圣元素如何进入人之中，以及它如何能返回其原初状态。《约翰密传》所讲述的故事（BG 47, 14-55, 17 及其平行文本 = Synopsis 37, 6-56, 10）与前一节并不完全连贯（这表明多种来源的糅合），但与伊里奈乌斯《反异端》I, 30 归给“其他人”而非他在 I, 29 所描述的“诺斯替派”的观点有许多共同之处。这种不连贯由于人与人之子作为至高神及其最初显现的突然引入而显现出来。由于雅尔达巴奥特宣称自己是唯一的神，一个声音响起说：“人存在，人之子也存在！”，而“神圣而完美的父，第一人”以人的形象向他显现。天上之人光辉的形象映在混沌的水中，造物主对侍立在他周围的诸权能说（或他们彼此说）：“让我们照着神的形象和样式造人”（参《创世记》1:26）。雅尔达巴奥特的七颗行星权能构成了制造人属魂身体的材料，这显示出柏拉图《蒂迈欧篇》的明显影响（van den Broek 1996, 67-85）。《约翰密传》的较长版本甚至将身体的构成归给不下365个“天使”（魔鬼），且都一一列名。毫无疑问，这份名单源自魔法资料（van der Vliet, 179-237）。造物主的助手们被证明无力唤醒并举起亚当那静止不动的属魂身体。于是万有之父派遣其子自生者偕四盏大光前往雅尔达巴奥特的世界，他们建议他：“向他脸上吹入你的一些灵，那造物便会起来”（参《创世记》2:7）。此时被等同于圣经创造者的造物主，将他的灵——即他母亲的神圣权能——吹入身体，身体便开始活动。神圣的灵就这样进入了人，人因这灵而比诸权能乃至造物主本人更有智慧。他们意识到他摆脱了邪恶，为囚禁他的神圣元素，便造了物质的身体。此后《约翰密传》讲述了乐园的故事，但它以诺斯替的意义加以解释：生命树是一棵死亡之树，禁止吃分别善恶树之果的命令，意在阻止亚当发现其神圣出身。

body.text: Even if a Gnostic text does not presuppose a myth of the kind described above, its perception of the human condition is the same as that of the mythological texts: man’s inner self is of divine origin, but he is unaware of it, because he is entangled in this material world and subjected to the passions of the body. He needs to be saved.
body.zh: 即使某个诺斯替文本并不以如上所述的神话为前提，它对人处境的看法也与那些神话文本相同：人的内在本真自我具有神圣本源，但他对此一无所知，因为他被纠缠于这个物质世界，并受身体情欲的支配。他需要被拯救。

body.text: c. Salvation Living in ignorance is often compared with a state of drunkenness or a sleep haunted by nightmares, and the attainment of knowledge is compared with becoming sober again and awakening in the bright daylight (for instance Gospel of Truth, NHC I, 22, 16-20; 28, 24-30, 16). Gnostic salvation is not the remission of sins but the rectification of a situation of ignorance. It might be said that ignorance is the original sin or, in the words of the Gospel of Philip, NHC II, 34, 30-31: ‘Ignorance is the mother of all evil’. In the section that precedes this statement, the author compares ignorance, the root of wickedness, with the root of a tree: if it is hidden in the earth, the tree sprouts and grows, but if it is exposed, the tree dries up and dies. And from this simile he draws the conclusion: ‘As for ourselves, let each one of us dig down after the root of evil that is within one, and let one pluck it out of one’s heart from the root. It will be plucked out if we recognize it. But if we are ignorant of it, it takes root in us and produces its fruit in our heart. It masters us. We are its slaves’. Gnosis is the spiritual understanding of our divine origin and the world we live in. As such, it is in fact self-knowledge, as Jesus says to his twinbrother Thomas in the Book of Thomas the Contender, NHC II, 138, 16-18: ‘For he who has not known himself has known nothing, but he who has known himself has at the same time already achieved knowledge about the depth of the All’ (a variant of the Armenian hermetic Definitions 9, 4; cf. Gospel of Thomas, 67, NHC II, 45, 19-20). But this spiritual knowledge of oneself and the All must be awakened: one must learn to understand. The spiritual leader of a Gnostic community can teach his pupils the essentials of Gnosis, but in the end his teachings derive from divine inspiration and revelation. This revelation is mostly given by a divine Revealer, who is often called the Saviour.
body.zh: c. 拯救 生活在无知之中常被比作醉酒状态或被噩梦缠绕的睡眠，而获得知识则被比作重新清醒过来、在明亮日光中醒来（例如《真理福音》NHC I, 22, 16-20; 28, 24-30, 16）。诺斯替的拯救不是罪的赦免，而是对一种无知状态的纠正。可以说，无知就是原罪；或者用《腓力福音》NHC II, 34, 30-31 的话说：“无知是万恶之母”。在这句话之前的一段中，作者将作为恶之根源的无知比作树根：若它藏在地下，树就发芽生长；若它被暴露出来，树就枯萎死去。他由这个比喻得出结论：“至于我们，让我们各人深挖自己里面恶的根，把它从心中连根拔除。若我们认出它，它就会被拔除。但若我们对它一无所知，它就在我们里面扎根，在我们心中结果。它辖制我们。我们是它的奴隶。”诺斯是对我们神圣本源以及我们所生活世界的灵性理解。就其本身而言，它实际上是自我认识，正如耶稣在《争战者多马之书》NHC II, 138, 16-18 中对其孪生兄弟多马所说：“因为那不认识自己的，什么也不知道；但那认识自己的，同时也已获得了关于万有之深度的知识”（这是亚美尼亚文赫尔墨斯《定义》9, 4 的一个异文；参《多马福音》第67则，NHC II, 45, 19-20）。但这种关于自身与万有的灵性知识必须被唤醒：人必须学会理解。诺斯替社团的灵性领袖可以教导其学生诺斯的要点，但他的教导最终源自神圣的灵感与启示。这种启示多半由一位神圣的启示者给予，他常被称为救主。

body.text: In Christian Gnostic texts the Saviour is identified with Christ, but in non-Christian texts, or at least those in which no Christian influence is discernible or which are only superficially Christianized, the Saviour is called by other names. In the Paraphrase of Shem (NHC VII, 1), the Revealer and Saviour is Derdekeas, the Son or Likeness of the Light, i.e. the second divine being, who gives his salvific revelation to a certain Shem. It has been suggested that this Shem is no other than Seth, the third Son of Adam, but there is no convincing evidence for this. However, in the Gospel of the Egyptians Seth appears as the Saviour, who imparts saving knowledge to those who belong to him (“the race of Seth”) and who, certainly secondarily, is identified with Christ (NHC III, 64, 1-3; IV, 75, 15-17: ‘Jesus the living one, he whom the great Seth has put on’). A similar doctrine about Seth was professed by the → Archontics. In the Apocryphon of John it is Christ who answers John’s questions, like a teacher instructs his pupil, but the real saving figure is a female power, called Epinoia of the Light, who ‘assists the whole creature, by toiling with him, and by restoring him to his fullness (plèròma) and by teaching him about the descent of his seed and by teaching him about the way of ascent’ (NHC II, 19-23 parr. = Synopsis 54, 8-13). The word epinoia means “thinking, reflection, thought” and is here virtually identical with ennoia, which in the Apocryphon is used as name of the Mother, the second divine being. At the end of the long version of the Apocryphon there is a beautiful Hymn of Pronoia, also called the Providence Monologue, in which it is not Epinoia or Ennoia but Pronoia (“Providence”) who acts as the Revealer and Saviour of mankind. There is no doubt that in this case Pronoia stands for the personified Wisdom, the manifestation of God in the world according to Jewish speculations (Waldstein 1995; van den Broek 1996, 86-116).
body.zh: 在基督教诺斯替文本中，救主被等同于基督；但在非基督教文本中，或至少在那些看不出基督教影响、或只是表面基督教化的文本中，救主另有其名。在《闪的释义》（NHC VII, 1）中，启示者与救主是德尔得卡斯（Derdekeas），即光之子或光之肖似，也就是第二位神圣存在，他把救赎的启示给予某个叫闪的人。有人提出，这个闪不是别人，正是亚当的第三个儿子塞特，但没有令人信服的证据。然而在《埃及人福音》中，塞特以救主的身份出现，将拯救的知识传授给属于他的人（“塞特的族类”），并且——无疑是次要地——被等同于基督（NHC III, 64, 1-3; IV, 75, 15-17：“活着的耶稣，伟大的塞特所披戴的那一位”）。执政官派（→ Archontics）也信奉类似的关于塞特的教义。在《约翰密传》中，回答约翰问题的是基督，就像老师教导学生一样，但真正起拯救作用的人物是一位女性权能，称为光之埃皮诺亚（Epinoia），她“扶助一切受造物，与他一同劳苦，使他恢复自己的丰盈（plèròma），教导他关于其种子的下降，并教导他关于上升之路”（NHC II, 19-23 及其平行文本 = Synopsis 54, 8-13）。epinoia 一词意为“思考、反思、思想”，在此实际上等同于 ennoia，后者在《约翰密传》中被用作母亲、即第二位神圣存在的名字。在《约翰密传》长版本的末尾，有一篇优美的《普罗诺亚颂》，又称“天意独白”，其中充当人类启示者与救主的不是埃皮诺亚或恩诺亚，而是普罗诺亚（Pronoia，“天意”）。毫无疑问，在此情形下普罗诺亚代表人格化的智慧，即按照犹太人的思辨，神在世界中的显现（Waldstein 1995; van den Broek 1996, 86-116）。

body.text: For Christian Gnostics, Christ was the Saviour par excellence. The Gospel of Truth, NHC I, 118, 16-20, says of Jesus that ‘he enlightened those who were in darkness through forgetfulness. He enlightened them and showed them a way. The way, then, is the truth which he taught them’ (cf. John 14:6). He is the Saviour because he reveals the truth about the unknown Father; his death on the cross has no salvific meaning. The Gnostics usually adhered to a docetic Christology, which means that they denied that Christ had a material body of flesh and blood. For them, and also for those who ascribed to Jesus a real human body and soul, as, for instance, Justin the Gnostic did, the crucifixion was primarily the event in which Christ’s pneumatic being was separated from its bodily envelope. Some Christian Gnostic texts, however, described the meaning of salvation in terms that were strongly influenced by biblical images and, for that reason, came close to those found in more “orthodox” writings. Thus the Gospel of Philip, NHC II, 52, 35-53, 4, uses the terminology of ransom: ‘Christ came to ransom some, to save others, to redeem others. He ransomed those who were strangers and made them his own’. But in this text as well, Christ is the Revealer of the hidden mystery of the Father. The Gospel of Truth in particular makes use of biblical images and expressions that even suggest a salvific meaning in the crucifixion. Christ was ‘nailed to a tree and became a fruit of the knowledge of the Father. It did not, however, cause destruction because it was eaten (cf. Genesis 2:17), but it gave gladness to those who ate it’ (NHC I, 18, 24-28). Jesus, ‘the merciful one, the faithful one, patiently accepted the sufferings . . ., since he knows that his death is life for many’ (NHC I, 20, 10-14). Nevertheless, the Gospel of Truth is a thoroughly Gnostic work: Christ ‘became a way for those who were gone astray and knowledge for those who were ignorant, a discovery for those who were searching, and a support for those who were wavering, immaculateness for those who were defiled’ (NHC I, 31, 28-35). Christian Gnostics of the 2nd century could sometimes speak about Jesus with much more warmth and spiritual depth than their non-Gnostic fellow Christians.
body.zh: 对基督教诺斯替派而言，基督是卓越的救主。《真理福音》NHC I, 118, 16-20 论耶稣说：“他光照了那些因遗忘而处于黑暗中的人。他光照他们，并指给他们一条道路。这道路就是他所教导他们的真理”（参《约翰福音》14:6）。他是救主，因为他启示了关于未知之父的真理；他在十字架上的死亡没有救赎意义。诺斯替派通常持幻影基督论，即否认基督有一个由血肉构成的物质身体。对他们来说，也对于那些把真实的人类身体与灵魂归于耶稣的人（例如诺斯替派的查士丁）来说，钉十字架首先是基督的属灵存在与其身体外壳分离的事件。然而，一些基督教诺斯替文本以深受圣经意象影响的措辞来描述拯救的意义，因而接近于那些更为“正统”的著作中的说法。例如《腓力福音》NHC II, 52, 35-53, 4 使用赎价的术语：“基督来，为要赎回一些人，拯救另一些人，救赎另一些人。他赎回了那些外人，使他们成为自己的”。但即便在此文本中，基督仍是父之隐秘奥秘的启示者。《真理福音》尤其使用了一些圣经意象与表述，甚至暗示钉十字架具有救赎意义。基督“被钉在木头上，成了关于父的知识的果子。然而它并未因被吃而带来毁灭（参《创世记》2:17），反而给吃它的人带来喜乐”（NHC I, 18, 24-28）。耶稣，“那位怜悯者、信实者，耐心地承受了苦难……，因为他知道他的死是许多人的生命”（NHC I, 20, 10-14）。尽管如此，《真理福音》仍是一部彻底的诺斯替著作：基督“成了迷途者的道路，无知者的知识，寻求者的发现，动摇者的支撑，污秽者的纯洁”（NHC I, 31, 28-35）。2世纪的基督教诺斯替派有时谈论耶稣时，比他们非诺斯替的基督徒同伴怀着更多的温情与灵性深度。

body.text: The completion of the Gnostic’s road of salvation is the return of his divine particle to the Pleroma. This happens at his death, but the salvation is in fact already enjoyed in this earthly life. The divine spark in human beings is often called the Pneuma (Spirit). The Valentinians, in particular, developed a subtle theory about the pneumatic, the psychic and the hylic (material) natures in the individual human being as well as in humankind as a whole. The treatise On the Origin of the World, NHC II, 122, 1-9, also distinguishes between three types of human beings: Pneumatics, Psychics and Choics (earthly people), which may point to Valentinian influence. However, many texts simply speak about the soul as the divine element in man. This is found, for instance, in the reports on the Archontics and the Naassenes, who both adhered to mythological forms of Gnosis, and also in non-mythological writings such as the Treatise on the Soul (NHC II, 6) and the Authentikos Logos (NHC VI, 3). In the Apocryphon of John, Christ describes three possible fates of the soul. The soul that has come to knowledge ‘is saved and taken up to the repose of the aeons’. Those who have not yet come to know the All are reincarnated in the prison of the body ‘until they are saved from forgetfulness and the soul acquires knowledge and thus becomes perfect and is saved’. Only those who once had Gnosis but renounced it ‘will be tortured with eternal punishment’ (BG 67, 18-71, 2 = Synopsis 70, 19-73, 14).
body.zh: 诺斯替派救赎之路的完成，是其神圣微粒返回普累若麻。这发生在他死时，但拯救实际上在此世生命中已经可以享有。人里面的神圣火花常被称为普纽玛（Pneuma，灵）。尤其是瓦伦廷派，就个体人以及整个人类中的属灵、属魂与属物（物质）本性，发展出一套精细的理论。《论世界的起源》NHC II, 122, 1-9 也区分三种类型的人：属灵者、属魂者与属土者（Choics，即地上之人），这可能表明瓦伦廷派的影响。然而，许多文本只是把灵魂说成人里面的神圣元素。例如，关于执政官派与纳阿森派的记载便是如此，这两派都坚持神话形式的诺斯；非神话性的著作如《论灵魂》（NHC II, 6）与《真言》（NHC VI, 3）亦然。在《约翰密传》中，基督描述了灵魂三种可能的命运。已达到知识的灵魂“得救，被提到诸移涌的安息之中”。那些尚未认识万有的人，则重新投生于身体的牢狱中，“直到他们从遗忘中被拯救，灵魂获得知识，从而变得完美并得救”。只有那些曾有过诺斯却背弃它的人，“将受永恒惩罚的折磨”（BG 67, 18-71, 2 = Synopsis 70, 19-73, 14）。

body.text: The ascent of the soul to the divine realm could only take place if it knew the passwords or possessed the seals that permitted it to pass the hostile rulers of the seven heavens. This idea was not typically Gnostic in itself, but it played an important role in the Gnostic imagination. Examples of passwords are to be found in the first Apocalypse of James, (NHC V, 32, 24-36, 1), the Gospel of Mary (BG 15, 1-17, 7), the Gospel of Thomas, log. 50 (NHC II, 41, 31-42, 7), and Origen’s Contra Celsum, VI, 30-31. The two Books of Jeû give an elaborate description, with drawings, of the “seals” and “signs” and the many aeons the soul has to pass through on its way upwards. Finally, the soul or the pneuma arrives at the place of its origin, the Pleroma. The state of bliss that it enjoys there is often called the Anapausis (“rest, repose”).
body.zh: 灵魂上升至神圣领域，只有在其知道口令或拥有印记——这些使它得以通过七重天的敌意统治者——的情况下才可能发生。这一观念本身并非诺斯替派特有，但它在诺斯替的想象中起了重要作用。口令的例子见于《雅各第一启示录》（NHC V, 32, 24-36, 1）、《马利亚福音》（BG 15, 1-17, 7）、《多马福音》第50则（NHC II, 41, 31-42, 7），以及奥利金《驳塞尔苏斯》VI, 30-31。两部《耶乌之书》配有图绘，详尽描述了“印记”与“标记”，以及灵魂在上升途中必须经过的众多移涌。最终，灵魂或普纽玛抵达其本源之处，即普累若麻。它在那里享有的至福状态常被称为阿纳帕乌西斯（Anapausis，“安息、休憩”）。

body.text: The Gospel of Truth, in which this conception plays a prominent role, says of those who have found the Anapausis of the Pleroma that ‘they rest in him who is at rest, . . . and the Father is within them and they are in the Father, being perfect, being undivided in the truly Good One, being in no way deficient in anything, but they are set at rest, refreshed in the Spirit’ (NHC I, 42, 21-33).
body.zh: 这一观念在其中占显著地位的《真理福音》，论到那些找到普累若麻之阿纳帕乌西斯的人说：“他们安息在那安息者里面，……父在他们里面，他们也在父里面，他们是完美的，在真正善者里面不可分割，丝毫不缺什么，而是得享安息，在灵里得以更新”（NHC I, 42, 21-33）。

body.text: d. Ethics Not only the anti-Gnostic writers, but the authentic Gnostic sources as well, testify that the Gnostic believers felt themselves elected and predestined to Gnosis. They were the ‘Immovable race’ and belonged to the ‘generation without a king’ (Apocalypse of Adam, NHC V, 82, 19f. and 83, 1ff.), and as such they had overcome the power of evil. The anti-Gnostic writers often inferred from this possibly somewhat arrogant attitude that the Gnostics felt themselves morally free to do whatever they wanted. The accusation of moral licentiousness – a well-known means of bringing opponents into disrepute – was often raised against the Gnostic believers. This has led to the long-standing scholarly opinion that there were two different types of Gnostics: ascetics, who stuck to a thoroughly ascetic way of life, including the rejection of marriage, and libertines, who rejected asceticism and even indulged in sexual licentiousness. However, the reports of the anti-Gnostic authors contain very little information that gives colour to their allegations of immoral behaviour in Gnostic groups; and even if they seem to have a point, for instance in the case of the → Carpocratians and the → Borborites, the evidence asks for a careful interpretation. Of more weight is the fact that there are no authentic Gnostic texts that advocate immoral behaviour. On the contrary, the whole Nag Hammadi Library is thoroughly ascetic, and it may be assumed that it was because of their asceticism that some non-Gnostic writings, such as the Teachings of Silvanus and the Sentences of Sextus, were included in the collection. But even if the Gnostics themselves taught a strong asceticism and did not show any indication of immoral or non-ascetic behaviour, their opponents suggested that they simply were keeping up appearances. Examples of such negative polemics are Irenaeus on → Satornilus (Adversus haereses, I, 24, 2), Clement of Alexandria on the followers of Prodicus (Stromateis, III, 30, 2-3), and Epiphanius on the Archontics (Panarion, 40, 2, 4). All the evidence suggests that the adherents of the Gnostic movement propagated and practised an ascetic way of life, which, however, did not need to imply the rejection of marriage. An important group like the Valentinians, for instance, held marriage in high esteem and considered it an image of the union of the soul with its heavenly counterpart in the Pleroma. The moral ideas of Clement of Alexandria, to whom we owe this information (Stromateis, III, 1, 1), did not differ much from those of Valentinus. At most there may have been a relative difference of emphasis between Gnostic and non-Gnostic Christians with respect to moral ideas and practices, in so far as the former tended to have a more negative view of the material world and the body and, therefore, may have been more inclined to a strongly ascetic way of life than their non-Gnostic fellow-Christians.
body.zh: d. 伦理 不仅反诺斯替作家，真正的诺斯替资料也证明，诺斯替信徒自认为是被拣选、预定得诺斯的人。他们是“不可动摇的族类”，属于“没有王的世代”（《亚当启示录》NHC V, 82, 19 以下与 83, 1 以下），因此他们已战胜恶的权势。反诺斯替作家常从这种或许有些傲慢的态度推断，诺斯替派自认为在道德上可以随心所欲。对道德放荡的指控——一种使对手名誉扫地的常用手段——常被加于诺斯替信徒。这导致了长期存在的学术见解，认为有两种不同的诺斯替派：严守彻底禁欲生活方式（包括拒绝婚姻）的禁欲者，以及拒绝禁欲、甚至沉溺于性放纵的放荡者。然而，反诺斯替作者的记载中，很少有什么信息能为其关于诺斯替团体不道德行为的指控提供依据；即便他们似乎言之有据，例如在卡波克拉底派（→ Carpocratians）与博尔博里特派（→ Borborites）的情形中，证据也需要谨慎解释。更有分量的是这样一个事实：没有任何真正的诺斯替文本提倡不道德行为。相反，整个拿戈玛第文库都是彻底禁欲的；可以设想，正因其禁欲主义，一些非诺斯替著作如《西尔瓦努斯教诲》与《塞克斯图斯箴言》才被收入该文集。但即便诺斯替派自己教导强烈的禁欲主义，且未显出任何不道德或非禁欲行为的迹象，其对手仍暗示他们只是装模作样。此类负面论战的例子有伊里奈乌斯论萨托尼卢斯（→ Satornilus，《反异端》I, 24, 2）、亚历山大的克莱门论普罗狄库斯的追随者（《杂记》III, 30, 2-3），以及埃皮法尼乌斯论执政官派（《药柜》40, 2, 4）。一切证据都表明，诺斯替运动的追随者宣传并实践一种禁欲的生活方式，然而这未必意味着拒绝婚姻。例如，瓦伦廷派这样一个重要群体就高度尊重婚姻，视之为灵魂与其在天上普累若麻中的对应者结合的映像。我们应把这一信息归功于亚历山大的克莱门（《杂记》III, 1, 1），而其道德观念与瓦伦廷的并无多大差别。充其量，诺斯替派与非诺斯替派基督徒在道德观念与实践上可能存在重点上的相对差异，因为前者倾向于对物质世界与身体持更否定的看法，因而可能比其非诺斯替的基督徒同伴更倾向于一种强烈禁欲的生活方式。

body.text: 3. Backgrounds and Relationships The origin of the Gnostic movement has been the subject of much debate, but this has not led to any kind of scholarly consensus. The main reason for this is that actually there never existed one clearly definable “Gnosticism”, but only a variety of related religious ideas and currents, which had the idea of salvific, revealed Gnosis as their common denominator. Michael Williams (1996) has convincingly argued that it is useless to continue the search for the origin of this complicated and variegated religious phenomenon. However, as he also pointed out, it is quite possible to clarify the origin and history of specific Gnostic traditions, such as those of Valentinianism and of what he called the “biblical demiurgical texts”. The authentic Gnostic texts of the Nag Hammadi Library show that important notions derived from Judaism, Greek philosophy and Christianity had a considerable influence on the various elaborations of the central Gnostic idea of salvation through knowledge.
body.zh: 3. 背景与关联 诺斯替运动的起源一直是许多争论的主题，但并未带来任何学术共识。其主要原因在于，实际上从未存在过一个清晰可定义的“诺斯替主义”，而只存在种种彼此相关的宗教观念与潮流，其共同点是对救赎性的、被启示的诺斯的观念。迈克尔·威廉斯（1996）令人信服地论证说，继续追寻这一复杂而多样的宗教现象的起源是徒劳的。然而，正如他也指出的，澄清具体诺斯替传统——如瓦伦廷主义的传统，以及他所谓的“圣经造物主论文本”的传统——的起源与历史，是完全可能的。拿戈玛第文库中真正的诺斯替文本表明，源自犹太教、希腊哲学与基督教的重要观念，对诺斯替关于通过知识得救这一核心观念的各种阐发产生了相当大的影响。

body.text: a. Judaism There is a broad scholarly consensus that Jewish traditions played an important part in the formation of mythological Gnosis, although opinions differ about the interpretation of this phenomenon [→ Jewish influences I]. As was already pointed out above (2A), the figures of Anthropos and Sophia can only be explained from Jewish speculations about the first manifestations of the transcendent God. Traditions found in the Jewish apocrypha and pseudepigrapha, but also speculations known only from Merkavah mysticism (Gruenwald 1982) have contributed to the formation of the Gnostic myths. Close analysis of such basic mythological texts as the Apocryphon of John, the Hypostasis of the Archons and On the
body.zh: a. 犹太教 学界广泛共识认为，犹太传统在神话性诺斯的形成中起了重要作用，尽管对这一现象的解释意见不一［→ 犹太影响 I］。如上文（2A）所指出的，安特罗波斯与索菲亚的形象只能从犹太人关于超越之神首批显现的思辨中得到解释。见于犹太伪经与伪托著作的传统，以及仅从梅卡瓦神秘主义才得知的思辨（Gruenwald 1982），都对诺斯替神话的形成有所贡献。对《约翰密传》《执政官的本质》和《论

body.text: Origin of the World has brought to light such a wealth of Jewish parallels that the conclusion that they originated in a Jewish milieu is inescapable. This has raised the question of whether the emergence of the Gnostic Demiurge and his identification with the biblical Creator can also be explained from Jewish sources. Rabbinic polemics show that there were minim, dissident Jews, who speculated about the existence of Two Powers in heaven, God and his agent or vice-regent, who was known under various names (Angel of the Lord, the Lesser Jahweh, the Name, Shekina, Man, Wisdom, etc.) and who shared in or was wholly responsible for the creation of the world (Segal, Fossum). The rabbis were vehemently opposed to this idea, because they considered it a serious threat to Jewish monotheism. It should be noticed, however, that in the Jewish (and Samaritan) sources there is no evidence whatsoever that this divine agent or intermediary was ever placed in opposition to God. Various suggestions have been made to explain how Jews could have come to a degradation of the God of their fathers to the status of a lower and bad Demiurge, but none of them have succeeded in convincing the majority of scholars. There is no evidence that suggests the existence of a distinctly mythological Gnosis in Judaism. Nevertheless, it seems certain that the earliest myths about the origin of evil and the world were developed by Jews who were well informed about apocryphal and mystical Jewish traditions, but had apparently lost the faith of their fathers in the God of Israel as the creator of the world. This might be explained out of a deeply felt disappointment with the apparent inability of this God to prevent the tragic events that happened to the Jewish people in the first century. However this may be, there is no reason to see the whole Gnostic movement as derived directly from Judaism.
body.zh: 世界的起源》这类基本神话文本的细致分析，揭示了如此丰富的犹太平行材料，以至于它们起源于犹太环境的结论不可避免。这引出了一个问题：诺斯替造物主的出现及其与圣经创造者的等同，是否也能从犹太来源得到解释。拉比论战表明，存在弥民（minim），即持异议的犹太人，他们思辨天上存在两种权能，即神及其代理者或摄政者，后者以各种名字为人所知（主的使者、较小的雅威、那名、舍金纳、人、智慧等），并且分享或完全负责世界的创造（Segal, Fossum）。拉比们激烈反对这一观念，因为他们认为它对犹太一神论构成严重威胁。然而应当注意，在犹太（以及撒玛利亚）资料中，绝无证据表明这位神圣代理者或中介曾被置于与神对立的位置。人们提出了各种建议，试图解释犹太人何以会把他们祖先的神贬低为一个较低而邪恶的造物主，但没有一种能说服大多数学者。没有证据表明犹太教中存在一种明确神话性的诺斯。尽管如此，似乎可以肯定，最早关于恶与世界之起源的神话，是由一些熟悉伪经与犹太神秘传统的犹太人发展出来的，但他们显然已丧失其祖先对以色列之神作为世界创造者的信仰。这或许可以解释为一种深切的失望：这位神显然无力阻止1世纪降临于犹太民族的悲剧事件。无论如何，没有理由把整个诺斯替运动视为直接源自犹太教。

body.text: b. G reek Philosophy The authentic Gnostic texts demonstrate beyond doubt the influence of Greek philosophy on Gnostic thought. Hippolytus of Rome (ca. 220) already argued that the Gnostics, like all heretics, had derived their ideas and systems from Greek philosophy and → astrology (Koschorke 1975). More recently, several experts in classical philosophy have studied the complicated relationship between philosophical and Gnostic ideas, with less prejudice and more competence than Hippolytus (inter al.
body.zh: b. 希腊哲学 真正的诺斯替文本无可置疑地证明了希腊哲学对诺斯替思想的影响。罗马的希波吕托斯（约220年）已经论证说，诺斯替派像所有异端一样，其观念与体系源自希腊哲学和→ 占星学（Koschorke 1975）。晚近以来，几位古典哲学专家以比希波吕托斯更少的偏见和更高的能力，研究了哲学观念与诺斯替观念之间的复杂关系（其中包括

body.text: Mansfeld, Armstrong, Dillon, Turner). The central question is whether or not Greek philosophy could have given rise to the Gnostic idea of the bad world and the evil Demiurge. In Orphism and early Pythagoreanism one may find an anthropological pessimism (incarnation as punishment, the body as a tomb) of which most Gnostics would have approved, but it is neither based on nor does it correspond to an equally pessimistic cosmology. Almost all Greek philosophers were convinced of the essential goodness of the cosmos; if they accepted a Demiurge, they declared him to be good as well. Only the Epicureans held that the world is not good, but a ‘random, meaningless, transitory and very badly arranged cosmos’ (Armstrong); but not only did they reject the idea of a Demiurge, their whole philosophy of life was in sharp contrast with that of the Gnostics. Especially in the 2nd century, there were Platonists who in several respects came close to the position of the more radical Gnostics. Plutarch and Atticus assumed a maleficent world soul as the principle of evil in the material universe, and Numenius taught the existence of two souls, a good and a bad one, both in the universe and in man; but neither of them introduced a Gnostic kind of strict cosmic dualism. The Neoplatonists [→ Neoplatonism I], and Plotinus in particular, espoused a more positive and worldaccepting attitude and strongly opposed the Gnostic view of the universe and its maker (Elsas).
body.zh: 曼斯菲尔德、阿姆斯特朗、狄龙、特纳）。核心问题是：希腊哲学是否可能产生诺斯替关于邪恶世界与恶的造物主的观念。在俄耳甫斯教与早期毕达哥拉斯主义中，可以找到一种人类学上的悲观主义（降生为惩罚，身体为坟墓），大多数诺斯替派会赞同它，但它既不基于、也不对应于同样悲观的宇宙论。几乎所有希腊哲学家都确信宇宙本质上是善的；若他们接受一位造物主，也宣称他是善的。只有伊壁鸠鲁派认为世界不是善的，而是一个“随机的、无意义的、短暂的、安排得极糟的宇宙”（Armstrong）；但他们不仅拒绝造物主的观念，其整个生命哲学也与诺斯替派形成鲜明对照。特别是在2世纪，有些柏拉图主义者在若干方面接近较激进的诺斯替派的立场。普鲁塔克与阿提库斯假定一个恶意的世界灵魂作为物质宇宙中恶的本原，努梅尼乌斯则教导存在两个灵魂，一善一恶，既在宇宙中也在人之中；但他们都没有引入诺斯替式严格的宇宙二元论。新柏拉图主义者［→ 新柏拉图主义 I］，尤其是普罗提诺，持一种更积极、更肯定世界的态度，并强烈反对诺斯替派关于宇宙及其制造者的观点（Elsas）。

body.text: The problems that were the philosophers’ concern – the relationship between the One and the many, or between the supreme God and lower levels of being, and the origin of evil – were of equal interest for the Gnostic thinkers. Since the latter did not live in a vacuum, they inevitably made use of current philosophical ideas to express their religious convictions. Moreover, from Hellenistic times onward, philosophy, and later Platonism in particular, had become increasingly religious. Under these circumstances, one understands that it is often difficult to draw a sharp borderline between philosophical and Gnostic writings, especially in the case of non-mythological Gnostic texts. In general, however, one can say that the philosophers sought philosophical solutions to philosophical problems, even if their language was religiously coloured, whereas the Gnostic thinkers sought religious answers to religious problems, even if they made use of philosophical terminology. The philosophers aimed at understanding, the gnostics sought and proclaimed salvation through revealed knowledge. A good example of the relationship between (even mythological) Gnosis and philosophical speculation is provided by the Gnostic treatise Zostrianus, which was known in the school of Plotinus. Describing the supreme God by means of the terminology of negative and affirmative theology (NHC VIII, 64, 11- 84, 22), the author makes use of the same Middle-or Neoplatonic source that was also used by the fourth-century Christian writer Marius Victorinus in his Adversus Arium, I, 49-50 (Tardieu 1996). Comparison of the texts shows that the Gnostic author quotes his source literally. However, he presents its contents as a revelation, which Zostrianus has received from an angelic interpreter called Salamex, during a heavenly journey. This Salamex has revealed to him the three aeons of Barbelo, which contain numerous other aeons, who are mentioned by name. The vision ends with the words: ‘Behold, Zostrianus, you have heard all these things of which the gods are ignorant’. Although the work testifies to a considerable Neoplatonic influence on third-century Gnostic speculations, its author was a fully-fledged Gnostic, who adhered to a type of “Sethian” Gnosis. Gnostic thought was not “a Platonism run wild” (Nock), nor was it a department of the “Platonic underworld” (Dillon).
body.zh: 哲学家所关注的问题——一与多的关系，或至高神与较低存在层次的关系，以及恶的起源——同样令诺斯替思想家感兴趣。由于后者并非生活在真空中，他们不可避免地使用当时的哲学观念来表达其宗教信念。此外，从希腊化时代起，哲学、尤其是后来的柏拉图主义，已变得越来越宗教化。在这种情况下，人们便能理解，为何往往难以在哲学著作与诺斯替著作之间划出鲜明界限，尤其是在非神话性的诺斯替文本方面。然而总的来说可以说，哲学家寻求对哲学问题的哲学解答，即便其语言带有宗教色彩；而诺斯替思想家寻求对宗教问题的宗教答案，即便他们使用哲学术语。哲学家的目标是理解，诺斯替派则寻求并宣告通过被启示的知识而得救。诺斯替论文《佐斯特里亚努斯》为（甚至神话性的）诺斯与哲学思辨之间的关系提供了一个好例子，该文在普罗提诺的学派中为人所知。作者以否定神学与肯定神学的术语描述至高神（NHC VIII, 64, 11-84, 22），使用了与4世纪基督教作家马里乌斯·维克托里努斯在《驳阿里乌》I, 49-50 中所用的同一中期或新柏拉图主义来源（Tardieu 1996）。文本比较表明，诺斯替作者逐字引用了其来源。然而，他把其内容呈现为一种启示，是佐斯特里亚努斯在一次天界之旅中从一位名为萨拉梅克斯（Salamex）的天使解读者那里接受的。这位萨拉梅克斯向他启示了芭比洛的三个移涌，其中包含众多其他移涌，且都一一列名。异象以这样的话结束：“看哪，佐斯特里亚努斯，你已听见所有这些连诸神都不知道的事。”尽管该著作证明3世纪诺斯替思辨受到相当大的新柏拉图主义影响，其作者却是一位彻底的诺斯替派，坚持一种“塞特派”诺斯。诺斯替思想既不是“一种失控的柏拉图主义”（Nock），也不是“柏拉图式地下世界”的一个部门（Dillon）。

body.text: c. Hermetism The philosophical Hermetica [→ Hermetic Literature I] and Gnostic literature in general have much in common, but there are also considerable differences. The similarities between Gnosticism and Hermetism are due to the fact that both originated and developed in the same time, in the same oriental part of the Mediterranean world, Egypt, and Alexandria in particular, and in the same spiritual climate. Both Gnostics and hermetists adhered to the widespread philosophical concept of God as a completely transcendent Being, who can only be described in the terms of negative theology. An important difference, however, was that according to the hermetists, the human mind was able to know God at least partially through the contemplation of the cosmos. Alhough the hermetists recognized that the material world could wholly absorb the human being, the cosmos always remained for them the beautiful product, the first son, of the supreme God. They could sometimes speak of the world as the ‘plenitude of vice’ (C.H. VI, 4), but they never ascribed the origin of the world to an imperfect and evil Demiurge. The “Way of Hermes” implied instruction concerning the nature of the cosmos, with the help of all kinds of sciences: theories of space and movement, astronomy (which included → astrology), medicine and → magic. Its aim was to make the world transparent toward God. Gnostic cosmological instruction, especially that of the mythological and radical type, only aimed at explaining how this world of darkness and evil had come into being. Another difference is that the abundant Gnostic mythology has no counterpart in Hermetism. The hermetic speculations about the divine world have nothing to offer that might be compared with the abundant Gnostic descriptions of the divine Pleroma. The only hermetic text that relates the origin of the world and man in the form of a myth is the Poimandres (C.H. I), but it is precisely this text that shows most clearly, inter alia by the introduction of the heavenly Anthropos, that it comes from the same background as, for instance, the Apocryphon of John. The Poimandres could be called a gnosticizing hermetic composition, but the author nevertheless remains a hermetist. He does not teach that the cosmos and the human body are bad in themselves, as the radical Gnostics did, but finds the origin of evil in sexual desire, which makes him an ascetic hermetist. In many respects, Gnosticism seems to have been a radicalization of important hermetic notions. Just like the Gnostics, the hermetists were convinced that the human soul or mind had its origin in God and that only through the gift of knowledge the original integrity could be restored, – an integrity which could already be experienced in this earthly life. Both offered a road to salvation, but this has led to two different religious systems.
body.zh: c. 赫尔墨斯主义 哲学性的赫尔墨斯文集［→ 赫尔墨斯文献 I］与诺斯替文献总体上有许多共同之处，但也有相当大的差异。诺斯替主义与赫尔墨斯主义的相似，是由于二者都起源并发展于同一时代、地中海世界同一东方地区（埃及，尤其是亚历山大里亚）以及同一精神氛围之中。诺斯替派与赫尔墨斯主义者都坚持一种广为流传的哲学观念：神是一个完全超越的存在，只能用否定神学的术语来描述。然而一个重要差异是，按照赫尔墨斯主义者的看法，人的心灵能够通过对宇宙的沉思至少部分地认识神。尽管赫尔墨斯主义者承认物质世界可能完全吞没人，但宇宙对他们来说始终是至高神美好的产物、他的长子。他们有时会说世界是“恶的充盈”（C.H. VI, 4），但从未把世界的起源归给一个不完善而邪恶的造物主。“赫尔墨斯之道”意味着借助各种科学——关于空间与运动的理论、天文学（包括→ 占星学）、医学与→ 魔法——来传授关于宇宙本性的知识。其目标是使世界对神透明。诺斯替的宇宙论教导，尤其是神话性的与激进类型的教导，则只旨在解释这个黑暗与恶的世界是如何产生的。另一个差异是，丰富的诺斯替神话在赫尔墨斯主义中没有对应物。赫尔墨斯主义关于神圣世界的思辨，没有什么可与诺斯替派对神圣普累若麻的丰富描述相比。唯一以神话形式叙述世界与人起源的赫尔墨斯文本是《波伊曼德勒斯》（C.H. I），但恰恰是这一文本最清楚地表明——除其他方面外，通过引入天上安特罗波斯——它与例如《约翰密传》来自同一背景。《波伊曼德勒斯》可称为一部诺斯替化的赫尔墨斯作品，但其作者仍是一位赫尔墨斯主义者。他并不像激进的诺斯替派那样教导宇宙与人的身体本身是恶的，而是在性欲中找到了恶的起源，这使他成为一位禁欲的赫尔墨斯主义者。在许多方面，诺斯替主义似乎是对重要赫尔墨斯观念的激进化。正如诺斯替派一样，赫尔墨斯主义者确信人的灵魂或心灵源于神，只有通过知识的恩赐才能恢复原初的完整——这种完整在此世生命中已经可以体验到。二者都提供了一条得救之路，但这导致了两个不同的宗教体系。

body.text: d. Christianity The Gnostic movement did not arise as a Christian heresy. Although there are no Gnostic works that in their present form are demonstrably pre-Christian, several treatises are certainly non-Christian or so superficially Christianized that the non-Christian original is still clearly recognizable. Moreover, the Gnostic religion of the → Mandaeans (“Gnostics”) cannot by any means be explained as an offshoot of early Christianity. A Gnostic work should only be called Christian if it presents Jesus or Christ as the decisive Saviour, who imparts salvific knowledge to the Gnostic believer.
body.zh: d. 基督教 诺斯替运动并非作为基督教异端而兴起。尽管没有一部诺斯替著作以其现存形式可证明是前基督教的，但有几篇论著确实是非基督教的，或只是表面基督教化，以至于其非基督教的原本仍清晰可辨。此外，曼达派（→ Mandaeans，“诺斯替派”）的诺斯替宗教绝不能解释为早期基督教的一个分支。一部诺斯替著作只有把耶稣或基督呈现为决定性的救主、由他向诺斯替信徒传授拯救的知识时，才应被称为基督教的。

body.text: In New Testament scholarship there has been much debate concerning the question of possible Gnostic influences on earliest Christianity. As an example, we may mention the discussion about the relationship between the prologue of the Gospel of John and the Trimorphic Protennoia (NHC XIII, 1). It has been claimed that the latter represents an earlier and better Gnostic version of the threefold descent of the Saviour than the prologue ascribes to the Logos. However, this threefold descent, which also determines the structure of the Hymn of Pronoia at the end of the Apocryphon of John, is derived from Jewish speculations about three descents of Wisdom. These speculations have apparently determined the myth of the threefold descent of the Saviour into the world of darkness, both in evidently Gnostic mythological texts and in the Gospel of John (van den Broek 1996, 86-116). Although this Gospel rejects the idea of a bad Demiurge (John 1:3, but cf. 8:44), it may nevertheless be called Gnostic too, since it puts much emphasis on the salvific meaning of Gnosis (John 1:18; 17:3). As a matter of fact, the Gospel of John easily lent itself to Gnostic exegesis (Pagels). If this Gospel had been unknown and had first come to light with the Nag Hammadi Library, it would certainly have been classified as a Gnostic or “gnosticizing” work.
body.zh: 在新约学界，关于诺斯替思想对最早基督教可能有何影响，曾有大量争论。举例来说，我们可以提到关于《约翰福音》序言与《三形的普洛特诺娅》（NHC XIII, 1）之间关系的讨论。有人主张，后者代表了一个比序言归于逻各斯的更早、更好的关于救主三重降临的诺斯替版本。然而，这一三重降临——它也决定了《约翰密传》末尾《普罗诺亚颂》的结构——源自犹太人关于智慧三次降临的思辨。这些思辨显然决定了关于救主三重降临黑暗世界的神话，既见于明显是诺斯替的神话文本，也见于《约翰福音》（van den Broek 1996, 86-116）。尽管这部福音拒绝邪恶造物主的观念（《约翰福音》1:3，但参 8:44），它仍可被称为诺斯替性的，因为它极为强调诺斯的救赎意义（《约翰福音》1:18; 17:3）。事实上，《约翰福音》很容易接受诺斯替式的解经（Pagels）。假如这部福音不为人知，而是随拿戈玛第文库首次问世，它必定会被归类为一部诺斯替的或“诺斯替化”的著作。

body.text: The relationship between the Gnostic movement and early Christianity can be best explained from the fact that both developed in the same spiritual climate, which was strongly influenced by Jewish ideas expressed in mythical forms. As said above (section 3A), Jews must have played an important role in the formation of the Gnostic myths. From Philo we know that there were Jews in Alexandria who rejected the beliefs and practices of their paternal religion. But the deeply pessimistic view of the human condition expressed in the early Gnostic myths cannot have been limited to some apostate Jews. It apparently reflected a more general experience of alienation from the world and a longing for salvation by spiritual knowledge, which is also evident in those Gnostic writings that do not show any specific Jewish influence. The Christian anti-Gnostic works of the 2nd and 3rd centuries testify to the great attraction of Gnostic views, and of the religious experience upon which they were based, on Christian thinkers or teachers and their followers. The result was a distinct Gnostic current within the variegated world of early Christianity. The most influential Gnostic variant of Christianity seems to have been Valentinianism, which was based on older mythological constructions (see above). That Valentinus and even his pupil Ptolemy were simply well educated Christian Platonists, who did not yet teach the “Valentinian” mythological Gnostic system that was taught by their followers, as has been argued from a church-historical point of view (Markschies), is highly unlikely. In the middle of the 2nd century, ecclesiastical leaders in Rome began to define the boundaries of the Church and, accordingly, to reject views that for a time had been acceptable within the Christian communities. The Christian teachers who taught the prevalence of Gnosis over faith or ascribed the creation of the world to a lower Demiurge were expelled from the Church and vehemently fought.
body.zh: 诺斯替运动与早期基督教之间的关系，最好从这一事实来解释：二者都发展于同一精神氛围之中，而这种氛围深受以神话形式表达的犹太观念影响。如上文（第3A节）所说，犹太人在诺斯替神话的形成中必定起了重要作用。从斐洛（Philo）我们得知，亚历山大里亚有一些犹太人拒斥其父辈宗教的信仰与实践。但早期诺斯替神话中对人类处境所作的深切悲观看法，不可能仅限于少数背教的犹太人。它显然反映了一种更为普遍的与世界相疏离的体验，以及一种通过灵性知识得救的渴望；这一点在那些未显示任何特定犹太影响的诺斯替著作中也很明显。2、3世纪的基督教反诺斯替著作证明，诺斯替观点以及其所依据的宗教体验，对基督教思想家或教师及其追随者具有巨大吸引力。其结果是在早期基督教多样的世界中形成了一个独特的诺斯替潮流。基督教中最有影响力的诺斯替变体似乎是瓦伦廷主义，它基于更古老的神话建构（见上文）。至于瓦伦廷乃至其学生托勒密只是受过良好教育的基督教柏拉图主义者、尚未教导其追随者所教导的“瓦伦廷派”神话诺斯替体系——这是从教会史角度提出的论点（Markschies）——则极不可能。2世纪中叶，罗马的教会领袖开始界定教会的边界，并据此拒斥那些一度在基督教社团内可被接受的观念。那些教导诺斯高于信仰、或把世界创造归给一个较低造物主的基督教教师，被逐出教会并遭到激烈攻击。

body.text: impossible. The scholarly term “Gnosticism” suggests a uniformity that never existed. If used at all – and then, of course, without any pejorative connotation –, the term should be reserved for the more elaborate mythological systems that were developed from the 2nd century onward. The Gnostic character of a considerable number of texts can be disputed, since their contents show a position intermediate between a distinct Gnostic and more philosophical, hermetic, or generally Christian views. The decisive criterion is whether or not esoteric knowledge is held to be indispensable for personal salvation, i.e. the return to one’s divine origin. But even this criterion is not always easy to apply, because the indispensability of Gnosis is sometimes merely presupposed rather than explicitly expressed. However, all these ambiguities are no reason to deny the existence of Gnostic religiosity in the Roman world and to declare terms as “Gnostic”, “Gnosticism”, “Gnostic movement”, etc. meaningless. The Gnostic religion, its mythological variants included, was not a degenerated form of Greek philosophy, nor did it arise as a Christian heresy. To some extent it was a religion in its own right, or at least a distinct religious mentality, which expressed itself in an almost inextricable combination of important notions derived from Jewish mysticism, Greek philosophy, and Christian theology. Its central belief found a succinct expression in the Christian Gnostic Testimony of Truth, NHC IX, 44,30-45, 6: ‘When man comes to know himself and God who is over the truth, he will be saved, and he will crown himself with the crown unfading’.
body.zh: 不可能。学术术语“诺斯替主义”暗示了一种从未存在过的统一性。若终究要使用这一术语——当然不带任何贬义——它应保留给2世纪以后发展起来的那些更为精致的神话体系。相当多文本的诺斯替性质是可以争论的，因为它们的内容显示出一种介于明确的诺斯替观点与更具哲学性、赫尔墨斯性或一般基督教观点之间的立场。决定性的标准在于，秘传知识是否被认为对个人得救、即对回归人神圣本源不可或缺。但即便这一标准也并不总是容易应用，因为诺斯不可或缺这一点有时只是被预设，而非明确表达。然而，所有这些含糊之处都不构成否认罗马世界存在诺斯替式宗教性、并宣布“诺斯替的”“诺斯替主义”“诺斯替运动”等术语毫无意义的理由。诺斯替宗教，包括其神话变体，既不是希腊哲学的退化形式，也不是作为基督教异端而兴起的。在某种程度上，它是一种自成一格的宗教，或至少是一种独特的宗教心态，它以源自犹太神秘主义、希腊哲学与基督教神学的重要观念几乎不可分割的结合来表达自身。其核心信仰在基督教诺斯替著作《真理见证》NHC IX, 44, 30-45, 6 中得到了简洁的表达：“当人认识了自己以及那在真理之上的神，他就会得救，并将以不朽的冠冕为自己加冕。”
