body.text: 1. Introduction
body.zh: 1. 导论

body.text: The literary works attributed to → Hermes Trismegistus reflect the various activities he was thought to have deployed. In accordance with his function as a teacher of → magic, → astrology, → alchemy and philosophically coloured religious knowledge, there are under his name magical spells, astrological and alchemical treatises and religious-philosophical discourses. In recent scholarship, there has been much discussion about the relationship between the “occult” magical, astrological and alchemical works on the one hand and the more philosophical religious tracts on the other. The two great scholars who worked on the Hermetica in the 20th century, Walter Scott and André-Jean Festugière, made an almost complete separation between the two kinds of literature. Festugière’s distinction between “popular Hermetism” (hermétisme populaire) and “learned” or “philosophical” Hermetism (hermétisme savant/philosophique) became almost universally accepted. In recent research, however, the more neutral term of “technical Hermetica” has become current for the magical, astrological and alchemical texts that go under the name of Hermes. This term indeed fits these texts better than the word “popular”, since they present primarily techniques to achieve personal objectives. The second kind of hermetic writings is still mostly called “philosophical”, and sometimes “theoretical”. The latter term should be avoided since it suggests that these works provide a theoretical basis for the technical, more practical Hermetica, which is by no means certain. In the first centuries of our era, Greek philosophy became increasingly religious and thinking about religion became more and more philosophical. To find confirmation of their ideas on ultimate reality, philosophers turned to divine revelation, and religious thinkers liked to express their beliefs in terms of Greek philosophy. Therefore, the term “philosophical Hermetica” is acceptable for almost all the works that are usually covered by that name, since they are strongly influenced by Greek philosophical ideas, especially those of Platonism and Stoicism. It would be wrong, however, to consider them as primarily philosophical works. On the contrary, they are essentially religious tracts, which make free use of Greek philosophical ideas to express their views on religious knowledge and individual salvation. As a matter of fact, the word “theosophical” would provide a better term, if it could be stripped of its modern connotations.
body.zh: 归于→赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯（Hermes Trismegistus）名下的文学作品，反映了他被认为曾从事的各种活动。与他作为→魔法、→占星学、→炼金术以及带有哲学色彩的宗教知识之教师的职能相应，他的名下流传着魔法咒语、占星学与炼金术论著，以及宗教—哲学论说。晚近的学术研究对“秘传的”魔法、占星学与炼金术著作同更具哲学性的宗教论著之间的关系，讨论甚多。20世纪研究赫尔墨斯文献的两位大学者沃尔特·斯科特（Walter Scott）与安德烈—让·费斯蒂吉耶（André-Jean Festugière），几乎把这两类文献完全割裂开来。费斯蒂吉耶对“通俗赫尔墨斯主义”（hermétisme populaire）与“博学”或“哲学”赫尔墨斯主义（hermétisme savant/philosophique）的区分，几乎被普遍接受。然而在晚近的研究中，对于归于赫尔墨斯名下的魔法、占星学与炼金术文本，较为中性的“技术性赫尔墨斯文献”（technical Hermetica）一词已日渐通行。这个名称确实比“通俗”一词更适合这些文本，因为它们主要提供的是达成个人目标的技艺。第二类赫尔墨斯著述仍多被称为“哲学性”的，有时也称“理论性”的。后一名称应当避免，因为它暗示这些著作为技术性、亦即更偏实践的赫尔墨斯文献提供了理论基础，而这一点绝非确定无疑。在我们纪元的最初几个世纪里，希腊哲学日益宗教化，而对宗教的思考也日益哲学化。哲学家为了给自己的终极实在观念寻求确证，转向神的启示；宗教思想家则乐于用希腊哲学的语言表述其信仰。因此，对于通常归入“哲学性赫尔墨斯文献”这一名下的几乎所有著作来说，这个名称都是可以接受的，因为它们深受希腊哲学观念、尤其是柏拉图主义与斯多亚主义观念的影响。然而，若把它们视为以哲学为主的著作，那就错了。相反，它们在本质上乃是宗教论著，自由地借用希腊哲学观念来表达其关于宗教知识与个人得救的看法。事实上，倘若“神智学的”（theosophical）一词能够摆脱其现代涵义，它倒会是一个更好的名称。

body.text: In recent research, the sharp distinction between technical and philosophical hermetic texts has been questioned. Scott and Festugière were convinced that the authors and audiences of the two kinds of hermetic literature were almost completely different. However, Garth Fowden has convincingly argued that both the technical and the philosophical hermetic writings emanated from the same cultural and religious milieu, namely that of Graeco-Roman Egypt in the centuries around the beginning of our era. According to Fowden, the technical and the philosophical Hermetica corresponded to successive stages on ‘the way of Hermes’, but there is no decisive proof for this contention. In some hermetic treatises initiation into the hermetic mysteries is attended by magic and astrology, but that does not imply that all magical or astrological texts ascribed to Hermes presuppose the typical ideas about knowledge and salvation that characterize the philosophical Hermetica.
body.zh: 晚近的研究对技术性与哲学性赫尔墨斯文本之间的截然区分提出了质疑。斯科特与费斯蒂吉耶确信，两类赫尔墨斯文献的作者与读者几乎完全不同。然而，加思·福登（Garth Fowden）令人信服地论证说，技术性与哲学性赫尔墨斯著述都出自同一个文化与宗教环境，即我们纪元开端前后几个世纪中的希腊化—罗马时期的埃及。按照福登的看法，技术性赫尔墨斯文献与哲学性赫尔墨斯文献对应于“赫尔墨斯之路”上先后相继的阶段，但这一主张并没有决定性的证据。在某些赫尔墨斯论著中，进入赫尔墨斯秘仪的入门礼伴有魔法与占星术，但这并不意味着所有归于赫尔墨斯的魔法或占星学文本都以哲学性赫尔墨斯文献所特有的那套关于知识与得救的观念为前提。

body.text: Unfortunately, an edition of all the technical Hermetica in one or more volumes does not exist, but there are two editions of the Greek and Latin philosophical Hermetica. Walter Scott made an edition in four volumes (1924-1936), with English translations and notes (the fourth volume, containing testimonia and fragments, was published by A.S. Ferguson). Though Scott’s works remains very valuable because of its wealth of information, the text edition itself is generally considered a failure, because of its hypercritical character, which resulted into a great number of unwarranted textual emendations. The standard edition of the Greek and Latin Hermetica, also in four volumes, has become the one published by A.D. Nock and A.-J. Festugière (1946-1954).
body.zh: 遗憾的是，目前并不存在一部把全部技术性赫尔墨斯文献汇为一卷或多卷的版本，但希腊文与拉丁文哲学性赫尔墨斯文献却有两部版本。沃尔特·斯科特编成四卷本（1924—1936），附英译文与注释（第四卷包含见证材料与残篇，由A. S. 弗格森［A. S. Ferguson］出版）。斯科特的著作因其材料丰富至今仍极有价值，但文本校勘本身通常被认为是一次失败，因为它过分挑剔，导致大量没有根据的文本改订。希腊文与拉丁文赫尔墨斯文献的标准版本，同样是四卷本，则是A. D. 诺克（A. D. Nock）与A.-J. 费斯蒂吉耶所刊行的版本（1946—1954）。

body.text: 2. Technical Hermetica
body.zh: 2. 技术性赫尔墨斯文献

body.text: The basic idea behind the technical Hermetica, and the philosophical as well, is the notion that all things that exist, both in the spiritual and in the material world, in some way or another are interconnected. This universal coherence or sympatheia could be the basis for quite different practices. It enabled the magician to bend gods or daemons to his will if he knew the appropriate divine names and the required materials to make a spell, but it also enabled the astrologer to foretell which days would be auspicious or inauspicious to take certain actions, because of the unalterable course of the heavenly bodies (fatum). The art of alchemy was based on two fundamental assumptions. The first is that there is a material substratum, some kind of “first matter”, which forms the basis of ordinary matter, and the second that all precious metals derive from lead and therefore can be made from it by performing the right alchemical procedure. In the first volume of his Révélation, Festugière has collected, translated and thoroughly studied a great number of astrological, magical and alchemical texts and fragments in Greek and Latin that are ascribed to Hermes. Though most of these texts date from the first centuries of the present era, there is little doubt that similar texts already circulated in the Hellenistic (Ptolemaic) period. In his Stromateis, VI, 35-37, → Clement of Alexandria describes a procession of Egyptian priests, possibly derived from the Egyptian priest and Stoic philosopher Chaeremon (1st century A.D.), who each carry the symbols and books that mark their position in the hierarchy. Clement mentions forty-two books, which he all attributes to Hermes, i.e. Thot. Among them are books containing hymns and instructions concerning the cult of the gods, but also four astrological books, ten hieroglyphic books on cosmography and geography, Egypt, the Nile, the construction of temples etc., and six medical books. Similar books are mentioned in a catalogue of books, inscribed on the walls of the library of the temple of Edfu. The library, which dates from 140-124 B.C., contained, inter alia, magical and astrological books, such as Spells for the averting of the evil eye, Knowledge of the recurrence of the two stars (i.e. sun and moon) and Control over the recurrence of the stars (cf. Fowden, 57-59). Hellenistic astrology owed only a little to earlier Egyptian observations of the celestial phenomena, even though its invention was ascribed to Thot/Hermes, but the Greek magical texts continued the early Egyptian magical literature under the name of Thot, even though they show unmistakable Hellenistic features.
body.zh: 技术性赫尔墨斯文献——哲学性文献亦然——背后的基本观念是：存在的一切事物，无论灵性世界还是物质世界中的，都以某种方式彼此相联。这种宇宙的普遍关联或“交感”（sympatheia），可以成为极为不同的各种实践的基础。它使魔法师在知道适当的神名以及制作咒语所需材料的情况下，能够迫使诸神或诸灵（daemons）服从他的意志；它同样使占星家能够预言，由于天体的运行不可更改（fatum，命运），哪些日子宜于或不宜于采取某些行动。炼金术这门技艺建立在两个基本假设之上。第一，存在某种物质性的基底，即某种“原初物质”，它构成普通物质的基础；第二，一切贵金属都源自铅，因而可以通过施行正确的炼金程序由铅制造出来。费斯蒂吉耶在其《启示》（Révélation）第一卷中，收集、翻译并详尽研究了大量归于赫尔墨斯的希腊文与拉丁文占星学、魔法与炼金术文本及残篇。这些文本大多属于我们纪元的最初几个世纪，但几乎无可怀疑的是，类似的文本在希腊化（托勒密）时期已经流传。→亚历山大的克莱门（Clement of Alexandria）在《杂缀集》（Stromateis）VI, 35-37中，描述了一队埃及祭司的游行，这一记载可能源自埃及祭司兼斯多亚哲学家凯瑞蒙（Chaeremon，公元1世纪）；这些祭司各自携带标志其等级地位的象征物与书籍。克莱门提到四十二部书，并全部归之于赫尔墨斯，即托特。其中有包含赞美诗与有关诸神崇拜之训示的书，也有四部占星学书、十部论述宇宙志与地理、埃及、尼罗河、神庙建造等的象形文字书，以及六部医书。类似的书籍见于一份书目录，该目录刻在埃德夫神庙图书馆的墙壁上。这座图书馆建于公元前140—前124年，其中收藏有魔法与占星学书籍，例如《驱避邪眼之咒》、《关于二星（即日与月）复现的知识》以及《对星辰复现的掌控》（参Fowden, 57-59）。希腊化占星学对更早的埃及天象观察所承甚少，尽管其发明被归之于托特／赫尔墨斯；而希腊魔法文本则在托特名下延续了早期埃及魔法文献，尽管它们带有明白无误的希腊化特征。

body.text: 3. Philosophical Hermetica
body.zh: 3. 哲学性赫尔墨斯文献

body.text: a. The Corpus Hermeticum The standard edition by Nock and Festugière has the comprehensive title Corpus Hermeticum on the front-page of each of the four volumes. As a matter of fact, all the hermetic philosophical texts preserved from Antiquity could indeed be said to constitute one great hermetic Corpus, for they all have the same literary structure, that of a dialogue, and the same kind of teaching. However, the title Corpus Hermeticum (C.H.) usually refers to a specific Byzantine collection of 17 hermetic texts, and it is in that sense that also Nock and Festugière take the term in their introductions and notes. The Byzantine scholar Michael Psellus (11th century) seems to have known the C.H. proper in roughly its present form, but there are no witnesses that attest its existence in earlier centuries. Stobaeus (5th century, see below) cited parts of C.H. II, IV, and IX in his Anthology, but he apparently did not yet know the C.H. as a collection. Nevertheless, the Vienna hermetic fragments, published by Mahé, show that such collections already existed at an early date. These fragments, which date from the late second or early 3rd century, were apparently part of a collection of at least 10 numbered treatises, for fragment B contains the end of treatise number 9 and the beginning of number 10. Bishop Cyril of Alexandria [ca. 440] also knew a collection of 15 books, called Hermaika, which had been composed by someone in Athens (Contra Julianum I, 41), but his quotations show that he had not the present C.H. before him. This evidence proves that the C.H. as a collection may be much older than the 11th century.
body.zh: a. 《赫尔墨斯文集》 诺克与费斯蒂吉耶的标准版本，在四卷各卷的扉页上都冠以《赫尔墨斯文集》（Corpus Hermeticum）这一总名。事实上，可以说古代保存下来的所有赫尔墨斯哲学文本确实构成了一部伟大的赫尔墨斯“文集”，因为它们都具有相同的文学结构，即对话体，以及同一类教导。然而，《赫尔墨斯文集》（C.H.）这一名称通常指某个特定的拜占庭时期汇编，共收十七篇赫尔墨斯文本；诺克与费斯蒂吉耶在其导论与注释中也正是在这个意义上使用该词的。拜占庭学者米海尔·普塞洛斯（Michael Psellus，11世纪）似乎已知道大体以现存形态流传的C.H.正编，但没有证据表明它在更早的世纪已经存在。斯托拜乌斯（5世纪，见下文）在其《文选》中引用了C.H. II、IV、IX的部分内容，但他显然尚不知道作为一部汇编的C.H.。尽管如此，由马埃（Mahé）刊布的维也纳赫尔墨斯残篇表明，此类汇编在很早的时期就已存在。这些残篇属于2世纪末或3世纪初，显然是一部至少含十篇编号论著的汇编的一部分，因为残篇B包含第九篇的结尾与第十篇的开头。亚历山大的主教西里尔［约440年］也知道一部名为《赫尔迈卡》（Hermaika）的十五卷集，它由雅典的某人所编纂（《驳尤利安》I, 41），但他的引文表明，他手头并没有现今的C.H.。这一证据证明，作为汇编的C.H.可能远早于11世纪。

body.text: The C.H. became known in the West through → Marsilio Ficino’s Latin translation (1463; published 1471) of a Greek manuscript that had been brought to Florence by the monk Leonardo of Pistoia, who presented it to Cosimo de Medici in 1460. This manuscript of the 15th century contains only the treatises I-XIV (Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Plut. 71, 33, ff. 123r-145r; Gentile & Gilly, 41-43). Ficino apparently did not know that the Greek cardinal Bessarion, already in 1458 and also in Florence, had acquired a more complete 14th century manuscript of the C.H., which also contained the tractates XVI-XVIII (Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana [Venice], Cod. Marc. Gr. Z. 242 [= 993]; Gilly & Van Heertum, II, 15-16). Treatise XV has never existed. Adrien Turnèbe, the first editor of the Greek text (Paris 1554; Gentile & Gilly, 126-128), made a fifteenth tractate from some hermetic excerpts by Stobaeus. This artificial treatise was left out again by later editors, who, however, retained Turnèbe’s numbering, so that the C.H. contains the treatises I-XIV and XVI-XVIII. Ficino gave his 14 treatises the collective title of Pimander (later editors wrote Poemander), after the title of the first tractate, Poimandres. However, the writings of the C.H. are not chapters of one and the same work, as Ficino thought, but completely independent compositions. The criterion that determined their selection into one collection is unknown. It has been suggested that Byzantine scholars selected them because of their relatively pure philosophical and religious contents; according to another view, they may have expurgated them of suspicious magical and astrological elements. As a matter of fact, the Coptic treatise On the Ogdoad and the Ennead (see below) gives these elements a prominent place in its description of an inner religious experience, whereas they are lacking in the otherwise closely related C.H. XIII. The Asclepius (see below) has in chapter 37 a famous passage about the theurgical conjuration of divine powers into the statues of the gods (a related idea is expressed in C.H. XVII), but the book as a whole is an excellent summary of hermetic religious philosophy. In view of the fact that magic and astrology were integral parts of the spiritual world in which the Hermetica originated, it may be assumed that magical and astrological elements appeared in many hermetic philosophical treatises. With respect to the C.H. we can only say that some cleansing by Byzantine editors cannot be excluded, but the Asclepius shows that there is no need to assume that this has happened on a large scale. It is not the place here to discuss the importance of the C.H. for our knowledge of classical → Hermetism, but some of its tractates deserve a closer examination.
body.zh: 《赫尔墨斯文集》是通过→马尔西利奥·费奇诺（Marsilio Ficino）的拉丁文译本（1463年译，1471年出版）而为西方所知的；他翻译的是一部由修士皮斯托亚的列奥纳多（Leonardo of Pistoia）带到佛罗伦萨的希腊文抄本，后者于1460年将其呈献给科西莫·德·美第奇。这部15世纪的抄本只包含第I—XIV篇（Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Plut. 71, 33, ff. 123r-145r；Gentile & Gilly, 41-43）。费奇诺显然不知道，希腊血统的枢机贝萨里翁（Bessarion）早在1458年也已在佛罗伦萨购得一部更完整的14世纪C.H.抄本，其中还包含第XVI—XVIII篇（Biblioteca Nazionale Marciana［威尼斯］, Cod. Marc. Gr. Z. 242 ［= 993］；Gilly & Van Heertum, II, 15-16）。第十五篇从未存在过。阿德里安·图尔内布（Adrien Turnèbe）是希腊文文本的第一位校勘者（巴黎，1554年；Gentile & Gilly, 126-128），他从斯托拜乌斯所保存的一些赫尔墨斯摘录中拼凑出第十五篇。这篇人为的论著后来又被晚出的校勘者删去，但他们保留了图尔内布的编号，因此C.H.包含第I—XIV篇与第XVI—XVIII篇。费奇诺仿照第一篇的标题《波伊曼德列斯》（Poimandres），给他所译的十四篇取了一个总名《皮曼德》（Pimander；后来的编者写作Poemander）。然而，C.H.中的各篇并不是费奇诺所设想的那种同一部著作的章节，而是完全独立的作品。把它们选入同一部汇编的标准是什么，已不得而知。有人提出，拜占庭学者之所以选取这些作品，是因为其哲学与宗教内容相对纯粹；另一种看法则认为，他们可能删去了其中可疑的魔法与占星学成分。事实上，科普特文论著《论八重与九重》（见下文）在描述一种内在宗教经验时，赋予这些成分以显著地位，而在与之关系密切的C.H. XIII中，这些成分却付之阙如。《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》（见下文）第37章有一段著名文字，论述以神术（theurgy）召请神力进入神像（C.H. XVII中也表达了相关的观念），但整部书仍是赫尔墨斯宗教哲学的一份出色概述。鉴于魔法与占星学是赫尔墨斯文献赖以产生的精神世界中不可分割的组成部分，可以设想，魔法与占星学成分曾出现在许多赫尔墨斯哲学论著中。就C.H.而言，我们只能说，不能排除拜占庭编者的某种净化处理，但《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》表明，并无必要假定这种处理曾大规模发生。此处不宜讨论C.H.对我们认识古典→赫尔墨斯主义的重要性，但其中若干篇值得更仔细的考察。

body.text: b. Some Treatises of the Corpus Hermeticum C.H. I, the first tractate of the C.H., entitled Poimandres, is the most well-known and one of the most important hermetic writings, but at the same time it is singular because of its strongly mythological character. It is not a first-hand teaching of Hermes Trismegistus to a pupil but a report of an unnamed person about a revelation received from a divine being, who introduces himself as ‘I am Poimandres, the intelligence (nous) of the supreme authority’. The recipient of this revelation was later identified with Hermes Trismegistus, as appears, inter alia, from the title in the manuscripts and C.H. XIII, 15. The idea that the divine Nous instructs Hermes is also found in C.H. XI. The name Poimandres has often been interpreted as “Shepherd (poimèn) of men (andres)”, both in the later hermetic tradition and by modern scholars, but this is linguistically impossible. Peter Kingsley has convincingly argued that the name is a Greek form of the Egyptian p-eime nte-rè, ‘the intelligence (or understanding) of Re’, and that the rest of the introductory formula, ‘the intelligence of the supreme authority (tès authentias nous)’, simply is a Greek translation of the name Poimandres.
body.zh: b. 《赫尔墨斯文集》中的若干论著 C.H. I是C.H.的第一篇，题为《波伊曼德列斯》，是最著名、也是最重要的赫尔墨斯著述之一，但与此同时，它因其强烈的神话色彩而显得独特。它不是赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯对弟子的第一手教导，而是一个未具名者关于从一位神性存在那里获得启示的报告，这位存在自我介绍说：“我是波伊曼德列斯，至高权威的努斯（nous，心智）。”这一启示的接受者后来被等同于赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯，这一点从抄本标题以及C.H. XIII, 15等处可以看出。神性努斯教导赫尔墨斯的观念，也见于C.H. XI。“波伊曼德列斯”一名常被解释为“人的（andres）牧者（poimèn）”，无论在后期赫尔墨斯传统中还是在现代学者那里都是如此，但这在语言学上是不可能的。彼得·金斯利（Peter Kingsley）令人信服地论证说，这个名字是埃及语p-eime nte-rè（“瑞［Re］的智能或理解”）的希腊语形式，而开场套语中其余部分“至高权威的努斯（tès authentias nous）”，不过是对波伊曼德列斯这一名字的希腊语翻译。

body.text: After the introduction, the Poimandres presents, in the form of a vision, a cosmological, anthropological and eschatological myth, followed by the command to preach the hermetic message, and a final hymn. The Poimandres teaches a dualism between light and darkness, spirit and matter, but not an absolute dualism. Primeval matter was a watery substance that came into existence within the darkness, which somehow had originated out of the light. The light was the divine Intelligence or Mind (nous), and out of it appeared the Word (logos), which is the ‘Son of God’. From this, the author immediately draws an anthropological consequence by establishing a distinct parallelism between God and man: ‘That what sees and hears within you is the word of the Lord, and your mind is God the Father; they are not separate from one another, for their union is life’ (I, 6). In the process of creation, the Word separated the elements, so that fire and air went on high, whereas water and earth remained below. The divine Mind, ‘being androgyne and existing as light and life’, gave birth to two other divine beings: a second Mind (nous), a craftsman, who created the seven planets ‘whose government is called fate’, and Man (Anthropos), who had his father’s image and was loved by him as his own form and received from him the dominion over everything that had been made (I, 9-13). The heavenly Anthropos looked though the cosmic framework and displayed the form of God to lower nature. Nature saw his shape in the water and his shadow on the earth, and she smiled with love (similar ideas on the Anthropos in → Gnosticism). When the divine Man saw the reflection of his image, he loved it and wanted to be united with it, and nature ‘enfolded him completely and they united, for they loved each other’. For this reason, man is a double being: ‘mortal because of the body, immortal because of the real Man’ (I, 14-15). After a period of seven androgyne generations the human beings became male and female, for which no reason is given, and they were commanded to increase and multiply. This command is clearly influenced by Gen. 1:28, but it has some negative overtones, for the dissolution of androgyny entailed sexuality, procreation, birth and death. By all this, human beings run the risk of forgetting their divine descent, and, therefore, the injunction to increase and multiply is followed by the warning not to lose sight of one’s origin: ‘Let him who is endowed with mind (nous) recognize that he himself is immortal and that sexual desire is the cause of death, and let he so know all that exists’ (I, 18). Who has understood himself comes to God (I, 21), which is the basic idea of hermetic salvation. In ascending to its origin the soul leaves its characteristic (mostly bad) features to the planets from which it had received them at its descent, and then, stripped of the astral influences, its real self enters the eighth sphere and joins the hymns sung by those who are there. Finally, they all ascend to the heaven above the eighth sphere, become powers and are merged in God: ‘This is the final good for those who have received knowledge (gnosis): to become God’ (I, 26).
body.zh: 在引言之后，《波伊曼德列斯》以幻象的形式呈现一则宇宙论、人类学与末世论的神话，随后是传扬赫尔墨斯信息的命令，以及结尾的赞美诗。《波伊曼德列斯》教导光与暗、灵与物之间的二元论，但不是绝对的二元论。原初物质是一种水样的实体，在黑暗之中生成，而黑暗又以某种方式出自光。光就是神性的智能或心智（nous），从它之中显现出“言”（logos），即“神之子”。作者由此立即引出人类学的结论，在神与人之间建立起一种清晰的平行关系：“在你之内观看和聆听的，是主的言；你的心智则是父神；二者彼此并不分离，因为它们的结合就是生命”（I, 6）。在创世过程中，言把诸元素分开，于是火与气升至上处，水与土则留在下方。神性心智“既是雌雄同体的，又作为光与生命而存在”，它生出另外两个神性存在：第二个心智（nous），一位工匠，造出七颗行星，“其统治被称为命运”；以及人（Anthropos），他具有其父的形象，被父作为自身的形相所爱，并从父那里获得对一切受造之物的统辖权（I, 9-13）。天上的Anthropos透过宇宙的框架观看，把神的形相显示给低级自然。自然在水中看见他的形貌，在地上看见他的影子，便怀着爱微笑（关于Anthropos的类似观念，见→诺斯替主义）。当神性之人看见自己形象的倒影时，他爱上了它，并想与之结合，于是自然“把他完全裹住，他们结合了，因为他们彼此相爱”。正因如此，人是一种双重存在：“因身体而会死，因真正的人而不死”（I, 14-15）。经过七个雌雄同体的世代之后，人类分化为男与女，文中未给出理由，他们且被吩咐要生养众多。这一命令显然受到《创世记》1:28的影响，但它带有某种消极的弦外之音，因为雌雄同体状态的解体伴随着性、生殖、出生与死亡。凡此种种，使人类有忘记其神性来源的危险，因此，在生养众多的命令之后紧接着便是警告，不可忘记自己的本源：“凡被赋予努斯者，应认识他自己是不死的，并认识性欲是死亡之因，且应如此认识一切存在者”（I, 18）。凡认识了自己的人便走向神（I, 21），这是赫尔墨斯得救观念的基本思想。灵魂在上升返回其本源时，把它特有的（大多是恶劣的）特征留给诸行星——这些特征是它在下降时从它们那里领受的；随后，在剥除星体影响之后，它真正的自我进入第八重天，加入那里诸存在所唱的赞美诗。最后，它们全都上升到第八重天之上的天界，成为诸权能，并融入神之中：“对于已获得知识（gnosis）的人，这是最终的善：成为神”（I, 26）。

body.text: After the command to preach the hermetic gospel, a short description of its contents and the reaction it received (I, 26-29), the Poimandres concludes with a hymn of nine lines, which might be called a triple Trishagion since all lines begin with “Holy”: “Holy is God” (3x) and “Holy are you” (6x). The hymn passes into a prayer in prose, in which “Hermes” bears witness to his salvation: ‘I go to life and light. You are blessed, Father’(I, 32). This hymn has also had an independent circulation and was even included in a Christian hymn book of the 3rd century, but most probably it was part of the Poimandres from the beginning. The hymn and the Poimandres as a whole are permeated with Jewish ideas, which suggest that this writing originated in a milieu in which Jews played an important part (Dodd, Philonenko, Pearson). Other elements can be best explained from an Egyptian background, which points to
body.zh: 在传扬赫尔墨斯福音的命令、对其内容的简短描述以及它所得到的反应（I, 26-29）之后，《波伊曼德列斯》以一首九行的赞美诗作结；由于所有诗行都以“圣哉”开头，它或可称为三重《三圣颂》：“圣哉，神”（3次）与“圣哉，你”（6次）。这首赞美诗转入一段散文祈祷，其中“赫尔墨斯”为自己的得救作证：“我走向生命与光。你是有福的，父啊”（I, 32）。这首赞美诗也曾独立流传，甚至被收入一部3世纪的基督教赞美诗集，但它很可能从一开始就是《波伊曼德列斯》的组成部分。这首赞美诗以及整篇《波伊曼德列斯》都浸透着犹太观念，这表明该著作出自一个犹太人起重要作用的圈子（Dodd, Philonenko, Pearson）。其他成分最好从埃及背景加以解释，这指向

body.text: Alexandria as its place of origin. Since the large Jewish community in Alexandria was almost completely extirpated during the revolt of A.D. 117-119, it seems probable that the Poimandres dates from the 1st century or the beginning of the second, which would make it one of the earliest hermetic writings. It has some central themes in common with the Gospel of John, e.g. God as life and light, but there is no indication of a direct Christian influence, let alone that it would represent a “paganization” of original Christian ideas (Büchli).
body.zh: 亚历山大里亚为其成书地点。由于亚历山大里亚庞大的犹太社群在公元117—119年的起义中几乎被彻底消灭，因此《波伊曼德列斯》很可能成书于1世纪或2世纪初，若然，它便是最早的赫尔墨斯著述之一。它与《约翰福音》有一些共同的核心主题，例如神作为生命与光，但没有任何迹象表明存在直接的基督教影响，更谈不上它是对原初基督教观念的“异教化”（Büchli）。

body.text: – C.H. IV has a double title: The mixing bowl (Crater) or the Monad, which refers to the two parts of this “Discourse of Hermes to Tat”. The first part (IV, 1-10) argues, contrary to the whole Greek philosophical tradition, that intelligence or mind (nous) is not the possession of every human being, but a heavenly gift which may be added to his reasoning capacity (logos). As a result the text distinguishes between two classes of men, the ‘reasonable people’ (logikoi) and those who have received nous. Closely related ideas are found among the Valentinian Gnostics [→ Valentinus and Valentinians]. As a matter of fact, the nous of this treatise identifies with the pneuma that characterizes the Gnostic. Though being a gift of God, the nous is in this treatise at the same time a prize, in the form of a mixing bowl, which has to be won in the contest of life. The crater is presented as a kind of baptismal font, in which the souls of the logikoi that make use of their logos have to immerse themselves. It has often been suggested that this passage alludes to a hermetic initiatory rite or “sacrament”, which implied the drinking from a crater, as in the Greek mystery religions. The second part of this treatise, which deals with God as a Monad, the origin and root of everything, remains within the framework of Greek philosophy.
body.zh: ——C.H. IV有一个双重标题：《调合碗（Crater），或论单体》，分别指这篇“赫尔墨斯对塔特的讲说”的两个部分。第一部分（IV, 1-10）与整个希腊哲学传统相反，论证智能或心智（nous）并非人人都拥有，而是一种天赐的礼物，可以加于人的推理能力（logos）之上。因此，文本区分了两类人：“有理性者”（logikoi）与那些领受了努斯的人。在瓦伦廷派诺斯替教徒中可以看到密切相关的观念［→瓦伦廷与瓦伦廷派］。事实上，这篇论著中的努斯与诺斯替教徒所特有的普纽玛（pneuma）是同一回事。努斯虽是神的礼物，在这篇论著中同时又是一种奖品，以调合碗的形式出现，必须在人生的竞赛中赢得。这只碗被描述为一种洗礼池，那些运用其逻各斯的“有理性者”的灵魂须在其中浸入。人们常提出，这段文字暗指某种赫尔墨斯入门仪式或“圣事”，其中包含从碗中饮用，一如希腊秘仪宗教中的做法。这篇论著的第二部分讨论神作为单体，即万物的本源与根基，仍处于希腊哲学的框架之内。

body.text: – C.H. V is also a discourse of Hermes to Tat, entitled: God is invisible and entirely visible. It argues that God can be known from the contemplation of his works, which in itself is a common Stoic idea. According to the author, however, this is not a “natural” knowledge of God, for God is unknowable; it is a divine gift, an act of divine grace: ‘Ask him the grace to enable you to understand so great a God, to permit even one of his rays to illuminate your thinking’ (IV, 2).
body.zh: ——C.H. V同样是赫尔墨斯对塔特的讲说，题为《神不可见而又全然可见》。它论证，人可以从对神之作品的沉思中认识神，这本身是斯多亚派的常见观念。然而，按照作者的说法，这并不是对神的“自然”认识，因为神是不可知的；它是神的礼物，是神恩典的行为：“向他祈求恩典，使你能理解如此伟大的一位神，允许他的哪怕一道光芒照亮你的思想”（IV, 2）。

body.text: – C.H. VI has often been used to demonstrate that in Antiquity there existed a radical negative form of Hermetism, alongside a more positive one. Starting from the common idea that the Good is in fact identical with God, the author draws a conclusion that would have been subscribed by radical
body.zh: ——C.H. VI常被用来证明，在古代存在一种激进的否定式赫尔墨斯主义，与一种较为肯定的形式并存。作者从善实际上与神同一这一常见观念出发，得出一个只有激进的

body.text: Gnostics only. It is aptly expressed in the title of the treatise: The Good is alone in God and nowhere else. For that reason, ‘the cosmos is the plenitude (pleroma) of evil, as God is the plenitude of the good, or the good of God’ (VI, 4).
body.zh: 诺斯替教徒才会赞同的结论。这一结论恰当地体现在该论著的标题中：《善唯在神之中，别无他处》。正因如此，“宇宙是恶的普累若麻（pleroma），正如神是善的普累若麻，或神之善的普累若麻”（VI, 4）。

body.text: – C.H. VII, entitled Ignorance concerning God is the greatest evil, is a hermetic sermon, an incitement to leave the drunkenness of ignorance behind and to seek the way to the ‘gate of knowledge’, where the pure light is and nobody gets drunk but all are sober and look with the heart at Him who wants to be seen, but who can only be seen by the nous and the heart. The human body is in the strongest terms described as an impediment to see the beauty of truth and the Good.
body.zh: ——C.H. VII题为《对神的无知是最大的恶》，是一篇赫尔墨斯布道文，劝人摆脱无知的醉态，寻求通往“知识之门”的道路；在那里有纯净的光，无人醉倒，众人皆清醒，并以心仰望那位愿意被看见、却只能被努斯与心看见的神。人的身体被以最强烈的措辞描述为看见真理之美与善的障碍。

body.text: – C.H. X, entitled The Key, is a discussion of some basic hermetic tenets: God the Father as the supreme Good, the contemplation of God as a divine gift, ignorance as the greatest evil for the soul, the immortal Cosmos as the second level of being and mortal man as the third. This treatise is interesting in particular because of its doctrine of the soul and its fate after death (X, 13-25). The mind (nous) is enclosed within reason (logos), reason within the soul (psychè), the soul within the astral body (pneuma), which passes through veins, arteries and the blood and moves the living carnal body. At death the nous of a pious soul puts on its own garment of fire and becomes pure Nous, but the impious soul has to reincarnate in a new human body.
body.zh: ——C.H. X题为《钥匙》，讨论若干赫尔墨斯基本教义：父神作为至高的善；对神的沉思作为神赐的礼物；无知作为灵魂最大的恶；不死的宇宙作为存在的第二层级；有死的人作为第三层级。这篇论著尤其因其关于灵魂及其死后命运的学说而有趣（X, 13-25）。心智（nous）包藏于理性（logos）之内，理性包藏于灵魂（psychè）之内，灵魂包藏于星体之体（pneuma）之内，而后者穿行于静脉、动脉与血液之中，推动活着的肉身。虔诚灵魂的努斯在死亡时穿上它自己的火之衣袍，成为纯粹的努斯；而不敬的灵魂则必须转生于新的人体之中。

body.text: – C.H. XIII is one of the most important hermetic writings. It is a ‘discourse of Hermes Trismegistus to his son Tat’, entitled A Secret Discourse on the Mountain about Rebirth and the Promise to be Silent. As a matter of fact, it is a dialogue that is said to have taken place after Hermes and Tat had come down from a mountain. Hermes says about his own rebirth that he has come out of his former self into an immortal body, which has no colour and cannot be touched or measured; he is re-born in the divine Nous (XIII, 3). Tat is exhorted to turn into himself and to cleanse himself from the twelve tormenting spirits of the material world, which are somehow connected with the twelve signs of the Zodiac: ignorance, sorrow, intemperance, lust, injustice, greed, deceit, envy, treachery, anger, recklessness, and malice. They withdraw one by one from the one who receives God’s mercy: ‘This is the manner and meaning of rebirth’ (XIII, 7 and 12). Spiritual rebirth is actualised by the arrival of ten good ‘spirits’: knowledge of God, joy, self-control, steadfastness, justice, generosity, truth, the good, life and light. Whoever has attained divine birth by God’s mercy ‘knows himself as constituted of these powers and he rejoices’ (XIII, 8-10). Within the exposition of the twelve bad and the ten good powers, the tractate somewhat unexpectedly describes a spiritual experience by Tat, which apparently is the effect of his own rebirth. This experience, in which he falls together with the whole cosmos (XIII, 11), differs from that of the ascent to the ninth sphere as described in the Poimandres and in the Ogdoad and the Ennead, which shows that initiation into the hermetic mysteries could lead to quite different mystical experiences. Through his rebirth Tat has been born a god, a child of the One, and he wants to hear the hymn of praise that according to the Poimandres was sung in the Ogdoad (I, 26). This song, the hymn of rebirth, can be heard in silence only; it cannot be taught; it is a secret kept in silence. Then follows, after some instructions, a beautiful hymn, which celebrates the beauty of the cosmos and the glory of its creator. It is indicated in the manuscripts as ‘Secret Hymn Book, Song 4’, which suggest that once it was part of a collection of hymns and may have had an independent circulation. Whether this is true or not cannot be established with any certainty, but it is by no means impossible, for also the hymns at the end of both the Poimandres and the Asclepius were transmitted independent of the texts to which they now belong. C.H. XIII concludes its report of a spiritual enlightenment with the words: ‘Now you have come to spiritual knowledge of both yourself and our Father’.
body.zh: ——C.H. XIII是最重要的赫尔墨斯著述之一。它是“赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯对其子塔特的讲说”，题为《论重生与守默之誓的山中秘谈》。事实上，这是一场据说发生在赫尔墨斯与塔特下山之后的对话。赫尔墨斯谈到自己的重生，说他已从先前的自我中走出，进入一个不死的身体，这个身体没有颜色，不可触摸，也不可测量；他是在神性努斯中重生的（XIII, 3）。塔特被劝勉转向自身，并从物质世界的十二个折磨人的恶灵中洁净自己，这些恶灵与黄道十二宫有某种联系：无知、悲伤、无节制、淫欲、不义、贪婪、欺诈、嫉妒、背叛、愤怒、鲁莽与恶意。它们从一个蒙受神怜悯的人身上逐一退去：“这就是重生的方式与意义”（XIII, 7与12）。属灵的重生因十个善“灵”的到来而成为现实：对神的知识、喜乐、自制、坚忍、正义、慷慨、真理、善、生命与光。凡因神的怜悯而获得神性诞生的人，“认识自己是由这些权能构成的，并且欢欣”（XIII, 8-10）。在阐述十二个恶的权能与十个善的权能之间，这篇论著出人意料地描述了塔特的一种灵性经验，这显然是他自身重生的效果。在这一经验中，他与整个宇宙合而为一（XIII, 11），它不同于《波伊曼德列斯》以及《论八重与九重》中所描述的升入第九重天的经验，这表明进入赫尔墨斯秘仪的入门礼可能导向颇为不同的神秘经验。通过重生，塔特已作为一个神、太一之子而诞生，他想听那首据《波伊曼德列斯》所说在八重天中咏唱的赞美诗（I, 26）。这首歌，即重生的赞美诗，只能在静默中听到；它不可传授；它是守于静默之中的秘密。接着，在若干指示之后，是一首优美的赞美诗，歌颂宇宙之美及其造物主的荣耀。抄本中把它标为“秘诗篇，第四歌”，这暗示它曾属于一部赞美诗集，并可能曾独立流传。此事是否属实无法确证，但绝非不可能，因为《波伊曼德列斯》与《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》末尾的赞美诗也都是独立于它们如今所属的文本而流传的。C.H. XIII在结束其关于灵性启悟的记述时写道：“如今你已获得关于你自己和我们父的灵性知识。”

body.text: – Whether the last three writings (XVI-XVIII) were part of the C.H. from the beginning or were added at a later date is difficult to decide, but they certainly stand a little apart from the rest of the collection. Not Hermes Trismegistus, or the Nous through Hermes, is the teacher but Asclepius (XVI), Tat (XVII, a fragment, in which a king is exhorted to honour the statues of the gods), and an unknown panegyrist, who hardly can be called a hermetist at all (XVIII).
body.zh: ——最后三篇（XVI—XVIII）是否从一开始就属于C.H.，抑或是后来增补的，难以断定，但它们无疑与其余各篇稍有距离。教师不是赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯，也不是通过赫尔墨斯说话的努斯，而是阿斯克勒庇俄斯（XVI）、塔特（XVII，一篇残篇，其中劝勉一位国王敬奉诸神的雕像），以及一位不知名的颂辞作者，此人几乎不能被称为赫尔墨斯主义者（XVIII）。

body.text: C.H. XVI, which presents itself as a letter of Asclepius to king Ammon, is a distinct hermetic writing. It pretends to have been written in the Egyptian language, ‘which preserves the (magical) power of the words’, and urges the king not to have it translated, ‘in order that these mysteries do not reach the Greeks’ (XVI, 1-2). In this treatise, the Creator is identified with the Sun, whose energy gives life to the whole cosmos (XVI, 5-9). The role of daemons, who are subjected to the planets, is extensively discussed: they are not only responsible for natural catastrophes, such as earthquakes and volcanic eruptions, but also for the evil deeds of human beings, while at the same time they serve to punish them for these deeds (XVI, 10-17). The tractate concludes with a summary of a hymnal character (XVI, 18-19). It praises God the Father and the Sun as the creator of everything: ‘All things are parts of God, but if all things are parts of God, then everything is God. Therefore, in making all things, he makes himself’.
body.zh: C.H. XVI自称是阿斯克勒庇俄斯致国王阿蒙（Ammon）的书信，是一篇独立的赫尔墨斯著述。它声称原文以埃及语写成，而埃及语“保存着词语的（魔法）力量”，并劝国王不要让人把它译出，“以免这些秘义传到希腊人那里”（XVI, 1-2）。在这篇论著中，造物主被等同于太阳，太阳的能量赋予整个宇宙以生命（XVI, 5-9）。文中详尽讨论了臣属于诸行星的诸灵（daemons）的作用：它们不仅造成地震、火山爆发等自然灾变，也造成人类的恶行，同时又用来惩罚人类这些恶行（XVI, 10-17）。该篇以一段具有赞美诗性质的总结作结（XVI, 18-19）。它赞美父神与太阳为万物的创造者：“万物都是神的各部分；但若万物都是神的各部分，那么一切就是神。因此，他在创造万物时，也创造了他自己。”

body.text: c. Greek and Latin Fragments The great number of quotations of now lost hermetic texts in authors of the 4th and 5th centuries shows that in late Antiquity many more hermetic philosophical treatises were in circulation than have been preserved today. The earliest quotation of a hermetic writing is found in Tertullian (ca. A.D. 200), De anima, 33, 2 (Nock & Festugière, IV, 104). Forty fragments have been preserved in the Anthology that John of Stobi, usually called Stobaeus, composed in the first decades of the 5th century for the instruction of his son Septimius. Ten of them derive from C.H. II, IV and IX and one from the Asclepius; they are valuable since they represent an earlier and better textual tradition than the preserved complete manuscripts. The other 29 fragments of Stobaeus were taken from hermetic writings that are now lost. Most of them deal with the central themes of hermetic philosophy, God, cosmos and man, but there are some remarkable exceptions. In Fragm. VI (NF III, 34-39), for instance, Hermes explains to his son Tat the activity of the 36 decans and their relationship with the other celestial bodies, which shows that astrology and philosophical Hermetism did not belong to completely separate areas. A very interesting fragment is Stobaeus’ large excerpt from ‘a holy book of Hermes Trismegistus’ called Daughter (or Pupil) of the World, mostly indicated by its Greek title Korè kosmou (Fragm. XXIII, NF III, 1-50). In this writing, the teacher is not Hermes but Isis, who instructs her son Horus after herself having been instructed by Hermes. ‘All-knowing Hermes’ is said to have written down all the cosmic mysteries before the creation of the world and to have hidden the books near the secret symbols of Osiris, with a prayer and magical formulas (XXIII, 1-8). Then follows an artificial myth about the creation of the cosmos: first God made Nature, then 60 different kinds of souls of diminishing grades of purity, and the bodies of birds, fish and quadrupeds. The human body was made to imprison and punish disobedient souls (XXIII, 9-52). Ignorance reigned on earth, but Osiris and Isis, ‘instructed by Hermes of the secret ordinances of God’ were appointed to regulate life on earth by giving laws and teaching crafts and sciences (XXIII, 53-70).
body.zh: c. 希腊文与拉丁文残篇 4、5世纪作者对今已失传的赫尔墨斯文本的大量引用表明，在古代晚期流传的赫尔墨斯哲学论著远多于今日保存下来的。最早的赫尔墨斯著述引文见于德尔图良（约公元200年）《论灵魂》33, 2（Nock & Festugière, IV, 104）。有四十则残篇保存在斯托比的约翰——通常称斯托拜乌斯——于5世纪最初几十年为其子塞普提米乌斯（Septimius）的教育而编纂的《文选》中。其中十则出自C.H. II、IV、IX，一则出自《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》；它们很有价值，因为它们代表了一种比现存完整抄本更早、更好的文本传统。斯托拜乌斯所保存的其他二十九则残篇取自今已失传的赫尔墨斯著述。它们大多讨论赫尔墨斯哲学的核心主题——神、宇宙与人——但也有一些值得注意的例外。例如在残篇VI（NF III, 34-39）中，赫尔墨斯向其子塔特解释三十六旬星（decans）的活动及其与其他天体的关系，这表明占星学与哲学赫尔墨斯主义并不属于完全分离的领域。一则极有趣的残篇是斯托拜乌斯从“赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯的一部圣书”中摘录的长篇段落，该书名为《世界之女（或世界之童女）》，通常以其希腊文标题Korè kosmou标示（残篇XXIII，NF III, 1-50）。在这部著述中，教师不是赫尔墨斯，而是伊西斯（Isis）；她在自己受教于赫尔墨斯之后，教导其子荷鲁斯（Horus）。据说“全知的赫尔墨斯”在世界创造之前已写下一切宇宙秘义，并伴以祈祷与魔法咒语，把那些书藏于奥西里斯（Osiris）的秘密象征物附近（XXIII, 1-8）。接着是一则人为构造的关于宇宙创造的神话：神首先造了自然，然后造了六十种纯度递减的不同灵魂，以及鸟、鱼与四足动物的身体。人的身体被造出来，是为了囚禁并惩罚不服从的灵魂（XXIII, 9-52）。无知统治着大地，但奥西里斯与伊西斯“受赫尔墨斯教导，知晓神的秘密规定”，被任命通过颁立法律、教授工艺与科学来治理大地上的生活（XXIII, 53-70）。

body.text: The author has apparently used a lost hermetic treatise as one of his sources, which explains the inconsistencies that can be observed in this work (Festugière, in NF III, CXXXIII-CLXVIII).
body.zh: 作者显然把一部失传的赫尔墨斯论著用作其史料之一，这解释了在这部作品中可以观察到的种种不一致（Festugière, in NF III, CXXXIII-CLXVIII）。

body.text: A considerable number of important fragments have been preserved in the Christian writers Lactantius and Cyril of Alexandria. Lactantius, who was born and educated in Africa, became a professor of Latin rhetoric in Nicomedia in Bythinia by special request of the emperor Diocletian (284- 304). Since he had become a Christian, he had to resign his chair in 303, when the Great Persecution began. About 317, the emperor Constantine the Great summoned him to Treves in Gaul to become the teacher of his son Crispus. In his most important work, the Divinae Institutiones in seven volumes, written between 304 and 314, he frequently invokes Hermes Trismegistus as a pre-Christian witness to Christ. The work contains a great number of hermetic quotations (Wlosok, 261-262), of which 13 are unknown from other sources (NF IV, 106-114). Some quotations are in Greek, which is sometimes very helpful to recover the original text, especially in the case of the Latin Asclepius. Lactantius himself composed an Epitome of his principal work, which has some value of its own, since he used the opportunity to make corrections and additions that sometimes affect his hermetic quotations.
body.zh: 相当数量的重要残篇保存在基督教作家拉克坦提乌斯（Lactantius）与亚历山大的西里尔那里。拉克坦提乌斯生于非洲并在那里受教育，应皇帝戴克里先（284—304）的特别邀请，出任比提尼亚的尼科米底亚的拉丁修辞学教授。由于他已成为基督徒，303年大迫害开始时，他不得不辞去教席。约317年，皇帝君士坦丁大帝召他到高卢的特里尔，担任其子克里斯普斯（Crispus）的教师。在他最重要的著作、七卷本《神圣教义》（Divinae Institutiones，写于304至314年之间）中，他屡次援引赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯，作为基督的前基督教见证人。该书包含大量赫尔墨斯引文（Wlosok, 261-262），其中十三则不见于其他来源（NF IV, 106-114）。有些引文为希腊文，这对恢复原文有时极有帮助，尤其是在拉丁文《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》的情况下。拉克坦提乌斯本人为其主要著作编了一部《摘要》（Epitome），它自有其价值，因为他借此机会作了修正与增补，这些有时影响到他的赫尔墨斯引文。

body.text: Cyril of Alexandria, who occupied the Alexandrian see from 412-444, appealed 13 times to Hermes Trismegistus in his Apology against Julian (Contra Julianum), which was directed to emperor Julian’s Against the Galilaeans. Cyril wrote this work between 430 and 440, when vehement polemics against Nestorius and the Nestorians, about God and man in Christ, monopolized his attention almost completely. That he nevertheless felt himself compelled to write this enormous work of at least 20 volumes, of which the first ten books have been preserved and fragments of books 11-20 exist (books 20-30 were probably never written), about 80 years after the death of Julian “the Apostat” (363), shows how dangerous he even then still considered Julian’s attack on the Christians. Cyril did not embrace Hermes as wholeheartedly as Lactantius had done, but he adduced his testimony as a pre-Christian prophecy of the coming of Christ and even of the doctrine of the Trinity. Though he seems to have had a direct knowledge of hermetic sources, in some cases Cyril apparently borrowed his hermetic passages, and their interpretation as well, from a work on the Trinity, De trinitate, which by tradition and also by most modern scholars is ascribed to Didymus the Blind (313-398), the last head of the famous Alexandrian School. In Contra Julianum I, 47, Cyril presents an alleged testimony of the Trinity by Plato and two hermetic fragments (nrs. 23 and 24, NF IV, 126-129), which, together with their interpretation, are already found in Didymus’ De trinitate, II, 27, though not in the same order (Scott, IV, 171-173).
body.zh: 亚历山大的西里尔自412至444年担任亚历山大里亚主教，他在《驳尤利安》（Contra Julianum）中十三次援引赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯；这部辩护之作针对的是尤利安皇帝的《驳加利利人》。西里尔于430至440年间撰写此书，当时针对聂斯脱利与聂斯脱利派、关于基督中神与人的激烈论战几乎完全占据了他的注意力。尽管如此，他仍感到不得不写下这部至少二十卷的巨著——其中前十卷保存下来，第11—20卷有残篇存世（第20—30卷可能从未写成）——时距“叛教者”尤利安之死（363年）约八十年，这表明他当时仍认为尤利安对基督徒的攻击何等危险。西里尔并不像拉克坦提乌斯那样全心拥抱赫尔墨斯，但他援引其见证，作为对基督来临乃至三一学说的前基督教预言。他虽然似乎直接了解赫尔墨斯文献，但在某些情况下，西里尔显然是从一部论三一的著作《论三一》（De trinitate）中借用了赫尔墨斯段落及其解释；该书按传统并据大多数学者之说，归于盲者狄迪莫斯（Didymus the Blind，313—398），即著名的亚历山大里亚教理学校的最后一位主持人。在《驳尤利安》I, 47中，西里尔提出柏拉图一则所谓的关于三一的见证，以及两则赫尔墨斯残篇（第23、24号，NF IV, 126-129）；这些连同其解释已见于狄迪莫斯《论三一》II, 27，只是次序不同（Scott, IV, 171-173）。

body.text: After the publication of the then known Greek and Latin fragments by Scott and Nock & Festugière some new material has come to light: the Greek Vienna fragments, published by Mahé (see above), and some Greek extracts, in the Bodleian Library, Oxford, published by Paramelle and Mahé, of which some derive from an otherwise unknown treatise On the Soul and others from a work called Definitions, which has been preserved in Armenian (see below). Another hermetic fragment, quoted by C. Iulius Romanus (3rd century) and preserved in Charisius (4th century), Ars grammatica II, 239, was noticed by I.G. Taifacos (Fowden, xvii).
body.zh: 在斯科特以及诺克与费斯蒂吉耶刊布当时所知的希腊文与拉丁文残篇之后，又有一些新材料问世：马埃刊布的希腊文维也纳残篇（见上文），以及帕拉梅勒（Paramelle）与马埃刊布的牛津博德利图书馆所藏的一些希腊文摘录，其中一些出自一部别无所知的论著《论灵魂》，另一些出自一部名为《定义》的著作，后者以亚美尼亚文保存下来（见下文）。另一则赫尔墨斯残篇由C. 尤利乌斯·罗曼努斯（C. Iulius Romanus，3世纪）引用、保存在卡里西乌斯（Charisius，4世纪）《文法术》II, 239中，由I. G. 泰法科斯（I. G. Taifacos）注意到（Fowden, xvii）。

body.text: d. Asclepius The largest preserved hermetic treatise is the Asclepius, which has always had an independent existence. Its original Greek title was Logos Teleios (Perfect Discourse or Perfect Revelation), but the Greek text has been lost, except for a few fragments in later writers. Though some scholars prefer an earlier date, it was most probably written in the second half of the 3rd century. Augustine is the first to quote the Latin Asclepius, in his City of God (between 410 and 426), whereas Lactantius does not seem to know it, which might be an indication that the Latin translation dates from the 4th century. It survived among the works of Apuleius (ca. 150), who can hardly have been the translator of the Greek text, as has been suggested (Hunink), and it became the only known complete hermetic treatise in the West until the Renaissance.
body.zh: d. 《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》 保存下来的篇幅最大的赫尔墨斯论著是《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》，它一直独立流传。其原希腊文标题为《圆满之言》（Logos Teleios，即“完美论说”或“完美启示”），但希腊文文本已佚，仅在后期作者中存有少数残篇。虽然有些学者倾向于更早的年代，它最可能写于3世纪下半叶。奥古斯丁是第一个引用拉丁文《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》的人，见其《上帝之城》（410至426年间），而拉克坦提乌斯似乎并不知道它，这或许表明拉丁文译本出自4世纪。它保存在阿普列乌斯（约150年）的著作之中——如有人所提出（Hunink），阿普列乌斯几乎不可能是希腊文文本的译者——并且在文艺复兴之前，它一直是西方唯一为人所知的完整赫尔墨斯论著。

body.text: The Latin Asclepius appears to be a rather free translation of the Greek Logos Teleios. That became apparent after the discovery of a Coptic translation of Asclepius, 21-29, which inter alia contains the famous “Hermetic Apocalypse” (24- 26), in Codex VI of the Nag Hammadi Library. Comparison between the Latin and Coptic translations shows that the Latin translator took the liberty to abridge or expand the Greek original. A good example of the abridgement is offered by the description of the desolate state of the land of Egypt after the gods’ withdrawal from the earth to heaven. Having said that in those days the Egyptians will be prohibited from worshipping God and even punished if they do so, the Latin text simply says, in chapter 24: ‘Then this most holy land, seat of shrines and temples, will be completely filled with tombs and corpses’. The Coptic translation, however, presents this prophecy in a more elaborate form, NHC IV, 70, 30-36: ‘On that day, the country that was more pious than all (other) countries will become impious. No longer will it be full of temples but it will be full of tombs, neither will it be full of gods but (it will be full of) corpses.’The Latin translator has obviously suppressed the distinct antithetic parallelism of the original (pious/ impious, temples/tombs, gods/corpses); the gods are even not mentioned at all. That the Coptic translation represents the original text is confirmed by Augustine’s polemics against a pagan interpretation of this prophecy, in his City of God, VIII, 23- 27 (van den Broek [1]). The discovery of the Coptic translation has also made an end to the widespread scholarly opinion that between Lactantius and Augustine the Latin “Hermetic Apocalypse” had been interpolated with allusions to the Christian persecution of paganism. These “allusions” were already to be found in the Greek text that underlies the Coptic translation and must necessarily have been written down before the persecution of pagan religions began. As a matter of fact, the idea that strangers will occupy the land and destroy the traditional religious institutions of Egypt is one of the stock themes of ancient Egyptian prophetic and apocalyptic texts (Mahé 1982, II, 68-113).
body.zh: 拉丁文《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》看来是对希腊文《圆满之言》相当自由的译本。在拿戈玛第文库第六抄本中发现《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》21-29的科普特文译本之后，这一点变得明显；该译本尤其包含著名的“赫尔墨斯启示录”（24-26）。拉丁文译本与科普特文译本的比较表明，拉丁译者擅自对希腊文原本作了删节或扩充。删节的一个好例子，是对诸神从大地升回天界之后埃及国土荒凉状况的描述。拉丁文本在说过那些日子里埃及人将被禁止崇拜神、若仍崇拜甚至会受惩罚之后，仅在第24章说：“于是这片至圣之地，神龛与神庙的所在，将到处布满坟墓与尸体。”然而科普特文译本以更详尽的形式呈现这一预言，NHC IV, 70, 30-36：“在那一天，那比一切（其他）国度更为虔诚的国度将变得不敬。它将不再布满神庙，而是布满坟墓；它也不再布满诸神，而是（布满）尸体。”拉丁译者显然抑制了原文鲜明的对偶平行（虔诚／不敬、神庙／坟墓、诸神／尸体）；诸神甚至根本未被提及。科普特文译本代表原文，这一点由奥古斯丁在《上帝之城》VIII, 23-27中对这一预言的异教解释所作的驳斥得到证实（van den Broek [1]）。科普特文译本的发现也终结了一种广泛流行的学术观点，即认为在拉克坦提乌斯与奥古斯丁之间，拉丁文“赫尔墨斯启示录”曾被掺入影射基督教迫害异教的文字。这些“影射”已见于科普特文译本所依据的希腊文文本，因而必然写于对异教宗教的迫害开始之前。事实上，外人将占据这片土地并摧毁埃及传统宗教制度这一观念，是古埃及预言与启示文本的常见主题之一（Mahé 1982, II, 68-113）。

body.text: Of the original Greek text of the Asclepius only a few fragments are left. Two of them deserve to be mentioned here separately: a very influential quotation by Lactantius and the Greek version of the final hymn of the Asclepius. In his Divinae Institutiones IV, 6, 4, Lactantius cites the Greek text of the beginning of Asclepius 8, about the creation of the second god, which he interprets in a Christian sense as referring to the generation of the Son by the Father. The passage was translated into Latin by Quodvultdeus († ca. 453) in his Adversus quinque haereses, III, 4, a work that later gained great authority because of its attribution to Augustine. In a somewhat abbreviated and occasionally Christianized form the passage became one of the most cited hermetic texts in medieval theological literature. Its best-known variant is found in the famous representation of Hermes Mercurius in the Siena floor mosaic by Giovanni di Stefano (1488; van den Broek [2], 135).
body.zh: 《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》原希腊文文本只剩下少数残篇。其中两则值得在此单独提及：拉克坦提乌斯的一则影响深远的引文，以及《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》末尾赞美诗的希腊文版本。在《神圣教义》IV, 6, 4中，拉克坦提乌斯引用了《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》第8章开头的希腊文文本，内容关于第二位神的创造；他以基督教意义将其解释为父对子的生成。这段文字由奎德武尔忒乌斯（Quodvultdeus，†约453年）译成拉丁文，见其《驳五种异端》III, 4；此书后来因被归之于奥古斯丁而获得极大权威。这段文字以有所删节、间或基督教化的形式，成为中世纪神学文献中被引用最多的赫尔墨斯文本之一。其最著名的变体见于乔瓦尼·迪·斯特凡诺（Giovanni di Stefano）在锡耶纳大教堂地面马赛克中对赫尔墨斯·墨丘利（Hermes Mercurius）的著名描绘（1488年；van den Broek [2], 135）。

body.text: The final hymn of the Asclepius, in chapter 41, has had an independent circulation. The somewhat lacunal Greek text is found in a magical papyrus in Paris, the so-called Papyrus Mimaut (Pap. Louvre, N. 2391), where it is part of a longer prayer. A Coptic translation of the Greek text, usually called the Prayer of Thanksgiving, is found in Codex VI, 7 of the Nag Hammadi Library, where it immediately follows the Discourse on the Ogdoad and the Ennead (see below). Scholarly opinion is divided about the question of whether the hymn was part of the Asclepius from the beginning and afterwards started its independent circulation or that the process went the other way round. On the basis of the Latin, Coptic and Greek texts it has been possible to reconstruct the original Greek text to a high degree of probability. It is a beautiful hymn of thanksgiving for the gift of Gnosis, which glorifies the androgyne nature of the supreme God in such a bold language that the Latin translator thought it wise to mitigate it: ‘We know you, O spiritual Light, O Life of our life. We know you, O Womb of every creature. We know you, O Womb that is pregnant by the member (physis) of the Father. We know you, O begetting Father who eternally exists’(NHC VI, 64, 22-29 parr.).
body.zh: 《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》第41章的末尾赞美诗曾独立流传。略有残损的希腊文文本见于巴黎的一件魔法蒲草纸，即所谓《米莫蒲草纸》（Pap. Louvre, N. 2391），它是其中一篇较长祈祷文的组成部分。该希腊文文本的科普特文译本通常称为《感恩祷文》，见于拿戈玛第文库第六抄本第7篇，紧接在《论八重与九重》（见下文）之后。关于这首赞美诗究竟从一开始就属于《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》、后来才开始独立流传，还是情形恰好相反，学界意见分歧。根据拉丁文、科普特文与希腊文文本，已能以很高的或然性重构原希腊文文本。这是一首优美的赞美诗，为灵知（Gnosis）的恩赐而感恩，它以极为大胆的语言颂扬至高神的雌雄同体本性，以致拉丁译者认为明智的做法是加以缓和：“我们认识你，啊，灵性的光，啊，我们生命中的生命。我们认识你，啊，一切受造物的子宫。我们认识你，啊，因父的肢体（physis）而受孕的子宫。我们认识你，啊，永远存在的生育之父”（NHC VI, 64, 22-29及平行文本）。

body.text: It is impossible to detect a detailed structure in the Asclepius: the subjects discussed are only loosely connected, mostly by association, and often interrupted by the insertion of other material. But that does not diminish its importance, for it is an extensive compendium of ancient Hermetism, most probably based on existing hermetic treatises, which the author extracted and abridged ‘without much intelligence’ (Ferguson, in Scott, IV, x-xxxiii). It has the form of a discussion between Hermes, Asclepius, Tat and Ammon, situated in the adyton, the inner sanctuary, of an Egyptian temple. Already before Tat and Ammon have arrived, Hermes discloses to Asclepius a fundamental hermetic idea: ‘All things are part of the One, or the One is all things’ (omnia unius esse aut unum esse omnia). In the following discussion about the structure of the universe, matter and soul, gods and demons, the position of the human being receives special attention (ch. 6-12). The section begins with what might be the most renowned statement of the Asclepius, which had such a great influence on the Renaissance concept of man (→ Pico della Mirandola): ‘Man is a great wonder, a living being to be worshipped and honoured’ (magnum miraculum est homo, animal adorandum et honorandum). A special human faculty, which according to the Asclepius shows the greatness of man, is his power to create the earthly gods by conjuring heavenly powers into their statues (37, 38, cf. 24). This view has aroused the interest, and the opposition as well, of many later writers; it shows beyond doubt that the philosophical hermetists did not shun theurgical practices.
body.zh: 在《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》中无法辨认出详尽的结构：所讨论的主题只是松散地相连，多半靠联想，且常因插入其他材料而中断。但这并不减损它的重要性，因为它是一部古代赫尔墨斯主义的广博汇编，很可能以现存的赫尔墨斯论著为基础，作者“并未以多少才智”加以摘录与删节（Ferguson, in Scott, IV, x-xxxiii）。它具有赫尔墨斯、阿斯克勒庇俄斯、塔特与阿蒙之间讨论的形式，场景设在一座埃及神庙的adyton，即内殿。还在塔特与阿蒙到达之前，赫尔墨斯就向阿斯克勒庇俄斯透露了一个根本的赫尔墨斯观念：“万物都是太一的部分，或者说太一就是万物”（omnia unius esse aut unum esse omnia）。在随后关于宇宙结构、物质与灵魂、诸神与诸灵的讨论中，人的地位受到特别关注（第6-12章）。这一部分以《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》中或许最著名的一句话开始，它对文艺复兴时期的人之观念影响甚巨（→皮科·德拉·米兰多拉）：“人是一件伟大的奇迹，是一种应受敬拜与尊崇的活物”（magnum miraculum est homo, animal adorandum et honorandum）。按照《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》，显示人之伟大的一种特殊能力，是他通过把天上的权能召入雕像而造出地上诸神的力量（37, 38，参24）。这一观点引起了许多后世作家的兴趣，也招致他们的反对；它无疑表明，哲学赫尔墨斯主义者并不回避神术实践。

body.text: e. Coptic Hermetic Texts The Nag Hammadi Library presented the scholarly world with three Coptic Hermetic texts and a scribal note about other hermetic texts in his possession. The Coptic translations of two important parts of the Asclepius, namely chapters 21-29 (NHC VI, 65,15-78, 43; with the “Hermetic Apocalypse”), and chapter 41 (NHC VI, 63, 33-65, 7; the “Prayer of Thanksgiving”) have already been discussed in the preceding section. Between these two texts there is a note (NHC VI, 65,8-14) in which the scribe directly addresses those who had commissioned him, declaring that he has only copied ‘this one discourse’ of the very great number of treatises that he had at his disposal, because he did not know whether his addressees already had them in their possession. It is improbable that this note was taken over from the Greek manuscript upon which the translator based his translation, but it remains undecided whether ‘this one discourse’ refers to the preceding hermetic text or to the subsequent translation of Asclepius 21-29. In any case, it shows that in the 4th century there existed much more Coptic translations of hermetic texts than the three that are extant in NHC VI. The discovery of the first of these three texts, preserved in NHC VI, 52-63, was a surprise, for it was not only completely unknown previously, but it also proved to be of great importance. It has lost its original title, but on the basis of its contents it is usually called the Discourse on the Eighth and the Ninth (Sphere) or On the Ogdoad and the Ennead. Interspersed with didactic explanations, it describes the mystical experience of a pupil who is initiated into the hermetic mystery. The first part of the treatise explains that the elevation of the pupil’s mind into the eighth and the ninth sphere is not only a personal experience but at the same time the adoption into the brotherhood of the hermetic community, which makes him a son of Hermes Trismegistus. The initiate’s future brothers, all sons of Hermes Trismegistus, join his prayers during the initiation (VI, 52, 1-54, 22). The vision of the eighth and the ninth spheres concludes a way of spiritual progress, which comprised a study of hermetic books (VI, 54, 6-32) and a pious life. This was apparently compared to a journey through the seven planetary spheres, VI, 56, 27-32: ‘We have already advanced to the seventh sphere (the Hebdomad), since we are pious and walk in your law and always fulfil your will’. After a prayer to the supreme God, ‘to whom one speaks in silence’ (VI, 56, 11-12), Hermes and his pupil embrace each other (VI, 57, 26-27) and then experience the coming down of the divine Light-power. In this experience, the initiator, Hermes, somehow becomes identical with the supreme Mind that reveals itself, and the initiate attains an ecstatic state of mind: ‘I see myself. I want to speak. Fear restrains me. . . . I see a fountain bubbling with life! . . . I have seen!’(VI, 58, 8-14). Language is of no use any more; to sing a hymn in silence is the only way to adore the divine Mind [→ Hymns and Prayers], just like the souls and the angels do in the Ogdoad (VI, 58, 17- 21; 59, 28-32). A discussion of the importance of singing spiritual hymns in silence, with some examples of this form of mystic prayer, concludes the description of the initiation proper (VI, 58, 17- 61, 17). Moreover, the initiate is exhorted to keep silence about his experience: ‘Do not speak about the vision from now on. It is proper to sing a hymn to the Father until the day to quit the body’ (VI, 60, 3-5). It is of interest to note that the author speaks about prayer in words that betray a distinct biblical influence. In VI, 55, 10-14, Hermes says that it is fitting ‘to pray to God with all our mind and all our heart and our soul’, and in 57, 18-23, he calls the hermetic prayers spiritual sacrifices, ‘which we send to you with all our heart and our soul and all our strength’. It will be clear that this phraseology is strongly coloured by one of the basic texts of Judaism, Deuteronomy 6:5: ‘You must love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul and all your strength’ (cf. Mark 12:29 parr.).
body.zh: e. 科普特文赫尔墨斯文本 拿戈玛第文库向学界提供了三篇科普特文赫尔墨斯文本，以及一则抄写员关于他手中还有其他赫尔墨斯文本的附记。《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》两个重要部分的科普特文译本，即第21-29章（NHC VI, 65,15-78, 43；含“赫尔墨斯启示录”）与第41章（NHC VI, 63, 33-65, 7；“感恩祷文”），已在上节讨论。在这两段文本之间有一则附记（NHC VI, 65,8-14），抄写员在其中直接向委托他抄写的人说话，声明他手头有极多的论著，却只抄录了“这一篇讲说”，因为他不知道他的委托人是否已经拥有那些论著。这则附记不大可能是从译者所据的希腊文抄本中照录的，但“这一篇讲说”究竟指前面那篇赫尔墨斯文本，还是指后面《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》21-29的译文，仍无定论。无论如何，它表明在4世纪时，存在的科普特文赫尔墨斯文本译本远多于NHC VI中现存的三篇。这三篇文本中的第一篇保存在NHC VI, 52-63，它的发现令人惊喜，因为它不仅此前完全无人知晓，而且被证明极为重要。它失去了原来的标题，但根据其内容，通常被称为《论第八与第九（重天）》，或《论八重与九重》。它穿插着教义性的解释，描述一位被引入赫尔墨斯秘仪的学生的神秘经验。论著的第一部分说明，学生的思想被提升到第八与第九重天，不仅是一种个人经验，同时也是被接纳进赫尔墨斯团体的兄弟会，使他成为赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯之子。入道者未来的弟兄们——他们都是赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯之子——在入门过程中加入他的祈祷（VI, 52, 1-54, 22）。对第八与第九重天的观照，结束了一条灵性进步的路径，其中包括研读赫尔墨斯书籍（VI, 54, 6-32）与过虔诚的生活。这显然被比作穿越七重行星天的旅程，VI, 56, 27-32：“我们既已虔诚，行在你的律法中，并常成全你的旨意，便已前进到第七重天（Hebdomad）。”在对至高神——“人向之唯以静默言说”（VI, 56, 11-12）——祈祷之后，赫尔墨斯与其学生彼此拥抱（VI, 57, 26-27），随后经验到神性之光—权能的降临。在这一经验中，引导者赫尔墨斯以某种方式与自我启示的至高努斯合而为一，而入道者则达到一种出神的心境：“我看见我自己。我想说话。恐惧制止了我……我看见一泓涌动着生命的泉！……我看见了！”（VI, 58, 8-14）。语言已不再有用；在静默中咏唱赞美诗，是敬拜神性努斯的唯一方式［→赞美诗与祈祷］，正如八重天中的灵魂与天使所做的那样（VI, 58, 17-21；59, 28-32）。一段关于在静默中咏唱灵性赞美诗之重要性的讨论，附有这种神秘祈祷形式的若干例子，结束了关于入门本身的描述（VI, 58, 17-61, 17）。此外，入道者被劝勉对自己的经验保持缄默：“从今以后不要谈论这异象。宜于向父咏唱赞美诗，直到脱离身体的那一日”（VI, 60, 3-5）。值得注意的是，作者论及祈祷时所用的措辞带有明显的圣经影响。在VI, 55, 10-14中，赫尔墨斯说，应当“以我们全部的心志、全部的心和全部的灵魂向神祈祷”；在57, 18-23中，他称赫尔墨斯祈祷为灵性的祭献，“我们以全部的心、全部的灵魂和全部的力量将它献给你”。显然，这种措辞深受犹太教基本文本之一《申命记》6:5的影响：“你要尽心、尽性、尽力爱主你的神”（参《马可福音》12:29及平行经文）。

body.text: One of the most interesting features of The Ogdoad and the Ennead is its use of magical and astrological elements. The supreme God is addressed by the same enumeration of the seven vowels that is often used in magical papyri to express the deity’s hidden name. In VI, 56, 17-22, the series of vowels is preceded and followed by the magical names Zòxathazò and Zòzazòth. Each vowel is followed by a series of omegas (with scribal mistakes after the vowels i and ò): ‘Zòxathazò. a òò, ee òòò, èèè òòòò, iiii òòòòò, ooooo òòòòòò, uuuuuu òòòòòòò, òòòòòòò òòòòòòòò. Zòzazòth’. A similar but not identical series is found in the prayer at VI, 61, 8-15 (with three scribal mistakes): ‘I praise you. I call your name that is hidden within me: a ò, ee òò, èèè òòò, iiii òòòò, ooooo òòòòò, uuuuuu òòòòòò, òòòòòòò òòòòòòò’. Immediately after this prayer, Hermes instructs the initiate to write down what had happened on turquoise steles in hieroglyphic characters and to place them in his sanctuary at Diospolis (most probably Diospolis Magna, Thebes, which possessed a temple of Thot). The steles should be guarded by the sun and eight guardians, those on the right being male and frog-faced, those on the left female and cat-faced. They have to be placed there at an astrologically important moment, when the sun is in the first half of the day and the planet Mercury (Hermes) is in the Sign of the Virgin and has passed 15 degrees, i.e. when the influence of Hermes’ planet is most strongly felt (VI, 61, 18-62, 20; Mahé [1978] I, 129-130). The treatise ends with an oath to be sworn by everyone who reads the book: he has to swear by the four elements, the seven rulers of being and their creating spirit, and ‘the unbegotten God and the self-begotten one and him who has been begotten’. Who keeps this oath will be reconciled with God and the deities mentioned, but who violates it will experience their wrath (VI, 22-63, 30). All this shows again that hermetic authors who described highly spiritual experiences felt no hesitation to make use of magical and astrological ideas and practices: it all belonged to their world.
body.zh: 《论八重与九重》最有趣的特征之一，是它对魔法与占星学元素的运用。至高神以七个元音的同一种列举方式来称呼，这种列举常见于魔法蒲草纸，用以表达神祇的隐秘之名。在VI, 56, 17-22中，元音序列之前与之后分别是魔法名Zòxathazò与Zòzazòth。每个元音之后跟着一串omega（在元音i与ò之后有抄写错误）：“Zòxathazò。a òò，ee òòò，èèè òòòò，iiii òòòòò，ooooo òòòòòò，uuuuuu òòòòòòò，òòòòòòò òòòòòòòò。Zòzazòth”。在VI, 61, 8-15的祈祷中可见一个相似但不完全相同的序列（有三处抄写错误）：“我赞美你。我呼唤你那隐藏于我内的名：a ò，ee òò，èèè òòò，iiii òòòò，ooooo òòòòò，uuuuuu òòòòòò，òòòòòòò òòòòòòò”。紧接这段祈祷之后，赫尔墨斯指示入道者把所发生之事以象形文字写在绿松石石板上，并安放在他在狄奥斯波利斯（Diospolis，最可能是底比斯的狄奥斯波利斯·玛格纳，那里有托特的一座神庙）的圣所中。这些石板须由太阳与八位守护者看守，右侧的为男性、蛙面，左侧的为女性、猫面。它们须在一个占星学上重要的时刻安放于此，即太阳位于一日的前半、水星（赫尔墨斯）位于处女座且已行过15度之时，也就是赫尔墨斯之星的影响最为强烈之际（VI, 61, 18-62, 20；Mahé [1978] I, 129-130）。这篇论著以凡读此书者都须宣誓的誓言作结：他须以四元素、存在的七位主宰及其创造之灵，以及“非受生的神、自生的神和被生的那一位”起誓。遵守此誓者将与神及上述诸神祇和好，违犯者将遭受他们的震怒（VI, 22-63, 30）。这一切再次表明，描述高度灵性经验的赫尔墨斯作者们毫不犹豫地使用魔法与占星学观念及实践：这一切都属于他们的世界。

body.text: f. The Armenian Definitions The Coptic Discourse on the Eighth and the Ninth Sphere and the Armenian Definitions of Hermes Trismegistus to Asclepius are the most important hermetic texts discovered in the 20th century. The Armenian translation of the original Greek text most likely dates from the second half of the 6th century. It was first edited with a Russian translation in 1956, but it was only through Mahé’s magisterial edition, translation and commentary (1982, II) that its basic importance for the study of Hermetism became clear. Some Greek fragments of the Definitions have been discovered in the Bodleian Library, Oxford (Mahé & Paramelle, 1990-1991), which have been integrated into Mahé’s English translation of the Armenian text (1999). The Definitions do not have the usual form of a dialogue; they are a collection of short, often aphoristic summaries of the main points of hermetic doctrine. A similar collection has been preserved in Stobaeus’ Fragm. XI. In C.H. XIV, 1, Hermes seems to refer to such collections, when he writes to Asclepius that he will send him a summary of the most important points (kephalaia) he had discussed with Tat. These short sentences apparently had a mnemonic function (Stobaeus, Fragm. XI, 1), which explains that, with variations, they turn up through the whole of ancient hermetic literature. At the same time, they are meant to be the object of silent meditation: ‘When you keep silent, you understand; when you talk, you just talk’ (Def. 5, 2). The Definitions ‘as a whole can be regarded as a general outline of hermetic spiritual exercises aimed at developing individual nous and making the disciple worthy of undergoing mystic initiation’ (Mahé 1999, 103). They deal with the three great themes of hermetic thought – God, world and man –, which can be distinguished from one another but not completely separated: ‘God is within himself, the world is in God, and man is in the world’ (7, 5). The Definitions predominantly deal with the world (2-3) and man (4-10), but the relationship of these ‘images of God’ to each other and, above all, to God himself is never lost sight of.
body.zh: f. 亚美尼亚文《定义》 科普特文《论第八与第九重天》与亚美尼亚文《赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯致阿斯克勒庇俄斯的定义》，是20世纪发现的最重要的赫尔墨斯文本。亚美尼亚文译本所据的希腊文原文，最可能成于6世纪下半叶。它于1956年首次刊行，附俄译文，但只是通过马埃那部堪称典范的校勘、翻译与注释（1982, II），它对赫尔墨斯主义研究的基本重要性才得以显明。在牛津博德利图书馆发现了一些《定义》的希腊文残篇（Mahé & Paramelle, 1990-1991），它们已被纳入马埃对亚美尼亚文文本的英译（1999）。《定义》不具备通常的对话形式；它们是一部简短、往往格言式的摘要汇编，概述赫尔墨斯学说的要点。斯托拜乌斯残篇XI中保存了一部类似的汇编。在C.H. XIV, 1中，赫尔墨斯似乎在提及此类汇编，他写信给阿斯克勒庇俄斯说，将寄给他一份他与塔特所讨论的最重要要点（kephalaia）的摘要。这些短句显然具有助记功能（Stobaeus, Fragm. XI, 1），这解释了它们为何以各种变体出现在整个古代赫尔墨斯文献之中。与此同时，它们也被设定为静默沉思的对象：“当你静默时，你便理解；当你言谈时，你只是在言谈”（Def. 5, 2）。《定义》“整体上可以被视为赫尔墨斯灵性修炼的一般纲要，其目的在于发展个人的努斯，并使门徒有资格接受神秘入门”（Mahé 1999, 103）。它们涉及赫尔墨斯思想的三大主题——神、世界与人——这三者可以彼此区分，却不能完全分离：“神在自身之内，世界在神之内，而人在世界之内”（7, 5）。《定义》主要讨论世界（2-3）与人（4-10），但从未忽视这些“神的形像”彼此之间、尤其是它们与神本身的关系。

body.text: The aphoristic nature of Stobaeus’ Fragm. XI and the Definitions has led Mahé to an interesting theory about the development of hermetic literature, not in a pure chronological but in a more ideal-typical sense. According to him, the earliest form of hermetic literature was a series of independent sentences expressing the basic ideas of hermetic religious philosophy, such as still found in Stobaeus’ Fragm. XI. The next step was the grouping together of related sentences into chapters, as in the Definitions. In the third stage, the sentences were linked together into a coherent treatise, which might be interspersed with reflections and didactic expositions. Even in such mythological texts as the Poimandres (C.H. I) the hermetic maxims appear at the key points of the myth, determining both its structure and the arrangement of the mythic elements borrowed from older sources (Mahé 1982, II, 408-436). Moreover, based on the observation that the Poimandres reflects a considerable number of sentences of the Definitions, Mahé dated the original Greek version of the latter work to the 1st century A.D. Moreover, he also tried to establish a direct link with the earlier Egyptian wisdom literature (also Mahé 1999). These views have met with strong opposition from Fowden (71-72). It should be observed, however, that the development from hermetic sentence to hermetic treatise, as described by Mahé, has a distinct and undisputed parallel in Greek gnomic literature, as can be seen from an analysis of the sententious structure of Porphyry’s Letter to Marcella and, on the Christian side, the Teachings of Silvanus. Though the Egyptian connection is not to be excluded completely, it seems quite certain that the literary forms and contents of the hermetic sentences and treatises are more closely related to the Greek gnomic tradition than to Egyptian wisdom literature.
body.zh: 斯托拜乌斯残篇XI与《定义》的格言性质，使马埃提出了一种关于赫尔墨斯文献发展的有趣理论，这种发展不是纯粹按年代顺序，而是更带理想类型意味。据他所说，赫尔墨斯文献最早的形式是一系列表达赫尔墨斯宗教哲学基本观念的独立句子，如仍见于斯托拜乌斯残篇XI者。下一步是把相关的句子按章归类，如《定义》中那样。在第三阶段，这些句子被连缀成一部连贯的论著，其中可能穿插反思与教义性的阐述。即使在《波伊曼德列斯》（C.H. I）这样的神话文本中，赫尔墨斯箴言也出现在神话的关键之处，既决定其结构，也决定借自更早来源的神话元素的安排（Mahé 1982, II, 408-436）。此外，根据《波伊曼德列斯》反映了《定义》相当多句子的观察，马埃把后者的希腊文原稿定于公元1世纪。他还试图与更早的埃及智慧文学建立起直接联系（并见Mahé 1999）。这些看法遭到福登的强烈反对（71-72）。然而应当注意，马埃所描述的自赫尔墨斯语句向赫尔墨斯论著的发展，在希腊格言文学中有一个清晰而无争议的平行例子，这从对波菲利《致玛尔凯拉书》的格言式结构的分析，以及基督教方面的《西尔瓦努斯教诲》中可以看出。虽然埃及的关联不能完全排除，但相当确定的是，赫尔墨斯语句与论著的文学形式及内容，与希腊格言传统的联系比与埃及智慧文学的联系更为密切。

body.text: 4. “General” and “Detailed” Discourses
body.zh: 4. “一般性”与“详尽性”讲说

body.text: In the hermetic literature itself, a distinction is made between “general” and “detailed” discourses. This may be no more than a literary device, reflecting the usual practice in philosophical school teaching (Festugière, Révélation, II, 34-40), for there are no hermetic treatises that explicitly designate themselves as general or detailed discourses. Hermes (C.H. X, 1 and 7;
body.zh: 在赫尔墨斯文献本身之中，“一般性”讲说与“详尽性”讲说之间有所区分。这可能只是一种文学手法，反映哲学学派教学的通常做法（Festugière, Révélation, II, 34-40），因为没有任何赫尔墨斯论著明确自称是一般性或详尽性讲说。赫尔墨斯（C.H. X, 1与7；

body.text: Stobaeus, Fragm. III, 1; Vienna, Fragm. B, 6; Ogdoad and Ennead, NHC VI, 63, 2) or his pupils (C.H. XIII, 1; Stobaeus, Fragm. VI, 1) often refer to the “General Discourses” (genikoi logoi), which Hermes had delivered previously. C.H. X presents itself as a summary of the general lectures Hermes had given to Tat the preceding day. The second category of hermetic discourses is mentioned by Cyril of Alexandria (Contra Julianum, I, 46; NF IV, 135/6, Fragm. 30), who quotes a teaching of Hermes from ‘the first of the Detailed Discourses (diexodikoi logoi) to Tat’. The word exodikos, a shorter form of diexodikos and also meaning “detailed”, most probably appears in Asclepius 1, when Hermes says that he has written many physica and exotica for his son Tat. Here the word physica seems to refer to the technical Hermetica and the word exotica to the “detailed discourses”. An interesting passage of the Coptic Discourse on the Ogdoad and the Ennead, mentions both kinds of hermetic instruction, NHC VI, 62, 33-63, 8: ‘And he who will not first be begotten by God should stick to the general (genikos) and detailed (exòdiakos, corruption of exodikos) discourses. He will not be able to read what has been written in this book, although his conscience is pure within him . . . Rather by stages he advances and enters into the way of immortality’. Most of the preserved hermetic treatises can be assigned to these two types of hermetic instruction, though it is often impossible to distinguish them clearly. They suggest that the aspirant initiate was first instructed on an elementary level and then in a more detailed and fundamental manner, as succeeding stages on the way to initiation. The initiation itself, the direct vision of God, is a personal experience, which is not described but only hinted at in the hermetic oral or written instruction. This idea is clearly expressed in the opening sentence of C.H. XIII: ‘In the general lectures, O Father, you spoke in riddles and not openly about the divine nature. You have not revealed anything, saying that nobody can be saved before rebirth’. The only works that describe the initiation proper, though interspersed with didactic expositions, are C.H. XIII and the Discourse on the Ogdoad and the Ennead, but the quotation of the latter work, cited above, shows that the real meaning of these works can only be understood if one has been ‘begotten by God’, i.e. after the initiation.
body.zh: 斯托拜乌斯，残篇III, 1；维也纳残篇B, 6；《论八重与九重》，NHC VI, 63, 2）或其弟子（C.H. XIII, 1；斯托拜乌斯，残篇VI, 1）常提到赫尔墨斯此前所作的“一般性讲说”（genikoi logoi）。C.H. X自称是赫尔墨斯前一日对塔特所作一般性讲演的摘要。第二类赫尔墨斯讲说由亚历山大的西里尔提及（《驳尤利安》I, 46；NF IV, 135/6，残篇30），他引用赫尔墨斯的一则教导，出自“致塔特的《详尽性讲说》（diexodikoi logoi）第一部”。exodikos一词是diexodikos的较短形式，也意为“详尽的”，它最可能出现在《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》第1章，赫尔墨斯在那里说他为其子塔特写了许多physica与exotica。此处physica一词似乎指技术性赫尔墨斯文献，而exotica指“详尽性讲说”。科普特文《论八重与九重》中一段有趣的文字同时提到两类赫尔墨斯教导，NHC VI, 62, 33-63, 8：“凡尚未先由神所生者，应当持守一般性（genikos）与详尽性（exòdiakos，为exodikos之讹）讲说。他不能读懂这书中之所写，尽管他内心良知纯洁……他反而要循序渐进，进入不朽之道。”大多数保存下来的赫尔墨斯论著都可以归入这两类赫尔墨斯教导，尽管往往无法清楚区分二者。它们表明，有志入道者先接受初级教导，然后接受更详尽、更根本的教导，作为通往入门之路上相继的阶段。入门本身，即对神的直接观照，是一种个人经验，在赫尔墨斯的口传或书面教导中并未被描述，而只是被暗示。这一观念清楚地表达在C.H. XIII的开篇句中：“父啊，在一般性讲演中，你以谜语而非公开的方式谈论了神性。你什么也没有揭示，只是说：人若非重生，便不能得救。”唯一描述入门本身的著作——尽管穿插着教义性阐述——是C.H. XIII与《论八重与九重》，但上文所引后者的文字表明，这些作品的真正意义只有在一个“由神所生”的人、即入门之后的人那里才能被理解。

body.text: 5. Date and Place of Origin of the Philosophical Hermetica
body.zh: 5. 哲学性赫尔墨斯文献的年代与成书地点

body.text: Since Hermes was thought to have lived in remote Egyptian antiquity, his works were also generally dated to a time that long preceded
body.zh: 由于人们认为赫尔墨斯生活在遥远的埃及上古时代，他的著作通常也被定于远早于

body.text: Graeco-Roman civilization. The hermetic writings sometimes explicitly claimed to have been translated from the Egyptian (see about C.H. XVI above), but implicitly this was suggested by all of them. The idea of the extreme old age of the hermetic literature held the field until the beginning of the 17th century. That Luther had already declared the Asclepius a fraud in the thirties of the preceding century remained widely unnoticed. In his Disputations (ed. Hermelink, Weimarer Ausgabe, 39, 1, 179-180), he argues that the Greek philosophers did not know anything about God the Creator and man made of the dust of earth. He refers briefly to Augustine, who in his Confessiones VII, 13-14, had said that in the books of the Platonists he had found the same ideas about the Word of God that are also to be found in the first chapter of the Gospel of John, with one exception: that the Word became flesh. Then Luther continues: ‘But Hermegistus (sic) composed that book of Plato and stole everything from the Gospel of John. That book then came into the hands of Augustine and by its persuasive force he was deceived’. The suggestion is that Augustine’s Platonists did not teach similar ideas as John in his Gospel, but that they were dependent on it. It seems that Luther with ‘that book of Plato’ meant the Asclepius, which was extensively discussed by Augustine in his City of God, and not only in a negative sense. But the final blow to the idea that the Hermetica were authentic writings of the Egyptian sage Hermes Trismegistus came from Isaac Casaubon (1559- 1614). He was not the first to put the authenticity of the Hermetica, or at least of some parts of it, in doubt (Purnell; Mulsow), but his criticism proved to be decisive, even in the eyes of those who adhered, and continued to adhere, to the hermetic world view (Grafton). In 1614 Casaubon published his De rebus sacris et ecclesiasticis exercitationes XVI, in which he attacked Cardinal Cesare Baronio’s Annales ecclesiastici (12 vols., 1588- 1607). He shared with Baronio the common view that Hermes was a historical person, who had lived in Egypt before Moses and had invented the art of writing and all kinds of sciences. What provoked his reaction was Baronio’s passing remark that there had been pre-Christian pagan prophets, such as Hermes Trismegistus, Hydaspes and the Sibyls, who had predicted the coming of Christ. Against this view Casaubon’s main arguments were: 1) that the book Poemander, i.e. what we now call the C.H., was completely unknown to pre-Christian authors, which leaves little doubt about its peudepigraphic character, 2) that it could not have been written by Hermes, because it is inconceivable that God had already revealed the coming of Christ to a pagan before the Law was given to Moses, 3) that the hermetic writings ‘do not contain the Egyptian doctrines of Mercurius, but ideas which are partly Greek, taken from the books of Plato and the Platonists and often with the same words, partly Christian, drawn from the Sacred Scriptures’. In his discussion of these groups of texts, Casaubon showed his great philological skill and vast knowledge. He pointed out that the style and vocabulary of the Hermetica are typical for the late Greek and Christian period, without any indication that they had been translated from the Egyptian. He found a strong Christian influence especially in the treatises I, IV and XIII of the C.H. Casaubon’s criticism, especially his philological arguments, convinced all serious philologists and historians. After him, it became an established fact of classical scholarship that the Hermetic writings date from the first centuries of our era and betray a strong influence of later Platonism and Stoicism. The great hermetic studies published by Scott and Festugière in the 20th century, with their wealth of philosophical parallels, marked the culmination and the completion of the philological tradition that was inaugurated by Casaubon. These scholars, however, did not share his argument about the Christian inspiration of at least some of the hermetic writings, though this idea has been revived in more recent scholarship, without much success (Büchli). There is no need to doubt that the seemingly Christian elements were current in the spiritual milieu the Hermetica came from, whereas the obvious biblical expressions and ideas are due to a direct or indirect Jewish influence. After Scott and Festugière, scholars have become more sensitive to the possible and actual presence of original Egyptian elements in the Hermetica (Mahé, Fowden). There is a general scholarly consensus that the treatises that abound in biblical expressions and ideas, such as C.H. I and VII, belong to the oldest layers of Hermetic literature, probably dating from the first or the beginning of the 2nd century. There are also good reasons to date the Asclepius to the 3rd century, but for the bulk of the hermetic writings it is virtually impossible to go any further than to ascribe them to the first three centuries of our era.
body.zh: 希腊化—罗马文明的年代。赫尔墨斯著述有时明确声称译自埃及文（关于C.H. XVI见上文），而所有这类著作都隐含地作出此种暗示。赫尔墨斯文献极其古老这一观念一直占据主导地位，直到17世纪初。路德早在16世纪30年代就已宣布《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》为伪作，此事却广未为人注意。在其《论辩集》（Disputationes，Hermelink编，Weimarer Ausgabe, 39, 1, 179-180）中，他论证说，希腊哲学家对造物主神以及由地上尘土所造的人一无所知。他简要提及奥古斯丁，后者在《忏悔录》VII, 13-14中曾说，他在柏拉图派的书中发现了关于神之言的同样观念，这些观念也见于《约翰福音》第一章，只有一点例外：言成了肉身。接着路德继续说：“但赫尔墨吉斯图斯（原文如此）用柏拉图的观点拼凑了那本书，从《约翰福音》中窃取了一切。那本书后来到了奥古斯丁手中，他因其说服力而受了骗。”其言下之意是，奥古斯丁的柏拉图派所教导的并非与约翰福音相似的观念，而是依赖于它。看来路德所谓“柏拉图的那本书”指的是《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》，奥古斯丁在《上帝之城》中曾广泛讨论此书，且不只是在否定的意义上。但给予“赫尔墨斯文献是埃及智者赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯的真作”这一观念以致命一击的，是伊萨克·卡索邦（Isaac Casaubon，1559—1614）。他并非第一个怀疑赫尔墨斯文献、或至少其中某些部分之真实性的人（Purnell; Mulsow），但他的批判被证明是决定性的，甚至在那些坚持并继续坚持赫尔墨斯世界观的人眼中也是如此（Grafton）。1614年，卡索邦出版其《论神圣与教会事务的十六次练习》（De rebus sacris et ecclesiasticis exercitationes XVI），在其中攻击枢机切萨雷·巴罗尼奥（Cesare Baronio）的《教会编年史》（Annales ecclesiastici，12卷，1588—1607）。他与巴罗尼奥同样持有一种共同看法：赫尔墨斯是一个历史人物，生活在摩西之前的埃及，发明了书写技艺与各种科学。激起他反应的，是巴罗尼奥的一句顺带之言：曾有一些前基督教的异教先知，如赫尔墨斯·特里斯墨吉斯忒斯、许达斯佩斯（Hydaspes）与诸西比拉（Sibyls），预言了基督的来临。针对这一看法，卡索邦的主要论点是：（1）《波伊曼德》（Poemander）一书，即我们今天所称的C.H.，对前基督教作者完全无人知晓，这使人很难怀疑其伪托性质；（2）它不可能出自赫尔墨斯之手，因为在律法赐予摩西之前，神已向一个异教徒启示基督的来临，这是不可思议的；（3）赫尔墨斯著述“并不包含墨丘利的埃及学说，而包含部分希腊观念——取自柏拉图与柏拉图派的书，且常使用相同的词语——以及部分基督教观念——取自圣经”。在讨论这几组文本时，卡索邦显示出高超的语文学技巧与广博的学识。他指出，赫尔墨斯文献的风格与词汇是晚期希腊与基督教时期的典型特征，没有任何迹象表明它们译自埃及文。他尤其发现C.H.第I、IV、XIII篇有强烈的基督教影响。卡索邦的批判，尤其是其语文学论据，说服了所有严肃的语文学家与历史学家。在他之后，赫尔墨斯著述成于我们纪元最初几个世纪、并带有后期柏拉图主义与斯多亚主义的强烈影响，便成为古典学术的一项既定事实。斯科特与费斯蒂吉耶在20世纪发表的伟大赫尔墨斯研究，以其丰富的哲学平行材料，标志着由卡索邦开创的语文学传统的顶峰与完成。然而，这些学者并不赞同他关于至少某些赫尔墨斯著述具有基督教灵感的主张，尽管这一看法在晚近学术中又被重新提出，但未获多少成功（Büchli）。没有必要怀疑，那些看似基督教的成分，在赫尔墨斯文献所出自的精神环境中本已流行，而显然的圣经措辞与观念则源于直接或间接的犹太影响。在斯科特与费斯蒂吉耶之后，学者们对赫尔墨斯文献中可能存在并实际存在的原初埃及成分变得更加敏感（Mahé, Fowden）。学界普遍认为，那些充满圣经措辞与观念的论著，如C.H. I与VII，属于赫尔墨斯文献最古老的层次，可能成于1世纪或2世纪初。也有充分理由把《阿斯克勒庇俄斯》定于3世纪，但对于赫尔墨斯著述的大部分而言，几乎不可能进一步断定，只能把它们归于我们纪元的最初三个世纪。

body.text: The spiritual climate that pervades the Hermetica points to Alexandria in Egypt as the place of origin of the hermetic world-view. For that reason it is mostly assumed that the hermetic treatises were written in Egypt too. For some of them, for instance the Poimandres and the Discourse on the Ogdoad and the Ennead, an Alexandrian origin is indeed very likely, but it is quite possible that elsewhere in the Roman world adepts of the “way of Hermes” set themselves down to compose hermetic treatises as well. There is no reason to assume that the man in Athens, who according to Cyril of Alexandria composed a work called Hermaika in 15 books, was an exception.
body.zh: 弥漫于赫尔墨斯文献中的精神氛围，指向埃及的亚历山大里亚为赫尔墨斯世界观的发源地。因此，人们大多假定赫尔墨斯论著也是在埃及写成的。对于其中一些，例如《波伊曼德列斯》与《论八重与九重》，亚历山大里亚的来源确实很可能，但也完全可能，罗马世界其他地方“赫尔墨斯之路”的信徒也坐下来撰写赫尔墨斯论著。没有理由假定，据亚历山大的西里尔所说在雅典编成一部十五卷《赫尔迈卡》的那个人，是一个例外。

body.text: A. Philosophical-Religious Hermetism 1. The Asclepius in Latin Patristics 2. The Asclepius in the 12th Century 3. Apocrypha and Translations in 12th and 13th Centuries 4. The Interpretation of the Asclepius from William of Auvergne to Nicholas of Cusa 5. The Diffusion of the Liber Viginti Quattuor Philosophorum 6. The Liber de Sex Rerum Principiis in Medieval Thought

B. Technical and Operative Hermetism 1. Astrology, Medicine and Natural Magic, Divination a. Translations from the Greek b. Translations from the Arabic c. Latin Originals 2. Ceremonial Magic 3. The Fortune of Hermetic Ceremonial Magic in Latin: Translations and Disputes
A. Philosophical-Religious Hermetism

The Hermetic literature in Latin of the Middle Ages inherited from ancient →Hermetism (known just partially from Greek and Arabic versions) ambiguities and problems which would characterize it for centuries: the unresolved differences between philosophical-religious doctrines and operational techniques (→magic, →astrology, → alchemy); the inner tensions of the Asclepius, suspended in a cultural koiné that combines late Platonism and Stoicism with a ceremonial theurgy of Egyptian origin; and the mythological origin of →Hermes Trismegistus (Mercurius in Latin), seen as a primal source of wisdom, who appears at times as a prophet of monotheism and at times as the founder of idolatry, a source of spiritual truths and inventor of demonic liturgies. But beyond the difficulties inherited from ancient Hermetism, the Middle Ages had to face still others in its attempt to achieve a consistent exegesis: the formation of a Hermetic tradition in the Arab world; the cross-circulation of texts in different linguistic areas (Latin, Hebrew, Arabic) with complicated transitions from one area to another; and the emergence of pseudo-epigraphs and the attribution to Hermes of works by different authors, which credit him with doctrines extraneous to his tradition.
