body.text: Paracelsus was the son of the physician Wilhelm Bombast von Hohenheim and an unnamed bondswoman of Einsiedeln Abbey in Switzerland. The meaning of the name “Paracelsus”, first attributed in the 1520s, is not certain, but could have arisen through the Latinisation of “Hohenheim”; the sense of “beyond or surpassing Celsus” is unlikely. About 1502 Paracelsus moved with his father to Villach (Carinthia). Little is known about his schooldays or studies. According to his own statement, he took his doctorate in medicine at Ferrara (c. 1515). He then made his “great peregrination” through Europe in the capacity of field surgeon. In 1524/25 Paracelsus can be traced at Salzburg. In 1525 he was involved in the Peasants’ War. His role is unclear but he had to flee the city. On 5.12.1526 he registered as a resident in Strasbourg and evidently wished to settle here. In March 1527 he was appointed town physician and university lecturer at Basle. He caused a sensation by lecturing in German as well as Latin and attacked the ancient medical authorities. Disputes with the medical faculty, apothecaries, and the Town Council, compounded by a patient’s complaint of excessive fees, led to his flight from Basle at the beginning of 1528. After brief residence in Colmar and Esslingen he lived in Nuremberg for a short period. Documentary sources place him at Beratzhausen in 1530, at St. Gallen in 1531, and after numerous further stations he reached Augsburg in 1536, but even here he stayed only a while. In 1537 he travelled to Mährisch Kromau to treat Johann von Leipa, the hereditary Marshal of Bohemia, and was also resident at Vienna the same year. In 1538 he was briefly in Villach and St. Veit. Relatively little is known about Paracelsus in 1539-1540, but he was in Salzburg in 1541. Severely ill, Paracelsus wrote his will on 21.9.1541 and died three days later.
body.zh: 帕拉塞尔苏斯是医生威廉·博姆巴斯特·冯·霍恩海姆（Wilhelm Bombast von Hohenheim）与一位姓名不彰的瑞士艾因西德伦修道院（Einsiedeln Abbey）女农奴之子。“帕拉塞尔苏斯”这一名字最早于1520年代开始使用，其含义并不确定，可能源自“霍恩海姆”的拉丁化；“超越或胜过塞尔苏斯（Celsus）”之义则不太可能。约1502年，帕拉塞尔苏斯随父迁往（克恩滕的）菲拉赫。关于他的求学岁月与学业，所知甚少。据其自述，他约1515年在费拉拉获得医学博士学位。此后，他以战地外科医生的身份在欧洲各地进行“大巡游”。1524/25年间，帕拉塞尔苏斯在萨尔茨堡留有行迹。1525年，他卷入农民战争。其具体角色不明，但他被迫逃离该城。1526年12月5日，他在斯特拉斯堡登记为居民，显然有意在此定居。1527年3月，他被任命为巴塞尔的城市医生与大学讲师。他以德语和拉丁语授课，并抨击古代医学权威，引起轰动。他与医学院、药剂师及市议会发生争执，加之有病人投诉其收费过高，最终导致他于1528年初逃离巴塞尔。在科尔马与埃斯林根短暂居留后，他在纽伦堡住了一个短时期。文献资料显示，他1530年在贝拉茨豪森，1531年在圣加仑；经过多处辗转后，他于1536年抵达奥格斯堡，但即便在此也只停留了不长的时间。1537年，他前往梅里施克罗毛（Mährisch Kromau）为波希米亚世袭元帅约翰·冯·莱帕（Johann von Leipa）治病，同年又居于维也纳。1538年，他短暂逗留于菲拉赫与圣法伊特。关于1539至1540年间的帕拉塞尔苏斯，所知相对较少，但1541年他在萨尔茨堡。帕拉塞尔苏斯病重，于1541年9月21日立下遗嘱，三日后去世。

body.text: 2. Medical Writings
body.zh: 2. 医学著作

body.text: Paracelsus left an extensive opus. An initial observation concerning his most important medical works, is that the early writings raise special problems. It may be assumed that he composed medical works even before his Basle period. Yet all medical works usually classified as “early” works (all unpublished during his life) cannot be dated with any certainty. A precise chronological ordering, attempted by Karl Sudhoff in preparing his standard edition (and since widespread), such as “Works c. 1520” or “Works c. 1525/26”, is unsupported. The book called “Archidoxis” belong to those writings which can be attributed to his pre-Basle period. This is Paracelsus’s major “alchemical”, i.e. pharmaceutical-chemical text. Here he presents a medically applied →alchemy, whose goal is the separation of the pure from the impure chiefly through methods of distillation. It also treats of “chemical” remedies derived from metals and minerals (e.g. quintessences, arcana, magisteria, elixirs) associated later on with the name of Paracelsus. It is evident that Paracelsus knew the pertinent late medieval alchemical works of →Ramon Llull, →Arnau de Vilanova and especially John de Rupescissa [→Jean de Rocquetaillade]. However, it is also clear that he did not identify himself with their tradition (nor the academic medicine based on ancient authorities). Many of Paracelsus’s recipes in this work were almost incomprehensible for the reader, partly due to deliberate blinds and partly due to careless presentation. This question needs closer examination, as the so-called Volumen Paramirum (not to be confused with Opus Paramirum c. 1530) is also regarded as an “early” writing. In this text, five causes of disease are described (Ens astrale, Ens venenale, Ens naturale, Ens spiritale and Ens deale), an obvious deviation from the ancient medicine of Hippocrates or Galen. The so-called Treatise on Miner’s Disease also probably dates from this period. Here the various occupational diseases of the miners are described, explicitly stating that the ancient authors do not mention these diseases. All works mentioned so far remained unprinted during Paracelsus’s lifetime. Paracelsus’s first published medical text did not appear until 1529, a work on syphilis, Vom Holtz Guaiaco gründlicher heylung. Here Paracelsus objected to the uncritical use of guaiac wood, a contemporary wonder-cure. In 1530 (possibly even in 1529) a further syphilis text appeared Von der Frantzösischen kranckheyt Drey Bücher at Nuremberg. In 1530 Paracelsus was working at Beratzhausen on Opus Paragranum. Here he introduced the pillars of his new medicine: Philosophia; Astronomia; Alchimia and – last but not least – the Virtue of the physician (Proprietas or Virtus). In 1531 Paracelsus wrote his Opus Paramirum comprising four books at St. Gallen. In its first book Paracelsus dealt with the Tria prima of Mercury, Sulphur und Salt, the three fundamental Principles, which constitute all bodies, including the human being. Paracelsus explained the Tria prima by comparison with a burning piece of wood: that which burns, is Sulphur; that which smokes, is Mercury; that which becomes ashes, is Salt. On the basis of the Tria prima, Paracelsus also developed a new pathology, whereby he attributed a significant role to the stars besides bodily causes in the origin of diseases. The “spark of fire” from the stars could for instance make the Sulphur “ill”, and in consequence the whole body would suffer disease. The second book of Opus Paramirum, the Tartarus-Buch, relates directly to the Tria prima of the first. According to Paracelsus the Tria prima carry “excrement” (Kot) with them, and this excrement can also cause diseases in the body, called tartar-diseases by Paracelsus. The Opus Paramirum identifies the stomach as the seat of tartar production. The third book of the work dealt with women and gynaecological diseases under the title De matrice. In the beginning Paracelsus distinguished between the macrocosm, man and woman as three different worlds. Men’s diseases were thus distinct from women’s diseases. The fourth book of Opus Paramirum is entitled Buch von den unsichtbaren Krankheiten und ihren Ursachen (Book of Invisible Diseases and Their Causes). Its content was not psychiatry in any modern sense, but rather magic in the broadest sense. In the first part Paracelsus described how the Devil could gain influence through “false belief” over humans and their state of health. Like the
body.zh: 帕拉塞尔苏斯留下了卷帙浩繁的著作。关于其最重要的医学著作，首先应予指出的是：早期作品带来了特殊的问题。可以推定，他在巴塞尔时期之前便已撰写医学著作。然而，通常被归为“早期”作品的所有医学著作（它们在他生前均未刊行），都无法确切系年。卡尔·祖德霍夫（Karl Sudhoff）在编订其标准版时尝试作出的精确年代排序（此后被广泛沿用），如“约1520年著作”或“约1525/26年著作”，缺乏依据。名为《Archidoxis》的书属于可归入其巴塞尔时期之前的作品。这是帕拉塞尔苏斯主要的“炼金术”文本，亦即药物化学文本。在此，他提出一种应用于医学的→炼金术，其目标主要是通过蒸馏方法将纯净者与不纯者分离。书中还论述了从金属与矿物中制取的“化学”药物（如精质 quintessences、奥秘物 arcana、magisteria、酏剂 elixirs），这些后来与帕拉塞尔苏斯之名联系在一起。显然，帕拉塞尔苏斯熟悉→拉蒙·柳利（Ramon Llull）、→阿尔瑙·德·维拉诺瓦（Arnau de Vilanova），尤其是约翰·德·鲁佩西萨（John de Rupescissa）[→让·德·罗克塔亚德（Jean de Rocquetaillade）]相应的晚期中世纪炼金术著作。然而同样清楚的是，他并不认同他们的传统（也不认同以古代权威为基础的学院医学）。此书中帕拉塞尔苏斯的许多配方对读者而言几乎无法理解，部分是由于刻意的障眼法，部分是由于表述草率。这一问题需要更细致地考察，因为所谓的《Volumen Paramirum》（不要与约1530年的《Opus Paramirum》混淆）也被视为“早期”作品。该文本描述了疾病的五种原因（Ens astrale、Ens venenale、Ens naturale、Ens spiritale 与 Ens deale），这显然偏离了希波克拉底或盖伦的古代医学。所谓的《矿工病论》很可能也出自这一时期。书中描述了矿工的各种职业病，并明确指称古代作者未曾提及这些疾病。上述所有著作在帕拉塞尔苏斯生前均未付印。帕拉塞尔苏斯首次发表的医学文本迟至1529年才问世，即论梅毒之作《Vom Holtz Guaiaco gründlicher heylung》。在此，帕拉塞尔苏斯反对不加批判地使用愈疮木（guaiac wood）——当时的一种万灵药。1530年（或许早在1529年），另一部梅毒论著《Von der Frantzösischen kranckheyt Drey Bücher》在纽伦堡出版。1530年，帕拉塞尔苏斯在贝拉茨豪森撰写《Opus Paragranum》。在此，他提出了新医学的几大支柱：哲学（Philosophia）、天文学（Astronomia）、炼金术（Alchimia），以及——同样重要的——医生的德性（Proprietas 或 Virtus）。1531年，帕拉塞尔苏斯在圣加仑撰写了包括四卷的《Opus Paramirum》。其第一卷论述水银、硫磺与盐这“三原质”（tria prima），即构成包括人在内一切物体的三个基本原理。帕拉塞尔苏斯以一块燃烧的木柴作比来解释三原质：燃烧者为硫磺，冒烟者为水银，化为灰烬者为盐。在三原质的基础上，帕拉塞尔苏斯还发展出一种新的病理学，其中他在疾病起源的躯体原因之外，赋予星辰以重要角色。例如，来自星辰的“火花”可使硫磺“患病”，进而使整个身体罹患疾病。《Opus Paramirum》第二卷《Tartarus-Buch》与第一卷的三原质直接相关。据帕拉塞尔苏斯之说，三原质带有“排泄物”（Kot），这种排泄物也能在体内引发疾病，帕拉塞尔苏斯称之为“石垢病”（tartar-diseases）。《Opus Paramirum》将胃认定为石垢生成的所在。该书第三卷以《De matrice》为题，论述女性与妇科疾病。开篇处，帕拉塞尔苏斯将大宇宙、男人与女人区分为三个不同的世界。因此，男人的疾病与女人的疾病彼此有别。《Opus Paramirum》第四卷题为《Buch von den unsichtbaren Krankheiten und ihren Ursachen》（《无形疾病及其原因之书》）。其内容并非任何现代意义上的精神病学，而是最广义上的魔法。第一部分中，帕拉塞尔苏斯描述了魔鬼如何通过“虚假的信仰”对人及其健康状况施加影响。正如

body.text: Devil, man could also work curses through “belief”. Some remarks show that Paracelsus assumed the existence of witches. He treated this topic more extensively in Philosophia de divinis operibus et factis, which was probably written between 1529 and 1532, and where he distinguished between the marks and works of witches [→Witchcraft]. Witches who have not yet committed evil deeds can still be cured through Christian remedies such as prayer and fasting. Paracelsus gave no indication of the procedure against witches deemed to be active by their community. It may be assumed that he would have supported drastic measures including the death penalty in such cases. In 1535 Paracelsus’s balneological text, Vonn dem Bad Pfeffers . . . Tugenden (The Virtues of Bad Pfäffers) was published, followed in 1536 by his Grosse Wundartzney (Great Book of WoundSurgery), in which Paracelsus expounded internal diseases rather than surgical principles. Here Paracelsus also touched on the doctrine of signatures, which is often associated with his name. Many passages contain instructions for “magical” remedies, so that it is not entirely incomprehensible that Paracelsus was suspected of sorcery in his own lifetime. His Astronomia Magna (c. 1537/38) is a comprehensive medical anthropology and cosmology, yet remains in a fragmentary form. Here Paracelsus distinguished between a terrestrial and heavenly “part” of the human being, whereby the terrestrial is subject to the stars, while human freedom is of heavenly origin. The Christian aspect of Astronomia Magna is evident. The influence of neoplatonic thought [→Neoplatonism] in this writing is a matter of debate among scholars.
body.zh: 魔鬼一样，人也能通过“信仰”施行诅咒。一些论述表明，帕拉塞尔苏斯假定了女巫的存在。他在《Philosophia de divinis operibus et factis》中更详尽地处理了这一主题，该书可能写于1529至1532年间，其中他区分了女巫的印记与作为[→巫术]。尚未犯下恶行的女巫仍可通过祈祷、斋戒等基督教疗法获得救治。对于如何处置被其社群认定为实际活动的女巫，帕拉塞尔苏斯未作任何说明。可以推定，在此类情形下他会支持包括死刑在内的严厉措施。1535年，帕拉塞尔苏斯的浴疗文本《Vonn dem Bad Pfeffers . . . Tugenden》（《普费弗斯温泉的功效》）出版；1536年继之出版《Grosse Wundartzney》（《大外科书》），其中帕拉塞尔苏斯阐述的是内科疾病而非外科原则。在此，帕拉塞尔苏斯还论及了常与他之名相连的“征象说”（doctrine of signatures）。书中有许多段落载有“魔法”疗法的说明，因此他在生前被怀疑施行巫术，也并非全然不可理解。他的《Astronomia Magna》（约1537/38年）是一部综合性的医学人类学与宇宙论，但仍以残篇形式存世。在此，帕拉塞尔苏斯区分了人的属地“部分”与属天“部分”，其中属地部分受星辰支配，而人的自由则源于天。《Astronomia Magna》的基督教面向显而易见。该书所受新柏拉图主义思想[→新柏拉图主义]的影响，在学者间仍有争议。

body.text: 3. Astronomical and Divinatory Writings
body.zh: 3. 天文学与占卜著作

body.text: Paracelsus also wrote astronomical and divinatory works, of which twelve were published (some in several editions) in his lifetime. On closer examination these prove to be thoroughly heterogenous. The first prophetic exercise of Paracelsus was his Practica . . . gemacht auff Europen/anzufahen in dem nechstkunfftigen Dreyssigsten Jar/Biß auff das Vier und Dreyssigst nachvolgend (Almanac for Europe for 1530 until 1534). Seven editions of this very successful almanac were published in 1529-1530 alone; it is not certain whether the first edition appeared in Strasbourg or Nuremberg. Paracelsus substantiated the publication of a four-year almanac in a postscript, stating that one need not only take the chief planetary ruler of today’s skies as the basis of prediction. The constellation of the planets also had an effect over time. Moreover, he did not think it necessary to adduce the specific constellations of the year. The prognostications are relatively ambiguous. Closely linked with the four-year almanac was Pronosticatio . . . auf dis gegenwertig jar, betreffend ein Confederation, so von andern Astronomis und Practicanten dis jar ausgelassen und ubersehen ist, printed in 1530. A grand political future was predicted for this unspecified confederation, which would endure for a long time. This prognostication was connected with the so-called Auslegung über ettliche Figuren Johannes Liechtenbergers, which has survived only in fragmentary form. In 1488 Johannes Lichtenberger published a prophetic astrological work with 45 woodcuts, in which he prophesied the appearance of an angelic shepherd and a Kaiser of Peace. In his own unpublished text, Paracelsus violently contradicted Lichtenberger on account of his pro-French and pro-Habsburg stance. The Kaiser of Peace would come from “German blood”. A further magical pictorial commentary was written about 1529/30. This so-called Auslegung der Nürnberger Figuren also remained unprinted. It was a response to a work of the Nuremberg reformer Andreas Osiander of 1527. Osiander prophesied the end of the Papacy in his commentary on a series of pictures of the Pope (at this time ascribed to Joachim von Fiore, the 12th-century Calabrian abbot and prophet). He also saw the advent of Luther the reformer in the pictures. Paracelsus criticised the Papacy vehemently in his own commentary of the pictures, but he firmly rejected Osiander’s Lutheran partisanship. No one individual nor group could introduce the necessary reformation. At this time Paracelsus evidently no longer had any hopes of the Wittenberg reformer. In several writings of the period 1531- 1534 Paracelsus interpreted natural phenomena and events (e.g. comets) as divine omens. Man must read the Bible, in order to understand these signs (he did not reveal how the text should be read). His Prognostication auf xxiiii jar zukünfftig of the year 1536 is a mantic text based on personal inspiration and makes no reference to the stars. Paracelsus adopted the scheme of annual predictions in his last prognostical writings of the period 1536 to 1539. He gives no information regarding his methods of prediction.
body.zh: 帕拉塞尔苏斯也撰写天文学与占卜类著作，其中十二种在他生前出版（有些有多个版本）。经细致考察，这些著作显得十分驳杂。帕拉塞尔苏斯的第一部预言作品是《Practica . . . gemacht auff Europen/anzufahen in dem nechstkunfftigen Dreyssigsten Jar/Biß auff das Vier und Dreyssigst nachvolgend》（《1530至1534年欧洲年历》）。仅1529至1530年间，这部极为成功的年历就出版了七个版本；初版究竟出自斯特拉斯堡还是纽伦堡，尚不确定。帕拉塞尔苏斯在后记中为出版一部四年年历提出依据，称人们不必只以当下天象中居主导地位的行星统治者作为预测基础。行星的位形也会随时间发挥作用。此外，他认为没有必要引用该年具体的星象配置。这些预言相对含糊。与四年年历密切相关的是1530年印行的《Pronosticatio . . . auf dis gegenwertig jar, betreffend ein Confederation, so von andern Astronomis und Practicanten dis jar ausgelassen und ubersehen ist》。其中为这个未加指明的联盟预言了宏大的政治前途，它将长久延续。这一预言与所谓的《Auslegung über ettliche Figuren Johannes Liechtenbergers》相关联，后者仅以残篇形式留存。1488年，约翰内斯·利希滕贝格（Johannes Lichtenberger）出版了一部附有45幅木刻的预言性占星著作，其中预言了一位天使般的牧者与一位“和平皇帝”（Kaiser of Peace）的降临。在自己未刊行的文本中，帕拉塞尔苏斯因其亲法、亲哈布斯堡的立场而激烈反驳利希滕贝格。这位和平皇帝将出自“德意志血统”。约1529/30年，他又写了一部魔法性的图像评注。这部所谓的《Auslegung der Nürnberger Figuren》同样未付印。它是对纽伦堡改革者安德烈亚斯·奥西安德尔（Andreas Osiander）1527年一部作品的回应。奥西安德尔在评注一系列教皇图像（当时被归于12世纪卡拉布里亚的修道院长与先知约阿希姆·冯·菲奥雷）时，预言了教皇制的终结。他还在这些图像中看到了改革者路德的到来。帕拉塞尔苏斯在自己对这些图像的评注中猛烈批评教皇制，但坚决拒斥奥西安德尔的路德宗派性。任何个人或团体都无法带来必要的改革。此时，帕拉塞尔苏斯显然已对维滕贝格的改革者不再抱有任何希望。在1531至1534年间的若干著作中，帕拉塞尔苏斯将自然现象与事件（如彗星）解释为神所降的征兆。人必须阅读《圣经》，方能理解这些征兆（他并未揭示文本应如何阅读）。他1536年的《Prognostication auf xxiiii jar zukünfftig》是一部基于个人灵感的预言文本，并未提及星辰。在1536至1539年间的最后几部预言著作中，帕拉塞尔苏斯采用了逐年预言的框架。他对自己的预测方法未作任何说明。

body.text: 4. Theology
body.zh: 4. 神学

body.text: However opposed →magic and theology may seem, they form a inseparable unity in Paracelsus’s worldview. He understood magic as a method of using the secrets or fundamental laws of nature, while theology provided him with a philosophical basis to pursue the welfare and resurrection of the soul along the path of eternal ideas. Moreover, the miracles performed by Jesus and the apostles in healing the sick stimulated Paracelsus to postulate a new apostolic medicine, which even went beyond his first reformation of medieval medicine, proclaimed by him at the University of Basle in 1527.
body.zh: 无论→魔法与神学看似多么对立，在帕拉塞尔苏斯的世界观中，它们构成了不可分割的统一体。他将魔法理解为一种利用自然之秘密或基本法则的方法，而神学则为他提供了哲学基础，使他能沿着永恒理念之路追求灵魂的福祉与复活。此外，耶稣与使徒治病的神迹促使帕拉塞尔苏斯提出一种新的使徒医学，它甚至超越了他1527年在巴塞尔大学所宣告的对中世纪医学的第一次改革。

body.text: Paracelsus became interested in religious subjects at an early time. His mother had served at the great Benedictine abbey of his native Einsiedeln and he retained a lifelong and faithful devotion to this place. Paracelsus tells us there were several abbots and clergymen among his teachers from different places in his Grosse Wundartzney (Great Book of Surgery). The debate initiated by Martin Luther in 1517 about the need for a reformation of the Church must have exerted a strong influence on the youth, who always questioned the traditions and theories of the ancients. These attempts at reform found their way into Paracelsus’s first theological writings which stem from the years 1524/ 25, when trying to establish himself as a physician in Salzburg. De septem punctis idolatriae Christianae (Seven Points of Christian Idolatry) gives a harsh critique of the Mauerkirche (walled church), which symbolised a church paralysed in outer splendour and empty rituals, in contrast to an inner spiritualistic church. Paracelsus stated: ‘The way to bliss needs stillness, it shuns clamour, but proceeds from the innermost heart’. At this time he composed his works on the Holy Trinity and on the Virgin Mary. Paracelsus also wrote an important commentary on the first five chapters of St. Matthew. This was the starting point of a lifelong and intensive study of the Gospels, especially St. Matthew, to which he would dedicate several lengthy commentaries. It is evident that Paracelsus largely derived his ethics, be they personal, social or medical, from the Gospels and above all from the Sermon on the Mount (Matth. 5). The Beatitudes in the Sermon on the Mount contained guidelines for a righteous life leading to eternal bliss, which Paracelsus carried to their far-reaching but logical conclusions: he demanded not only the avoidance of quarrel and wars, but also strict social justice, in which the rich would share with the poor. These radical or even revolutionary social attitudes may have led Paracelsus to join with the revolting Salzburg miners, an act assumed to have been the cause of his sudden flight from the town in the summer of 1525.
body.zh: 帕拉塞尔苏斯早年便对宗教问题产生兴趣。他的母亲曾在故乡艾因西德伦的大本笃会修道院服役，他终其一生都忠贞地眷恋此地。帕拉塞尔苏斯在《Grosse Wundartzney》（《大外科书》）中告诉我们，他的老师中有几位来自不同地方的修道院长与教士。马丁·路德1517年发起的关于教会是否需要改革的争论，必定对这位始终质疑古人传统与理论的青年产生了强烈影响。这些改革的尝试进入了帕拉塞尔苏斯最早的神学著作，它们出自1524/25年，当时他正试图在萨尔茨堡以医生身份立足。《De septem punctis idolatriae Christianae》（《基督教偶像崇拜七点》）对“墙壁教会”（Mauerkirche）作了尖锐批评，后者象征着以外在华丽与空洞仪式而僵化的教会，与内在的灵性教会相对。帕拉塞尔苏斯说：“通往至福之路需要静寂，它回避喧嚷，却发自内心最深处。”此时，他撰写了关于三位一体与圣母马利亚的著作。帕拉塞尔苏斯还写有一部关于《马太福音》前五章的重要评注。这是其终生不辍地深入研读福音书——尤其是《马太福音》——的起点，他为此撰写了数部篇幅可观的评注。显然，帕拉塞尔苏斯的伦理——无论是个人、社会还是医学伦理——大都源自福音书，尤其是《登山宝训》（《马太福音》第5章）。《登山宝训》中的八福蕴含着通向永恒至福的正义生活准则，帕拉塞尔苏斯将其推演至极具影响却合乎逻辑的结论：他不仅要求避免争吵与战争，还要求严格的社会正义，即富人应与穷人分享。这些激进乃至革命性的社会态度，可能使帕拉塞尔苏斯加入了起义的萨尔茨堡矿工之列；人们推测，这一举动正是他1525年夏突然逃离该城的原因。

body.text: In the following years Paracelsus concentrated on his reformation of medicine, based on a system of natural philosophy, astronomy and alchemy. After several frustrations and set-backs in his career – including expulsion from Basle and loss of his university position, Vadianus’ snub in St. Gallen, and his censorship at Nuremberg – he seems to have developed a habit of regularly withdrawing to the Appenzeller country of Switzerland while pondering religious subjects, even to the point of completely giving up medical practice. Only the verse from St. Luke 5:31, as reported in the Grosse Wundartzney, that only the sick would need a physician, moved him sufficiently to return to his proper profession. This is but one example of how much the Gospels gave him solace and were a continuous source of inspiration. As he further tells us, he began to address the common people as a lay preacher in ‘taverns, inns and public houses’. In this period from 1529 to 1535, Paracelsus wrote the bulk of his theological writings. He wrote an extensive commentary to the Psalter, which remains his most voluminous work, even though only part of it has survived. From the same period we also have commentaries on the Ten Commandments and on the prophets Daniel and Isaiah, several minor monographs about ethical, social and political subjects, three large commentaries on the Gospel of St. Matthew, and several sets of sermons. Another two series of tracts are characteristic of Paracelsus’s theology: the writings on the Eucharist and on the Vita Beata (Beatific Life). The Eucharist played a central role in Paracelsus’s idea of the neue kreatur (new creation) bestowed on the world by Christ, which enabled the faithful disciples to perform the same works and miracles as their master. The Vita Beata comprises tracts concerning the attainment of the beatific life, and also on the eternal religion, the highest good, the grace of God, happy-mindedness, the martyrdom of Christ, the remission of sins, Christian duties, the honoured and the rich, the churches of the Old and the New Testament, the resurrection and glorification of the body, and baptism. The Vita Beata writings are also known as the Philosophiae Magnae Pars Altera (Second Part of the Great Philosophy), whereas the first part of the Philosophia Magna consists of tracts regarding popular magic (see below).
body.zh: 此后数年，帕拉塞尔苏斯专注于以自然哲学、天文学与炼金术体系为基础的医学改革。在职业生涯屡遭挫折与失利之后——包括被逐出巴塞尔、失去大学职位、在圣加仑受瓦迪亚努斯（Vadianus）冷遇，以及在纽伦堡遭审查——他似乎养成了一种习惯：定期退隐到瑞士的阿彭策尔地区，思索宗教问题，甚至到了完全放弃行医的地步。唯有《Grosse Wundartzney》中所引《路加福音》5:31“有病的人才用得着医生”这节经文，才足以打动他重返本业。这只是一个例证，说明福音书给了他多少慰藉，又是他持续不断的灵感之源。他进一步告诉我们，他开始以平信徒传道者的身份，在“酒馆、客栈与公共居所”向平民百姓讲道。在1529至1535年这一时期，帕拉塞尔苏斯写下了其神学著作的主体。他为《诗篇》写了一部篇幅宏大的评注，此乃其篇幅最大之作，尽管仅有一部分留存下来。同一时期还有对十诫以及对先知但以理和以赛亚的评注、若干关于伦理、社会与政治主题的较短专论、三部关于《马太福音》的大型评注，以及数套布道文。另外两组系列短论是帕拉塞尔苏斯神学的特色：关于圣体圣事的著作与关于《Vita Beata》（《至福生活》）的著作。圣体圣事在帕拉塞尔苏斯关于基督赐予世界的“新造物”（neue kreatur）的观念中居于核心地位，这一新造物使忠实的门徒能够行与其主相同的事与神迹。《Vita Beata》包括论述如何达到至福生活的短论，也论及永恒宗教、至善、上帝的恩典、心灵的喜乐、基督的受难、罪的赦免、基督徒的义务、尊贵者与富人、《旧约》与《新约》的教会、身体的复活与荣耀，以及洗礼。《Vita Beata》诸作又称《Philosophiae Magnae Pars Altera》（《大哲学》第二部分），而《Philosophia Magna》的第一部分则由关于民间魔法的短论构成（见下文）。

body.text: Towards the end of his life Paracelsus entered a third phase of literary production in his theological works. In his famous Astronomia Magna (Great Astronomy, 1537/38) he again summarised the central points of his theology and emphasised the difference between the “light of the nature” and the light of the Holy Ghost. Some years later, around 1540, reviewing the two decades that had elapsed since he first started to write, he laid down his De secretis secretorum theologiae (The Secrets of the Secrets of Theology), where he expounded his mature views on beatific life. Three further sets of sermons date from the same period: De antichristo, In incantatores (about sorcerers), and In pseudodoctores.
body.zh: 晚年，帕拉塞尔苏斯的神学写作进入了第三个阶段。在其著名的《Astronomia Magna》（《大天文学》，1537/38年）中，他再次概括了其神学的要点，并强调“自然之光”与圣灵之光之间的区别。数年后，约在1540年，他回顾自开始写作以来逝去的二十年，写下了《De secretis secretorum theologiae》（《神学之秘密中的秘密》），在其中阐发了其关于至福生活的成熟观点。同一时期还有另外三套布道文：《De antichristo》、《In incantatores》（论巫师）与《In pseudodoctores》。

body.text: The preserved theological writings consist of 40 monographs or single tracts, 16 Bible commentaries, 20 sermons, 20 writings on the Eucharist, and 7 Mariological tracts. As a whole, these writings make up a corpus quite as extensive as the medical and philosophical works, but to this day only half of them have found their way into print. The remaining and so far unedited works, most of them dealing with the New Testament, especially important to Paracelsus, are now being prepared for a scholarly edition.
body.zh: 留存下来的神学著作包括40部专论或单篇短论、16部圣经评注、20篇布道文、20篇论圣体圣事的著作，以及7篇圣母论短论。总体而言，这些著作构成的文集与医学及哲学著作同样浩繁，但至今仅有半数付梓。其余迄今尚未编订的著作——大多涉及对帕拉塞尔苏斯尤为重要的《新约》——目前正在筹备学术版本。

body.text: At first sight, Paracelsus’s theological style seems quite orthodox and not so different from traditional religious thought. For the true Christian there are laws and commandments to be followed, the remission of sins has to be attained, and righteous behaviour will pave the way to eternal life. How does this Christian theology relate to the Hermetic and alchemical thought of his medical writings? On closer investigation, the peculiarities become apparent. In contrast to many contemporary religious thinkers, Paracelsus’s theology is based on direct exegesis of the Gospels rather than on St. Paul’s epistles. The attainment of eternal life plays a role of the utmost importance. Paracelsus does not refer to a somewhat remote future: in “beatific life” man is given the opportunity to achieve a foretaste of eternity. God’s laws and teachings as laid down in the Bible must be observed, but also consist in an active belief in God, respect for God, charity, knowledge and hope. Mere outward observance is not enough: the Commandments have to become alive in Christ and should lead to perfect love of God and one’s neighbour.
body.zh: 乍看之下，帕拉塞尔苏斯的神学风格颇为正统，与传统宗教思想并无太大差异。对真正的基督徒而言，有律法与诫命须遵守，有罪的赦免须求得，而正直的行为将铺就通往永生的道路。这种基督教神学与他医学著作中的赫尔墨斯主义及炼金术思想有何关联？经进一步考察，其独特之处便显现出来。与当时许多宗教思想家不同，帕拉塞尔苏斯的神学建立在直接释读福音书之上，而非圣保罗书信。获得永生具有至关重要的意义。帕拉塞尔苏斯所指的并非某个较为遥远的未来：在“至福生活”中，人获得了预先品尝永恒的机会。《圣经》所载上帝的法度与教导必须遵守，但也在于对上帝积极的信仰、对上帝的敬畏、慈爱、知识与希望。仅仅外在的遵守是不够的：诫命必须在基督里活起来，并应导向对上帝与邻人的完全之爱。

body.text: Another marked feature of Paracelsus’s philosophy and theology becomes apparent in his speculation on the double body. Man has a mortal and an immortal body, one visible and one invisible, the former confined to the realm of nature, the latter ruled by the stars and tending to eternity. Accordingly, there is an inside and an outside, an above and a below, a microcosm and a macrocosm. This notion of a double corporeality may have been partly inspired by I Corinthians 15, but can also be found in the Middle Ages, in Neoplatonic and Hermetic philosophy, and in alchemical lore. Paracelsus’s bipartition also forms one major difference with the perspective of →Agrippa of Nettesheim who with his “mundus triplex” advocated a tripartite conception of the world. One might think that Paracelsus’s concept of the Tria prima consisting of Mercury, Sulphur and Salt would lead to a ternary philosophical system. However, this does not hold for Paracelsus’s view of the spiritual composition of man and the universe, but only for the composition of matter, or more precisely, of metals, minerals, stones, wood, herbs and all growing things. Paracelsus regarded these three principles as workmen (werkleut) in the process of creation helping the superior creative principle, the archeus, in differentiating and molding the classical four elements fire, air, water, and earth, which themselves constituted the building blocks of matter. The combustible Sulphur was bestowing a characteristic form upon things, the incombustible Salt was giving the solidity, and the volatile and mediating Mercury was taking care of the nutritional requirements. When alchemy proceeds to decompose a thing into its constituents, the mercurial principle will flee as a fume or manifest as a volatile liquid, the sulphurous principle is separated as a combustible oil or resin, and the salty principle remains as a crystalline or amorphous indestructible matter. The idea of Tria prima was highly influential on the conceptual development of chemistry, dominating chemical perceptions until the mid-18th century, and also on iatrochemistry, representing a promising attempt to explain bodily functions in terms of alchemy. Paracelsus had himself speculated in Opus paramirum (c. 1531) about the operating of Tria prima in the body. However, there is no firm evidence that an equation of the three Paracelsian principles Mercury, Sulphur and Salt with the corporeal tripartition Spirit, Soul and Body respectively, nor even with the Holy Trinity of Father, Son and Holy Ghost, was already part of Paracelsus’s own doctrine. These and further philosophical speculations in interpreting the universe chemically have their origin among Paracelsus’s followers.
body.zh: 帕拉塞尔苏斯哲学与神学的另一显著特征，体现在他关于“双重身体”的思辨中。人有一个可朽的身体和一个不朽的身体，一可见、一不可见；前者囿于自然领域，后者受星辰支配并趋向永恒。相应地，有内与外、上与下、小宇宙与大宇宙。这种双重身体性的观念，部分可能受《哥林多前书》第15章启发，但也见于中世纪、新柏拉图主义与赫尔墨斯主义哲学以及炼金术传统之中。帕拉塞尔苏斯的二分法也构成他与→阿格里帕·冯·内特斯海姆（Agrippa of Nettesheim）观点的一大差异；后者以其“三重世界”（mundus triplex）主张一种三分式的世界构想。人们或许会以为，帕拉塞尔苏斯由水银、硫磺与盐构成的三原质概念会导向一种三元的哲学体系。然而，这并不适用于帕拉塞尔苏斯关于人与宇宙之精神构成的看法，而只适用于物质的构成，更准确地说，是金属、矿物、石头、木材、草药以及一切生长之物的构成。帕拉塞尔苏斯将这三个原理视为创世过程中的工匠（werkleut），协助更高的创造原理“archaeus”（元始之力）分化并塑造古典四元素——火、气、水、土，而四元素本身构成了物质的基石。可燃的硫磺赋予事物以特有的形式，不可燃的盐赋予其坚固性，而挥发性且起中介作用的水银则负责营养需求。当炼金术着手将一物分解为其成分时，水银性的原理会化为烟气逸散，或显现为一种挥发性液体；硫磺性的原理被分离为可燃的油或树脂；盐性的原理则留存为结晶状或无定形的不可毁灭之物。三原质的观念对化学的概念发展影响深远，支配了化学观念直至18世纪中叶，同时也影响了医疗化学（iatrochemistry），后者代表了一种以炼金术解释身体功能的有希望的尝试。帕拉塞尔苏斯本人曾在《Opus paramirum》（约1531年）中思辨三原质在体内的运作。然而，没有确凿证据表明，将帕拉塞尔苏斯的三个原理——水银、硫磺与盐——分别等同于灵、魂、体的三重身体划分，甚至等同于父、子、圣灵的三位一体，已然属于帕拉塞尔苏斯本人的学说。这些以及进一步以化学解释宇宙的哲学思辨，都起源于帕拉塞尔苏斯的追随者之中。

body.text: In his early Volumen paramirum (c. 1520), where he tries to give a new classification of the causes of disease, Paracelsus is well aware of his “pagan style” in explaining nature and disease in terms of alchemy and magic, but hastens to emphasise that he is a true Christian. It is possible that Paracelsus understood “pagan” philosophy not only as synonymous with ancient, but also in a narrower sense with Hermetic or Neoplatonic philosophy. On the one hand, Paracelsus felt obliged to study nature in its light as well as dark aspects, while on the other, he had to observe a framework of Christian philosophy. An attempt to combine the two viewpoints produced an inevitable tension. One might say he was bound to Mother Nature as well as to his Mother Church, and this dual allegiance may have been one cause of his personal failure during his lifetime. His Astronomia Magna attempts to give a late synthesis of these obviously conflicting worldviews, whereby Paracelsus exhorts man to become a centrum between his earthly origin and his heavenly destination.
body.zh: 在其早期的《Volumen paramirum》（约1520年）中，帕拉塞尔苏斯试图对疾病的原因作出新的分类；他十分清楚自己以炼金术和魔法解释自然与疾病的“异教风格”，但又急于强调自己是真正的基督徒。帕拉塞尔苏斯对“异教”哲学的理解，可能不仅是古代的同义词，也在较窄的意义上指赫尔墨斯主义或新柏拉图主义哲学。一方面，帕拉塞尔苏斯感到有义务研究自然的光明面与幽暗面；另一方面，他又必须遵守基督教哲学的框架。试图结合这两种观点的努力，产生了不可避免的张力。可以说，他既受缚于自然母亲，也受缚于其母教会；这种双重效忠或许是他生前个人失意的一个原因。他的《Astronomia Magna》试图对这些显然冲突的世界观作出晚期的综合；在其中，帕拉塞尔苏斯劝勉人成为介于其尘世起源与天国归宿之间的“中心”（centrum）。

body.text: As an alchemist, Paracelsus was deeply impressed with the mystery of the immaculate conception of Christ and its implications. He was familiar with medieval theories of creation and had written a tract on the generation of man (Das Buch von der Gebärung, c. 1520). He obviously attempted to apply these ideas to the heavenly birth described in the New Testament. He adopted the medieval notion of “limbus” as the womb from which God had created man. Paracelsus saw the limbus as a kind of primordial seed or clay which was handed down from generation to generation starting with Adam, and so constituted the very core of man’s spiritual potentialities. The “limbus” of Adam came from below, from nature, and was thus limited. The birth of Christ represented a neue kreatur coming into the world, a new eternal “limbus” from above, which transferred to man unprecedented possibilities. By the power of this “new creation” Jesus and the apostles were able to perform miracles, such as curing the sick, healing the blind and the lame, and even expelling evil spirits and raising the dead. Paracelsus regarded the power to perform such miracles as the cornerstone of a new and supreme apostolic medicine, surpassing even his own earlier medical reformation. The new “limbus” was bestowed on a person in baptism and renewed during the Last Supper. The Eucharist assumed the utmost importance to Paracelsus, inspiring an entire set of tracts conceived as a complete Philosophia de limbo aeterno. In soteriological terms, his central theme was not so much Jesus’death on the Cross, but first and foremost the birth of this new heavenly body.
body.zh: 作为炼金术士，帕拉塞尔苏斯对基督无玷始胎的奥秘及其含义深感震撼。他熟悉中世纪的创生理论，并撰写过一部论人的生成的短论（《Das Buch von der Gebärung》，约1520年）。他显然试图将这些观念应用于《新约》所描述的天上诞生。他采纳了中世纪“limbus”（原初质料）的观念，视之为上帝创造人类的子宫。帕拉塞尔苏斯将 limbus 视为一种原初的种子或泥土，自亚当起世代相传，因而构成了人的精神潜能的真正核心。亚当的“limbus”来自下方，来自自然，因而是有局限的。基督的诞生代表一个“新造物”（neue kreatur）进入世界，一个来自上方的新的永恒“limbus”，它将前所未有的可能性赋予了人。凭借这一“新创造”的力量，耶稣与使徒得以施行神迹，如治愈病人、使盲者与跛者康复，甚至驱除邪灵、使死者复活。帕拉塞尔苏斯将施行此类神迹的能力视为一种新的、至高无上的使徒医学的基石，它甚至超越了他自己早先的医学改革。新的“limbus”在洗礼中赐予人，并在最后的晚餐中得以更新。圣体圣事对帕拉塞尔苏斯而言具有至高的重要性，激发了一整套短论，被构想为一部完整的《Philosophia de limbo aeterno》（《论永恒 limbus 的哲学》）。从救赎论的角度看，他的核心主题与其说是耶稣在十字架上的死，不如说首先是这个新的属天之体的诞生。

body.text: For Paracelsus, the true Christian Church was not an external institution with its buildings, priests, bishops and human laws, but rather an inner church based on continuous personal revelation. Paracelsus took the foundations for this spiritualistic view of what it meant to be a true Christian from the Gospels. Here St. Peter played a major role, because he was the first to recognise Jesus as the Christ, the Son of God. According to Paracelsus, this was not revealed to Peter out of the lower light of nature, but out of the light of the Holy Ghost. Thus Peter became the prototype of the mystic, illumined by God; and obviously it was on him – Peter the rock – that Jesus wanted to build his new Church. Paracelsus suggested that the keys to heaven will be handed to “every Peter” who attempts to let himself be guided by the inner light. This is why for Paracelsus there were “two churches”, one being St. Peter’s living church of ongoing revelation, and the other one the Steinkirche (stony church) for the blind believers made by man and founded on human laws.
body.zh: 对帕拉塞尔苏斯而言，真正的基督教会并非拥有其建筑、祭司、主教与人为律法的外在制度，而是一个建立在持续的个人启示之上的内在教会。帕拉塞尔苏斯从福音书中取用了这一灵性主义观点的依据，以界定何为真正的基督徒。在此，圣彼得扮演了重要角色，因为他是第一个认出耶稣是基督、是上帝之子的人。据帕拉塞尔苏斯之说，这一认识并非通过较低的自然之光启示给彼得，而是出于圣灵之光。因此，彼得成为受上帝光照的神秘主义者的原型；显然，耶稣正是要在他——磐石彼得——之上建立自己的新教会。帕拉塞尔苏斯提出，天国的钥匙将交给“每一个彼得”，即每一个力图让自己受内在之光引导的人。正因如此，帕拉塞尔苏斯认为存在“两个教会”：一个是圣彼得那持续启示的活教会，另一个是为盲信者而设的“石头教会”（Steinkirche），由人所造，奠基于人为律法。

body.text: 5. Magic
body.zh: 5. 魔法

body.text: From his study of the Bible Paracelsus was able to make a direct link to magic. The period of antiquity, and with it the world of the New Testament, was swarming with ghosts, demons, devils, gods and magicians, and thus provided an ideal setting to discuss this topic. Paracelsus followed →Albertus Magnus in identifying the three kings or magi from the Orient, who had found the Christ child with the aid of the stars, as ideal references for the vindication of magic. Paracelsus repeatedly commented on this passage from the Gospel of St. Matthew. The model of the three kings gave him the opportunity to define a magus as someone who interprets the prophets and performs miracles in front of the people, and foretells events by the help of spirits or the stars. Only a prophet (in later years Paracelsus would prefer to speak of a “divine magician”) can accomplish more: he speaks and acts by direct divine assistance and inspiration, as seen in the case of →Moses, who opposed the Egyptian sorcerers. Paracelsus thought that the three magi were also proficient in medicine, commenting that their gifts were of direct medicinal use. Frankincense helped to protect mother and child from “flying ghosts”, and myrrh, by way of the mother’s milk, freed the baby from threatening worms. This kind of interrelation of medicine, philosophy, astronomy and magic was quite commonplace in the Middle Ages, as can be seen in →Peter of Abano. In his later years, Paracelsus interpreted magic as the art of drawing down the powers of the stars, which he considered proxies of celestial ideas, and to make them work for man. Unsurprisingly, he used the term “astronomy” as a synonym for, or even saw it as superior to magic.
body.zh: 通过对《圣经》的研究，帕拉塞尔苏斯得以直接联系到魔法。古代时期，连同《新约》的世界，充斥着鬼魂、恶魔、魔鬼、神祇与术士，因而为讨论这一主题提供了理想的背景。帕拉塞尔苏斯追随→大阿尔伯特（Albertus Magnus），将来自东方、借星辰之助找到基督婴孩的三王或术士视为为魔法辩护的理想依据。帕拉塞尔苏斯屡次评注《马太福音》中的这一段。三王的典范使他有机会将“术士”（magus）定义为：解释先知之言、在众人面前施行神迹，并借助精灵或星辰预知未来之事的人。唯有先知（晚年帕拉塞尔苏斯更愿意称之为“神圣术士”）能成就更多：他凭直接的神助与灵感言说和行动，如→摩西对抗埃及术士之例所示。帕拉塞尔苏斯认为三王也精通医学，并评述说他们的礼物具有直接的药用价值。乳香有助于保护母子免受“飞鬼”侵扰，而没药则经由母乳使婴儿摆脱威胁性的肠虫。这种医学、哲学、天文学与魔法的相互关联在中世纪颇为常见，→阿巴诺的彼得（Peter of Abano）即为一例。晚年，帕拉塞尔苏斯将魔法解释为一种技艺：将星辰的力量——他视之为天上理念的代理者——引下，并使之为人类服务。毫不奇怪，他将“天文学”一词用作魔法的同义词，甚至视其高于魔法。

body.text: At the turn of the 16th century, the learned discussion of natural magic was in full flood, but Paracelsus remained relatively silent about his sources. Among the abbots mentioned in his Grosse Wundartzney, there was one ‘von Spanheim’, which may be identified with →Johannes Trithemius, the authority on demonology, witchcraft and cryptography. Paracelsus called →Marsilio Ficino the ‘best Italian physician’, and there is evidence that he knew the German translation of Ficino’s De Vita. But in the authentic writings of Paracelsus there is no direct reference or even allusion to →Giovanni Pico della Mirandola, →Agrippa of Nettesheim, or any other representative of the Renaissance tradition of magia naturalis. However, Paracelsus was deeply indebted to his father who himself was a physician and who had instructed him in the “philosophia adepta”, by which Paracelsus may have meant Hermetic or Neoplatonic philosophy. In view of this paucity of direct references, the question of the sources of his magic arises, which is a matter of debate among specialists on Paracelsus. Will-Erich Peuckert, Walter Pagel and Kurt Goldammer were firmly convinced that Paracelsus had involved himself in the already-existing tradition of natural magic, to whose theories he gave further elaboration. Pagel even believed that Paracelsus was indebted to sources from antiquity, → Gnosticism in particular; as his main evidence he pointed to Paracelsus’s ideas on the eightfold nature of Adam. Charles Webster, in contrast, largely denied the Neoplatonic and Gnostic origins of Paracelsus’s magic, pointing instead to his extensive Biblical references. The truth of the matter may lie somewhere between these two extremes. Paracelsus’s dependence on biblical sources and his theological arguments have already been discussed above. On the other hand, in Paracelsus’s time knowledge was frequently passed on by oral teaching rather than the study of books, and Paracelsus, who had been to Italy himself, was certainly well informed about the prevailing philosophical trends and may have looked upon them as common knowledge. He was obviously influenced to some degree by Gnostic ideas, because Western alchemy, being the art that had motivated him most, went straight back to Hellenistic Egypt and was related to Gnosticism. Paracelsus was deeply convinced that all things – minerals, plants, animals and even man – had their invisible counterparts in the macrocosm, where they existed as “astra”, which represented their essence. This notion of something like eternal ideas lying behind all things, which is basic to Paracelsus’s theory of signatures, can certainly be called quintessentially (neo)platonic.
body.zh: 16世纪之交，关于自然魔法的学术讨论正如火如荼，但帕拉塞尔苏斯对其资料来源却相对缄默。在其《Grosse Wundartzney》提到的修道院长中，有一位“冯·施潘海姆”（von Spanheim），可能即→约翰内斯·特里特米乌斯（Johannes Trithemius）——恶魔学、巫术与密码学的权威。帕拉塞尔苏斯称→马尔西利奥·费奇诺（Marsilio Ficino）为“最优秀的意大利医生”，且有证据表明他熟悉费奇诺《De Vita》的德译本。但在帕拉塞尔苏斯的真作中，没有直接提及乃至暗示→乔瓦尼·皮科·德拉·米兰多拉（Giovanni Pico della Mirandola）、→阿格里帕·冯·内特斯海姆，或文艺复兴“自然魔法”（magia naturalis）传统的任何其他代表人物。然而，帕拉塞尔苏斯深受其父之恩惠；其父本人亦是医生，曾教授他“philosophia adepta”（成就哲学），帕拉塞尔苏斯所指的或许是赫尔墨斯主义或新柏拉图主义哲学。鉴于直接引证如此稀少，其魔法的来源问题便浮现出来，这也是帕拉塞尔苏斯研究者之间争论的问题。维尔-埃里希·波伊克特（Will-Erich Peuckert）、瓦尔特·帕格尔（Walter Pagel）与库尔特·戈尔德哈默（Kurt Goldammer）坚信，帕拉塞尔苏斯投身于已然存在的自然魔法传统，并对其理论作了进一步阐发。帕格尔甚至认为，帕拉塞尔苏斯受惠于古代资料，尤其是→诺斯替主义；他指出的主要证据是帕拉塞尔苏斯关于亚当八重本性的观念。与之相对，查尔斯·韦伯斯特（Charles Webster）大体上否认帕拉塞尔苏斯魔法的新柏拉图主义与诺斯替主义渊源，转而指出其广博的圣经引证。事情的真相或许介于这两个极端之间。帕拉塞尔苏斯对圣经资料的依赖及其神学论证，已在上文讨论过。另一方面，在帕拉塞尔苏斯时代，知识常常通过口授而非研读书籍流传；帕拉塞尔苏斯本人曾到过意大利，必定对当时流行的哲学潮流颇为熟悉，并可能视之为常识。他显然在某种程度上受到诺斯替观念的影响，因为西方炼金术——这一最激励他的技艺——直接上溯至希腊化时期的埃及，并与诺斯替主义相关。帕拉塞尔苏斯深信，万物——矿物、植物、动物乃至人——在大宇宙中都有其不可见的对应物，它们作为“astra”（星辰）而存在，代表着其本质。这种认为万物背后皆潜藏着某种类似永恒理念之物的观念，是帕拉塞尔苏斯征象说的基础，完全可称之为（新）柏拉图主义的典型。

body.text: Another problem in studying the magical works of Paracelsus is that some of them are certainly spurious. Although they reflect a thorough familiarity with Paracelsian thought, they lack the originality characteristic of the genuine works. They often contain a wild mixture of magical concepts and ideas. These spurious magical writings, combined with spurious alchemical tracts, were accepted as authentic by posterity for at least three centuries, thus giving rise to the false academic perception of Paracelsus as a gold-making alchemist and a heretical magician consorting with demons and the Devil.
body.zh: 研究帕拉塞尔苏斯魔法著作的另一难题在于，其中有些肯定是伪作。尽管它们反映出对帕拉塞尔苏斯思想的透彻熟悉，却缺乏真作所特有的原创性。它们往往将各种魔法概念与观念杂乱地混合在一起。这些伪托的魔法著作与伪托的炼金术短论一起，被后世当作真作接受了至少三个世纪，从而造成一种错误的学术印象：帕拉塞尔苏斯是一位造金的炼金术士，一位与恶魔和魔鬼往来的异端魔法师。

body.text: In this context it is useful to itemise some spurious magical works. The tract De occulta philosophia touches on various magical subjects. Although rejecting ceremonial magic as un-Chris-tian, it advocates the magical use of pentacles and characters. It contains a discussion of visions and dreams, and earthly ghosts referred to as gnomes. It reviews the power of the →imagination, which, when used with malicious intent, may even provoke pestilence or wars; and it treats of possession by spirits and the magical background of thunderstorms. De pestilitate contains a further disquisition on the imagination as causing diseases, and plague in particular. In this context it develops a complicated system of alchemical speculation, including the four elements and the three principles, and continues by discussing the meaning of Kabbalah [→Jewish Influences], imagination, magic, the poison from the stars and the magnetic power of human “mumia” which may either cause or heal pestilence. The Liber principiorum deals with the magical and medicinal meaning of venomous animals such as snakes, worms, spiders, crayfish and suchlike. The book Archidoxis magica instructs in the use of magical seals, numbers and signs. The Liber Azoth contains a kabbalistic theory of the “linea vitae” (the line of life). Although spurious, all these tracts played a certain role in the reception of Paracelsian thought that began in the late 16th century and exercised a decisive influence on the spiritualistic and mystic currents of the early modern period (see →Paracelsianism).
body.zh: 在此语境下，逐一列举若干伪托的魔法著作是有益的。《De occulta philosophia》短论涉及各种魔法主题。尽管将仪式魔法斥为不合基督教，它仍主张魔法性地使用五芒符（pentacles）与符记（characters）。其中讨论了异象与梦境，以及被称为“地精”（gnomes）的世间鬼灵。它考察了→想象力的力量——若以恶意运用，甚至可能引发瘟疫或战争；它还论述了精灵附体与雷暴的魔法背景。《De pestilitate》进一步论述了想象力致病、尤其是引发瘟疫的问题。在此语境下，它展开了一套复杂的炼金术思辨体系，包括四元素与三原理，继而讨论了卡巴拉[→犹太影响]、想象力、魔法、来自星辰的毒，以及人体“mumia”（穆米亚，一种人体灵质）的磁力——后者既可致病，也可治愈瘟疫。《Liber principiorum》论述蛇、虫、蜘蛛、淡水螯虾等有毒动物的魔法与药用意义。《Archidoxis magica》一书讲授魔法印记、数字与符号的使用。《Liber Azoth》包含一种关于“linea vitae”（生命之线）的卡巴拉理论。尽管出于伪托，所有这些短论都在16世纪末开始的帕拉塞尔苏斯思想接受中发挥了一定作用，并对近代早期的灵性主义与神秘主义潮流产生了决定性影响（见→帕拉塞尔苏斯主义）。

body.text: In his genuine writings Paracelsus discussed magic from an early date on. In his Volumen Paramirum (c. 1520), alongside his theory of the cause of disease, Paracelsus also discussed the use of evil spells and enchanted images by “nigromancia” (black magic), which may evoke an illness in the victim. Already in his Elf Traktat (Eleven Tracts), written around the same time, he hinted that there were two theories in medicine, corresponding to his double body speculations: the “physica” for the visible world and the “magia” for the invisible realm. Only on the basis of the latter could one find the true cause and cure of an illness. In his early years Paracelsus did not elaborate this medical aspect of magic. In his famous Paragranum (1529/ 30) Paracelsus built his house of medicine not on magic but on the four pillars of natural philosophy, astronomy, alchemy and virtue.
body.zh: 在其真作中，帕拉塞尔苏斯早在早期便讨论了魔法。在《Volumen Paramirum》（约1520年）中，帕拉塞尔苏斯除了阐述其疾病原因理论外，还讨论了“nigromancia”（黑魔法）施用恶咒与魔法图像的做法，这可能使受害者患病。在约同一时期写成的《Elf Traktat》（《十一种短论》）中，他已暗示医学中有两种理论，与其关于双重身体的思辨相对应：面向可见世界的“physica”（自然学）与面向不可见领域的“magia”（魔法）。唯有在后者的基础上，才能找到疾病的真正原因与疗法。早年，帕拉塞尔苏斯并未详述魔法的这一医学面向。在其著名的《Paragranum》（1529/30年）中，帕拉塞尔苏斯将医学之屋建立在自然哲学、天文学、炼金术与德性这四根支柱之上，而非魔法之上。

body.text: From about 1530 onwards, however, Paracelsus evinced a growing interest in magical issues. He first hinted at a scientific view of natural magic in his important five books Von den unsichtbaren Kranckheiten und deren Ursachen (The Invisible Diseases and Their Causes, 1531/32). He not only pondered the impact of belief and imagination on the origin of disease and its cure, but also discussed the medical and magical effect of mumia and characters at some length. Mumia was a medicinal preparation derived from an embalmed human corpse (the Latin word is cognate with the mummy of ancient Egyptian funerary practice). Paracelsus believed that the quintessence of the invisible human body and its vital force clung to mumia even after death, and could thus be used for marvellous purposes. Paracelsus sought to explain the power of pilgrimage sanctuaries harbouring a sepulchre in terms of the mumia of the saint’s corpse attracting the pilgrims.
body.zh: 然而自约1530年起，帕拉塞尔苏斯对魔法问题表现出日益浓厚的兴趣。他首先在其重要的五卷本《Von den unsichtbaren Kranckheiten und deren Ursachen》（《无形疾病及其原因》，1531/32年）中暗示了一种关于自然魔法的科学观点。他不仅思考了信仰与想象力对疾病起源及其治疗的影响，还相当详尽地讨论了 mumia 与符记的医学及魔法效力。mumia 是一种取自经防腐处理的人尸的药物制剂（该拉丁词与古埃及丧葬习俗中的“木乃伊”同源）。帕拉塞尔苏斯相信，人不可见身体的精质及其生命力在死后仍附着于 mumia，因而可用于奇妙的目的。帕拉塞尔苏斯试图以圣徒遗骸的 mumia 吸引朝圣者，来解释容纳圣墓的朝圣圣地的力量。

body.text: Paracelsus did not regard characters as the spells of medieval magic. In his view, magical words and phrases embodied the very language of angels and spirits, who in turn had received their powers from God. This subjection to heavenly forces signified a strong vindication of magic to Paracelsus. The magician was allowed to perform his art as long as he was strictly adhering to the good. Consequently, characters were the only way to retrieve the heavenly powers. Like the physician administring herbs to heal a patient, the magician attained his goal with the aid of characters. Regarding theories of magic, this represents an important shift from the medieval idea of a demoniac influence to that of an impersonal and quasi-natural agent, and thus can be considered as a attempt to establish natural magic on a scientific basis. In the early 1530s Paracelsus produced a set of writings (if, indeed, they are genuine) called Philosophia de divinis operibus et factis, et de secretis naturae (Philosophy of Divine works and Actions, and of the Secrets of Nature), but also referred to as the first part of the Philosophia Magna (the second part being the set of Vita Beata writings mentioned above). Here Paracelsus offers what is in fact a lengthy collection of independent tracts on various aspects of popular magic, such as witches, demons and cases of possession, lunatics, sleep, prophets and fortunetellers, elementals including fairies, gnomes and salamanders, apparitions, the imagination, characters, homunculi and monsters, invocation and necromancy.
body.zh: 帕拉塞尔苏斯并不将符记视为中世纪魔法的咒语。在他看来，魔法词语与语句体现的正是天使与精灵的语言，而后者又从上帝那里获得其力量。这种对天上力量的服属，在帕拉塞尔苏斯看来有力地证明了魔法的正当性。只要魔术师严格依附于善，便被允许施行其技艺。因此，符记是获取天上力量的唯一途径。如同医生施用草药以治愈病人，魔术师借助符记达成其目标。就魔法理论而言，这代表着一种重要转变：从中世纪关于恶魔影响的观念，转向一种非人格的、近乎自然的动因，因而可视为将自然魔法奠基于科学基础之上的尝试。1530年代初，帕拉塞尔苏斯写下一组著作（倘若它们确为真作），题为《Philosophia de divinis operibus et factis, et de secretis naturae》（《论神圣作品与作为及自然之秘密的哲学》），但也被称为《Philosophia Magna》的第一部分（第二部分即上文提到的《Vita Beata》诸作）。在此，帕拉塞尔苏斯提供的实际上是一部篇幅冗长的独立短论合集，涉及民间魔法的各个方面，如女巫、恶魔与附体案例、疯癫者、睡眠、先知与算命者、包括仙女、地精与火蜥蜴在内的元素精灵、幽灵显现、想象力、符记、人造人（homunculi）与怪物、召唤术与通灵术（necromancy）。

body.text: In his Erklerung der ganzen astronomei (Explanation of All Astronomy, c. 1536) Paracelsus made a further attempt at elevating magic to the status of a comprehensive philosophy of nature. Man and nature had to rely on the “astra” or stars referred to above as variation on the theme of celestial ideas. This led Paracelsus to define magic as the art of bringing the power of the heavens down into stones, herbs, words and characters. Magic also taught one how to transmute one thing into another, and demonstrated the significance of the stars, comets and other celestial bodies. Thus he used “astronomy” as a notion superior to magic, since the essence of things was hidden in the stars. The seven subdivisions of astronomy according to this tract were “astrologia” (the art of knowing the course and the properties of the stars), “magia”, “divinatio” (divination), “nigromantia” (the art of controlling astral bodies), “signatum” (the art of detecting man’s individual star), “artes incertae” (the arts of imagination), and “manualis” (the art of making magical instruments and talismans). Within the existing tradition of natural magic there were no models for such a subdivision, so we may assume that it was his own invention.
body.zh: 在《Erklerung der ganzen astronomei》（《全部天文学的解释》，约1536年）中，帕拉塞尔苏斯进一步尝试将魔法提升为一种综合性的自然哲学。人与自然都必须依赖上文提及的“astra”或星辰，此即天上理念这一主题的变奏。这使帕拉塞尔苏斯将魔法定义为一种技艺：将天界的力量引入石头、草药、词语与符记之中。魔法还教人如何将一物转化为另一物，并揭示星辰、彗星及其他天体的意义。因此，他将“天文学”用作一个高于魔法的概念，因为事物的本质隐藏在星辰之中。据该短论，天文学的七个分支为：“astrologia”（认识星辰运行与属性的技艺）、“magia”、“divinatio”（占卜）、“nigromantia”（控制星体的技艺）、“signatum”（探知个人本命星的技艺）、“artes incertae”（想象力的技艺）与“manualis”（制作魔法器具与护符的技艺）。在既有的自然魔法传统中，并无此种划分的范本，因此可以推想这是他自己的发明。

body.text: At the end of his life, Paracelsus attempted to summarize his teachings and describe its key points as clearly as possible. Thus in his Labyrinthus medicorum errantium (Labyrinth of Erring Physicians, 1537/38) he once again set forth the foundations of his medicine. As in the earlier Paragranum, he emphasized the importance of understanding nature, the firmament and alchemy, but this time he also philosophised about the process of attaining knowledge. He spoke about experience, science, and the role of magic. The medical art should not be grounded in mere speculation, but in a certain revelation; then it would be a “magica inventrix” that revealed to the physician all he needed to know. Thus Paracelsus advocated a scientific method that included intuition as a legitimate way of attaining knowledge.
body.zh: 晚年，帕拉塞尔苏斯试图总结其学说，并尽可能清晰地描述其要点。因此，在《Labyrinthus medicorum errantium》（《迷途医生的迷宫》，1537/38年）中，他再次阐述了其医学的基础。与此前的《Paragranum》一样，他强调理解自然、苍穹与炼金术的重要性，但这一次他还对获取知识的过程作了哲学思考。他谈到了经验、科学以及魔法的作用。医学技艺不应奠基于纯粹的思辨，而应奠基于某种启示；如此，它便是一种“magica inventrix”（发现性的魔法），向医生揭示其所需要知道的一切。因此，帕拉塞尔苏斯提倡一种将直觉视为获取知识之正当途径的科学方法。

body.text: The crowning of his philosophical endeavours, however, was his voluminous Astronomia Magna or Philosophia Sagax [Great Astronomy or Philosophy of the Wise, 1537/38], that has remained incomplete. Here he tried to outline a scientific system that should explain nature as well as the supernatural world, that combined his medical and his theological convictions, and that showed the way to knowledge and its application. In this sense, the immense philosophical edifice of the Astronomia Magna can be seen as standing at the turning point between the Middle Ages and the Early Modern Period, and comprises an early but so far only poorly appreciated contribution to the rise of scientific thinking. In the first chapters Paracelsus summarized his philosophy of the two worlds and of the eternal limbus, which in fact constituted the very foundations of his belief and served him as tools to make magic and the biblical wonders plausible or even accessible to the true physician. Thus, for him, “astronomy” in the sense of magic was the cornerstone of medicine, and indeed the mother of all arts. But Paracelsus also stated that where astronomy ended, there religion should start. The conveyance of knowledge takes place by the two corresponding lights: the light of nature, being the light of the firmament, in the natural world, and the light of the Holy Ghost in the eternal, divine world. Paracelsus continued by proposing a sophisticated classification of astronomy that surpassed his former division in the Erklerung. The “mother astronomy” is split into four subdivisional “astronomies”: one that is called “naturalis” and reigns in the realm of nature; one that is called “supera” and springs from Christ; one that is called “olympi novi” and comes from faith; and finally one that is called “inferorum” and is used by the infernal spirits that dominate black magic. Each of these four astronomies is again divided into nine “membra” (members): “magia”, “nigromantia”, “necromantia”, “astrologia”, “signatum”, “artes incertae”, “medicina adepta”, “philosophia adepta”, and “mathematica adepta”. There are even more refined subdivisions, not enumerated here. In this complicated system of philosophy, magic played only a restricted role. According to the definition given in the Astronomia Magna, magic was the means to induce the heavenly powers to come down to man, who served as a “centrum” or “medium” to receive and control them. As the physician was able to extract medicinal virtues from herbs and plants, the magician could likewise summon the astral powers, and he could do even more: he could transform them and lead them to a higher state, thus becoming a master alchemist who perfects creation. If man taps into the infernal realm, he is a sorcerer; if he depends on nature and interprets the light of the firmament, he is a magus or wise man; and if he relies solely on the Holy Ghost and heaven, then he is a divine magus or prophet, capable of performing the same wonders as Christ. Thus at the end of his life, Paracelsus succeeded in uniting his conflicting doctrines derived from “pagan” and Christian sources into one great synthesis.
body.zh: 然而，其哲学努力的顶峰是卷帙浩繁的《Astronomia Magna》或《Philosophia Sagax》[《大天文学》或《智者哲学》，1537/38年]，该书始终未能完成。在此，他试图勾勒一个科学体系：它应能解释自然与超自然世界，结合其医学与神学信念，并指明通往知识及其应用的道路。在这个意义上，《Astronomia Magna》的庞大哲学建筑可被视为矗立于中世纪与近代早期之间的转折点上，并且包含了对科学思维兴起的一份早期却迄今未获充分重视的贡献。在最初几章中，帕拉塞尔苏斯概括了他关于两个世界与永恒 limbus 的哲学；这实际上构成了其信仰的根基，并成为他使魔法与圣经神迹对真正的医生而言显得可信、甚至可及的工具。因此，对他而言，魔法意义上的“天文学”是医学的基石，实为一切技艺之母。但帕拉塞尔苏斯也指出，天文学终止之处，宗教便应开始。知识的传递通过两种相对应的光进行：自然世界中的自然之光，即苍穹之光；以及永恒神圣世界中的圣灵之光。帕拉塞尔苏斯接着提出了一种精巧的天文学分类，超越了他先前在《Erklerung》中的划分。“母亲天文学”分为四个分支“天文学”：其一名为“naturalis”，统辖自然领域；其一名为“supera”，源自基督；其一名为“olympi novi”，来自信仰；最后其一名为“inferorum”，为支配黑魔法的地狱精灵所用。这四种天文学每一种又分为九个“membra”（成员）：“magia”、“nigromantia”、“necromantia”、“astrologia”、“signatum”、“artes incertae”、“medicina adepta”、“philosophia adepta”与“mathematica adepta”。还有更为精细的划分，此处不予列举。在这一复杂的哲学体系中，魔法只扮演有限的作用。依据《Astronomia Magna》所给的定义，魔法是促使天上力量降临于人的手段，而人则作为“centrum”（中心）或“medium”（中介）来接受并控制这些力量。正如医生能从草药与植物中提取药用效能，魔术师同样能召唤星体力量，且能做得更多：他能转化这些力量，将其引向更高的状态，从而成为完善造化的炼金大师。若人接通地狱领域，便是巫师（sorcerer）；若依赖自然并解读苍穹之光，便是术士（magus）或智者；若仅倚靠圣灵与天，便是神圣术士或先知，能够施行与基督相同的神迹。因此，在生命末期，帕拉塞尔苏斯成功地将源自“异教”与基督教资料的相互冲突的学说统合为一个宏大的综合。

body.text: Paracelsus’s teachings exerted a powerful influence on posterity. In chemistry, the notion of the Tria prima became predominant for two centuries. The attempt to interpret bodily functions in terms of chemical processes stimulated the development of iatrochemistry with →Joan Baptista van Helmont and Franciscus de le Boë Sylvius as important representatives of the 17th century. In pharmacology, after years of ardent debate, the Paracelsian way of preparing chemical remedies by extracting the active medicinal principle finally grew to general acceptance. No less important was Paracelsus’s sway over various currents in Western esotericism and religious movements, and here only a few can be mentioned. It has been shown that the Vier Bücher vom wahren Christentum (Four Books on True Christendom), written by the eminent Pietist precursor Johann Arndt (1555- 1621) and a source of religious edification until the 19th century, is full of allusions to Paracelsus. There are also interconnections between Paracelsus and the theosophic writer →Valentin Weigel (1533-1588), and the same is definitely and extensively the case in the works of the mystic →Jacob Boehme (1575-1624). In turn, the Christian theosophy of →Johann Georg Gichtel (1638-1710) was deeply influenced by Boehme. Needless to say, Paracelsian philosophy plays an important role in the esoteric literature of the 18th century, including alchemical, Rosicrucian [→Rosicrucianism] and partly Masonic [→Freemasonry] sources.
body.zh: 帕拉塞尔苏斯的学说对后世产生了强有力的影响。在化学领域，三原质的观念主导了两个世纪。以化学过程解释身体功能的尝试，促进了医疗化学的发展，→扬·巴普蒂斯塔·范·海尔蒙特（Joan Baptista van Helmont）与弗朗西斯库斯·德·勒·博埃·西尔维乌斯（Franciscus de le Boë Sylvius）是其17世纪的重要代表。在药理学中，经过多年的激烈争论，帕拉塞尔苏斯式以提取有效药用原理来制备化学药物的方法，最终获得普遍接受。同样重要的是帕拉塞尔苏斯对西方秘传主义各种潮流与宗教运动的影响，此处只能提及少数几例。已有研究表明，杰出的虔敬主义先驱约翰·阿恩特（Johann Arndt，1555—1621）所著、直至19世纪仍为宗教启迪之源的《Vier Bücher vom wahren Christentum》（《论真正基督教的四书》），充满了对帕拉塞尔苏斯的暗指。帕拉塞尔苏斯与神智学作家→瓦伦丁·魏格尔（Valentin Weigel，1533—1588）之间也存在关联，而在神秘主义者→雅各布·波墨（Jacob Boehme，1575—1624）的著作中，这种关联确实而广泛地存在。反过来，→约翰·格奥尔格·吉希特尔（Johann Georg Gichtel，1638—1710）的基督教神智学又深受波墨影响。毋庸赘言，帕拉塞尔苏斯哲学在18世纪的秘传文献中扮演重要角色，包括炼金术、玫瑰十字会[→玫瑰十字会]以及部分共济会[→共济会]的文献。
